preguntas.pregunta: What makes an interpreter 'qualified' under the ADA effective-communication rules?
opciones: Interprets accurately, impartially and effectively, receptively and expressively
Holds a state license and is directly employed by the covered entity
Is a family member fluent in sign language and already known to the patient
Is certified only for the specialized vocabulary of the medical setting
preguntas.explicacion: A qualified interpreter is someone who can interpret accurately, impartially and to effect, both receptively, understanding the person, and expressively, carrying the information back, using whatever specialized vocabulary is needed. Family members often lack the impartiality and the vocabulary, and the definition turns on skill rather than on employment or licensing.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Glucose specimen integrity · CPT D5 5B time k89 · PBT III.D.3 time · CCMA 3E k138 preanalytical
preguntas.pregunta: Serum from an OGTT was left on the clot at room temperature for three hours before centrifugation. What happens to the glucose result?
opciones: It reads falsely low; glucose falls about 5% to 7% an hour in unseparated blood
It reads falsely high, because water shifts out of the cells into the serum
It is unchanged, since a clotted sample no longer consumes glucose
It is unchanged for 72 hours, as in a tube with a gel separator
preguntas.explicacion: Left at room temperature, whole blood burns its own glucose at roughly 5% to 7% an hour, about 10 mg/dL, and faster still where the white count is high or bacteria have got in; serum should not sit on the cells beyond 90 minutes without an inhibitor. Fluoride holds glucose for 72 hours, and a gel-separator tube holds it once spun, at least a week at 4 °C. The 10% water-shift effect in fluoride tubes lowers glucose; nothing here raises it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Central Line Management", section Clinical Significance: catheter connections; StatPearls, "Care of a Central Line", section Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes
preguntas.subtema: Assisting with lines · CPT D4 4B k80 equipment and transfer procedures for non-tunneled and tunneled lines
preguntas.pregunta: Before a central line hub or needleless connector is accessed, how should it be disinfected?
opciones: Scrubbed with 70% alcohol or chlorhexidine for 15 to 30 seconds each time
Scrubbed with 70% alcohol or chlorhexidine for 2 to 3 seconds each time
Wiped with sterile saline, because antiseptics degrade the connector
Left alone if a disinfecting cap has been in place since the last use
preguntas.explicacion: Catheter hubs, needleless connectors and injection ports get scrubbed before every use, 15 to 30 seconds with a swab of chlorhexidine or 70% alcohol, on top of hand hygiene. Access ports may also be scrubbed with povidone-iodine or an iodophor, and only sterile devices go into them. Antiseptic caps holding 70% alcohol are a continuous barrier between uses, not a substitute for scrubbing before access.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Fire Hazards, 29 CFR 1910.38(b) and 1910.39(b)
preguntas.subtema: Emergency action plan · CPT D1 1A 1L k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.a / 2027 I.B.7.a · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 · CMAA 3A k45
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic with 8 employees asks whether its emergency action plan must be in writing. What does OSHA's rule provide?
opciones: With 10 or fewer employees the plan may be communicated orally
It must be in writing regardless of size and posted at each exit
With fewer than 25 employees it may be oral; above that it must be written
It may be oral only if the clinic also has no fire prevention plan
preguntas.explicacion: Under 29 CFR 1910.38(b), as the eTool summarizes it, an emergency action plan is normally written, kept at the workplace and available to employees; where there are 10 employees or fewer, the employer may simply brief them orally. Section 1910.39(b) sets the same threshold for the fire prevention plan. The two plans stand apart, so having or lacking one changes nothing for the other. With 8 employees this clinic may brief its staff by word of mouth, though the minimum elements of 1910.38(c) still have to be covered.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Cardiac Muscle and Electrical Activity, Conduction System of the Heart; Atrioventricular Bundle, Bundle Branches, and Purkinje Fibers
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A student is asked to put the conduction system in order, from where the impulse starts to where it reaches the ventricular muscle. Which sequence is right?
opciones: SA node, AV node, bundle of His, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
SA node, bundle of His, AV node, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
AV node, SA node, bundle of His, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
SA node, AV node, Purkinje fibers, bundle of His, bundle branches
preguntas.explicacion: The conducting components run in order: the sinoatrial node starts the impulse, internodal pathways carry it across the atria to the atrioventricular node, where it pauses about 100 ms; it then runs down the bundle of His in the interventricular septum, splits into the two bundle branches, and reaches the Purkinje fibers, which spread it through the ventricular muscle from the apex up.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Clotting Factors Involved in Coagulation and Table 18.1; and MedlinePlus, Coagulation Factor Tests, Why do I need a coagulation factor test?
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k74) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with severe liver disease and a vitamin K deficiency bleeds longer than usual after a draw. Why is coagulation impaired?
opciones: The liver makes most clotting factors and needs vitamin K for many
Vitamin K is factor IV, the calcium needed for the entire cascade
The liver stores the platelets that release ADP and serotonin
Vitamin K activates plasmin, so clots dissolve as fast as they form
preguntas.explicacion: Clotting factors come mostly from the liver and the platelets, and the liver cannot build several of them without vitamin K, which is fat-soluble: factors II, VII, IX and X carry that mark in the table. Serious liver disease and a shortage of vitamin K are both listed causes of bleeding. Calcium is factor IV, and it is the spleen, not the liver, that stores platelets.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fecal culture (003758), How to Prepare for the Test; and MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Ova and Parasite Test, What happens during an ova and parasite test?
preguntas.subtema: Multiple stool bottles · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is given several stool collection bottles with different colored caps for a culture and a parasite exam. What should he be told?
opciones: Each bottle may carry different instructions, so read them all before starting and follow each exactly
All bottles take the same sample, so fill them from a single bowel movement in any order
Only the culture bottle matters; the others are spare containers for repeat collections
The bottles should be refrigerated for 24 hours before being returned, as for urine culture
preguntas.explicacion: Depending on which stool tests are ordered, the patient may receive several bottles, and they can come with different instructions; the advice is to read everything ahead of time and follow each set carefully. The specimen goes back to the laboratory as soon as possible, labeled with name, date and time of collection, and the patient washes the hands with soap and water afterward.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1242(c), Standard: Specimen submission, handling, and referral
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k92 · PBT VI.F (CLIA) · CCMA 3E14 k146 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic laboratory cannot perform a test and wants to send the specimen out. To which kind of laboratory may it refer the specimen under CLIA?
opciones: Only to a CLIA-certified laboratory or one CMS deems to meet equivalent requirements
To any laboratory that agrees in writing to return results within the clinic's turnaround time
To any hospital laboratory, since hospitals are exempt from the CLIA certificate requirement
To any laboratory accredited by a private body, whether or not it holds a CLIA certificate
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1242(c) restricts referral to laboratories that hold a CLIA certificate or that CMS has determined meet equivalent requirements. A turnaround agreement, hospital status or private accreditation on its own does not satisfy the rule. When a laboratory accepts referrals, it must in turn give its clients written instructions on preparation, collection, labeling, storage, transport, processing and acceptability.

preguntas.subtema: Additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: How does the red-gray tiger top or gold serum separator tube separate the serum, according to the WHO table?
opciones: A gel at the bottom of the tube separates blood from serum when it is centrifuged
A clot activator on the tube wall makes the blood clot so the serum can be poured off
Lithium heparin keeps the blood liquid and a gel separates the plasma on spinning
Sodium citrate binds calcium and the serum rises above the cells within an hour
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 lists no additive for the serum separator tube and describes its action as a gel at the bottom that separates blood from serum on centrifugation, for chemistries, immunology and serology. The clot activator belongs to the plain red tube; lithium heparin with a gel is the light green PST, which yields plasma; and sodium citrate is the coagulation tube, which never yields serum.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Undetected hemolysis in POCT · CPT D5 k90 · PBT IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 k111 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Why is hemolysis a particular concern for fingerstick whole blood point-of-care tests such as potassium?
opciones: Hemolysis cannot be seen in whole blood, so an affected result may be reported without anyone noticing it
Hemolysis is detected automatically by every whole blood device, which then refuses to display any result
Hemolysis only develops after 24 hours of storage, so it never affects a sample tested at the bedside
Hemolysis affects urine reagent strips but not blood analytes, so potassium results are unaffected by it
preguntas.explicacion: Detecting hemolysis in whole blood samples, including fingerstick specimens, is challenging. Central laboratories measure hemolysis, icterus and lipemia indices spectrophotometrically, but in POCT these can be recognized only by looking at a centrifuged aliquot, a step whole blood devices skip. Hemolysis, icterus and lipemia can give inaccurate or incalculable results, and potassium measurements are especially susceptible, so a hemolyzed fingerstick potassium can pass unnoticed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Cerebrospinal Fluid Samples); and MedlinePlus, Medical Tests, Flu (Influenza) Test
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: A cerebrospinal fluid specimen for bacterial culture cannot be plated for two hours, and a technician places it in the refrigerator to preserve it. What is wrong with that?
opciones: CSF for microbiology is never refrigerated: cold cuts the survival of Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria meningitidis
CSF for microbiology must be frozen at −20 °C or lower, because refrigeration alone does not stop cellular degeneration
CSF for microbiology must travel on wet ice, since room temperature lets the glucose fall before the culture is set up
CSF for microbiology belongs in a carbon dioxide incubator only; room temperature is not an accepted alternative for it
preguntas.explicacion: Hold cerebrospinal fluid for microbiology at room temperature, or in a carbon-dioxide-enriched incubator, until it is worked up. Chilling costs the survival of fastidious organisms, Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria meningitidis among them, and the culture can come back falsely negative. Freezing belongs to delayed serology, wet ice to bronchoalveolar lavage, refrigeration to serum awaiting prompt serology.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157(e)(2), (3), (4) and (5), Inspection, maintenance and testing
preguntas.subtema: Extinguisher inspection · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.5.c · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: How often must portable fire extinguishers be visually inspected, and how often given a maintenance check?
opciones: Visually inspected monthly; maintenance check annually, with the date recorded
Visually inspected annually; maintenance check every 6 years
Visually inspected weekly; maintenance check every 12 years, the hydrostatic interval
Visually inspected monthly; maintenance check every 3 years, kept with training records
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (e) of 29 CFR 1910.157 puts inspection, maintenance and testing on the employer: a visual inspection every month, and once a year a maintenance check whose date is written down and kept for a year past the last entry, or for as long as the shell lasts, whichever comes first. Stored-pressure dry chemical units due for a 12-year hydrostatic test are also emptied and serviced every 6 years. While a unit is away for maintenance or recharging, equivalent protection has to be provided.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1252(e); CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Ready?: Preparing for Testing; Appendix A
preguntas.subtema: Do not mix kit lots · CPT D1 1F · PBT IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.9.a · RMA III.C.3.f
preguntas.pregunta: A kit of rapid test cassettes is running low on extraction reagent, and an opened kit with a different lot number has plenty left. May the reagents be combined?
opciones: No; components of kits with different lot numbers are not interchanged unless the manufacturer allows it
Yes, provided both lots are within their expiration dates and stored at the same temperature
Yes, if an external control is run once with the mixed reagent and gives the expected result
No, unless the two lots were received in the same shipment from the same distributor
preguntas.explicacion: Components from kits of different lot numbers are not to be swapped around unless the manufacturer says otherwise, and the waived-testing guidance says the same: every component reagent of a kit comes from one kit lot, and reagents are never mixed across lot numbers. Lot numbers are recorded as well, so any result can be traced back. A passing control does not make a combination the manufacturer forbids acceptable.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Considerations; and CDC, Information on Collection of Respiratory Specimens for Influenza Virus Testing, Outpatients
preguntas.subtema: Alternatives to the NP swab · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.C.2 / V.D.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(c)
preguntas.pregunta: An infant needs a specimen for influenza testing and a nasopharyngeal swab cannot be taken. What does the CDC offer as an alternative?
opciones: A combined nasal and throat swab, or an aspirate specimen, both of which give good yield
A sputum specimen coughed deeply into a sterile cup, which gives an equivalent yield
A throat swab on its own, which in infants gives a higher yield than any nasal specimen
A blood specimen for antibody testing, which replaces the swab in patients under one year
preguntas.explicacion: The nasopharyngeal swab is the best upper respiratory specimen for influenza, but an infant cannot give one and plenty of older patients will not tolerate it. What is offered instead is a combined nasal and throat swab, or an aspirate. Combining nose and throat in one specimen detects more influenza than either site alone, and a nasopharyngeal aspirate may itself be out of reach in infants.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Layers; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Structure of the Heart, Layers of the Heart Wall
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Name the three layers of the heart wall from outside in, and identify the thickest.
opciones: Epicardium, myocardium, endocardium; the myocardium is thickest
Endocardium, myocardium, epicardium; the myocardium is thickest
Epicardium, myocardium, endocardium; the epicardium is thickest
Pericardium, myocardium, endothelium; the endocardium is thickest
preguntas.explicacion: From superficial to deep the wall is epicardium, myocardium and endocardium. The epicardium is also the visceral layer of the pericardium; the myocardium, made of cardiac muscle in a swirling pattern, is the middle and thickest layer and does the pumping; the endocardium lines the chambers. Reversing the order puts the endocardium outside, which is wrong.

preguntas.fuente: 21 CFR 640.5(b) and (c)
preguntas.subtema: Donor unit testing · CPT D4 4D k82 complete screening
preguntas.pregunta: How is the ABO group of a unit of whole blood established before it can be issued?
opciones: At least two grouping tests must agree, by different methods or antiserum lots
At least two grouping tests must agree, both run with the same lot of antiserum
One grouping test is enough if it is confirmed against the donor's record
One grouping test is enough if the unit is also typed for the Rh factor
preguntas.explicacion: Each container of whole blood is classified as to ABO group, at least two grouping tests are made, and the unit is not issued until the tests agree, using different methods or different lots of antiserum. The Rh type is determined on the same sample: a negative result has to be confirmed by further testing that includes the weak D before the unit may be labeled Rh negative.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Results
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital maps where its rejected specimens are collected, so it can aim its training at the worst areas. What did the published audit find?
opciones: Rejections came mainly from the adult emergency department, not the pediatric one
Rejections came mainly from the pediatric emergency department, well above the adult one
Rejections came mainly from surgical intensive care, well above the non-surgical units
Rejections came mainly from inpatient services, ahead of every emergency department
preguntas.explicacion: Emergency departments produced 41 % of the rejected samples, intensive care 31 % and inpatient services 28 %. Broken down by service, the adult emergency department alone accounted for 31 % and the pediatric one for 10 %, a threefold difference the authors themselves called surprising. Neurology intensive care followed at 14 % and internal medicine inpatients at 10 %.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), sections 1 and 4
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5B · PBT III.A.3 · CCMA 3D5 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory wants to hold specimens longer than the kit insert allows so that it can batch its runs. What does it owe before changing the acceptability criteria?
opciones: An in-house study showing the specimen still holds up under its own conditions
Written approval from the manufacturer covering the modified storage condition
A comment on every report stating that the insert conditions were not followed
Registration of the modified condition with the organization that accredits it
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratories do modify manufacturer instructions to suit their workflow or to stretch a reagent, and the responsibility for validating specimen stability, and so for defining what it will accept, falls on the laboratory itself under accreditation requirements. Most supplement the kit recommendations with their own stability studies, and where resources will not stretch to that, the advice is to take the more conservative published criteria rather than the longer one.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination: A Quality Tool for Clinical Laboratory Professionals, Collect Multiple Sets to Achieve the Optimal Volume
preguntas.subtema: Blood culture collection · CPT D4 4A k77 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139
preguntas.pregunta: Apart from reaching the optimal volume, why does the CDC require at least two blood culture sets per episode?
opciones: To decide whether a skin commensal that grows is a possible contaminant
To keep a spare set if the first one is lost during transport
To draw one set before the antibiotic and one after the first dose
To compare aerobic growth in one arm with anaerobic growth in the other
preguntas.explicacion: Without two sets there is no way to decide whether a commensal that grows should be called a possible contaminant; one set leaves nothing to compare it with. Both sets are drawn before antimicrobial therapy where possible, and each set already carries its own aerobic and anaerobic bottle, so the arms are not being compared by bottle type. A spare for transport is not a reason the CDC gives.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Capillary sample, Why the Test is Performed and Risks
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 k71 capillary considerations · PBT I.B.1 types of blood, II.I · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii advantages and disadvantages · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: Which laboratory values may a capillary sample falsely elevate?
opciones: Sugar, electrolytes and blood counts
Bilirubin, cholesterol and clotting times
Blood gases, lactate and ammonia
Hormones, drug levels and iron studies
preguntas.explicacion: The drawbacks listed for a capillary sample are results that can read wrong, with sugar, electrolytes and cell counts coming out too high, the small amount of blood available, and cells damaged in the collection that force a repeat from a vein. Its advantages are that it is easy to get, especially in infants, that sites can be rotated, and that it works at home.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Equipment; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 3.1
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge sizes · CPT D3 k55 k56 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A cannula hub is marked 24G and another 18G. What does the difference in number mean?
opciones: The 24G is the narrower of the two, since higher numbers are finer
The 24G is the wider of the two, since higher numbers are coarser
The numbers give the length in millimeters, not the internal bore
The numbers give the flow rate in milliliters per minute of fluid
preguntas.explicacion: Gauge describes the internal diameter, and a higher gauge number means a narrower device; the sizes commonly stocked run from fourteen through to twenty-four, with the hub color-coded to the gauge. The same convention explains why sixteen to eighteen gauge is reserved for blood donation.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern, Contamination
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and contamination · CPT D3 k57 3B · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: While setting up, a phlebotomist's ungloved finger brushes the top of a blood culture bottle. Why does this matter?
opciones: The sterility of the culture bottle cap must be preserved, or the results are unreliable
The cap is where the bottle's vacuum is stored; touching it lets the vacuum escape early
Skin oils degrade the SPS anticoagulant inside the culture bottle within minutes
It does not matter, because the bottle is mixed 8 to 10 times after filling
preguntas.explicacion: Among the issues of concern in tube collection is contamination before, during or after the collection, with the specific example that the sterility of the cap of blood culture bottles must be ensured and kept from any potential source of contamination, or the results become incorrect and unreliable. Mixing 8 to 10 times combines blood and medium; it does not undo contamination of the cap.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 no squeezing · PBT II.F II.I · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: Blood flows slowly from a heel puncture and the phlebotomist begins squeezing the heel firmly. What does this do to the specimen?
opciones: It dilutes the specimen with tissue fluid and increases the probability of hemolysis
It concentrates the specimen with red cells and raises the measured hematocrit
It speeds the flow safely, as long as the first drop has already been wiped away
It draws in skin flora, which is why the WHO limits capillary blood to a few tests
preguntas.explicacion: Hard squeezing pushes tissue fluid into the sample and raises the chance of hemolysis; heavy massaging of a finger does the same and slows the flow besides. When blood is slow, the answers are warmth and asking the parent to tighten and release the child's wrist in a rhythm.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Tips for communicating with older patients
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.D Interpersonal Relations · CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · RMA I.D.1.a age-group specific responses · CMA II.F.1.c(7)(a) geriatric
preguntas.pregunta: An 82-year-old woman arrives for a fasting draw. How should the phlebotomist address her?
opciones: By a formal title such as Ms. at first, then ask how she prefers to be addressed
By a friendly word such as dear, which settles an anxious older patient more quickly
By her first name from the start, since informality shortens the social distance
By asking the daughter beside her how her mother prefers to be addressed today
preguntas.explicacion: Older patients are often used to more formal terms of address, so the default is a title and a surname, and the simplest way to get it right is to ask the patient herself. Familiar words like dear read as disrespectful. The wider rule behind it is to speak to an older patient as a fellow adult: an impairment does not reduce an adult's maturity.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D3) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why the tube feels warm right after the draw. Compared with a core temperature of 37 °C, what is the normal temperature of blood?
opciones: About 38 °C (100.4 °F), a little above the core
About 37 °C (98.6 °F), the same as the core
About 37.5 °C, half a degree above the core
About 36.5 °C, half a degree below the core
preguntas.explicacion: The normal temperature of blood is about 38 °C (100.4 °F), slightly higher than the 37 °C (98.6 °F) of an internal body reading, and daily swings of 0.5 °C are normal. The extra heat comes from friction as blood flows against vessel walls, especially as vessels age and lose elasticity. Half a degree above or below 37 °C describes the daily variation, not the difference between blood and core temperature.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(1); OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Label Elements
preguntas.subtema: Label elements · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: Which elements must appear on the label of a shipped container of a hazardous chemical under the Hazard Communication standard?
opciones: Product identifier, signal word, hazard and precautionary statements, pictograms and supplier contact
Product identifier, CAS number, concentration, flash point, PEL and the date of preparation
Signal word, pictograms, the 16-section SDS summary, lot number, expiration date and PPE symbol
Chemical name, NFPA hazard rating, storage temperature, disposal method, supplier name and phone
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(1) of 29 CFR 1910.1200 and OSHA's labeling brief list six elements for a container that leaves the workplace: the product identifier, a signal word, hazard statements, precautionary statements, pictograms, and the supplier's name, address and telephone, be that the manufacturer, the importer or another responsible party. The product identifier has to match section 1 of the SDS. CAS numbers, concentrations, flash points and exposure limits live in the SDS sections on composition, physical properties and exposure controls, not on the label; an HMIS-style PPE symbol may be added only as supplementary information.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Test!: Performing the Test
preguntas.subtema: Timing of strip reading · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.1 / IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.a.(2) · RMA III.C.3.a · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: While dipping three urine specimens at once, a medical assistant reads all the strips four minutes after the last dip, well past the times printed on the bottle. Which error is this most likely to produce?
opciones: False positives from colors that kept developing after the specified reading time
False negatives on every pad, because all reagent pads fade within the first minute
No error, because reagent strip reactions stop on their own once the pad has dried out
Invalid results only on the pH pad, which is the single time-critical reaction on the strip
preguntas.explicacion: Each pad must be read at the interval the manufacturer specifies, using a timer if indicated. Reading after the stated time can produce false positives from over-development of color, false negatives when a reaction fades, or invalid results when the reaction moves beyond the visible area; reading too soon gives invalid or false-negative results because sample and reagent have not finished reacting. Running several tests at once is exactly when timing slips.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: When the order of draw is summarized in four groups (sterile tubes, coagulation tubes, plain or gel tubes, additive tubes), where do the plain and gel tubes fall?
opciones: After the coagulation tubes and before the other additive tubes
Before the coagulation tubes and immediately after the sterile tubes
After all the additive tubes, at the very end of the sequence
Before the blood culture bottles, as the first tubes drawn
preguntas.explicacion: Compressed into four steps, the order runs: blood culture or sterile tubes first, coagulation tubes second, plain tubes and gel tubes third, and tubes with additives last. This matches the WHO table, where red clot activator and serum separator tubes occupy positions 4 and 5, after the light blue tube and ahead of heparin, EDTA, ACD and fluoride.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(g)(1)(ii)(A) and (B), Signs
preguntas.subtema: Signs at the laboratory door · CPT D1 1G k32 · PBT VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which information must the warning sign at the entrance to an HIV research laboratory carry?
opciones: The infectious agent, any special entry requirement, and the director's phone
The date of the last decontamination and the brand of disinfectant that was used
The single legend BIOHAZARD, in a color that contrasts with the background
The list of employees trained to enter and the date of their last training
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(1)(ii)(A) sets out three lines for that sign: the name of the infectious agent, any special requirement for entering the area, and a name with a telephone number for whoever is responsible, usually the laboratory director. Subparagraph (B) puts the sign in fluorescent orange-red, or mostly that color, and the lettering and symbols on it in a color that contrasts. The single-word legend belongs to the warning labels of (g)(1)(i), which go on containers, refrigerators and contaminated equipment.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 3R k22 · PBT II.I III.B · CCMA 3E12 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: Which three problems are named as the major consequences of errors made while a blood sample is being collected?
opciones: Inaccurate labeling, contamination and hemolysis
Hemolysis, clotting and delayed transport to the bench
Contamination, clotting and an expired collection tube
Inaccurate labeling, clotting and an underfilled tube
preguntas.explicacion: A poorly collected sample can give inaccurate and misleading results and cost the patient a repeat test, and the three major issues singled out are inaccurate labeling, contamination and hemolysis. Each of the three is decided at the bedside, before the specimen reaches the analyser.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Phlebotomy and Medical Lab Technology; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Chapter 1, section 1.5
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k3 (applied D3 k71 dermal puncture) · PBT I.B.1
preguntas.pregunta: Only a few drops of blood are needed for a test. Where is a capillary stick performed?
opciones: On a fingertip, on an infant's heel, or on an earlobe
On a surface vein of the arm, such as the median cubital
On the radial artery at the wrist, as for blood gases
On the dorsal venous arch of the hand or of the foot
preguntas.explicacion: The three collections differ by volume and by vessel: venipuncture from a surface vein of the arm when more than a few drops are wanted; a capillary stick, on a fingertip, on an infant's heel or on an earlobe, when only a small quantity is needed; and an arterial stick for blood gases. Finger and heel pricks, and rarely the ear lobe, are the capillary sites used for tests such as glucose monitoring.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 2; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, Home Care
preguntas.subtema: Preventing syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E1 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: During the interview before a draw, a patient mentions having fainted during a previous blood test. What should be done?
opciones: Have the patient lie down for the draw
Draw quickly while the patient stands
Postpone the draw until after a meal
Seat the patient with the head between the knees
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 asks about allergies, phobias and any history of fainting during injections or blood draws, and settles the patient comfortably, lying down where that can be done; patients who faint with blood draws are told to warn the provider and be lying down when the test is done. Head between the knees is a measure for someone who has already fainted and cannot lie flat.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(v); OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Biological Hazards, Wear gloves; CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings
preguntas.subtema: Gloves and hand hygiene · CPT D1 1K k35 k36 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: The CDC warns that putting on gloves does not replace cleaning the hands. Which rule in the OSHA standard says the same thing?
opciones: Hands are washed immediately or as soon as feasible after gloves are removed
Gloves are worn whenever hand contact with blood can reasonably be anticipated
Disposable gloves are replaced as soon as feasible when torn or punctured
Utility gloves may be decontaminated and reused while they remain intact
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA's paragraph (d)(2)(v) has hands washed the moment gloves or other PPE come off, or as soon after as is feasible, which is the regulatory form of the CDC's warning. The Hospitals eTool supplies the reasons: gloves can carry small defects, can tear while in use, and hands can pick up contamination as the gloves come off, so gloving never stands in for washing and gloves change between patients. The other three options are OSHA glove rules too, in (d)(3)(ix)(A) and (C), but they govern when gloves go on or get replaced, not hand hygiene.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Body Fluid Samples)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: A pleural fluid aspirate is split for cell count, chemistry and culture. How is the portion for microbiological culture transported?
opciones: Promptly, at room temperature, to keep the organisms viable
Promptly, on wet ice, to slow down cellular degeneration
Refrigerated at 2 to 8 °C until the culture can be set up
Frozen at −20 °C if the culture cannot be set up the same day
preguntas.explicacion: Serous and joint fluids, pericardial, peritoneal, pleural and synovial, are aspirated with aseptic technique into sterile containers. Color, turbidity, viscosity and any clot are noted, and aliquots go out to cell count and differential, to protein and glucose, to culture and to cytology. The culture aliquot travels promptly at room temperature so the organisms stay alive; like CSF for culture it is never chilled, and ice, refrigeration and freezing are instructions written for other specimens.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Blood Culture Contamination: An Overview for Infection Control and Antibiotic Stewardship Programs (2022), Tracking the Blood Culture Contamination Rate
preguntas.subtema: Blood culture contamination · CPT D4 4A · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139
preguntas.pregunta: Two blood culture sets were drawn five minutes apart. One grows Staphylococcus epidermidis; the other stays negative. How is the positive set generally classified?
opciones: A probable contaminant: a commensal in one of several sets
True bacteremia that calls for empiric vancomycin
A single-set culture that must be recollected in full
A catheter-associated bloodstream infection of the line
preguntas.explicacion: A blood culture generally counts as contaminated when, of several sets drawn, one comes up positive for a commensal organism, and the CDC's worked example uses exactly that case, a coagulase-negative staphylococcus in one of two sets, to compute a contamination rate. It is one reason two sets are required: with a single set there is no way to judge whether a commensal is a contaminant. Nothing in the scenario involves a catheter.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(b)(3)(i)-(iii), Hazard Communication, laboratories
preguntas.subtema: SDS access · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: When must safety data sheets be accessible to laboratory employees under the Hazard Communication standard?
opciones: During each work shift, while employees are in their work areas
Within 10 working days of a request, through the safety officer
During business hours only, in the administrator's office
At the annual training, when the chemical inventory is reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b)(3)(ii) of 29 CFR 1910.1200 has the employer keep the safety data sheets that arrive with shipments of hazardous chemicals and keep them readily accessible on every shift to laboratory employees while they are in the areas where they work; the same wording governs sealed-container operations in (b)(4)(ii). Labels on incoming containers stay intact, and the training of paragraph (h) is given. A sheet obtainable only days later, or only in an office during business hours, fails the test.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1241(c)(1), Standard: Test request
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5E 5G · PBT VI.F (CLIA) · CCMA 3E13
preguntas.pregunta: Why does CLIA require the requisition to name a contact person for the authorized person who ordered the test?
opciones: So that imminently life-threatening results or panic values can be reported to someone
So that the laboratory can bill the correct account for the tests performed
So that the patient can be called back if a second specimen is needed
So that the laboratory can send its written client instructions to the right person
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1241(c)(1) ties the contact person on the requisition to one purpose: making it possible to report imminently life-threatening results and panic or alert values. That requirement pairs with 493.1291(g), which obliges the laboratory to alert the requester immediately in those cases. Billing, recollection calls, and the written client instructions a referral laboratory owes under 493.1242(d), are all real duties, but none of them is why the contact person is solicited.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes; and StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: The patient's medicine list shows a blood thinner. Which team member does the phlebotomy guidance say to consult?
opciones: The pharmacist, about medicines that might cause complications
The pathologist, who supervises the laboratory that will test it
The phlebotomist, who chooses which tube additive will be used
The ward clerk, who records the medicines on the requisition
preguntas.explicacion: Providers have to know the patient's medical history and any pre-existing condition, and where the patient takes blood thinners, or other medicines liable to bring on unwanted complications, the pharmacist is the one consulted. When a case is complex and the veins are hard to find, it is a certified phlebotomist who gets called; the pathologist supervises the laboratory itself.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT III.E · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory reports a critical glucose value three hours after it was measured because the result sat unreviewed. In which phase of the total testing process did this error occur?
opciones: Post-analytical, which includes failure or delay in reporting critical values
Analytical, which includes undetected failure of the quality control system
Pre-analytical, which includes sorting, routing and labeling of specimens
Post-post-analytical, which includes the clinician's delayed reaction to the report
preguntas.explicacion: The post-analytical phase, 13 to 20 % of errors, covers wrong validation of data, failure in reporting or addressing the report, excessive turnaround time, transcription mistakes and failure or delay in reporting critical values, which is exactly a result left unreviewed for three hours. The clinician's own delayed reaction to a report that did arrive would be post-post-analytical.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k127 k138 · NCMA 2C.5 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Insufficient volume was the second most common reason for rejection in the emergency laboratory. Which measure did the laboratory adopt for pediatric, geriatric, oncology and neonatal ICU patients?
opciones: Preferring microtainers and microtubes, together with analyzers that need minimal specimen and dead volume
Drawing a second full set of tubes from every such patient so that one set can serve as a backup
Accepting any fill level from these units and adding a comment on the ratio to the report
Pooling the blood from two partially filled tubes of the same patient before centrifugation
preguntas.explicacion: Because collecting enough blood from newborns, children, oncology and intensive care patients is difficult, and because frequent draws put children at risk of anemia, the laboratory prefers microtainers and microtubes for those groups and uses automated instruments with minimized specimen and dead volume. Short fills still fail the ratio criterion, extra sets increase the blood taken, and pooling tubes is not an option offered.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 9
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k41 k42 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3E12 k124 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: According to WHO step 9, which information does the laboratory typically require on the tube label?
opciones: The names, the date of birth, the file number, and when the blood was taken
Names, room number, date of birth, and the ordering physician's full name
Names, file number, diagnosis code, and the phlebotomist's initials
Names, date of birth, the tests ordered, and the tube's additive
preguntas.explicacion: Step 9 asks the phlebotomist to check label and forms for accuracy, and describes the usual content: the patient's first and last names, the date of birth, the file number, and the date and hour at which the blood was taken. Room numbers are not identifiers, and diagnosis codes, tests and additives belong on the requisition or in the laboratory's own records, not on this label.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 technique · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: During a heel-prick the phlebotomist presses the lancet device hard against the skin to be sure it fires. What is the problem with this?
opciones: Too much compression can produce a deeper puncture than is needed for good flow
Too much compression makes the puncture shallower, so a second stick is usually needed
Pressing hard is required, because a lancet held loosely will not reach 2.4 mm
Pressing hard is acceptable on the heel but not on the finger, where bone is closer
preguntas.explicacion: Leaning hard on the device is avoided: it drives the tip in further than the flow requires. Skin flattens under pressure, so the wound ends up a little deeper than the lancet is long, and that is exactly why the length chosen is a little under the depth wanted.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Nonmaleficence
preguntas.subtema: Nonmaleficence and competence · CPT D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7C · CMA II.E.7 · RMA I.C.4.a · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist declines to attempt an arterial puncture she has not been trained to perform. Which ethical principle does this reflect?
opciones: Nonmaleficence: avoiding a risky procedure outside one's competence
Beneficence: bringing goodness by attempting any procedure the patient needs
Justice: giving each patient the same procedures regardless of skill
Autonomy: the phlebotomist's right to choose which tasks to do
preguntas.explicacion: Nonmaleficence means not bringing harm, and the Hippocratic tradition lists attempting a risky procedure outside the practitioner's competence among the things to avoid, together with violating privacy. Staying within one's training is therefore an ethical duty as well as a scope-of-practice rule. Beneficence would be misread if it meant attempting anything a patient needs regardless of skill; justice concerns fair distribution of resources; and autonomy in medical ethics refers to the patient's self-determination, not the worker's preferences.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2; and section 6.2.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C k42 · PBT II.A · CCMA 3E2 k124 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: The laboratory form arrives with the tests listed but no date of birth printed on it. Which step cannot be completed as it stands?
opciones: Matching the laboratory form to the patient's identity before the draw
Placing the requisition in the outer pocket of the transportation bag
Inverting the additive tubes the number of times the laboratory sets
Cleaning the entry site with 70% alcohol and letting it dry completely
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 has the health worker introduce themselves, ask the patient to state their full name, and then make sure the laboratory form and the identity in front of them agree. A form with no date of birth cannot be matched that way, and the pediatric section says what the form should carry: the hospital or file number, the date of birth and the name. The other three steps come later.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(iv) and (d)(2)(v), Methods of Compliance
preguntas.subtema: Hand hygiene · CPT D1 k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: According to OSHA, when must an employee wash their hands after removing gloves?
opciones: Immediately, or as soon as feasible, after the gloves come off
Only when blood or OPIM reached the skin beneath the gloves
At the end of the work shift, as with contaminated work surfaces
Not at all, if an antiseptic hand cleanser was used instead of soap
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(v) puts the duty on the employer: employees wash their hands right away, or as soon as it is feasible, once gloves or any other protective equipment come off. The rule does not wait for blood to reach the skin; that is a separate trigger in (d)(2)(vi). End of shift is the timing the standard gives for possibly contaminated surfaces, not for hands. And paragraph (d)(2)(iv) allows antiseptic cleansers or towelettes only where handwashing facilities are not feasible, adding that hands must still reach soap and running water as soon as that becomes feasible afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC6688222, Whitehead et al., Interventions to prevent iatrogenic anemia: a Laboratory Medicine Best Practices systematic review, Results and Conclusions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4E k83 pediatric volume, sources of information · PBT II.J equipment
preguntas.pregunta: What effect do closed blood sampling devices that return line-flush blood to the patient have on blood loss?
opciones: About 25% less blood loss in neonatal and adult ICU patients, with moderate evidence
About 50% less blood loss, but only in adult ICU patients, with no neonatal data at all
A clear fall in transfusions, but no measurable change in the volume of blood drawn
A 12% reduction in blood drawn per kilogram, achieved by changing clinicians' ordering habits
preguntas.explicacion: There is moderate, consistent evidence that devices which give back the blood drawn off when a venous or arterial line is flushed cut blood loss by around 25%, in neonatal as in adult ICU patients, though the evidence was not enough to show an effect on hemoglobin decline or on transfusion. The 12% reduction in blood out per kilogram came from a separate neonatal program that changed ordering habits.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7; and Annex E, Disassembly of needle from syringe
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D3 3M k54 k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: The last tube has been filled from the syringe. What does the guidance forbid at that point?
opciones: Recapping the needle and taking it off the syringe by hand
Placing the syringe and needle together into the sharps bin
Inverting the additive tubes before they leave the bedside
Checking the labels against the request form a second time
preguntas.explicacion: The step that covers filling tubes ends with an instruction not to recap and remove the needle. If a used needle really has to come off a syringe it is re-sheathed with a one-hand scoop and taken off with a removal device, never with bare hands, and discarded at once.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Auxiliary Aids and Services
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic's video remote interpreting picture is choppy and grainy. Under the ADA rules, what follows?
opciones: The service falls short of the performance standards set for that method
The service is acceptable, since remote interpreting carries no standards
The patient must accept it, because an on-site interpreter costs far more
The patient must supply a relative to interpret until the link is fixed
preguntas.explicacion: Where video remote interpreting is chosen, a set of performance standards has to be met in full: video and audio in real time and full motion, carried on a dedicated high-speed or wireless connection, with images of quality and no lag, nothing choppy, blurry or grainy; a picture sharp and large enough to show face, arms, hands and fingers; clear audio; and staff trained to set the thing up.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014), Use of preservatives; and StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Interfering Factors (Preservatives)
preguntas.subtema: Boric acid and strips · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.3 preservatives · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.8.c · RMA III.C.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory receives a urine in a boric acid tube and is asked to run both a culture and a reagent strip on it. What is the concern with the strip?
opciones: Boric acid can produce false-negative strip results for protein, leukocytes and ketones, and it alters the pH
Boric acid can produce false-positive strip results for leukocyte esterase, glucose and urobilinogen
Boric acid dissolves pus cells, so the leukocyte pad reads falsely high while the culture stays valid
Boric acid raises the pH above 7, which produces a false-positive protein reaction on the strip
preguntas.explicacion: Boric acid is the usual preservative for culture: it keeps the pH below 7 and prevents pus cells from dissolving, but it interferes with several strip pads and is linked to false-negative protein, leukocyte and ketone readings, which limits combining strip testing and culture in one tube. False-positive leukocyte esterase, glucose and urobilinogen are the effects of formaldehyde, and an alkaline pH is what boric acid prevents.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Complications
preguntas.subtema: Preventing syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · D2 2L k48 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which patients are described as more likely to have a vasovagal faint during a venous procedure?
opciones: Those seated rather than lying, with previous faints or marked anxiety
Those lying rather than seated, with previous faints or marked anxiety
Those seated rather than lying, when more than three tubes are drawn
Those lying rather than seated, when the needle is larger than 21 gauge
preguntas.explicacion: Fainting of this kind is reported more often in people who are sitting up than in those lying down, and in people who have fainted before or who are markedly anxious about blood or needles. Those are exactly the patients who are asked about earlier faints and offered a lying position.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, NICHD, Newborn Screening: How is newborn screening done?; and HRSA, Newborn Screening Process, Blood Spot Screening
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4C k81 filter paper technique · PBT III.A.4 newborn screening
preguntas.pregunta: When collecting blood on a newborn screening card, how is the blood applied and when is the collection finished?
opciones: The absorbent part of the card touches the blood drop, and collection continues until all printed circles hold blood
Blood is dripped from a capillary tube onto the card, and collection stops after two circles are filled
The heel is pressed directly onto the card, and collection stops once the largest circle is saturated
Blood is smeared across the paper with the lancet tip, and collection stops when the paper feels damp
preguntas.explicacion: Staff warm the heel, clean it, make a small puncture, and then bring the absorbent part of the card against the drop, going on until every printed circle on the card holds blood. The drops land on the small circles of filter paper. Only once the spots are dry does the card travel to the laboratory.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix B, Instructions for Recording Temperatures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: The morning reading shows the sample refrigerator drifted above its acceptable range some time overnight. What is the required sequence?
opciones: Stop testing, ask the person who supervises testing, and document what was done
Move the samples to a second refrigerator and carry on with the day's testing
Repeat the reading in an hour and act only if it is still out of range
Discard every reagent in the unit and record the loss in the maintenance log
preguntas.explicacion: If the temperature strays outside the recommended range for any length of time, testing stops and whoever directs or supervises it is contacted for guidance on what comes next, including whether the affected reagents, kits, controls or samples have to be thrown out and when testing may start again. Every corrective action taken is documented.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lactose tolerance tests (003500), Normal Results and What Abnormal Results Mean; StatPearls, "Lactose Intolerance", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Lactose breath test result · CPT D4 4H · PBT V.C.3 breath testing
preguntas.pregunta: What rise in breath hydrogen over the pre-test level is treated as a positive lactose breath test?
opciones: 20 parts per million or more
30 parts per million or more
20 milligrams per deciliter or more
2 parts per million or more
preguntas.explicacion: The breath test is normal when the increase in hydrogen stays under 20 parts per million above the fasting, pre-test level; a rise of 20 ppm or more over that baseline is positive and points to lactose malabsorption. Milligrams per deciliter is the unit of the blood version of the test, where a rise over 30 mg/dL within two hours is the normal finding, so the units are not interchangeable.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Petechiae", section Continuing Education Activity
preguntas.subtema: Complications: petechiae · CPT D3 k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these findings is an underlying cause of petechiae?
opciones: Thrombocytopenia
Hemoconcentration
Hypoglycemia
Venous fibrosis
preguntas.explicacion: Petechiae have four primary causes: too few platelets, platelets that work badly, coagulation disorders and a loss of vascular integrity. Hemoconcentration is the tourniquet artifact in the phlebotomy chapter, hypoglycemia is a mimic of syncope, and venous fibrosis is a local contraindication to puncture; none is listed as a cause of petechial bleeding.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Hemoglobin (003645), Normal Results; What Abnormal Results Mean
preguntas.subtema: Hemoglobin by age · CPT D5 5G · PBT IV.A.2 · CCMA 3D3 k141 · CMA I.C.10.b.(2) · RMA III.C.4.b.i / 4.d
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's point-of-care hemoglobin reads 19 g/dL. A new assistant wants to flag it as dangerously high. How should the result be interpreted?
opciones: It is within the newborn reference range of about 14 to 24 g/dL and is not abnormal for this age
It exceeds the adult male upper limit of 17.2 g/dL and should be reported to the provider as critical
It is above the infant range of 9.5 to 14 g/dL, so the sample was probably too concentrated
It is high for any age and suggests chronic low oxygen, which is the usual cause of a raised hemoglobin
preguntas.explicacion: Reference values depend on age: adult men run about 13.8 to 17.2 g/dL and women 12.1 to 15.1, but newborns normally measure 14 to 24 g/dL, and infants 9.5 to 14. A value of 19 g/dL in a newborn is therefore expected, not critical. Chronic hypoxia is the most common cause of a truly high hemoglobin in other patients, and laboratories' ranges vary slightly, so the age-specific range is what should be checked.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 6.2.1, Patient identification
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2E k41 k49 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3E1 k124 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: On a pediatric ward the child's wristband is found clipped to the cot rail rather than on the child. What does the WHO instruct?
opciones: Do not use it; ask the parent or guardian for the child's full name
Use it, because the cot is assigned to that child on the ward admission list
Use the cot number as the second identifier next to the form
Ask the child directly to state the full name and date of birth
preguntas.explicacion: Chapter 6 says a wrist or foot band counts only if it is attached to the patient; a band on the bed or cot, and the bed number, are not to be used. Where a parent or legal guardian is present, that person is asked for the child's first and last names, and the laboratory form is then matched to the child: the name on it, the date of birth, the hospital or file number.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Heart Valve Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which heart valve has two cusps, and where is it located?
opciones: The mitral valve, between the left atrium and left ventricle
The tricuspid valve, between the right atrium and right ventricle
The aortic semilunar valve, at the base of the ascending aorta
The pulmonary semilunar valve, at the base of the pulmonary trunk
preguntas.explicacion: The mitral valve, also called bicuspid or left atrioventricular, has two cusps that chordae tendineae tie to a pair of papillary muscles, and it guards the doorway from the left atrium into the left ventricle; in the clinic it is called mitral. The tricuspid carries three flaps, and the pulmonary and aortic semilunar valves have three flaps each and no chordae tendineae.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation · CPT D3 3G k63 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E5 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is preparing the skin. For which collection does the thirty-second alcohol swab instruction not apply?
opciones: A blood culture set
A coagulation panel
A fasting glucose
A cross-match sample
preguntas.explicacion: The alcohol swab for thirty seconds with thirty seconds of drying is written for routine draws, and the exception named is a blood culture, which is prepared differently. Alcohol is preferred over povidone iodine for the routine case, because iodine can raise potassium, phosphorus and urate.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(5)(i), Sharps injury log; govinfo, Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, Pub. L. 106-430, sec. 3(5)
preguntas.subtema: Sharps injury log · CPT D1 k12 k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: Which three items must the OSHA sharps injury log record for each incident?
opciones: The type and brand of device, the department or work area, and how the incident happened
The injured employee's name, the source patient's status, and the prophylaxis given
The date of the training, the trainer's qualifications, and the attendees' job titles
The route of exposure, the written opinion, and the vaccination dates of the employee
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(5)(i), added by the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, asks the log for three things at minimum: which device was involved, by type and brand; where it happened, meaning the department or the work area; and an explanation of how the incident came about, all of it written so that the injured employee's confidentiality holds. Names, source status and prophylaxis live in the confidential medical record; training details in the training record; and the route of exposure and the written opinion in the post-exposure evaluation file.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D2 2O k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the median cubital vein the most common choice for a blood draw?
opciones: Its thick walls tolerate the negative pressure of the draw
It is the only vein in the fossa that lacks an accompanying nerve
It is the site of choice when an intravenous line has to be started
It is the most prominent vein without any tourniquet applied
preguntas.explicacion: The median cubital vein is superficial, sits over the bicipital aponeurosis and is the usual choice because its thick walls can withstand the negative pressures used when drawing blood. The dorsum of the hand, not this vein, is described as the preferred site for an IV; and the chapter does not claim the vein is nerve-free or always visible without a tourniquet.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Ready?: Actions for Unexpected QC Results; Figure 1
preguntas.subtema: Control out of range · CPT D1 1F · PBT IV.B.1 / IV.B.3 · CCMA 3D3 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.9.c · RMA III.C.3.d · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: The glucometer's liquid control reads outside the range printed on the bottle. Three patients are waiting. What should the operator do?
opciones: Hold patient results, look for the cause, correct it, repeat the control, then retest the patients
Test the patients now and note on each result that the control was out of range that morning
Repeat the control once; if it is still out, average the two readings and proceed if within range
Switch to a new bottle of control solution and report the patients if the second control passes
preguntas.explicacion: An unexpected control result, internal or external, stops patient reporting until the problem is found and fixed. The checklist: were the instructions followed, are the reagents, kits or controls outdated, were they stored correctly, could caps have been switched and cross-contaminated the vials, and what do the insert's troubleshooting steps say. Only after acceptable repeat QC are patient samples retested and final results reported.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Temperature Log Instructions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.3.e · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: The morning temperature log for the specimen refrigerator reads 10 °C (50 °F). Why does this reading call for action?
opciones: A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 2 and 8 °C (36 to 46 °F), so 10 °C is above range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 15 and 30 °C (59 to 86 °F), so 10 °C is below range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between −25 and −15 °C (−13 to 5 °F), so 10 °C is far above range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 0 and 4 °C (32 to 39 °F), so 10 °C is above range
preguntas.explicacion: Patient samples are normally refrigerated between 2 and 8 °C (36 to 46 °F); the 15 to 30 °C band is room temperature for testing and storage, and −25 to −15 °C is the usual sample freezer. What fixes the acceptable range for any given unit is the manufacturer's instructions for the reagents, kits, controls and samples inside it, and the temperature is read and logged every day even where an alarm or a data logger is fitted.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Application of PPE; StatPearls, "Universal Precautions", Proper Donning
preguntas.subtema: Donning sequence · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: In what order does the CDC-recommended sequence put on personal protective equipment?
opciones: Gown, then mask or respirator, then eye protection, then gloves
Gloves, then gown, then mask or respirator, then eye protection
Mask or respirator, then gloves, then gown, then eye protection
Eye protection, then mask or respirator, then gown, then gloves
preguntas.explicacion: The donning order is gown first, covering neck to knees and wrapping the back; then the mask or respirator, with the nose band fitted and a fit check for respirators; then goggles or a face shield; and gloves last, pulled over the cuffs of the gown. Donning takes place outside the patient room. Gloves go on last so that they are the cleanest item when patient contact begins and so that they cover the gown cuffs.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Materials and methods, Sample identification
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I 5F · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.9.a
preguntas.pregunta: A physician calls asking why no result was issued for a specimen sent that morning. The specimen had been rejected. What does the emergency laboratory do with rejected samples?
opciones: Stores them up to 24 hours at 4 °C and issues an immediate LIS report stating the sample was not processed
Discards them at once as biohazardous waste and telephones the ward within 30 minutes of rejection
Runs the tests anyway and reports the results with a comment noting the reason for rejection
Freezes them at –20 °C for one week in case the physician asks for the analysis to be repeated
preguntas.explicacion: Unsuitable samples are recognized at arrival by visual inspection and serum indices; those rejected are kept for up to 24 hours at 4 °C, and a report goes out immediately through the laboratory information system saying the sample was not processed. That report is how the ordering physician learns that a new specimen is needed; testing a rejected tube or discarding it unrecorded defeats the purpose.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Antigens, Antibodies, and Transfusion Reactions
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.C · RMA I.B.2.a · NCMA 1.2 EKB 3 · CPT Core k3 k5 (applied D4 4D)
preguntas.pregunta: Blood bank reports may call the surface antigens of red cells by another name. Which term is it?
opciones: Agglutinogens
Agglutinins
Isoantibodies
Immunoglobulins
preguntas.explicacion: With red cells the antigens may be called isoantigens or agglutinogens, and the antibodies isoantibodies or agglutinins, though the plainer words antigen and antibody are more common. Immunoglobulin is another name for antibody. The agglutinogen is the marker on the cell; the agglutinin is the Y-shaped antibody that clumps cells carrying it.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Contact Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Contact Precautions PPE · CPT D1 1I k34 k36 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is sent to draw blood from a patient on Contact Precautions for a multidrug-resistant organism. Which PPE does the CDC call for?
opciones: A gown and gloves, put on when entering the room and discarded before leaving
A surgical mask put on at the door, with gloves only for the venipuncture itself
A fit-tested N95 respirator, with gown and gloves added only if the patient has a draining wound
Gloves alone, since Standard Precautions already cover blood contact during the draw
preguntas.explicacion: For Contact Precautions the CDC recommends a gown and gloves for any interaction that may bring contact with the patient, or with the environment around them, put on as the room is entered and taken off before leaving so the pathogen stays inside. A mask on entry is the Droplet rule, and the fit-tested N95 belongs to Airborne. Standard Precautions still run underneath, so the gloves the phlebotomist would wear anyway are not enough on their own; the gown is added because this pathogen travels by contact with the patient and the surroundings.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1241(b), Standard: Test request
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D k112 · NCMA 2C.1 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.9.a
preguntas.pregunta: A physician phones the laboratory to order a test and says the written order will follow. Under CLIA, how long does the laboratory have to obtain the written or electronic authorization?
opciones: 30 days from the oral request
7 days from the oral request
24 hours from the oral request
90 days from the oral request
preguntas.explicacion: Under 42 CFR 493.1241(b) an oral request is acceptable provided the laboratory then solicits authorization in writing or electronically inside 30 days, and keeps either that authorization or a record of its attempts to obtain it. The default is a written or electronic request from an authorized person; the oral route is the exception, and its ceiling is 30 days, not a day, a week or three months.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Tort in Healthcare", Clinical Significance and Issues of Concern (damages)
preguntas.subtema: Burden of proof · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.a · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31
preguntas.pregunta: What is the burden of proof in a civil tort case such as a malpractice claim?
opciones: A preponderance of the evidence: more likely than not
Beyond a reasonable doubt, as in criminal cases
Clear and convincing evidence agreed by a unanimous jury
Proof to a certainty, the standard applied to damages
preguntas.explicacion: A tort case is decided on a preponderance of the evidence, meaning more likely than not, better than 50 percent. The criminal yardstick of beyond a reasonable doubt has no place here, and in a number of states the jury need not even be unanimous to hold a tortfeasor responsible. One is liable for a tort rather than guilty of it. Damages are a separate question: they have to be proved to a certainty instead of estimated, and statutes may cap them, but that goes to the amount awarded, not to the burden for establishing liability.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fasting", section Cellular Level
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: How far into a fast are the liver's glycogen stores described as running out?
opciones: After about 24 hours
After about 8 hours
After about 12 hours
After about 72 hours
preguntas.explicacion: During a fast, blood glucose is first held up by glycogen in the liver and skeletal muscle, and the liver carries the greatest part of that work through the first 24 hours. After roughly 24 hours the stores are depleted and the body turns to fat and protein. Eight and twelve hours are fasting windows asked of patients, not the glycogen limit.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Electrical Safety, Recognized Controls and Work Practices
preguntas.subtema: GFCI protection · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G · CMA I.B.8.a / 2027 I.B.7.a · RMA II.B.7.d III.C.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which protective device belongs on all 120-volt, single-phase, 15- and 20-ampere receptacles in a hospital, according to OSHA's recognized controls?
opciones: A ground-fault circuit interrupter, which shuts off power on a ground fault
A surge protector, which absorbs voltage spikes from the power line
A three-prong adapter, which grounds equipment lacking a ground prong
A step-down transformer, which lowers the voltage below 1,000 volts
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA's Hospitals eTool recommends ground-fault circuit interrupters on all 120-volt, single-phase, 15- and 20-ampere receptacles. A GFCI is a fast-acting circuit breaker that cuts power the moment a ground fault occurs, so that current from a damaged cord or an energized metal enclosure does not flow through a worker's body and cause burns or electrocution. The standard also requires electrical service near water sources to be properly grounded under 29 CFR 1910.304(g)(6); adapters that bypass a missing ground prong are the kind of damaged connection the eTool warns against.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 3.4 Specimen contamination
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k88 · PBT III.C · CCMA 3D9 k117 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.b
preguntas.pregunta: A molecular laboratory sees sporadic false-positive results in negative specimens. Which workflow controls does the review recommend against sample and amplicon contamination?
opciones: One-way workflow through separate pre- and post-amplification areas, frequent glove changes, aerosol-barrier tips
A single shared bench for extraction and amplification, so that every step is handled by the same pair of gloves
Reusing pipette tips within one patient's series of tubes, so that no foreign template can enter the reaction
Leaving opened sample tubes uncapped in the post-amplification area to let aerosols settle before analysis
preguntas.explicacion: Because amplification makes millions of copies from a few templates, a positive sample or its amplicons can contaminate a negative one at collection, processing or analysis. Guidelines therefore ask for separate pre- and post-amplification areas, ideally physically apart, a one-way workflow from pre to post, separate clean protective equipment for each area with frequent glove changes, dedicated equipment, aerosol-barrier tips and pipetting technique that limits aerosols, plus routine cleaning with 10 to 15 % bleach and wipe-tests of the environment.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Where is the HIPAA Privacy Rule Applicable; 45 CFR 164.520(b)(1)(ii)(C)
preguntas.subtema: Stricter state law · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.2.a(2) · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: State law is stricter than HIPAA about disclosing HIV test results. Which rule governs the disclosure?
opciones: The more stringent rule, in this case the state law
HIPAA, since federal law always preempts state law
Whichever rule the facility's privacy official prefers
Neither; HIV results are excluded from PHI altogether
