opciones: An instrument with a short two-edged blade that draws drops of blood
A hollow needle with a bevel that draws blood into an attached tube
A tubing system with a needle used to deliver drugs into the body
A needle that connects to tubing for transferring fluids in and out
preguntas.explicacion: A lancet, also called a fingerstick device, is an instrument with a short two-edged blade used to obtain drops of blood for testing, and it is commonly used in diabetes care. Infusion sets and connection needles are separate categories of sharp, used to deliver or transfer fluids.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3, "3) ISO 15189: 2007", item 5.4.6
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: An accredited laboratory is asked to show how it monitors the journey its specimens make from the collecting clinics. Which four aspects does the quality standard name?
opciones: Temperature, time frame, safety and the preservatives used
Time frame, distance, courier training and safety
Temperature, humidity, light exposure and safety
Temperature, container type, preservatives and cost
preguntas.explicacion: The medical laboratory quality standard wants the transport of samples into the laboratory monitored on four counts: how long it takes, at what temperature, with which preservatives, and how safely. It is less prescriptive than the accreditation checklists on most extra-analytical matters, but on transport it names those four outright.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", How do you ensure password protection; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Passwords and Unique User Identification
preguntas.subtema: Password safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38
preguntas.pregunta: Which password practice is consistent with HIPAA security guidance?
opciones: Unique passwords for each user, never shared, written down or emailed
A single department password changed each year at annual training
Passwords posted near the workstation so that coverage staff can log in quickly
Passwords of consecutive digits, which are easier to audit
preguntas.explicacion: Every worker who accesses patient records needs a unique, strong password that mixes letters, numbers and symbols, is changed periodically, is never shared, verbalized, written down near the computer or emailed, and is not built from consecutive digits or easily guessed information; the IT department checks password quality before granting access. Uniqueness matters because HITECH requires systems to track each user's activity. Passwords alone are considered weak protection, which is why some institutions add biometric authentication.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, NICHD, Newborn Screening: How is newborn screening done?; and HRSA, Newborn Screening Process, Blood Spot Screening
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4C k81 filter paper technique · PBT III.A.4 newborn screening, III.B labeling
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn screening card is being prepared. What is filled out before the heel is punctured?
opciones: The baby's name, sex and weight, the date and time of birth, and the collection time
Only the mother's name and hospital number; the rest is added by the state laboratory
The infant's blood type and Apgar score, which the laboratory needs to read results
The date and time of collection only; the identity details go on once the spots dry
preguntas.explicacion: Before anyone touches the heel, hospital staff fill in the card with the baby's particulars, name, sex, weight, when it was born and when the blood is being taken. One part of the card is the absorbent paper that receives the sample; the other part is what tells the laboratory whose blood this is and how to reach the family and the provider.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.530(d), (f), (g) and (h), Administrative requirements
preguntas.subtema: No retaliation · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: A patient files a privacy complaint against a clinic. What does HIPAA say about how the clinic may respond?
opciones: It may not intimidate or retaliate against the patient for filing the complaint
It may decline further treatment, since the relationship of trust has been broken
It may require the patient to waive the complaint as a condition of care
It may share the complaint with other providers so they are warned
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.530(g) forbids a covered entity from intimidating, threatening, coercing, discriminating against or retaliating against any individual for exercising a right under the rule or taking part in any of its processes, including filing a complaint, and 164.530(h) forbids requiring individuals to waive their rights as a condition of treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits. The entity must have its own complaint process, document complaints and their disposition, and mitigate any harm from a violation. Sharing the complaint with other providers would itself be an unpermitted disclosure.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k89 · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3E k136 k139 · NCMA 2C.6 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d)
preguntas.pregunta: A phenytoin level is ordered and the phlebotomist draws it into a serum separator tube with gel. Why will the laboratory not accept that tube for therapeutic drug monitoring?
opciones: The barrier gel can absorb drugs such as carbamazepine, lidocaine, phenobarbital and phenytoin
The clot activator in the gel tube breaks down phenytoin before the serum can be separated
The gel prevents the sample from being carried on ice and in the dark as drug levels require
The gel tube cannot be centrifuged, and drug assays are run only on centrifuged specimens
preguntas.explicacion: For therapeutic drug monitoring the laboratory turns away tubes with serum separator gel, because the barrier can soak up some drugs, carbamazepine, lidocaine, phenobarbital and phenytoin among them; they were recovered from the gel after extraction with methanol, and plain tubes without gel are suggested instead. Ice and darkness are the methotrexate rule, not a property of the tube.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Compensating for hearing deficits
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 k16 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2)(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(3)(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: A hard-of-hearing patient cannot make out her date of birth when it is read back to her for identification. What does the guidance suggest?
opciones: Give the sounds context: name a word for each confusable letter, and say the digits one by one
Give the sounds volume: repeat the whole date louder and at a higher pitch until she agrees
Give the sounds time: repeat the whole date slowly, one syllable at a time, until she agrees
Give up on speech: hand her the requisition and have her point to her own date of birth on it
preguntas.explicacion: Some letters and numbers sound so alike that no amount of repeating separates them for a patient who is hard of hearing. The advice is to build context around them instead: pin a letter to a word that starts with it, and split a two-digit number into its digits rather than saying the number whole. Care is asked for especially with the letters that sound alike. Volume is the wrong lever — shouting distorts the sounds of speech and a raised pitch is harder to hear, not easier.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern: Time Pressures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Consent for a therapeutic phlebotomy is signed in the holding area, minutes before the procedure and after the sedative has already been given. Why is that way of obtaining it criticized?
opciones: The talk belongs where there is time to ask and to reflect, not minutes ahead with a medicated patient
The signature needs a staff witness, and the holding area rarely has a second employee free to sign it
The risks have to be read aloud once more in the holding area, and a sedated patient cannot repeat them
The consent lapses the moment a sedative is charted, so a fresh form has to be signed once it wears off
preguntas.explicacion: Time pressure is one of the recognized threats to consent: when the clock rules, the discussion gets trimmed and the person signs feeling uninformed but obliged to go ahead. Three habits are named as bad practice — raising the procedure only just before it happens, taking the signature in the pre-operative holding area, and asking someone who has been medicated or is close to falling asleep. What is asked for instead is an office or clinic setting, a conversation that runs both ways, and enough room for the patient to put questions and weigh the answers. No witness rule and no restart clock is at stake here.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern, Problems with the collection tube
preguntas.subtema: Adjustments for blood flow · CPT D3 k67 k58 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.11
preguntas.pregunta: During a draw, an evacuated tube that was briefly uncapped earlier is pushed onto the needle and no blood enters it. What is the likely cause?
opciones: The vacuum inside the tube was lost when it was uncapped
The anticoagulant was missing from the tube during packaging
The needle bevel is lying against the wall of the vein
The tube was drawn out of sequence and its additive was spent
preguntas.explicacion: Among the issues of concern, the review notes that tubes can be damaged and that the vacuum can be lost when a tube is uncapped; without vacuum the tube cannot pull blood. A missing anticoagulant is listed as a separate packaging defect that turns plasma into serum, not a cause of no flow, and tube order affects additive carry-over rather than filling.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 9: Address Language Differences, Provide written materials and videos in patients' languages
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: How are an interpreter and a translator distinguished in the health-literacy guidance?
opciones: Interpreters listen or watch then speak or sign; translators work in writing
Interpreters work in writing; translators listen and then speak or sign
Interpreters must be certified by the state; translators need no training
Interpreters handle spoken tongues; translators handle sign language only
preguntas.explicacion: They are described as two different professions with different skills. An interpreter listens or watches in one language and then speaks or signs in another; a translator reads text in one language and writes what it meant in another. Where materials are not available in the patient's language, an interpreter trained in sight translation reads the document aloud.

preguntas.fuente: SAMHSA, Urine Specimen Collection Handbook for Federal Agency Workplace Drug Testing Programs (2024), Chapter and 24a
preguntas.subtema: Chain of custody form · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 · CCMA 3E k127 chain of custody · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: A donor refuses to put their initials on the tamper-evident seals of the two bottles. What is the consequence?
opciones: It is noted on the remarks line and the collection is completed as usual
It is recorded as a refusal to test and the urine is discarded at once
The collector initials the seals instead and the specimen goes out normally
A second collection is done under direct observation with new bottles
preguntas.explicacion: The donor is asked to initial each label or seal, but failing or refusing to do so is noted on the remarks line of the chain of custody form and the collection is completed; it is not a refusal to test. Refusing to sign the certification statement, or to give the donor information, is handled the same way. What does count as a refusal is walking out before the process ends, or refusing a second attempt.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E7 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A hemolyzed specimen arrives for an erythrocyte sedimentation rate. Why is that a particular problem for this test?
opciones: Free hemoglobin reddens the plasma and hides the boundary that is read
Free hemoglobin clots the specimen and stops the red cells from settling
Free hemoglobin binds the citrate and leaves the specimen unanticoagulated
Free hemoglobin raises the viscosity so the red cells settle far too quickly
preguntas.explicacion: The reading is taken where the settled red cells end and clear plasma begins. Hemolysis releases hemoglobin into the plasma and turns it red, so that boundary can no longer be picked out; an icteric sample causes the same trouble with dark yellow plasma.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.2; and Section 3.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which two practices are forbidden once a sharps container is in service?
opciones: Overfilling it, and emptying its contents out to use it again
Sealing it with a lid, and moving it closer to the drawing chair
Labeling it, and keeping it within arm's reach of the worker
Overfilling it, and sealing it before it has been fully filled
preguntas.explicacion: The container is sealed with a tamper-proof lid, and the two things not to do are overfilling it and decanting it. Keeping it within arm's reach and clearly visible is the correct practice, since the used device is meant to go in immediately rather than travel across the room.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(iii)(A)(2) and (A)(3), Contaminated Sharps Discarding and Containment
preguntas.subtema: Moving a full sharps container · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist finds the sharps container at her station filled to the marked line. What does the standard require before it is carried away?
opciones: Close it immediately before removal, and use a second closable container if leakage is possible
Press the contents down so the lid will close, then carry it to the soiled utility room
Open the lid and tip the sharps into a red bag that is closed before it is removed
Leave it in place until the end of the shift, the deadline set for contaminated surfaces
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(iii)(A)(3) covers the moment a sharps container leaves the area where it was used: the lid goes on first, so nothing can spill or poke out while it is handled, and if the container could leak it travels inside a second one that closes, holds everything and carries the label or the color code. Paragraph (A)(2) already required the container to be replaced routinely and never allowed to overfill, so pressing the contents down is the opposite of the rule, and (A)(4) forbids opening or emptying a reusable container by hand. The end-of-shift deadline belongs to work surfaces in (d)(4)(ii)(A).

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: Preventing syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · D2 2L k48 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: What is gained by teaching a patient to recognize the warning signs of a faint?
opciones: The faint is often prevented and the risk of a traumatic fall drops
The faint is shortened, although the risk of a traumatic fall is unchanged
The blood pressure stays high enough for the draw to be completed
The pulse rate rises enough that the tourniquet may be left in place
preguntas.explicacion: Knowing the symptoms often prevents the episode outright and reduces the risk of a traumatic fall, because the patient lies down before consciousness goes. That is the practical reason for asking, before a draw, whether the person has ever fainted during an injection or a blood test.

preguntas.subtema: Calibration verification every 6 months · CPT D1 1F / k27 · PBT VI.A.2 · CCMA 3D k115 · CMA I.C.9.b · RMA III.C.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: How often must a nonwaived laboratory perform calibration verification, and what materials does it use?
opciones: At least every 6 months, with a low or zero, a mid-point and a high value near the top of the range
At least every 12 months, with two control materials at different concentrations run in duplicate
Only when a control fails, with a calibrator from the same lot that was used to calibrate the system
Each day of testing, with a single calibrator traceable to a certified reference material
preguntas.explicacion: Calibration verification confirms the system still reads accurately across its reportable range. It runs at least once every 6 months, and again after a complete change of reagents, after major maintenance or after a critical part is replaced, when controls drift oddly or fall outside limits that other corrective steps will not fix, and whenever the laboratory's own schedule says so. Materials cover a minimal, a mid-point and a maximum value.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(g)(1)(i)(B), (C) and (E), Labels
preguntas.subtema: Biohazard label · CPT D1 1G k32 · PBT VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: What color and legend does OSHA require on a biohazard warning label?
opciones: Fluorescent orange or orange-red, with the biohazard symbol and legend in a contrasting color
Bright yellow with a black skull and crossbones, the GHS pictogram for acute toxicity
Red with white lettering, matching the red bags that may replace the label
Fluorescent orange-red with a black frame set on a point, as on chemical labels
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraphs (g)(1)(i)(B) and (C) fix both the color and the wording. The background is fluorescent orange, or orange-red, or a color that is predominantly one of the two; against it the BIOHAZARD legend and symbol are printed in a contrasting color; and the label is affixed so that it cannot be lost or removed by accident. Red bags or containers may stand in for the label under (g)(1)(i)(E), but the label itself is nowhere described as red with white text. A skull and crossbones, and a red square standing on one point, belong to Hazard Communication chemical labels rather than to this standard.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Grading the exposure · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: In the three-step assessment of an occupational HIV exposure, what does the first step establish?
opciones: Whether an infectious fluid was involved, and by which route and how severe
Whether the source patient is on treatment and what the viral load is
Whether prophylaxis is indicated or observation alone is enough
Whether the worker completed the hepatitis B vaccine series
preguntas.explicacion: The three steps run in a fixed order, and the first describes the exposure itself: blood, another body fluid able to carry infection, or a device with blood on it, together with the route and the severity. Intact skin carries no meaningful risk. On a mucous membrane the volume and the contact time count. For a percutaneous injury what matters is whether the needle was solid or hollow-bore and whether it had been sitting in a vein or artery. Step two is the source patient's status, and step three is the decision on prophylaxis.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Common Pitfalls), Unsolicited advice
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 k40 · CCMA 6 k199 k202 · CMA F.1.g / 2027 F.1.d · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: A patient mentions she is thinking of stopping a medicine, and the phlebotomist tells her what to do. Which pitfall is that?
opciones: Unsolicited advice, which can feel intrusive and unempathetic
Providing false reassurance, which can rupture the relationship
Changing the subject abruptly, which can come across as dismissive
Responding defensively, which closes off the patient's own view
preguntas.explicacion: Advice the patient never asked for lands as intrusive and lacking in empathy, unless they have expressly asked to be advised. False reassurance risks a severe rupture in the relationship, above all when the desired outcome is not achieved; an abrupt change of subject can be perceived as dismissive; and a defensive answer leaves the patient no room to express frustration.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 482.13(c) and (d), Standards: Privacy and safety; Confidentiality of patient records
preguntas.subtema: Access to hospital records · CPT D1 k13 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: Under 42 CFR 482.13(d), how may a hospital patient request access to their own medical records?
opciones: By oral or written request, in the format requested if readily producible
Only by written request notarized and signed by the attending physician
Only through an attorney, since records are hospital property
Only after discharge, once the record has been completed and coded
preguntas.explicacion: The confidentiality standard gives the patient access to their medical records, the current ones included. The request may be spoken or written; the record arrives in whichever form and format was asked for when that is readily producible, electronic included, and otherwise as readable hard copy or in some agreed format, within a reasonable time. The hospital may not frustrate legitimate efforts to obtain records, and it has to answer as fast as its record system allows. The same standard protects the confidentiality of clinical records and, separately, the right to personal privacy and to care in a safe setting.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cultural Competence in the Care of LGBTQ Patients", section Definitions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k18 · CCMA 6 k194 · CMA F.2.b / 2027 F.1.c · RMA I.D.1.e
preguntas.pregunta: What does 'gender identity' mean?
opciones: One's own sense of gender, matching or differing from the sex assigned at birth
The appearance, dress, mannerisms and speech associated with femininity or masculinity
The sex recorded for an infant on the basis of the external genitalia
The gender that an observer assigns to a person on first meeting them
preguntas.explicacion: The glossary defines gender identity as the sense a person has of their own gender, which may line up with the sex assigned at birth or may differ from it. The neighbouring entries are the distractors: gender expression covers appearance, dress and mannerisms; sex assigned at birth rests on an infant's external genitalia; and gender attribution is the gender an observer takes someone to be.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.E · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: In published studies of laboratory errors, which phase of the total testing process consistently accounts for more than half of all errors?
opciones: The pre-analytical phase
The analytical phase
The post-analytical phase
The post-post-analytical phase
preguntas.explicacion: Taken together the two extra-analytical phases carry four to five times the errors of the analytical phase, and the pre-analytical phase on its own accounts for over half of all errors in the published series; an Italian stat laboratory found the same split in 1996 and again in 2006, 62 % of errors before the analysis, 15 % inside it and 23 % after it. The analytical phase itself runs close to 5 sigma.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Auxiliary Aids and Services
preguntas.pregunta: A blind patient needs to review the consent information. Which ADA auxiliary aid fits?
opciones: A qualified reader, large print, or Braille
A qualified sign language interpreter or captioning
A qualified speech-to-speech transliterator
A companion who reads and signs the form for him
preguntas.explicacion: For people who are blind or have vision loss, the ADA's auxiliary aids include a qualified reader, large print, Braille, an accessible electronic file for a screen reader, or an audio recording. Interpreters and real-time captioning are aids for people who are deaf, and speech-to-speech transliteration serves speech disabilities. Braille works only for those who read it, so the person's own method matters.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Tips for communicating with older patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2D k15 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: How should a phlebotomist decide how to address an older patient?
opciones: Default to formal terms such as Mr. or Ms., and ask how they prefer to be addressed
Use first names, which feel warmer to most older adults than formal titles
Use affectionate terms such as 'dear' to put the patient at ease quickly
Use the name the companion uses for the patient during the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Speak to the patient as a fellow adult and establish respect by using formal language as the default, such as Mr. or Ms., and avoid familiar terms like 'dear', which can be perceived as disrespectful; staff can also check with patients about the form of address they prefer. Older people may be used to more formal terms of address.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.2
preguntas.subtema: Scope of practice · CPT D3 k62 · D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.F.2 · CCMA 3E4 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which collections fall outside the scope of the best-practice guidance on drawing blood?
opciones: Indwelling central lines, arterial lines, cord blood and stem cells
Pediatric venous draws, capillary sampling and donor collection
Arterial blood gases, capillary sampling and adult venous draws
Blood for transfusion, cord blood and adult capillary sampling
preguntas.explicacion: The document covers venous and arterial sampling and collection for transfusion in adults and children, but it says it does not deal with collection from indwelling central lines, from arterial lines or of cord blood, and it does not cover stem cell collection.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC5580822, Hall et al., Influence of Hematocrit and Total-Spot Volume on Performance Characteristics of Dried Blood Spots for Newborn Screening, Conclusions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4C k81 filter paper technique · PBT III.A.2 III.A.4 specimen quality, newborn screening
preguntas.pregunta: A dried blood spot is visibly smaller than its printed circle. What does this tell the laboratory?
opciones: That total spot volume is well below the 75 to 100 µL target, so punches may hold too little
That the newborn's hematocrit was high, because hematocrit is the main driver of the spot's diameter
That the spot dried too fast, which shrinks the paper fibers and the visible stain
That the collector used the second drop, which spreads less than the first
preguntas.explicacion: What drives the diameter of the spot is the total volume laid down, not the hematocrit, so a spot smaller than the printed circle signals a volume well short of the 75 to 100 µL target and punches whose volume may fall outside the acceptable range. Hematocrit shows in the edges instead: lower-hematocrit spots have smoother borders, higher ones more irregular.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003), Treatment for the Exposure: HCV; CDC, Guidelines for Health Care Personnel Exposed to Hepatitis C Virus, HCV postexposure prophylaxis
preguntas.subtema: Hepatitis C after exposure · CPT D1 k31 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is stuck with a needle used on a patient known to have hepatitis C. What does the CDC say about prophylaxis?
opciones: No vaccine and no recommended PEP exist; follow-up testing finds infection early so it can be treated
Immune globulin is given within 24 hours, followed by baseline and 6-month antibody tests
A 28-day antiviral course is started within 72 hours, as for HIV
A single dose of vaccine plus HBIG is given if the worker's antibody level is under 10 mIU/mL
preguntas.explicacion: Hepatitis C has no vaccine and no post-exposure treatment that prevents infection: no immune globulin and no antiviral therapy are recommended once the exposure has happened. The 2020 guidance declines to recommend routine PEP with direct-acting antivirals, noting a percutaneous transmission risk near 0.2 percent, and sets a testing schedule instead so that infection is caught and treated early. Immune globulin, and HBIG with vaccine, are hepatitis B measures; the 28-day course begun within 72 hours is HIV PEP.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Hemoglobin A1C (HbA1C) Test, Is there anything else I need to know about an A1C test?
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · CPT D3 k57 D2 k47 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a blood disorder is told her A1C may not be the right test for diagnosing diabetes. Which conditions are named alongside hers as making the figure unreliable?
opciones: Anemia and other blood disorders, kidney failure and liver disease
Anemia and other blood disorders, high cholesterol and heart disease
Prediabetes, polycystic ovarian syndrome and a family history of diabetes
Being overweight, a stroke in the past and gestational diabetes
preguntas.explicacion: Where a condition affects the red cells, as anemia and other blood disorders do, the coated fraction stops mirroring the average glucose; kidney failure and liver disease can shift the figure as well, and another test is used instead. The test is also not used to diagnose gestational diabetes. Weight, a stroke and a family history are reasons to be tested, not reasons to distrust the number.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC11422196, Bowman et al., Reducing Iatrogenic Blood Losses in Premature Infants, Introduction; and PMC, PMC6688222, Whitehead et al., LMBP systematic review, Results
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4E k83 pediatric volume, D3 3D minimum volume tubes · PBT II.J equipment, II.I considerations
preguntas.pregunta: Which practices are current ways to reduce iatrogenic blood loss in neonates?
opciones: Placental blood for admission tests, microtiter tubes, and laboratory analyzers that need less sample
Larger single draws once a day, standard tubes filled to the line, and weekly transfusion
Arterial sampling only, heparinized syringes, and discarding the first 2 mL of each line draw
Capillary sampling for every test, adhesive strips, and iron supplementation from day one
preguntas.explicacion: What is done today to spare a newborn's blood: placental blood for the admission panel, microtitre tubes for the samples, and analysers that need less to work with, though what clinicians order remains the biggest driver. Add closed devices that give the line-flush blood back, worth about a quarter of the loss in neonatal and adult ICUs, and small tubes, which seem to lower the risk of anemia.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1242(b), Standard: Specimen submission, handling, and referral
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D5 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.9.a
preguntas.pregunta: A courier delivers a batch of specimens from a clinic. Which piece of information does CLIA require the receiving laboratory to document at that moment?
opciones: The date and time the specimen was received
The name of the courier and the vehicle used
The temperature inside the transport container
The number of tubes drawn from each patient
preguntas.explicacion: Under 42 CFR 493.1242(b) the laboratory must record the date and time at which it receives each specimen; the same data point reappears in 493.1283 as a required element of the test record system. Transport temperature and packaging belong to the laboratory's own written procedures for transport conditions, and courier or tube counts are not federal requirements.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding into the skin, Considerations; and StatPearls, "StatPearls (NBK482331) — Petechiae" (NBK482331)
preguntas.subtema: Terminology: petechiae, purpura, ecchymosis · CPT D3 k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: How is bleeding into the skin distinguished from simple redness (erythema)?
opciones: Bleeding into the skin does not blanch when pressed; erythema does
Bleeding into the skin blanches when pressed; erythema does not
Bleeding into the skin is always larger than 2 mm; erythema is smaller
Bleeding into the skin is warm to the touch; erythema is cool
preguntas.explicacion: Redness of the skin should not be taken for bleeding: an area of bleeding into the skin does not go paler under pressure, whereas the redness of erythema does. The same test defines a non-blanching spot: one that does not disappear after brief pressure. Size separates petechiae (under 2 mm) from purpura (over 2 mm), not bleeding from erythema.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Application of PPE; Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Putting on the mask · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: What must be done as a mask or respirator is put on, before the eye protection?
opciones: Shape the band to the bridge of the nose and check the fit
Loop the straps under the chin so it can be pulled down later
Tuck the lower edge under the collar of the gown that is on
Wet the inner layer so it seals against the skin of the face
preguntas.explicacion: In the donning sequence the mask or respirator comes second, after the gown. Its ties or straps are placed around the head and neck, the flexible band is adjusted to the bridge of the nose so that it fits, and a respirator gets a fit check. Anyone required to use a respirator such as an N95 must also have been fit tested beforehand, and where fit testing cannot be done a powered air purifying respirator may be considered.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Health Topic: Patient Rights, What is informed consent?; 42 CFR 482.13(b)(2)
preguntas.subtema: Withdrawing consent · CPT D1 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA II.E.3.a · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who signed a consent form for a procedure says she has changed her mind. What does patient-rights guidance say?
opciones: She may change her mind about consent at any time
She is bound by the signed form until the procedure is done
She may withdraw only if a second physician agrees
She may withdraw only in writing, with 24 hours' notice
preguntas.explicacion: Informed consent is a process in which the provider gives the information needed to decide, including the risks and benefits of the care and details of the condition, and the patient must understand it before consenting; a signature on a form is written consent, but the patient has the right to change her mind at any time. The CMS condition frames the same idea as the right to make informed decisions and to request or refuse treatment. No second opinion, notice period or written withdrawal is required to revoke consent.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Equipment quality checks · CPT D3 3B k57 k58 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A tube left the factory without the anticoagulant it should contain. What happens when it is used?
opciones: The blood clots and yields serum where plasma was required
The tube keeps its vacuum but draws only half its volume
The plasma settles above a gel barrier as in a PST tube
The red cells haemolyse because no additive protects them
preguntas.explicacion: Among the problems listed for collection tubes is an anticoagulant missing at packaging, which means serum is used for testing where plasma was meant to be. That is a different fault from a damaged tube whose vacuum was lost when it was uncapped, and no gel appears in a tube that never held one.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, What is it used for?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D II.G · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: Which set names medicines listed as commonly monitored by blood level?
opciones: Vancomycin, digoxin, phenytoin and lithium
Vancomycin, ibuprofen, phenytoin and insulin
Amoxicillin, digoxin, warfarin and lithium
Amoxicillin, ibuprofen, warfarin and insulin
preguntas.explicacion: The table of commonly monitored medicines groups antibiotics such as amikacin, gentamycin and vancomycin; heart medicines such as amiodarone, digoxin, lidocaine and procainamide; anti-seizure medicines such as phenobarbital and phenytoin; cyclosporine and tacrolimus for autoimmune disease; and lithium and valproic acid for mental health conditions.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge for coagulation · CPT D3 k56 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Coagulation factor testing is ordered. Which needle gauge range is suggested for coagulation specimens, and which end of the range is preferred for factor assays?
opciones: 19 to 22 G, with 19 G preferred to limit hemolysis
19 to 22 G, with 22 G preferred to limit hemolysis
16 to 18 G, with 16 G preferred for a faster fill
23 to 25 G, with 23 G preferred to protect the vein
preguntas.explicacion: For most coagulation tests the suggested needle range is 19 G to 22 G, and a wider needle, 19 G for instance, may be preferred for coagulation factor and platelet function testing to minimize hemolysis and keep the sample intact. Preferring 22 G gets the reasoning backward, 16 to 18 G is the blood donation range, and 25 G is not given in any of the sources.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 1.1.1 and 2.2.3, Step 3
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.11
preguntas.pregunta: Why is drawing a specimen through an intravenous or central line a hemolysis risk as well as a contamination one?
opciones: It sits on the published list of factors that increase hemolysis
It sits on the published list of factors that increase clot formation
It sits on the published list of factors that increase nerve damage
It sits on the published list of factors that reduce tube vacuum
preguntas.explicacion: Taking a specimen through an intravenous or a central line is itself one of the listed factors that raise hemolysis, quite apart from the contamination and the dilution by fluid and medication that make an existing peripheral access a poor source of specimens.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Compensating for visual deficits
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k40 patient communication, k49 age considerations · PBT II.B age-specific needs
preguntas.pregunta: What is recommended about lighting and print when giving written collection instructions to a patient with poor vision?
opciones: Adequate light, including on your own face, minimal glare, and type of at least 14 points
Dim, indirect light to reduce glare, and printed type of at least 10 points in a serif face
Bright overhead light behind you, and handwritten notes in block capitals on white paper
Normal room light, and instructions given only aloud to avoid any reading strain
preguntas.explicacion: For visual deficits, light the room well, with enough light on your own face and as little glare as possible, check that glasses or lenses are on, write instructions clearly by hand, and print in type big enough, 14-point at least, in an easy typeface. Where vision is low, offer diagrams, large pictures or spoken instructions instead.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Airborne Precautions; StatPearls, "Universal Precautions", Droplet precautions
preguntas.subtema: Airborne Precautions without an AIIR · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C2 k98 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.3
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic has no airborne infection isolation room and a patient with suspected measles arrives. What does the CDC advise?
opciones: Mask the patient and place them in a private room with the door closed until transfer or discharge
Place the patient in the waiting area at least 3 feet from others, as for Droplet Precautions
Seat the patient in an exam room with the door open so air can circulate freely
Turn the patient away, since without an AIIR there is no way to isolate airborne spread
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC anticipates settings that lack the engineering resources for an AIIR: put a mask on the patient, place them in a private room with the door shut, and the chance of airborne spread falls while they wait to be transferred to a facility with an AIIR or sent home. The 3-foot separation is the fallback StatPearls describes for Droplet Precautions when no room is available, not for airborne pathogens; an open door defeats the purpose; and turning the patient away is not among the CDC's options.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Manually retractable evacuated tube systems
preguntas.subtema: Safety-engineered devices · CPT D3 3A 3M k54 k66 · PBT II.J VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Why is a manually retractable evacuated tube system described as safer than a needle and syringe?
opciones: It needs no transfer of blood, and it allows many tubes per puncture
It needs no training, and it costs less than a needle and syringe does
It needs no tourniquet, and its vacuum is lower than in ordinary tubes
It needs no holder, so there is no disassembly step after the draw
preguntas.explicacion: This system is called safer because the blood never has to be transferred and several samples can be taken through one venepuncture, while its safety mechanism prevents reuse. It still requires skill and extra training, costs more, and reusing its holder brings back the disassembly risk.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Semen Analysis", Diagnostic Tests (Specimen Liquefaction, Volume Measurement)
preguntas.subtema: Semen liquefaction · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.1 · CCMA 3D5 k117
preguntas.pregunta: What is the first thing the laboratory does with a semen specimen when it arrives?
opciones: Lets it liquefy, on the bench or in a 37-degree incubator, which can take up to 60 minutes
Lets it cool to 4 degrees for 60 minutes, which separates the sperm from the seminal plasma
Measures the volume and the pH first, before any liquefaction has been allowed to occur
Divides it into three numbered tubes, one each for count, motility and morphology
preguntas.explicacion: Liquefaction comes first: the sample is left on the bench or at 37 degrees Celsius, and within about five minutes it starts to turn homogeneous and watery, freeing sperm that were trapped in the coagulum. It can take as long as an hour. Only afterward are volume and pH measured and wet preparations made, and motility is best assessed within an hour of collection. Numbered tubes belong to cerebrospinal fluid.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.1
preguntas.subtema: Quality assurance · CPT D3 k9 · D1 1E k28 · PBT VI.A.1 · CCMA 3E7 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which elements make up the quality assurance framework set out for phlebotomy?
opciones: Training, written procedures, patient identification, sample condition, transport, incident reports
Training, written procedures, patient billing, sample volume, storage, satisfaction surveys
Equipment purchase, staff rotas, patient identification, tube color, transport, audit visits
Training, tube color coding, patient billing, sample condition, storage, incident reports
preguntas.explicacion: Quality assurance here is built from education and training, standard operating procedures, correct identification of the patient, the condition of the sample, safe transportation and a system for reporting incidents. Each element is there to keep one kind of mishap out of the process.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1241(c)(7), Standard: Test request
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D4 k112 k124 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A requisition for a Pap smear arrives with the patient's name, date of birth, sex and the ordering provider, but nothing else. Which item specific to this test must the requisition solicit under CLIA?
opciones: Her last menstrual period, and any earlier abnormal report, treatment or biopsy
Her parity and the date of her last cervical examination by the ordering provider
The name and address of the laboratory that examined her previous cervical smear
The patient's fasting status and the time elapsed since her last sexual intercourse
preguntas.explicacion: On top of the general requisition elements, 42 CFR 493.1241(c)(7) makes the Pap smear requisition ask for the date of the patient's last menstrual period and whether she has had an abnormal report, treatment or biopsy before; paragraph (c)(8) then sweeps in whatever else a particular test relevantly and necessarily requires. Parity, contraception and the address of a previous laboratory are not named there, and fasting has nothing to do with this specimen.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5: Disinfect the entry site
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation · CPT D3 k63 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E 3E5 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: For a routine venipuncture (not a blood culture), how does the WHO say the site should be disinfected?
opciones: A 70% alcohol swab for 30 seconds, then let it dry completely, about 30 seconds
A 70% alcohol swab for 30 seconds, then insert the needle at once while the skin is still wet
Povidone iodine for 30 seconds, since it disinfects better than alcohol before a routine draw
A 70% alcohol swab kept wet for 10 minutes, the contact time given for bleach
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 gives the numbers: a 70% alcohol swab applied for 30 seconds, then complete drying, which takes about 30 seconds more. Blood cultures are the one exception the step names. The guideline says that too little contact time raises the risk of contamination, so the drying is part of the disinfection rather than a delay, and inserting while wet skips it. The same step prefers alcohol to povidone iodine, because iodine can falsely raise potassium, phosphorus or uric acid results. Ten minutes wet is the contact time the guideline gives for a bleach solution on a blood spill, not for skin.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1, Vacuum extraction systems
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: How is a double-ended needle joined to the barrel of a vacuum system?
opciones: The end covered by a rubber cuff screws in, past a central thread
The end that enters the vein screws in, past a central thread
Both ends are pushed in, and a locking collar holds them together
The cuffed end is held by a luer-lock connector, as a winged set is
preguntas.explicacion: The needle has a point at each end. The end sheathed in rubber screws into the barrel, which is also called the tube holder, and a thread between the two ends is where that connection is made. The barrel then holds the tube and keeps the worker away from direct contact with blood.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Bleeding", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 k78 · CMA I.B.9.a · 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 15 · CPT 1M k37
preguntas.pregunta: A patient cuts a forearm on a broken specimen tube and the wound is bleeding freely. What is the first step?
opciones: Press directly on the wound with a sterile dressing or a clean cloth
Press on the artery above the wound at the nearest pressure point
Wrap a tourniquet above the elbow and write down the time it went on
Rinse the wound under running water until the bleeding slows down
preguntas.explicacion: Direct pressure is the first and most important step, and it stops most external bleeding; gloves go on first. Pressure points are no longer recommended, because collateral circulation defeats them. A tourniquet is a later step, for bleeding that continuous pressure has failed to control and that threatens life.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2N k52 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient walks in from the car park, sits down, and the phlebotomist reaches for the tourniquet at once. What is wrong with that?
opciones: Have him sit for at least 15 minutes first; posture changes alter results
He should lie down for 2 minutes first, the time it takes the veins to fill
He should stand for a few minutes first so the arm veins distend
Draw right away; posture matters only for coagulation samples
preguntas.explicacion: Changing a patient's position produces statistically significant differences in several biochemistry parameters, so the position, lying or sitting, is kept for at least 10 to 15 minutes before the draw, and office patients are advised to sit for at least 15 minutes beforehand. Any unavoidable change of posture is recorded so that the results can be interpreted.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Diversity and Discrimination in Health Care", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6 k193 · CMA F.2.b / 2027 F.1.c · RMA I.D.1.e
preguntas.pregunta: A PNAS study looked at medical trainees who held false ideas about how Black and White bodies differ biologically. What did holding those ideas lead to?
opciones: Lower ratings of Black patients' pain and less accurate treatment recommendations
Higher rates of hypertension among the trainees who held the beliefs
More referrals of Black patients for kidney transplantation
Overtreatment of pain in Black patients compared with White patients
preguntas.explicacion: Medical students and residents who endorsed ideas such as thicker skin or duller nerve endings rated the pain of Black patients lower, and their treatment recommendations came out less accurate, a legacy still visible in the undertreatment of pain. The kidney example runs the other way: a race-corrected eGFR delays diagnosis and narrows access to transplantation.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Specific Techniques), Non-verbal communication; and section Other Issues
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 · CCMA 6 k197 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Which non-verbal behaviors signal active listening during the patient interview?
opciones: Eye contact, leaning forward, and sitting near the patient
Standing at a right angle to the patient, near the exit
Sitting at a safe distance and avoiding eye contact
Typing notes while nodding so the patient keeps talking
preguntas.explicacion: The table pairs expression, stance and gestures: eye contact and facial expressions that show interest, leaning forward, and sitting near the patient. Its footnote reserves distance and caution with eye contact for patients with psychosis or paranoia, and standing at a right angle near an exit is a de-escalation technique for agitation. NIA separately warns against talking while typing.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the light gray top tube (sodium fluoride and potassium oxalate) the usual choice for a glucose specimen?
opciones: Its antiglycolytic additive keeps the glucose level stable for days
Its gel separator keeps the plasma away from the cells after spinning
Its clot activator produces serum faster than a plain red top tube
Its broth mixture keeps microorganisms alive until they can be cultured
preguntas.explicacion: The WHO table describes the additive of the gray tube as an antiglycolytic agent, that is, one that blocks the breakdown of glucose, and says it keeps the glucose value stable for up to five days. Glucose is the use the table gives for it, with a note that it needs a full draw because a short draw may cause hemolysis. Gel separators belong to the serum separator and PST tubes, the clot activator to the red top, and the broth to the blood culture bottle.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k54 k66 · PBT II.J VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Safety cannulae come with active and with passive mechanisms. How do the two differ?
opciones: Active ones need the user to act; passive ones deploy on withdrawal
Active ones deploy on withdrawal; passive ones need the user to act
Active ones retract the needle; passive ones bend the tip over safely
Active ones work only in adults; passive ones work only in children
preguntas.explicacion: Both kinds shield the needle once it leaves the cannula hub. An active system waits for the user, typically a button that pulls the needle into a plastic sheath, while a passive system puts a small guard out by itself as the needle is withdrawn. The same split is used for phlebotomy devices.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CPT D5 5H k94 distributing results · CCMA 7E k220 · NCMA 4.4 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the laboratory for a copy of his own completed test report. How long does the Privacy Rule give the laboratory to act on that request?
opciones: No later than 30 days after receiving it, extendable once by no more than 30 days
No later than 60 days after receiving it, extendable once by no more than 30 days
No later than 30 days after receiving it, with no extension available in any case
No later than 10 days after receiving it, extendable once by no more than 20 days
preguntas.explicacion: The access clock runs 30 days from receipt of the request, and a covered entity that cannot meet it may take one extension of no more than 30 further days. CLIA was amended to match: a laboratory may give patients and their personal representatives access to completed reports it can authenticate as theirs. The 60-day figure is the breach notification deadline.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vancomycin", section Mechanism of Action: Absorption; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia — Therapeutic drug levels (artículo 003430) (003430)
preguntas.subtema: Peak timing · CPT D2 k45 high and low levels · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: At what moment does an intravenous drug such as vancomycin reach its serum peak concentration?
opciones: Immediately after the intravenous infusion is completed
Immediately before the intravenous infusion is started
About 12 hours after the intravenous infusion is completed
About 30 minutes before the following dose is administered
preguntas.explicacion: Vancomycin has a rapid onset, with the serum peak concentration reached immediately once the intravenous infusion finishes; that is the moment a peak sample represents. The 30-minutes-before-the-dose window is the trough, and 12 hours after the dose is the collection time for lithium, tacrolimus, cyclosporine and sirolimus, none of which are given as short intravenous infusions.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Health Information Privacy and Control
preguntas.subtema: Minors and confidentiality · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A sixteen-year-old is seen alone for treatment of a sexually transmitted infection. Who usually controls that information?
opciones: The minor, since state law commonly grants confidentiality here
The parent, who is the personal representative in every case
The school nurse, who must be told of a reportable infection
The insurer, which receives the record with the claim it pays
preguntas.explicacion: When a patient lacks the legal capacity to decide, information goes to a surrogate, and for a child that is normally the parent. State law carves out exceptions: a minor who has been emancipated keeps control, and so does one who is sexually active and comes in alone for contraception or for care of a sexually transmitted infection. Reportable infections still reach public health authorities under a separate exception, which is not the same as sending word to a school.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, How to Obtain a CLIA Certificate of Waiver (2019): How do I apply?; When can I begin testing?
preguntas.subtema: CMS-116 to the state agency · CPT D1 k29 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.1.a.v · NCMA 4.12
preguntas.pregunta: A new urgent care wants to run only waived tests. What is the correct sequence to obtain its CLIA Certificate of Waiver?
opciones: Complete Form CMS-116, send it to the state agency, pay the fee, then test once the certificate arrives
Register with the FDA CLIA database, pay the fee to CMS, then begin testing the same day
Request an on-site survey from the state agency, pass it, then submit Form CMS-116 to CMS
Enroll in a proficiency testing program, submit the first results, then apply on Form CMS-116
preguntas.explicacion: The application for every certificate type is Form CMS-116. It goes to the state agency for the state where the site is located, which processes it and sends a fee coupon; after payment the certificate is mailed. Testing generally begins once the certificate is received, and the state may add its own requirements. No survey or proficiency testing is a precondition for a Certificate of Waiver.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.15(e)(1); CDC, MMWR RR-54(13) (2005), CLIA Requirements for Waived Testing
preguntas.subtema: Follow the manufacturer's instructions · CPT D1 k29 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: Once a site holds a Certificate of Waiver, what is the ONLY CLIA requirement for how each waived test is performed?
opciones: Work to the test's current instructions from the manufacturer
Run external controls each day patient samples are tested
Enroll every analyte in an approved proficiency testing program
Have testing personnel who meet the CLIA education requirements
preguntas.explicacion: A waived site is not routinely inspected and has no personnel requirements to meet: it obtains the certificate, pays the biennial fee, runs only waived tests, and works to the manufacturer's current instructions. Quality control is required only where the insert requires it, and proficiency testing is voluntary. That single requirement is also the one CMS surveys of waived sites find broken most often.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which preanalytical problem tops the list of reasons clinical laboratories reject a sample, and how big is it?
opciones: In vitro hemolysis, up to 3.3 % of routine samples and 40 to 70 % of all unsuitable specimens
Clotted samples, up to 3.3 % of routine samples and 40 to 70 % of all unsuitable specimens
In vivo hemolysis, present in about 2 % of routine samples and most rejected specimens
Insufficient volume, up to 22 % of routine samples and the majority of unsuitable specimens
preguntas.explicacion: Hemolysis is the preanalytical error seen most often, and hemolysis occurring in vitro is the single largest reason samples are rejected: it reaches 3.3 % of all routine samples and covers 40 to 70 % of unsuitable specimens, close to five times more than other causes such as clotted or incorrect samples. Fewer than 2 % of samples with detectable hemolysis broke down in vivo, so the damage is done during collection and transport.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, What is it used for? and Why do I need TDM?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C k45 · PBT II.A II.D · CCMA 3E2 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A prescriber orders a drug level with the note 'is he actually taking it?'. Which listed use is that?
opciones: Making sure the medicine is being taken as it was prescribed
Finding the best dose when the medicine is first started
Watching for the symptoms of a serious side effect of the drug
Checking that an immune response has not rejected the drug
preguntas.explicacion: Therapeutic drug monitoring may also be used to make sure a patient is taking the medicine as prescribed. Its other listed uses are settling the right dose when a medicine is first started, testing regularly so it stays effective without becoming harmful, and testing where symptoms of a serious side effect appear. Rejection by the immune system is watched for with biologics.

preguntas.pregunta: What should training for everyone who draws blood include, according to the quality assurance table?
opciones: Anatomy, the risks of blood exposure, and what poor infection control causes
Anatomy, the cost of consumables, and how to file an insurance claim
Pharmacology, the risks of blood exposure, and the layout of the laboratory
Anatomy, the history of bloodletting, and the maintenance of centrifuges
preguntas.explicacion: Education and training is required for all staff who draw blood, and it should cover the anatomy, an awareness of what exposure to blood can bring, and what follows when infection prevention and control are poor. Written procedures sit beside it as a second element.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.4; and NIA, Skin Care and Aging
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 k73 bandaging considerations, age and skin type · PBT II.I complications · CCMA 3E9 · NCMA 2C.10
preguntas.pregunta: Which patients are most prone to skin breakdown from repeated adhesive strips after capillary punctures?
opciones: The very young and the very elderly
Patients with bleeding disorders
Premature neonates below 1500 g
Patients cleaned with povidone iodine
preguntas.explicacion: Skin breakdown from adhesive strips used over and over is a recognized complication of capillary sampling, and the very old and the very young are the ones it strikes; enough pressure at the time and a look at the site afterwards prevent it. Age makes the elderly vulnerable because the outer skin turns thinner and less elastic and the vessels grow fragile.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(1)(ii), Medical Records
preguntas.subtema: Contents of the medical record · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these belongs in the confidential medical record an employer keeps for a phlebotomist with occupational exposure?
opciones: The hepatitis B vaccination dates and the written opinion of the professional
The type and brand of the device involved and the work area where it happened
The names and job titles of everyone who attended the annual training session
A copy of the exposure control plan, signed by the employee once every year
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(1)(ii) fills the record with the employee's name; the hepatitis B vaccination status, with the date of every dose and any record bearing on whether the person could be vaccinated; the results of examinations and of follow-up after an exposure incident; the copy the employer holds of the written opinion from the healthcare professional; and a copy of everything sent to that professional. Device brand and work area are sharps injury log entries under (h)(5)(i); names and job titles of those who attended belong to the training record under (h)(2)(i).
