preguntas.pregunta: A finger-prick is planned for a 5-year-old. What puncture depth does the WHO recommend for this age?
opciones: 1.5 mm
2.4 mm
preguntas.explicacion: Section 7.1.2 gives 1.5 mm as the recommended finger-prick depth for a child over 6 months and under 8 years, and 2.4 mm for a child over 8 years, which is also the limit an adult finger-prick should never exceed. The 0.85 mm lancet is the one available for premature neonates, and 3.32 mm is the distance from skin to bone at the medial and lateral heel of a 3 kg baby.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(2)(i) and (f)(2)(ii), Hepatitis B Vaccination
preguntas.subtema: Hepatitis B vaccination offer · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A newly hired phlebotomist begins drawing blood on Monday. By when must the employer make the hepatitis B vaccine available to her?
opciones: Within 10 working days of the initial assignment, after the required training
Within 15 days of the initial assignment, the deadline for the written opinion
Within 30 days of the initial assignment, before the first annual training
Only after a prescreening antibody test shows the employee is not immune
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(2)(i) sets the clock: the vaccine and the series are offered within 10 working days of the initial assignment to a job with occupational exposure, and only after the employee has had the training on the vaccine described in (g)(2)(vii)(I). The offer is not owed if the employee already completed the series, has antibody testing showing immunity, or has a medical contraindication. Fifteen days is the deadline for the written opinion in (f)(5), and (f)(2)(ii) forbids making a prescreening program a condition of getting the vaccine.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, Clinical Safety guidance, nails and rings; StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Personnel
preguntas.subtema: Fingernails and rings · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What does the CDC recommend for a phlebotomist's fingernails?
opciones: Natural nails no longer than the fingertip; no artificial nails with high-risk patients
Artificial nails are acceptable if hand hygiene is performed with soap rather than sanitizer
Nail polish is recommended to seal the nail surface against transient organisms
Nails may be any length as long as gloves are worn for every patient contact
preguntas.explicacion: A natural nail is kept level with the fingertip and no longer, and artificial nails or extensions are not worn by anyone in direct contact with high-risk patients; the CDC also notes that the skin under a ring carries more germs. StatPearls adds that long or artificial nails have been tied to outbreaks in intensive care and surgical settings, that current guidance holds nails under 0.5 cm, and that they should be free of polish and of artificial coverings. Gloves cancel none of this, since they do not stand in for hand hygiene.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 2 and section 4.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.A.3 III.D.3 · CCMA 3E10 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: An add-on for a viral RNA test is requested on an EDTA whole blood tube that has been in the refrigerator for two days. Under the general stability guidelines for whole blood, can it be used?
opciones: No: whole blood at 2 to 8 °C is listed as acceptable for RNA targets for only about 4 hours, though DNA holds 72 hours
Yes: whole blood at 2 to 8 °C is listed as acceptable for RNA targets for 72 hours, the same period given for DNA
Yes: EDTA whole blood is stable for RNA targets at 2 to 8 °C for 5 days, the figure the guideline gives for plasma
No: whole blood is never acceptable for RNA targets; only serum stored for 2 to 7 days at 2 to 8 °C can be used
preguntas.explicacion: The general guideline for whole blood gives room temperature for 24 hours and 2 to 8 °C for 72 hours when DNA is the target, but only 4 hours at 2 to 8 °C for RNA, with EDTA or ACD as the additives; plasma is the specimen listed at 2 to 8 °C for 5 days and serum for 2 to 7 days. When RNA is the target the recommendation is a tube with an RNA-stabilising reagent, so a two-day-old EDTA tube fails the add-on.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6: Take blood
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet application · CPT D3 k70 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Blood is flowing well into the tubes. When does the WHO say the tourniquet should be released?
opciones: Before the needle is withdrawn, once enough blood has been collected
After the needle is withdrawn, while gentle pressure is applied with clean gauze
After it has been in place for two minutes, even if more tubes remain to be filled
As soon as the needle enters the vein, before any blood flow is established
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 is explicit: once sufficient blood has been collected, the tourniquet comes off BEFORE the needle is withdrawn; the gauze and gentle pressure come after the needle is out. The guideline adds that some other guidelines go further and recommend removing it as soon as blood flow is established, and in any case before two minutes have passed with it in place. Two minutes is therefore a ceiling, not the moment to release, and before flow is established is earlier than any guideline the WHO cites.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC11422196, Bowman et al., Reducing Iatrogenic Blood Losses in Premature Infants, Introduction and Results
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4E k83 pediatric volume considerations, sources of information · PBT II.I considerations
preguntas.pregunta: A very low birth weight infant (under 1500 g) is in its second week of intensive care. What is typical of its cumulative phlebotomy loss?
opciones: It often matches or passes the infant's own circulating volume, driving anemia of prematurity
It rarely passes 5% of the circulating volume, since microtiter tubes keep each draw under 0.5 mL
It is made good within days by the infant's own marrow, so transfusion is seldom required
It stays near 15 mL/kg over three weeks, the floor a reduction program managed to reach
preguntas.explicacion: In very low birth weight babies, blood taken for testing is a real driver of anemia: over the first weeks the cumulative loss often matches or exceeds the volume they have in circulation, and it tracks closely with how many transfusions they need. One unit found it had drawn more than half of its infants' blood volume; after a reduction program, blood out fell from 18.1 to 15.0 mL/kg across three weeks.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.508(b)(5), Revocation of authorizations; 164.508(b)(2), Defective authorizations
preguntas.subtema: Revoking an authorization · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.b · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A patient wants to cancel an authorization she signed to release her records to her employer. How may she revoke it under HIPAA?
opciones: In writing at any time, except for actions already taken in reliance on it
Only before the covered entity has received and acted on the request
Orally at any time, and the covered entity must recall records already sent
Not until the expiration date or event stated on the form has passed
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.508(b)(5) lets an individual revoke an authorization at any time, provided the revocation is in writing; the exceptions are actions the covered entity has already taken in reliance on the authorization, and certain insurance situations where other law gives the insurer a right to contest a claim. Records already sent cannot be recalled by the revocation, but no further disclosures may be made under it. An authorization whose expiration has passed or that is known to be revoked is defective and cannot be used.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", Introduction; NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Figure 2
preguntas.subtema: Hands-free passing · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.3.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: How are sharp instruments passed in a procedure room so that two people are not put at risk at once?
opciones: Through a neutral zone, so the device is never handed person to person
By the person who used it, who announces the pass before letting go
With the tip capped by hand, which is allowed whenever a device is passed
Inside the sharps container, which is carried between the two workers
preguntas.explicacion: Operating rooms and other procedural areas use a standardized neutral zone, or hands-free passing technique, so that the instrument is set down and picked up instead of traveling from one hand to another. Handing and passing devices during or after use accounts for about a tenth of hollow-bore needle injuries in surveillance hospitals, and collisions with a coworker for another eight percent. Capping a used needle by hand is prohibited unless no alternative is feasible.

preguntas.fuente: HRSA, Newborn Screening Process, Blood Spot Screening; and HRSA, About Newborn Screening, History
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4C metabolic screening information · PBT III.A.4 newborn screening
preguntas.pregunta: A parent asks why the nurse called the heel stick 'the PKU test'. What is true of that name?
opciones: It is no longer accurate, because the screen now checks for many conditions beyond PKU
It is the official name, because phenylketonuria is the one condition every state must screen for first
It is accurate only in two-screen states, where the second card tests for PKU alone
It refers to the pulse oximetry part of screening, not to the blood spots
preguntas.explicacion: Blood spot screening is sometimes called the heel stick or the 24-hour test; although some providers still call it the PKU test, the term is no longer accurate because newborn screening now checks for many conditions. Screening began in the 1960s with Dr Guthrie's blood test for PKU. The name survives only as habit.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, footnote d
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: The only test ordered is a routine prothrombin time. According to footnote d of the WHO order-of-draw table, what may the phlebotomist do?
opciones: Draw a single light blue citrate tube and nothing else
Draw a non-additive tube first and discard it in every case
Draw a red clot activator tube first to prime the needle
Draw two light blue tubes and discard the first one
preguntas.explicacion: Footnote d of Table 2.3 says that when the only test ordered is a routine coagulation assay, a single light blue tube may be collected. The plain tube drawn ahead of it is an option kept for the case in which tissue fluid or thromboplastin contamination is a worry; it is not a rule for every draw. Neither a red tube nor a duplicate citrate tube is mentioned as a primer.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Steps 7 and 8
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw with a syringe · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 II.F · CCMA 3E6 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: Blood was collected with a syringe and now has to be transferred into a citrate tube, an SST and an EDTA tube. Does the WHO order of draw still apply?
opciones: Yes; the table is given for vacuum tubes or syringe and needle, so citrate, SST, EDTA
No; once the blood is already in the syringe, additive carry-over is no longer possible
Yes, but reversed, so the EDTA tube that needs a full draw is filled first
No; with a syringe the largest tube is always filled first to protect the vacuum
preguntas.explicacion: Step 8 presents Table 2.3 as the recommended order for vacuum tubes or for syringe and needle, so the same sequence is followed when transferring: citrate (3), serum separator (5), EDTA (8). Step 7 adds the transfer technique: pierce the stopper from directly above with slow, steady pressure and never push the plunger, because extra pressure raises the risk of hemolysis.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Shape and Structure of Erythrocytes
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: What does a reticulocyte count estimate, and what proportion of the red cells should reticulocytes normally be?
opciones: The rate of red cell production; about 1 to 2 percent of erythrocytes
The rate of platelet production; about 2 to 4 percent of formed elements
The share of immature neutrophils; about 2 to 8 percent of leukocytes
The share of red cells being hemolyzed; less than 1 percent of the count
preguntas.explicacion: A reticulocyte is a red cell in its first day or two out of the marrow, still holding leftovers of its organelles. It should account for 1 to 2 percent of the red cell count, and that share works as a rough gauge of how fast cells are being turned out; a figure too low or too high points to a production problem. Immature neutrophils, the bands, are a separate measure.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Clean catch urine sample (007487), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Clean-catch cleansing, male · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: An uncircumcised man is handed a clean-catch kit. What is the first cleaning step he should be told to perform?
opciones: Retract the foreskin first, then wipe the glans with a sterile wipe
Wipe the glans with a sterile wipe, leaving the foreskin where it is
Wash the tip of the penis downward with soap and water, as for an infant
Wipe the urethral opening twice, front to back, with two separate wipes
preguntas.explicacion: For a man the instruction is to wipe the glans with a sterile wipe, and if he is not circumcised the foreskin comes back first so the wipe reaches it. Leaving the foreskin in place defeats the cleaning. Washing with soap and water from the tip downward is the infant routine, and the two front-to-back wipes are the female instruction. He then voids a little into the toilet, stops, and collects until the cup is half full.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory with a 4 % hemolysis rate wants to know where it stands. What did the survey of 772 laboratories report?
opciones: Most of them, 71 %, stayed under 3 %, and 15 % fell between 3 % and 6 %
Most of them, 71 %, stayed under 1 %, and 15 % fell between 1 % and 3 %
Most of them exceeded 6 %, with emergency samples pulling the average up
Most of them clustered near 10 %, the figure reported for emergency rooms
preguntas.explicacion: In that survey 71 % of the laboratories had a hemolysis rate below 3 % and 15 % fell between 3 % and 6 %, with the highest values coming from emergency department specimens. A separate report put emergency samples at 10 % to 30 %. A laboratory at 4 % therefore sits in the upper range, which the authors of one such laboratory explained by their neonatal and emergency workload.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 5
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A tube reaches the lab with a label for the wrong patient. The unit calls and asks the technician to print a new label and stick it over the old one. What does good practice say?
opciones: Relabeling is discouraged no matter who does it, lab staff, ward staff or anyone else; recollect instead
Relabeling is acceptable if the nurse who drew the specimen confirms the patient's identity by telephone with the unit
Relabeling is acceptable when it is done by laboratory personnel and documented in the record system
Relabeling is acceptable for hematology tubes but never for specimens intended for blood bank testing
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratories are expected to hold a written procedure for unlabeled and mislabeled specimens, and relabeling is discouraged whoever does it: once the tie between patient and tube is broken, no phone call and no note in the record puts it back. A mislabeled tube is a misidentification, the error that carries the worst outcomes for patients, so the safe course is to draw again. No test type is exempt.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Clean catch urine sample (007487), How the Test is Performed; and StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Midstream portion · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: During a clean-catch collection, at what point should the patient start filling the cup?
opciones: After voiding a small amount into the toilet and stopping, then collecting until the cup is about half full
As soon as the stream begins, collecting the first portion until the cup is about half full
After voiding a small amount into the toilet, then collecting every drop until the bladder is empty
After the stream has ended, collecting the last portion that remains and filling the cup to the top
preguntas.explicacion: The patient voids a small amount into the toilet, stops the flow, holds the cup a few inches from the urethra and fills it to about half, then finishes voiding into the toilet. The first portion carries the most contaminating cells and bacteria, which is why it is discarded; collecting every drop is the rule for a timed collection and for semen, not for a midstream sample. About 15 to 30 mL is enough for analysis, so the cup is never filled to the top.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: Four tubes are needed: a serum separator tube, a light green PST, a purple EDTA tube and a light blue citrate tube. In the WHO order, which sequence is correct?
opciones: Light blue, serum separator, light green PST, purple EDTA
Serum separator first, light blue, purple EDTA, light green PST
Light blue, light green PST, serum separator, purple EDTA
Purple EDTA, light blue, serum separator, light green PST
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 assigns position 3 to the citrate tube, 5 to the serum separator tube, 7 to the light green plasma separator tube with lithium heparin and gel, and 8 to EDTA. So the sequence runs light blue, SST, PST, EDTA. Footnote d adds that the PST, when used, is drawn in the position shown, that is, after the serum tubes and before EDTA.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Complications
preguntas.subtema: Complications · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I III.B · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which two problems are attributed specifically to improper venipuncture technique?
opciones: More pain than expected, and possible injury to a nerve
More pain than expected, and clotting inside the citrate tube
A mislabelled specimen, and possible injury to a nerve nearby
A short draw in the gray tube, and bruising around the site
preguntas.explicacion: Increased pain and potential nerve injury are the two complications tied to improper technique, and both can be avoided with correct technique and equipment. Identifying the wrong patient and labeling a tube badly are reported separately as the errors most likely to happen.

preguntas.fuente: SAMHSA, Urine Specimen Collection Handbook for Federal Agency Workplace Drug Testing Programs (2024), Chapter 7 collection step 16 and Chapter 8 Section C
preguntas.subtema: Insufficient specimen · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 · CCMA 3E k127 · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: A donor hands over a container with about 30 mL of urine. What does the collector do?
opciones: Discard it and begin a second collection with a new container and the same form
Pour the 30 mL into bottle A and leave bottle B empty for a later collection
Send it as an insufficient specimen and let the laboratory decide what to do
Keep it and ask the donor to add to the same container after drinking water
preguntas.explicacion: Below 45 mL the specimen is discarded and a second collection begins immediately, using a new collection container and the same chain of custody form; temperature and physical characteristics are checked again on the second one. If the donor still cannot produce 45 mL after three hours, the collection stops, the reason is recorded and the agency's representative is notified about an alternate specimen.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, What types of blood tests require fasting?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C 2K k46 · PBT II.A II.D · CCMA 3E2 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: The order reads 'liver function tests' with no note about fasting. When does that group call for a fast?
opciones: In some cases, for instance when ordered as part of a metabolic panel
Always, because liver enzymes climb sharply after any meal is eaten
Never, because liver enzymes are not affected by food or by drink
Only when the patient also takes medicines that act on the liver
preguntas.explicacion: Liver function tests sit on the list of tests a patient may also be asked to fast for, alongside the renal function panel. Whether a fast is asked for depends on several factors, and the example given is that some of these tests require it only when they arrive as part of a comprehensive metabolic panel. Where the form is silent, the provider is asked.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Critical Limits of Laboratory Results for Urgent Clinician Notification" (EJIFCC 2003, PMC6178782), introductory text
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT VI.D · CCMA 3E13
preguntas.pregunta: A first-run potassium on an inpatient comes back far above the laboratory's critical limit. According to the published guidance on critical limits, what happens before the physician is called?
opciones: The value is confirmed by a second determination in the same sample, and a senior laboratory member verifies it
A new specimen is drawn by venipuncture, since the first tube is assumed to be hemolysed or contaminated
The result is released to the chart at once; confirmation is done only if the physician questions the value
The sample is recentrifuged and re-run on a second analyzer to rule out an instrument error before release
preguntas.explicacion: A critical result stays inside the laboratory until a second determination on the same sample confirms it and a senior member of staff, the laboratory doctor, clinical chemist or senior technologist, verifies it and talks it through with the clinician. Preanalytical influences are a frequent source of results that only look critical, glucose drawn through a line running glucose being the classic; another properly collected sample settles those.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Laboratory: Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders, Recognized Controls and Work Practices
preguntas.subtema: Ergonomic controls · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G · CMA I.B.9 / 2027 I.B.8 · NCMA 2A.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which control does OSHA suggest for a phlebotomist who sorts specimens at a bench for hours at a stretch?
opciones: Rotate tasks; provide an adjustable bench with knee room and a chair with a footrest
Provide a back belt and require two-person lifts for every full specimen rack
Limit sorting to 20 minutes per shift and assign the rest to housekeeping
Install anti-fatigue mats and require standing for the whole shift
preguntas.explicacion: The recognized controls for laboratory musculoskeletal hazards include automated specimen delivery systems to cut reaching and repetition, supportive chairs with footrests, adjustable workstations with enough knee clearance so the knees do not hit the bench, rotating tasks or limiting time on them, ergonomic computer stations for sitting and standing, anti-fatigue mats for standing stations, and handling devices for heavy carboys. Mats help where standing is unavoidable but do not justify standing all shift, and back belts are not among the listed controls.

preguntas.pregunta: Which accessory allows a winged needle to be used with an evacuated tube system?
opciones: A luer-lock connector
A rubber sleeve adapter
A screw-thread reducer
A one-hand scoop guard
preguntas.explicacion: A vacuum system can also take a winged butterfly needle joined to it by luer-lock connectors, and winged butterfly needles come with safety-engineered features as well. The one-hand scoop is not a connector at all: it is the maneuver used to re-sheath a used needle.

preguntas.subtema: Assisting with lines · CPT D4 4B assist other healthcare professionals · k80 equipment and transfer procedures
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse asks you to hand her supplies while she flushes a patient's multi-lumen central catheter. What is the routine she is following?
opciones: Flush every day, each lumen in the same order, with heparin or saline
Flush every day, choosing a different lumen order each time, with saline
Flush once a week, each lumen in the same order, with heparin only
Flush before every blood draw only, using the largest lumen first
preguntas.explicacion: A central venous catheter is flushed daily so that it neither clots nor holds blood, each lumen in the same order every time, with heparin or saline according to the type of catheter. Needleless systems are recommended to cut complications, and connectors change with the administration set, no more often than every 72 hours.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet application · CPT D3 3E k60 k70 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: An intravenous cannula has just been threaded and blood samples are wanted through it. What happens to the tourniquet?
opciones: It is loosened after threading and put back briefly to get adequate flow
It stays tight from the first puncture until the last tube has been filled
It is removed for good once the flashback appears in the chamber
It is moved down the forearm below the cannula before the tubes are filled
preguntas.explicacion: During cannulation the band is loosened or removed once the cannula is in and the needle is being withdrawn. If samples are to be taken at that point with a syringe or a phlebotomy adaptor, the band is put back for a moment to give enough flow, and then taken off again.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 3.5 Inhibitors: Endogenous and exogenous
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT V.B · CCMA 3D1 k113 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.b
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is about to give a saliva specimen for a molecular test and has just finished a coffee and brushed his teeth. Why does the collection instruction usually ask for a waiting period?
opciones: Food, non-water drinks, oral hygiene products and tobacco introduce substances that inhibit the molecular assay
Food and drink dilute the saliva so that its volume no longer reaches the minimum the collection device needs
Toothpaste raises the pH of saliva, which the assay reads as a positive result for most respiratory viruses
Coffee stains the collection swab, which blocks the optical reading of the amplification curve on the instrument
preguntas.explicacion: Saliva and buccal samples are normally taken only after a set interval with no food, no drink other than water, no oral hygiene products and no tobacco: what has been swallowed carries substances that interfere with molecular techniques, mainly polysaccharides and glycogen, enzymes like the plasmin of milk products, and minerals, calcium among them. One study of children found interference from food minimal when saliva was collected 20 minutes after a meal; the interval that applies is the manufacturer's.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.2, Definitions: Waived test, Nonwaived test, Certificate for PPM procedures
preguntas.subtema: Waived tests · CPT D1 1B k25 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1 · NCMA 4.12
preguntas.pregunta: Under CLIA, what is a waived test?
opciones: A test HHS has found to meet the statutory criteria for waiver under the PHS Act
A test performed by a physician or midlevel practitioner during a patient visit
A test that a laboratory chooses not to perform and refers to an accredited laboratory
A test of moderate complexity that has been exempted from proficiency testing
preguntas.explicacion: Under 42 CFR 493.2 a waived test is an assay, an examination or a whole test system that HHS has found to satisfy the waiver criteria written into the Public Health Service Act at section 353(d)(3); everything else counts as nonwaived, whether of moderate or of high complexity. Tests carried out by a physician, a midlevel practitioner or a dentist during a visit describe provider-performed microscopy, a subcategory with its own certificate. Sending a specimen to another laboratory does not change the category the test belongs to.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure; and "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Fill level and ratios · CPT D3 k59 k51 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A light blue citrate tube for a PT/INR comes back only about half full. What is the fill requirement for this tube, and why is a half-filled tube a problem?
opciones: Filling to at least 90% of the tube volume, to keep the 9:1 blood-to-citrate ratio
Filling to at least 50% of the tube volume, so that the 9:1 ratio is still within range
Filling to at least 90% of the tube volume, to keep the 1:9 blood-to-citrate ratio
Filling to the line only when the patient's hematocrit is above 55 percent
preguntas.explicacion: The tube has to be filled to within 90% of its full volume so that blood and sodium citrate stay in a 9 to 1 ratio; a half-filled tube breaks that ratio. The coagulopathies review adds that underfilling, like a hematocrit above 55%, raises the relative citrate level and disturbs the recalcification step of the assay. The ratio is nine parts blood to one of citrate, not the reverse.
