preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b) defines decontamination as treating a surface or an item, physically or chemically, so that the bloodborne pathogens on it are removed, inactivated or destroyed to the point of no longer transmitting infection, leaving the item safe to handle, use or throw away. Killing every form of microbial life, endospores included, is the neighbouring definition of sterilize; handling all blood as infectious is Universal Precautions; and altering the way a task is done is a work practice control.

preguntas.pregunta: How is the bilirubin blood test performed on a newborn?
opciones: A heel stick: the heel is cleaned with alcohol and punctured, and a few drops are collected
A venipuncture from a vein in the arm with a small needle, which takes less than five minutes
A finger stick on the middle finger after warming the hand in warm water for a minute
A cord blood sample taken at delivery, before the baby's first feeding of milk
preguntas.explicacion: For an adult the bilirubin sample comes from a vein in the arm, but a newborn has a heel stick: the heel is cleaned with alcohol, poked with a small needle, a few drops of blood are collected and a bandage is put on the site. Bilirubin from a heel poke hours after birth is a classic neonatal draw. Alcohol, not povidone iodine, is the antiseptic for a child's skin puncture.

preguntas.pregunta: What is claimed for double gloving in relation to a sharps injury?
opciones: It lowers the volume of blood transferred, but the puncture risk remains
It lowers the puncture risk, but the volume of blood transferred remains
It removes both the puncture risk and the volume of blood transferred
It changes neither, and is recommended only for surgical procedures
preguntas.explicacion: Wearing two pairs of gloves may reduce the amount of blood passed on during a sharps injury, but it does not stop the needle from puncturing the skin. Gloves are credited with the same limited benefit in a needle-stick: less blood transmitted, not an injury prevented.

preguntas.pregunta: A colleague keeps a jar of cotton balls soaking in alcohol and tears the cotton by hand as she goes. What is wrong with that?
opciones: Cotton pre-torn by bare hands is already contaminated, and bacteria grow in it
Alcohol evaporates from an open jar and is too weak to prepare the skin
Cotton fibers stick to the puncture site and cause the wound to keep oozing
Alcohol stored in an open jar has to be discarded at the end of the shift
preguntas.explicacion: Skin preparation calls for 70 percent alcohol applied with a single-use swab or a clean cotton-wool ball. Cotton torn ahead of time with bare fingers is already contaminated, and bacteria multiply in it as the hours pass, so jars of cotton left soaking in alcohol are not to be kept; the cotton is moistened right at the moment of use, and the main container must not be contaminated while doing it. For a blood donation the recommended preparation is a single step of 2 percent chlorhexidine in 70 percent isopropyl alcohol, left to air dry.

preguntas.pregunta: How does the standard say every procedure involving blood must be carried out?
opciones: In a way that keeps splashes, sprays, spatter and droplets to a minimum
Inside a certified biological safety cabinet, never on the open bench
With a mask and face shield worn for every procedure regardless of splash risk
Behind a protective covering that is replaced at the end of every shift
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xi) requires every procedure with blood or OPIM to be carried out so that splashing, spraying, spatter and the making of droplets are kept to a minimum. Biological safety cabinets become mandatory under (e)(2)(ii)(E) only where HIV or HBV research, or production work with those viruses, is going on. A mask with eye protection is required by (d)(3)(x) when splashes may be generated and facial contamination is anticipated, not for every task, and the protective coverings of (d)(4)(ii)(B) are an option for surfaces, not a way of performing a procedure.

preguntas.pregunta: A blood type is reported as A positive. What does the 'positive' refer to, and what share of Americans share that status?
opciones: The Rh D antigen is on the red cells; about 85 percent
The Rh D antigen is on the red cells; about 50 percent
Anti-D antibodies are in the plasma; about 85 percent
The A antigen is on the red cells; about 15 percent
preguntas.explicacion: The Rh group is separate from ABO, and only one Rh antigen, D, matters clinically; those who carry it, about 85 percent of Americans, are Rh positive, and the word positive or negative is added to the ABO letter. Anti-D antibodies are not preformed; they appear only in Rh negative people after sensitization. The lab reports the result simply as Rh+ or Rh−.

Damp and lying flat inside the tray
Chilled and upright in a small cooler
Dry and lying flat under the request forms

preguntas.pregunta: The needle has just been withdrawn. What does the WHO ask the patient to do, and what must the patient avoid?
opciones: Hold the gauze in place with the arm extended and raised, and not bend the arm
Bend the arm firmly over the gauze and keep it tightly bent for at least five minutes
Lower the arm below the heart so the puncture seals under gravity

preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 says to withdraw the needle gently, apply gentle pressure with clean gauze or cotton wool, and ask the patient to hold it in place with the arm extended and raised; the patient is told not to bend the arm, since bending it brings on a hematoma. preguntas.pregunta: A surgical hand scrub with an antimicrobial agent usually lasts how long?
opciones: About 2 to 6 minutes
About 15 to 20 seconds
About 10 to 15 minutes
About 30 to 60 seconds
preguntas.explicacion: Surgical antisepsis is a scrub that usually lasts 2 to 6 minutes; the clinical literature adds that scrubs of 10 minutes or more give no extra benefit and irritate the skin. The scrub is done with hands above the elbows, jewelry removed, nails cleaned under running water and a sterile brush or sponge, followed by drying with a sterile towel before sterile gloves. Fifteen to twenty seconds is routine handwashing, not surgical antisepsis.

opciones: Blood and medication infusions, and anesthesia
Routine vital signs and a height measurement
Transport of specimens to a reference laboratory
Storage of leftover serum for one further week
preguntas.explicacion: Informed consent is required for treatment, for dissemination of patient information, for the discussion of the HIPAA rules, for specific procedures, for surgery, for blood and medication infusions, and for anesthesia. It is a communication process between clinician and patient, not merely a signature on a document.

Nine; none is optional under the 2012 revision

The names of the eight appear in a figure of the OSHA brief; the count and the exception are what the text states.

preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In the common pathway of coagulation, what is the job of thrombin?
opciones: Turns soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin
Turns inactive prothrombin into its active form
Cross-links and stabilizes the fibrin clot
Degrades the fibrin once the vessel has healed
preguntas.explicacion: The common pathway has three moves: once factor X is active, prothrombinase converts prothrombin (factor II) into thrombin; thrombin then converts fibrinogen (factor I) into insoluble fibrin strands; and factor XIII stabilizes the fibrin clot. Activating prothrombin is the job of prothrombinase, not of thrombin, and breaking fibrin down later is the work of plasmin.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, PKU Screening, What happens during a PKU screening test?
preguntas.subtema: Metabolic screening timing · CPT D4 4C k81 metabolic syndromes
preguntas.pregunta: Why is newborn screening for phenylketonuria usually done a day or two after birth rather than in the first hours?
opciones: The baby has to have taken protein, breast milk or formula, before the sample
The heel is too small to puncture safely during the first day of life
The screening card cannot be processed until the birth is registered
Maternal blood in the newborn's circulation invalidates an early result
preguntas.explicacion: An accurate result needs the baby to have taken protein first, whether breast milk or formula, and that is why the sample usually waits a day or two after birth. Drawn sooner than 24 hours old, a normal result does not close the matter: the baby may need testing again at one to two weeks of age. Nothing else by way of preparation is required.

preguntas.pregunta: On the top of the foot, which venous network collects blood from the digital veins?
opciones: The dorsal venous arch
The plantar venous arch
The great saphenous vein
The small saphenous vein
preguntas.explicacion: On the top of the foot the digital veins gather into the dorsal venous arch, which feeds the anterior and posterior tibial veins; the sole drains instead into the plantar veins and the plantar arch. The great saphenous climbs the inner leg and thigh to the femoral vein, and the small saphenous runs up the outside of the leg to the popliteal.

preguntas.pregunta: When preparing a needle and syringe, from which end does the WHO say each package should be opened?
opciones: The needle from the hub end, kept capped; the syringe from the plunger end, nozzle still protected
The needle from the tip end, with the cap removed; the syringe from the nozzle end, ready to attach
Both from the middle, so the two parts can be joined without touching either end
The needle from the hub end, cap removed; the syringe from the plunger end, nozzle exposed
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.2.1 opens the hypodermic needle from the hub end, the back of the needle, keeping it capped, and the syringe from the plunger end, keeping the nozzle protected in its packaging; the nozzle is then pushed firmly into the exposed hub of the still-capped needle, and the assembly is left in place until needed. Uncapping early or exposing the nozzle defeats the purpose of the sequence.

preguntas.subtema: OGTT interpretation · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139
preguntas.pregunta: A fasting plasma glucose of 112 mg/dL on the baseline sample of an OGTT falls into which category?
opciones: Impaired fasting glucose (100 to 125 mg/dL)
Normal fasting glucose (60 to 99 mg/dL)
Diabetes (126 mg/dL or higher on two tests)
Impaired glucose tolerance (140 to 199 mg/dL)
preguntas.explicacion: Impaired fasting glucose is a fasting plasma glucose of 100 to 125 mg/dL (5.6 to 6.9 mmol/L); the WHO and some other bodies set the lower limit at 110. A normal fasting value runs 60 to 99 mg/dL, and 126 mg/dL or higher on two different tests diagnoses diabetes. Impaired glucose tolerance is defined by the 2-hour post-load value, not by the fasting sample.

preguntas.pregunta: Which staff group is named as using teach-back to check that patients know what to do before the next visit?
opciones: Staff making appointments, covering arrival time, medicines and fasting
Only the clinician, at the end of the consultation that ordered the test
The laboratory staff, at the moment the specimen reaches accessioning
The billing staff, when the patient settles the account on the way out
preguntas.explicacion: Every member of staff who deals with patients should use teach-back, and the example offered is the person booking appointments confirming that the patient has understood what the next visit will require: when to arrive, which insurance documentation and which medicines to bring, whether to fast, and what a referral to another clinician involves.

preguntas.pregunta: Under the Medicare Conditions of Participation, 42 CFR 482.13, when must a hospital inform patients of their rights?
opciones: In advance of furnishing or discontinuing care, whenever possible
Within 30 days of admission, in a written notice signed by the patient
Only when the patient or a representative files a formal grievance
At discharge, together with the billing statement and visitation policy
preguntas.explicacion: The first standard of 482.13, notice of rights, has the hospital tell each patient, or the representative where state law allows one, what their rights are before care is given or withdrawn, whenever that can be done. The same standard calls for a grievance process: a clear procedure for grievances written or spoken, time frames for the review, and a written decision naming the contact person, the steps taken and the outcome. Visitation rights are explained along with the rest, not at discharge.

Is picked by the employee from the sizes the supplier keeps in stock at the site

preguntas.explicacion: The definition of appropriate in paragraph (d)(3)(i) is a performance test, not a brand or a label: under normal conditions of use, and for the whole time it will be worn, the item must not let blood, or any other potentially infectious material, through to work or street clothes, to undergarments, or to the skin, eyes, mouth or other mucous membranes. Paragraph (d)(3)(iii) is what puts the right sizes within reach; and the definitions in (b) exclude ordinary uniforms, pants and shirts from being protective equipment at all.

preguntas.pregunta: A worker who never reached a protective anti-HBs level after two complete vaccine series is exposed to an HBsAg-positive source. Per the CDC table, what is given?
opciones: Two doses of HBIG, the first right away and the second one month later

preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's guidance for vaccinated clinicians with anti-HBs below 10 mIU/mL after two complete series says that if the source is HBsAg-positive or unknown, the clinician receives two doses of HBIG, the first as soon as possible and the second 1 month later, and that further vaccine is not recommended because two series have already failed. preguntas.pregunta: While transferring blood from a syringe, a phlebotomist pushes the plunger to speed up filling of a slow tube. What does the WHO say about this?

Press the plunger only for tubes with additives, which need a full draw
Press the plunger gently once the stopper has been removed from the tube

There is no exception for additive tubes, for the last tube, or after removing the stopper.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Responding to HBV Exposures in Health Care Settings, Unvaccinated clinicians and Table 1; CDC, Exposure to Blood (2003)
preguntas.subtema: HBV PEP for unvaccinated workers · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: An unvaccinated phlebotomist is stuck by a needle used on an HBsAg-positive patient. According to the CDC, what is given and when?
opciones: HBIG and the first vaccine dose, as soon as possible and preferably within 24 hours, at separate sites
The vaccine series only, started within 7 days, since HBIG is reserved for known non-responders
HBIG only, repeated one month later, since starting the vaccine after exposure is too late
A 28-day antiviral course started within 72 hours, followed by the vaccine series
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's table covers a clinician never vaccinated, or one who never finished the series, exposed to a source that is HBsAg-positive or unknown: one dose of HBIG plus hepatitis B vaccine, as soon as possible, injected at a different anatomical site such as the other limb, the series then completed on schedule and anti-HBs measured 1 to 2 months after the last dose. The older brochure puts the start preferably inside 24 hours and no later than 7 days. Two doses of HBIG a month apart are for non-responders after two series, and the 28-day antiviral course is HIV PEP.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Compensating for hearing deficits and Families and caregivers as part of the health care team
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k40 patient communication, k49 age considerations · PBT II.B age-specific needs
preguntas.pregunta: You finish the fasting questions with a hard-of-hearing patient and now have to explain the finger stick. How should the change of subject be handled?
opciones: Pause a moment, lift the voice slightly or gesture toward what comes next, then explain
Move into the new topic in a higher pitch, since that register marks a change more clearly
Write the new topic on a notepad and hand it over without saying any of it out loud
Have the companion tell the patient that the subject is changing, then carry on speaking
preguntas.explicacion: A change of subject is announced to a patient with hearing loss: pause a moment, raise the volume a little, point toward what is going to be discussed, touch the patient gently or ask a question. The notepad is for writing down key terms, alongside the spoken explanation, not instead of it. A high pitch is hard to hear, and remarks are not directed only to the companion.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Radiologic PPE
preguntas.subtema: Radiologic PPE · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.3 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.8.a / 2027 I.B.7.a · RMA III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.3
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is called to draw blood in the fluoroscopy suite while imaging is under way. Which protection is meant for that setting?
opciones: A lead apron, leaded glasses and cap, and a thyroid collar
A fluid-resistant gown, a face shield and two pairs of gloves
An N95 respirator with eye protection, as for airborne cases
A chemical-resistant suit with a self-contained air supply
preguntas.explicacion: Where x-ray and gamma radiation are in use, above all in fluoroscopy and the other procedures guided by imaging, the protective equipment is leaded: an apron or vest, leaded glasses, a leaded cap and a protective collar, each of which cuts the dose received. A personal dosimeter is required for workers who enter a high radiation or restricted area, or who take in more than a quarter of the occupational limit within a calendar quarter.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.2, Definitions: Laboratory
preguntas.subtema: CLIA scope · CPT D1 1B k25 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1 · NCMA 4.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which facility falls outside the CLIA definition of a laboratory?
opciones: A draw station that only collects and prepares specimens, with no testing
A physician office that performs only waived tests on its own patients
A hospital laboratory accredited by a CMS-approved organization
A mobile unit that performs hematology testing on human specimens
preguntas.explicacion: CLIA calls a laboratory a facility that examines materials taken from the human body, by chemical, hematological, microbiological, serological or similar methods, to give information for diagnosis, prevention, treatment or the assessment of health, and it says that a facility only collecting or preparing specimens, or only acting as a mailing service, without doing any testing, is not a laboratory. An office running waived tests and a mobile unit running hematology both perform examinations and so need a certificate; a pure collection site does not.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(ii) and (b), Definitions: Engineering controls
preguntas.subtema: Maintaining engineering controls · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: What does the standard require of the safety devices and sharps containers a draw station uses every day?
opciones: They are inspected on a regular schedule, then maintained or replaced
They are examined only after an exposure incident has been reported and logged
They are replaced every three years, the period set for keeping training records
They are checked by the manufacturer at installation and then left in service
preguntas.explicacion: Engineering controls are the devices that take the hazard away from the worker: self-sheathing needles, needleless systems, sharps disposal containers. Paragraph (d)(2)(ii) says that on a regular schedule they are examined, and then maintained or replaced, so that they still do what they were bought to do. Waiting for an injury reverses that logic, and the three-year figure is the retention period for training records in (h)(2)(ii), not a replacement interval.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", sections Technique or Treatment and Complications; and StatPearls, "StatPearls (NBK482331) — Petechiae" (NBK482331)
preguntas.subtema: Complications: hematoma · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: What is a hematoma, and which two technique errors cause it?
opciones: Blood pooled under the skin; a needle pushed beyond the vein lumen, or too little pressure during and after the draw
Pinpoint bleeding into the dermis; leaving the tourniquet on too long, or using a needle that is too small
Pooling of blood under the skin; shaking the tube after filling, or drawing the tubes out of sequence
Bleeding into the skin larger than 2 mm; drawing from the basilic vein, or using povidone iodine
preguntas.explicacion: A hematoma is the pooling of blood under the skin, and two errors are linked to it: pushing the needle in past the lumen of the vein, and not applying enough pressure during and after the draw. The WHO adds a third, letting the patient bend the arm. Pinpoint dermal bleeding is petechiae, and spots larger than 2 mm are purpura in the petechiae chapter.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6 k199 k202 · CMA F.3.b / 2027 F.1.i · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Which item is among the barriers to therapeutic communication reported in the literature?
opciones: The patient's own anxiety
Sitting at the patient's level
Use of open-ended questions
Introducing yourself by name
preguntas.explicacion: The barriers reported in studies are the patient's own anxiety, cultural differences that go unrecognised, differences in colloquial language, overworked providers, shortages of time or of staff, a fear of abuse or of being sued, and expectations from the patient that are unrealistic. The other three options are techniques that lower barriers, drawn from the technique table and from AHRQ.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.5
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 k56 · PBT II.J VI.G · CCMA 3E7 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is named among the factors that shape the quality of a laboratory sample?
opciones: The gauge of needle chosen for the puncture
The color of the gloves worn for the draw
The brand of alcohol rub kept on the trolley
The height of the rack the tubes stand in
preguntas.explicacion: The factors named as shaping the quality of a laboratory sample are the knowledge of the staff, use of the correct gauge of needle so the sample is not hemolyzed or otherwise abnormal, the anatomical site chosen, the recommended tubes, matching patient to sample, transport conditions and interpretation.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 6.2.2, Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2N k49 · PBT II.B II.D · CCMA 3E1 k127 · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: The flow into the tube is slow during a child's draw. Which measure does the WHO offer for the parent to do?
opciones: Tighten and release the child's wrist rhythmically to help the flow
Lower the child's arm below the level of the table for a minute
Press firmly above the elbow until the vein stands out clearly
Rub the puncture site briskly with dry gauze between the tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Where venipuncture proves difficult, the parent may be asked to tighten and release the child's wrist rhythmically so there is adequate blood flow, the child may be kept warm, warm cloths may be laid over the puncture area to dilate the vessels, and a transilluminator or pocket pen light may be used to show the dorsal hand veins and those of the antecubital fossa.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT VI.B · CCMA 3D9 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: The laboratory notifies a phlebotomist that a specimen was rejected for a critically ill patient. Why must the recollection be arranged without delay?
opciones: Rejection forces a new sample request, prolongs turnaround and can delay diagnosis and treatment
Rejected specimens are discarded after 30 minutes, after which the original order is canceled
The laboratory cannot issue any report for the patient until the replacement sample is received
A second rejection from the same unit automatically triggers an accreditation incident report
preguntas.explicacion: Sample rejection stops the analysis and generates a new request, which lengthens turnaround time and delays diagnosis and treatment of critical patients, with adverse outcomes described in the literature; that is the reason the task of contacting the patient or unit for recollection matters. Rejected tubes are actually kept 24 hours at 4 °C, other reports are not blocked, and accreditation bodies ask for monitoring, not automatic incidents.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Petechiae", section Pathophysiology
preguntas.subtema: Complications: petechiae · CPT D3 3L k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which four mechanisms are given as the primary causes of petechiae and purpura?
opciones: Low platelets, platelet dysfunction, clotting disorders, loss of vascular integrity
Low platelets, high hematocrit, iron deficiency, loss of vascular integrity
High platelets, platelet dysfunction, clotting disorders, raised blood pressure
Low platelets, platelet dysfunction, dehydration, prolonged tourniquet pressure
preguntas.explicacion: These rashes come from hemorrhage into the dermis, and the underlying mechanisms named are a low platelet count, platelets that do not work, disordered coagulation and vascular integrity that has given way. Some clinical pictures produce the spots through a combination of more than one of them.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section Pathophysiology
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K k69 · D1 k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.B.9.l / 2027 I.B.8.l · RMA III.I · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Why does laying a patient flat bring them round after a faint?
opciones: Blood returns from the legs and the heart no longer pumps uphill
Blood leaves the legs and pools where the tourniquet had been
The vagus nerve is compressed and the heart rate rises at once
The cool, quiet space raises the blood pressure by itself
preguntas.explicacion: When the patient falls or is laid supine, circulating volume returns from the lower limbs and the heart no longer has to deliver blood against gravity, so consciousness comes back quickly. That is also why the person is asked to sit or lie down promptly as soon as the warning symptoms appear.

preguntas.fuente: The Joint Commission, National Patient Safety Goals for the Laboratory Program (January 2026), NPSG.01.01.01, Rationale
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k41 · PBT II.C
preguntas.pregunta: The Joint Commission gives a two-fold intent for NPSG.01.01.01. What are the two purposes?
opciones: Confirm the person is the one the service is meant for, and match the service to that person
Confirm the person is the one the service is meant for, and report critical results on time
Confirm the specimen label is complete, and match the container to the requisition form on file
Confirm the person's identity, and record the room number as a backup identifier
preguntas.explicacion: The rationale says wrong-patient errors happen at virtually every stage of diagnosis and treatment, so the goal has two aims: first, to identify reliably that this individual is the intended recipient, and second, to be sure the service or the treatment fits that same person. Timely reporting of critical results is Goal 2, a separate one, and the room number is expressly excluded as an identifier.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: The forearm a patient offers shows a hot, red area diagnosed as cellulitis. Why is that site excluded for venipuncture?
opciones: Cellulitis or an abscess raises the risk of bacteria entering the blood directly
The redness blanches under pressure, so it is erythema and not bleeding into the skin
The swelling dilutes the specimen with tissue fluid, just as squeezing a finger does
Alcohol cannot be used on inflamed skin, so the site cannot be disinfected
preguntas.explicacion: A condition such as cellulitis or an abscess raises the risk of bacteria getting straight into the blood, so another site is chosen. Blanching is the feature that tells erythema from bleeding into the skin, tissue fluid dilution is the WHO's capillary warning about squeezing, and nothing in the material forbids alcohol on inflamed skin.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 5
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5E k89 · PBT VI.B · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory wants to start monitoring extra-analytical quality but can only afford two indicators. Which two areas do accreditation criteria and the literature put first?
opciones: Patient and sample identification, and the handling of critical results
Reagent inventory control, and calibration of the chemistry analyzers
Phlebotomist productivity, and the number of tubes drawn per patient
Duplicate test requests, and the utility of interpretative comments on reports
preguntas.explicacion: Review of accreditation requirements and patient safety concerns points to two priorities: patient and sample identification on the pre-analytical side and the handling of critical results on the post-analytical side, both already required by regulation or safety goals in many places. Duplicate requests and interpretative reporting are suggested as a later step into the pre-pre and post-post phases, and inventory or productivity are not extra-analytical quality indicators.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Families and caregivers as part of the health care team
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 · CCMA 7B k216 k218 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: The son says, 'I'll sign the consent, she's forgetful.' No proxy or power-of-attorney paperwork exists. Who decides?
opciones: The patient remains responsible for her own choices; set clear boundaries with the family
The son may sign, because adult children are the default decision-makers for parents
A clinic staff member signs on the patient's behalf as a neutral third party
The draw is deferred until a court appoints a guardian for the patient
preguntas.explicacion: It is above all the adult children who want to take over for a parent whose cognition is failing. Only a family member named as health care agent or proxy holds, in some circumstances, the legal authority to decide about care; without that authority the patient stays responsible for her own choices, and the clinician sets clear boundaries with the family. Where there is no proxy and no advance directive at all, the short-term decision falls to the team or to an ethics committee, and a court assigns formal guardianship only when the need is long term.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix B, preparation steps
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant takes a refrigerated control and a refrigerated patient sample straight from the fridge to the bench and starts the run. What step was skipped?
opciones: Letting the refrigerated material come up to room temperature first
Recording the refrigerator temperature at the moment of removal
Checking that the kit lot matches the lot of the control material
Writing the date of opening on the outside of the reagent vial
preguntas.explicacion: The preparation checklist for waived testing puts several steps before the run: check vials and reagents for contamination, discoloration or damage; prepare them the way the current instructions say; write the opening date on a vial or kit just opened; let refrigerated reagents and samples warm to room temperature; and then run quality control as the instructions recommend.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Contact Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Dedicated equipment · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C2 k96 · CMA I.B.5.c / 2027 I.B.4.c · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: Under Contact Precautions, what does the CDC recommend for a blood pressure cuff and similar patient-care equipment?
opciones: Disposable or dedicated equipment; if sharing is unavoidable, clean and disinfect it before the next patient
Shared equipment may be used freely, since the pathogen spreads by contact with the patient, not with objects
Wrap shared equipment in a protective cover that is changed at the end of the shift
Autoclave the equipment after each use, since disinfection does not reach contact pathogens
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's Contact Precautions recommendations use blood pressure cuffs as the example: equipment for patient care should be disposable, or else dedicated to that one patient, and where sharing between patients cannot be avoided it is cleaned and disinfected before the next one. The reason is that contact transmission takes in the patient's environment and the objects in it, not only skin. The same page asks that these patients' rooms be cleaned and disinfected often, at least daily, or before another patient uses the space in outpatient settings, with attention to high-touch surfaces.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2 Prepare the skin
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 puncture technique · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: How should the puncture stroke itself be made in capillary sampling?
opciones: A single quick, firm, deliberate stroke, for good flow and no second stick
Two short strokes in the same track, so that the second one opens the bed fully
A slow stroke that stops as soon as the first drop of blood appears
A rocking stroke across the print lines, to widen it without going deeper
preguntas.explicacion: One stroke, quick and carried through, is what brings a flow good enough to avoid a second attempt. Going in again would mean either a used lancet or a used hole, and both are barred because they invite bacteria and infection. Depth is a matter of lancet length, not of rocking the device.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Use of Accompanying Adults or Children as Interpreters
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F Laboratory Regulations, ADA · CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA II.F.1.c(2) interpreter · CMAA 3A ADAAA compliance
preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient asks for a sign language interpreter for a long pre-test discussion. May the laboratory tell him to bring a family member instead?
opciones: No, responsibility for effective communication rests on the covered entity itself
Yes, if that family member signs and agrees to interpret for him on the day
Yes, if hiring an interpreter would be an undue burden for the laboratory
No, unless the laboratory offers video remote interpreting as the alternative
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may not oblige anyone to bring along a person to interpret. An accompanying adult may interpret in two narrow cases only: an emergency with an imminent threat where no qualified interpreter is at hand, and a non-emergency where the individual asks for it, the adult agrees and it is appropriate. Undue burden does not erase the duty either; it shifts it onto another effective aid.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Restraint and Seclusion", sections Removal of Restraints and Continuing Education Activity
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k49 · CCMA 3E1 k127 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: An agitated inpatient calms down 20 minutes into a 4-hour restraint order. What should happen?
opciones: Remove the restraints immediately; he is no longer a danger to anyone
Keep the restraints on until the 4-hour order expires, as written
Keep the restraints on until the next scheduled face-to-face evaluation
Loosen one limb every 15 minutes until the order runs out
preguntas.explicacion: The moment the patient stops being a danger, to himself or to anyone else, the restraints come off; the time limit on the order is a ceiling, not a duration to be served. Restraint and seclusion are interventions of last resort, required to be the least restrictive measure available, with no evidence that they are therapeutic or that they reduce aggression, and staff observe the patient regularly throughout.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(1)(ii) and (f)(1)(iii), Hepatitis B Vaccination and Post-exposure Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Terms of the medical follow-up · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: How must the hepatitis B vaccination and any post-exposure follow-up be made available to an exposed employee?
opciones: Free, at a reasonable time and place, and under a licensed healthcare professional
Free, but only at the occupational health service the employer has contracted
At the employee's expense, reimbursed once the written opinion has arrived
Free, and only during the first ten working days of the initial assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(1)(ii) puts four conditions on every medical evaluation and procedure the standard requires, prophylaxis included: no cost to the employee, a reasonable time and place, work carried out by a licensed physician or by any other licensed healthcare professional, or under their supervision, and agreement with the Public Health Service recommendations current at that moment. Paragraph (f)(1)(iii) adds that laboratory tests go to an accredited laboratory, also free. The ten working days are the deadline for offering the vaccine, not a window that closes on follow-up.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1; and StatPearls, "Needlestick", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which change in practice is credited with markedly reducing needle-stick injuries?
opciones: Dropping recapping and putting the sharp straight into a safety container
Recapping every needle carefully with the cap held in the other hand
Storing used needles on the tray until the end of the drawing session
Rinsing the used needle before it goes into the puncture-resistant bin
preguntas.explicacion: Eliminating needle recapping and disposing of the sharp immediately into a puncture-resistant container is described as markedly reducing these injuries. Routine recapping is no longer recommended precisely because handling a used needle is what creates the chance of a puncture.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Karyotype Genetic Test, What happens during a karyotype genetic test?
preguntas.subtema: Buccal swab · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(a) 2027
preguntas.pregunta: A karyotype has been ordered and a buccal specimen is requested. How is it collected?
opciones: A swab is put into the mouth and rubbed across the inside of the cheek to gather cells
A swab is put into the mouth and rubbed over the tongue and under it to gather saliva
The patient rinses with sterile saline and spits the rinse into a sterile screw-top tube
A blade scrapes the inner surface of the lower lip and the scraping goes onto a slide
preguntas.explicacion: A buccal swab is one of the specimens a karyotype can be run on: the swab goes into the mouth and is rubbed across the inside of the cheek to pick up cells. It needs no preparation and carries no risk. A normal report means 46 chromosomes with no unusual change in their structure.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, section Causes
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 · D2 2L k48 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Besides fear and pain, which everyday events are listed as bringing on a faint?
opciones: Coughing hard, straining at stool, standing still too long, passing urine
Eating a light meal, reading in poor light, walking upstairs, yawning
Drinking water, sitting down slowly, wearing loose clothing, resting
Breathing slowly, lying flat for an hour, raising the legs, whistling
preguntas.explicacion: Faints are described as happening during or just after coughing very hard, having a bowel movement with straining, standing in one place too long, or passing urine, especially at night. Emotional distress, fear and severe pain sit on the same list, and all of them can appear in a drawing room.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Galactose-1-Phosphate Uridyltransferase Deficiency" (galactosemia), section Evaluation; and HRSA, Newborn Screening Process, When Does Newborn Screening Happen?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4C galactosemia collection information · PBT III.A.4 newborn screening acceptability
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn received a blood transfusion before the screening card was collected. Why does that matter for galactosemia?
opciones: The screen measures enzyme activity, so normal enzyme from the transfused cells can mask an affected baby
The screen measures galactose in plasma, and the transfused donor plasma dilutes it below the cut-off value
The transfusion adds lactose, which raises galactose and causes a false positive
The transfusion does not matter, because the screen uses DNA that is unaffected by donor cells
preguntas.explicacion: Newborn screening for galactosemia measures enzyme activity, so it catches the disease before galactose ever reaches the diet; but where a transfusion came first, the transfused blood carries normal enzyme activity and the case can read as normal. That is why babies who have been transfused may be screened later or need further testing.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Materials and methods, Laboratory setting; Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5E 5I · PBT VI.C · CCMA 3D9 k117 · RMA III.C.1.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: An emergency laboratory wants its accessioning staff to apply rejection criteria consistently. What training scheme did the published laboratory use for the secretaries who accept or reject samples?
opciones: One week of specialized training on the rejection criteria, with the program updated by laboratory specialists every 6 months
One day of orientation on the rejection criteria, with an annual refresher delivered by the nursing education department
Three months of supervised practice on the rejection criteria, after which no further update of the program was required
Self-study of the rejection criteria table, verified by a written test at the time of hiring and not repeated afterwards
preguntas.explicacion: In that laboratory two specialized secretaries by day and one at night receive the samples and decide to accept or reject them against the laboratory's written criteria; they were trained for one week to specialize in those criteria, and laboratory specialists updated the training program every six months. For the clinical staff who collect, the laboratory added comprehensive education seminars every two months aimed at the emergency departments and intensive care units.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, Clinical Safety guidance for healthcare providers, moments for hand hygiene
preguntas.subtema: Hand hygiene after gloves · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wearing gloves finishes a draw and removes them. Which CDC moment for hand hygiene applies?
opciones: Immediately after glove removal, before anything else
Only if the gloves were visibly soiled with blood
Before touching the next patient, which covers this case
At the end of the shift, because gloves replace hand hygiene
preguntas.explicacion: Immediately after glove removal is one of the CDC's moments for hand hygiene. The others: before an aseptic task, immediately before touching a patient, when moving from a soiled site to a clean one, after touching the patient or their surroundings, and after contact with blood or a contaminated surface. The same page states that gloves do not substitute for hand hygiene. Waiting for the next patient skips the glove-removal moment, and visible soiling changes only the method, soap and water rather than alcohol rub, not whether hygiene happens.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.4, Availability of appropriate supplies
preguntas.subtema: Equipment quality · CPT D3 3A 3B k58 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.2 · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Why is a service expected to keep enough laboratory tubes in stock at all times?
opciones: So blood is never decanted from one tube into another to reuse tubes
So the tubes on the tray can be replaced before their expiry each month
So a second tube of every color is always drawn as a spare specimen
So the same manufacturer supplies the needles and holders in the tray
preguntas.explicacion: Management is asked to make enough sample tubes available precisely to keep dangerous shortcuts out of the room, and the example given is decanting blood so that tubes can be recycled. The single-manufacturer rule is a separate point about components fitting one another.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 4
preguntas.subtema: Hand hygiene and gloves · CPT D3 3A · D1 1K k35 · PBT II.F VI.G · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist finishes cleaning a spill and her hands are visibly soiled. Which form of hand hygiene is required before the next draw?
opciones: Soap and water, dried with single-use towels
Alcohol rub, worked in until the hands are dry
Alcohol rub, followed by a second pair of gloves
Soap and water, dried with a shared cloth towel
preguntas.explicacion: Hand hygiene before a draw can be done two ways: washing with soap and water and drying on single-use towels, or rubbing with alcohol when the hands are not visibly contaminated. Visible soiling therefore rules the rub out. Well-fitting non-sterile gloves go on once the hands are dry.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 9: Address Language Differences, Provide written materials and videos in patients' languages; and Never use unacceptable language access services
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: The fasting instruction sheet exists only in English and the patient reads Haitian Creole. What is offered?
opciones: An interpreter trained in sight translation reads the sheet aloud to her
A member of staff with school Creole writes a summary on the sheet
The sheet is handed over as it is, since a copy has to be given anyway
The sheet is dropped, and fasting is left to the appointment reminder
preguntas.explicacion: It should not be assumed that people who use another language will understand notes written in English. Where materials cannot be obtained in the patient's language, interpreters trained in sight translation are enlisted, which means reading a written document aloud in a language other than the one it is written in. Getting by on basic or intermediate skills is ruled out.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antiepileptic Drug Monitoring", section Other Issues, Trough Versus Free Levels
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: What does a 'trough level' represent in antiepileptic drug monitoring?
opciones: The lowest drug concentration, typically just before the next dose is due
The highest drug concentration, shortly after the dose has been taken
The unbound, pharmacologically active fraction of the drug in blood
The average concentration across the whole dosing interval
preguntas.explicacion: The trough catches the drug at its floor, which usually falls just ahead of the next dose, and it matters most for a drug with a short half-life because it shows the minimum kept up between doses. Free levels are the unbound, active fraction, measured where protein binding may be altered. The peak and the average across the interval are different quantities.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 3.5 Inhibitors: Endogenous and exogenous
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.A.2
preguntas.pregunta: A parent asks how long after breakfast a child's saliva specimen for a molecular test can be taken. What did the study of that question find?
opciones: Interference from the meal was minimal once the specimen was taken 20 minutes afterwards
Interference from the meal persisted until at least two hours had passed since eating
Interference from the meal was minimal at any interval, so no waiting period was needed
Interference from the meal was minimal only when the mouth had been rinsed with water
preguntas.explicacion: Saliva and buccal specimens are normally collected only after a defined interval without food or non-water drinks, oral hygiene products or tobacco, because food carries polysaccharides, glycogen, enzymes and minerals that interfere with molecular techniques. In five children giving saliva for SARS-CoV-2 detection, interference from eating was minimal when the sample came 20 minutes later.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.1 Structure and Function of Blood Vessels, Veins; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Classification & Structure of Blood Vessels, Veins
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Why do the veins of the limbs have valves, and roughly what share of the blood volume is in the veins at any moment?
opciones: To stop backflow under low pressure and gravity; almost 70 percent
To stop backflow under low pressure and gravity; about 10 percent
To produce the pulse felt at the radial artery; almost 70 percent
To regulate flow into the capillary beds; about 5 percent
preguntas.explicacion: Veins are low-pressure vessels, so the larger ones, in the limbs above all, carry valves that keep blood moving toward the heart against that low pressure and against the pull of gravity. Walls that are thinner and less rigid let the veins carry almost 70 percent of the total volume, against about 10 percent in the systemic arteries and 5 percent in the systemic capillaries.

preguntas.fuente: HRSA, Newborn Screening Process, Blood Spot Screening; and CDC, CDC Provides Quality Assurance for Newborn Screening
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4C k81 filter paper technique · PBT III.A.4 newborn screening, III.D transport
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's card has all its circles filled. What must happen before it is sent to the laboratory?
opciones: The blood spots must be allowed to dry
The card must be kept refrigerated
A second card must be collected first
The spots must be sealed under clear tape
preguntas.explicacion: The card is sent to the laboratory only once the blood spots have dried; the dried sample goes to the state's newborn screening laboratory. Even the CDC quality-assurance laboratory that makes reference cards leaves its spotted cards to dry overnight. Results usually reach the baby's provider in about five to seven days.

preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A technician who moves to another hospital finds a different list of specimen rejection criteria in force there. Why does that happen?
opciones: There are no internationally accepted guidelines for unacceptable specimens
Rejection criteria are issued by the accrediting body, and accreditors differ
Rejection criteria follow the analyser, so they change with the manufacturer
Each laboratory adopts the criteria of the outside laboratory it refers work to
preguntas.explicacion: For some of the most contested steps of the preanalytical phase there are still no internationally accepted recommendations, nor agreed quality measures. The criteria for rejecting a sample, and the way unacceptable samples are then managed, processed and reported, differ widely between laboratories, which is why harmonisation of this area is repeatedly called for.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation; and The Joint Commission, National Patient Safety Goals for the Laboratory Program (January 2026), NPSG.01.01.01, EP 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2E k41 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3E12 k124 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: A trainee wants to label the filled tubes at the bench. Why are tube identification and labeling both done with the patient present?
opciones: It cuts down the risk of mixing up which tube belongs to which patient
It lets the patient read the label and correct the spelling of the name
It shows that the fasting instructions were kept before the first tube
It lets the phlebotomist skip the wristband check on any later visit
preguntas.explicacion: Before the blood is withdrawn the identification data and the tube labeling are double-checked, and both the identification of the tubes and their labeling happen with the patient there, which is what lowers the risk of tube misidentification. The identification goal states the same requirement as its second element of performance.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: CPR - adult and child after onset of puberty, First Aid; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: CPR - adult (000013)
preguntas.subtema: CPR ratio and rate · CPT D1 1L k38 · CMA I.B.9.c / 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10
preguntas.pregunta: For adult CPR, what compression-to-breath ratio and compression rate are used?
opciones: 30 compressions to 2 breaths, at 100 to 120 compressions per minute
15 compressions to 2 breaths, at 60 to 80 compressions per minute
30 compressions to 5 breaths, at 100 to 120 compressions per minute
5 compressions to 1 breath, at 120 to 140 compressions per minute
preguntas.explicacion: Adult CPR runs in cycles of 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths, repeated until the person recovers or help arrives, at a rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute with pauses for breaths kept under 10 seconds. The heel of one hand goes in the center of the chest between the nipples with the other hand on top, elbows locked and shoulders over the hands. With two or more rescuers, compressors switch every 2 minutes or about 5 cycles to avoid fatigue, and an AED is used as soon as one is available.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (communication and anxiety)
preguntas.subtema: Preventing syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E1 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient admits to a history of panic attacks during blood draws. Which two simple measures are described to lower anxiety and prepare for a possible reaction?
opciones: Counting down before the puncture, and having the patient lie down when the history is severe
Drawing without warning so the patient has no time to react, and using a smaller needle
Applying the tourniquet early so the draw is quicker, and keeping the patient standing
Postponing the draw until a family member is present, and skipping the identification questions
preguntas.explicacion: Simple steps such as counting down can significantly reduce anxiety and improve the conditions for the venipuncture, and a patient who reports bad panic attacks during the draw may be asked to lie down; identifying patients afraid of blood tests or with a history of vasovagal attacks in advance lets the team prepare for a possible faint. Drawing without warning contradicts the emphasis on transparent communication and consent.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(ix)(A), (B) and (C), Gloves
preguntas.subtema: Torn gloves · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: During a venipuncture the phlebotomist notices a tear in one glove. What does the standard require?
opciones: Replace it as soon as feasible; a single-use glove is never washed for reuse
Finish the draw, then wash the glove with soap and water so it can be reused
Cover the tear with tape until the procedure ends, then discard the glove
Replace it only if blood reached the skin; otherwise finish the draw and discard it
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ix)(A) has a disposable glove changed as soon as it is practical once contaminated, and as soon as feasible if it is torn, punctured or otherwise no longer a barrier. Paragraph (d)(3)(ix)(B) adds that single-use gloves are never washed or decontaminated to be used again; only utility gloves may be reused, and only while they are intact, under (d)(3)(ix)(C). What triggers the change is the loss of the barrier, not whether blood has already touched skin.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, row 3; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k57 k59 · PBT II.H.1 II.G · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A prothrombin time and a partial thromboplastin time are ordered together. What does that mean for the order of draw?
opciones: Both are citrate tubes, so both are filled in the coagulation-tube position
The prothrombin tube keeps its usual place and the thromboplastin tube is filled last of all
Both are citrate tubes, but they are filled after the serum separator tube
The thromboplastin tube is filled ahead of the prothrombin tube
preguntas.explicacion: Both assays are run on citrated plasma, so both use the light blue tube, and the table puts that tube ahead of the clot activator, separator, heparin and EDTA tubes. Nothing separates two tubes of the same kind, so neither goes ahead of the other, and the position filled last belongs to the fluoride tube for glucose.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", section Other Issues; and Table (Common Pitfalls), Negative body language
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6 k199 k202 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: An agitated inpatient is refusing to sit for the draw. Which de-escalation techniques are described?
opciones: A moderate distance, calm body language, and awareness of the exits
Standing over the patient, speaking firmly, and blocking the doorway
Leaving without a word and returning with two more staff members
Sitting close and holding eye contact so he feels fully attended to
preguntas.explicacion: Verbal de-escalation borrows from the same set of therapeutic communication techniques and balances the provider's safety against the patient's comfort: hold a moderate distance without looking defensive, keep body language and tone calm and open, stand at a right angle to the person, know where the exits are, and let them leave easily. Standing over a patient is a pitfall.

preguntas.subtema: Access to the Exposure Control Plan · CPT D1 1H k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist asks to see the facility's Exposure Control Plan. What does the standard say?
opciones: A copy must be accessible to employees, and training must explain how to obtain it
It goes only to the Director and the Assistant Secretary, when they ask for it
It may be seen only with the employee's written consent filed in the medical record
It is a management document; employees receive only a summary in the annual training
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(1)(iii) requires each employer to make a copy of the plan accessible to employees, following 29 CFR 1910.20(e), and (g)(2)(vii)(D) makes an explanation of the plan, and of how to get hold of a copy, a mandatory element of the training program. The access granted to the Director and the Assistant Secretary by (c)(1)(vi) comes on top of employee access, not instead of it. Written consent is the condition for releasing an employee's medical record to others under (h)(1)(iii), not for reading the plan.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1283(a)(4), Standard: Test records
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F k92 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E k145 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: During an inspection the surveyor picks a result from three months ago and asks who ran that test. Which CLIA record has to supply the answer?
opciones: The record of specimen testing, which carries dates and who tested
The test report itself, which carries the person who released it
The requisition, which carries the orderer and the collector
The competency file kept for each member of the testing staff
preguntas.explicacion: The test records standard asks for an information or record system holding four things: positive identification of the specimen, the date and time it reached the laboratory, the condition and disposition of any specimen that failed the acceptability criteria, and the records and dates of all testing together with the identity of whoever performed it. That last item is what the surveyor wants.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Cholesterol Levels, section Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k45 k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: When fasting is requested for a blood cholesterol test, what is the usual window?
opciones: 9 to 12 hours, which is why the test is often done in the morning
8 hours, the same minimum as for a fasting plasma glucose
12 hours, the same window MedlinePlus gives for an iron test
24 hours, the same window StatPearls gives for avoiding alcohol
preguntas.explicacion: The patient may need to fast, taking neither food nor drink, for 9 to 12 hours before a blood cholesterol test, which is why the appointment usually falls in the morning; the provider says whether the fast is needed. The 8-hour figure is the glucose minimum, 12 hours is the iron test window, and 24 hours is the alcohol window.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, How to Prepare for a Lab Test, section What types of lab tests require special preparation; StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D V.B · CCMA 3D1 k113 k125 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(c)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient collecting a 24-hour urine for 5-HIAA asks which foods to avoid. Which list is correct?
opciones: Bananas, avocados, walnuts, pineapples and eggplants
Cooked meats, herbal tea and alcoholic beverages
Douching, tampons and sex in the 24 to 48 hours before
Coffee, energy drinks and lemon-flavoured water
preguntas.explicacion: For a 5-HIAA test the patient may be asked to steer clear of various foods, the examples given being bananas, avocados, walnuts, pineapples and eggplants. Other tests carry other restrictions: creatinine may call for fasting or for avoiding cooked meats, cortisol for resting before the draw and for eating, drinking and tooth-brushing to stop for a period, and a fecal occult blood test for certain foods and medicines to be dropped. The douching, tampon and intercourse restriction belongs to the Pap smear, not to a urine collection.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination: A Quality Tool for Clinical Laboratory Professionals
preguntas.subtema: Blood culture documentation · CPT D4 4A k75 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139
preguntas.pregunta: Besides the patient's identifiers, which item does the CDC's blood culture procedure require you to document for each set?
opciones: The anatomic site the blood came from, such as left antecubital
The temperature of the bottles at the moment of collection
The lot number of the skin disinfectant that was used
The tourniquet time for the venipuncture, in seconds
preguntas.explicacion: The procedure records the volume in each bottle; the anatomic site, left hand, left antecubital or right subclavian; the collection method, whether venipuncture, central or arterial line; the staff member who drew the cultures; the location in the facility; and, in the 2025 version, the exact date and time. Specimen temperature is a urine drug-test requirement, and tourniquet time and disinfectant lot are not on the list.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Hemoglobin
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1 · CPT Core k4 (applied D3)
preguntas.pregunta: How many oxygen molecules can a single hemoglobin molecule carry, and what binds them?
opciones: Four, one on the iron ion of each of its four heme groups
Two, one on each alpha-beta pair of globin chains
Four, one bound directly to each of the four globin proteins
About 300 million, one for every hemoglobin in the cell
preguntas.explicacion: Hemoglobin consists of four folded globin chains, two alpha and two beta, each holding a heme group with an iron ion. Oxygen binds to the iron, not to the globin protein, so each hemoglobin carries up to four oxygen molecules. A single red cell holds about 300 million hemoglobin molecules, which is why one cell can carry about 1.2 billion oxygen molecules.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Bleeding", When to use a tourniquet
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 k78 · CMA I.B.9.a · 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · CPT 1M k37
preguntas.pregunta: Where is a tourniquet placed once direct pressure has failed on a bleeding arm?
opciones: Two to three inches (5 to 7.7 cm) above the wound, clear of the joint
Directly over the wound itself, on top of the soaked dressing
As close as possible to the armpit, no matter where the wound is
Below the wound, between the bleeding point and the fingertips
preguntas.explicacion: The tourniquet goes on the limb 2 to 3 inches above the wound and away from a joint; if the joint is in the way, it moves higher, toward the trunk. Padding or clothing under it keeps the skin from being pinched. The time it was applied is written down and passed to the responders, because a tourniquet left on too long injures nerves and tissue.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Introduction; Issues of Concern: Medical Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Distributive justice · CPT D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k212 · CMA II.E.4 · RMA I.C.4 · NCMA 4.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which ethical principle is at work when a limited supply of a treatment is spread fairly across the patients who need it?
opciones: Distributing resources equitably across the patients
Preserving the patient's life and their autonomy
Avoiding acts known to expose a patient to harm
Placing a high value on the dignity of the person
preguntas.explicacion: Four principles underpin patient rights: the dignity of the person is held high; the clinician works in good will toward the patient, above all to preserve life and autonomy; anything known to place the patient in harm's way, done or left undone, is avoided; and what there is gets shared out fairly among those who need it. That last one is what governs a scarce supply. A right to receive treatment is usually traced back to good will, the sanctity of life and that same distributive fairness.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Nasopharyngeal/Nasal Aspirate and Nasopharyngeal/Nasal Wash
preguntas.subtema: Nasal wash versus aspirate · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.C.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(c)
preguntas.pregunta: How does a nasopharyngeal wash differ from a nasopharyngeal aspirate?
opciones: Several drops of sterile saline go into each nostril first, and only then is suction applied
Several drops of sterile saline go into each nostril afterward, to rinse the suction catheter out
The catheter is passed to a shallower depth, stopping short of the turbinates on either side
The specimen is placed on slides and air dried, rather than into a viral transport medium tube
preguntas.explicacion: Both use a catheter on suction with the head tilted back 70 degrees, and both go in to a depth matching the distance from nostril to the outer opening of the ear. The wash differs in that sterile normal saline, several drops of it, goes into each nostril first. Gentle suction follows, the catheter turns as it comes out, and the specimen goes into viral transport medium.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Latex Allergies and Hospital Patients; and StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", section Etiology
preguntas.subtema: Bandaging and allergies · CPT D3 k73 · D2 k48 · PBT II.I II.J · CCMA 3E9 k137 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.13
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a latex allergy. Which items on a routine phlebotomy tray are likely to contain latex?
opciones: Gloves, tourniquets and elastic bandages or wraps
Gloves and alcohol swabs, but not the elastic band
Evacuated tubes and their stoppers, and the labels
Sharps containers and the plastic transport bags
preguntas.explicacion: Latex turns up throughout health care, most commonly in gloves, and the medical items listed alongside them include tourniquets and elastic bandages and wraps. A patient with this allergy needs latex-free substitutes for those items, and the whole team has to be told about the allergy.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1283(a), Standard: Test records
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F k92 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D5 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.3.b · CMA I.C.9.a
preguntas.pregunta: A clotted EDTA tube is rejected. Under the CLIA test records standard, what must the laboratory's record system contain about that specimen?
opciones: Its condition and what was done with it, since it did not meet the acceptability criteria
Only the date of receipt, because no test was performed on the specimen
The name and title of the person who collected it and the reason the collection attempt failed
Only its positive identification, because the condition of a rejected specimen is not a record element
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1283(a)(3) puts on the record system what became of specimens that fail the laboratory's acceptability criteria, their state and where they ended up, together with positive identification of every specimen, the date and time it was received, and the dates each test was run and by whom. Who collected it is not on that list, and rejected specimens are named in, not out.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", section Epidemiology
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 k49 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A child with spina bifida is scheduled for a blood draw. Why is latex a particular concern?
opciones: The prevalence of latex hypersensitivity in spina bifida is 20% to 65%
The prevalence in spina bifida is 1% to 2%, the same as the general population
Spina bifida causes a type IV reaction to the cornstarch in gloves
Children with spina bifida are routinely allergic to bananas and kiwi
preguntas.explicacion: Patients with spina bifida are a recognized high-risk group, with reported prevalence of latex hypersensitivity between 20% and 65%, probably because of repeated corrective surgeries and procedures; patients with repeated catheterization are also at raised risk. One to two percent is the general-population figure, and the fruit link is a separate risk marker, not a rule.

preguntas.fuente: HRSA, Newborn Screening Process, Blood Spot Screening
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4C k81 filter paper technique · PBT II.F technique, III.A.4
preguntas.pregunta: How is the baby's foot prepared for the newborn screening heel stick?
opciones: Gently warm the foot to increase blood flow; the baby may stay swaddled
Cool the foot briefly so the puncture is felt less; the baby must be unwrapped
Massage the heel firmly for one minute; the baby is held upright
Soak the foot in warm water for 10 minutes; the baby is laid flat and undressed
preguntas.explicacion: The baby stays swaddled through blood spot screening, and to ease the process the provider warms the foot gently to bring the blood up before the quick pinprick on the heel. No temperature and no duration are specified. For any capillary draw the infant is kept warm and wrapped with only the sampling limb out, and massaging or squeezing causes hemolysis.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 6.1.1 and 6.2.2 Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4B assisting with pediatric collection · PBT II.B age-specific needs · CCMA 3E1 prepare patient
preguntas.pregunta: A parent is present for their toddler's blood draw. How should the parent be involved?
opciones: Ask whether they would like to help hold the child; give full instructions if they do
Ask them to wait outside, since the WHO requires two trained phlebotomists per draw
Have them hold the child without instruction, since parents know their own child best
Ask them to hold the child only once the needle is in, to avoid passing on anxiety
preguntas.explicacion: The phlebotomist asks the parent whether they would like to help by holding the child. A parent who says yes gets full directions on how and where to hold; a parent who would rather not is replaced by a second phlebotomist. One person is the technician, the other holds the child still, and that helper is not optional.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(b); StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Selective Access
preguntas.subtema: Minimum necessary in practice · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k36
preguntas.pregunta: A billing clerk asks a phlebotomist for a patient's full medical history to process a claim. Which HIPAA standard is at stake?
opciones: Minimum necessary: limit the PHI to what the payment purpose requires
Right of access: the clerk may see all records that the patient could see herself
Treatment exception: payment staff are exempt from all limits
De-identification: the clerk must receive only coded data
preguntas.explicacion: Payment is a permitted purpose, yet it is not among the exceptions to the minimum necessary standard, so the entity has to make a reasonable effort to hold what the clerk receives down to what processing the claim requires. The treatment exception covers providers treating the patient, not billing. De-identified data would not serve payment, and the right of access belongs to the individual rather than to workforce members. The same principle turns up in guidance that access should match the employee's role, so a laboratory technologist sees laboratory records and not the whole history.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Lack of Patient Comprehension
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2M k43 · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which tools are recommended for checking whether a patient really understood the risks, benefits and alternatives?
opciones: The teach-back or test/feedback method
A signed consent form and a staff witness
A formal psychiatric competency evaluation
A reading-level check of the consent form
preguntas.explicacion: Teach-back or the test/feedback method can be used to assess understanding, and open-ended questions and encouraging questions make the dialogue interactive. It also notes that the emphasis on a signature as proof of understanding is being questioned, and that a psychiatrist is consulted only when capacity is in doubt.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Sputum Gram stain (003765), How to Prepare for the Test; MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Routine sputum culture (003723), How the Test will Feel; and MedlinePlus, Sputum Culture, Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?
preguntas.subtema: Sputum timing and hydration · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.3 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(4) · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A sputum culture is scheduled. Which two instructions help the patient produce a usable specimen?
opciones: Drink plenty of fluids the night before, and collect first thing in the morning
Drink plenty of fluids the night before, and collect right after the evening meal
Fast completely for 12 hours, and then collect first thing in the morning
Take an over-the-counter cough suppressant, and collect first thing in the morning
preguntas.explicacion: Fluids the night before make the airways produce more phlegm and the sputum easier to raise, and the test is more accurate done first thing in the morning, before eating or drinking. A 12-hour fast is the preparation for bronchoscopy, not for a coughed specimen, and suppressing the cough would defeat the collection. The provider may tap the chest or offer a salty mist to help.

preguntas.pregunta: Who may obtain a copy of an employee's bloodborne pathogens medical record?

Any supervisor in the department where the exposure incident took place
The source patient, who is entitled to the results of the exposed worker
The employee's union representative, in the same way as training records
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(1)(iii) keeps these records confidential and bars disclosing them, inside the workplace or outside it, unless the employee has given express written consent, or the standard or another law demands it. Paragraph (h)(3)(iii) then names who does get them: the employee, anyone holding that written consent, the Director of NIOSH and the Assistant Secretary of Labor. Employee representatives appear one paragraph earlier, in (h)(3)(ii), and only for training records.
