preguntas.pregunta: A serum sample from a patient with very high triglycerides is milky. Which analytes did the study by Calmarza and colleagues find clinically affected, and what can remove the interference?
opciones: Calcium, total protein, creatinine and phosphorus; ultracentrifugation of the sample
Potassium, LDH, AST and total bilirubin; dilution of the sample before analysis
Sodium, chloride and bicarbonate; refrigeration of the sample at 2 to 8 °C overnight
Glucose, urea and uric acid; filtering the sample through a serum separator gel
preguntas.explicacion: Lipemia from hypertriglyceridaemia interfered to a clinically significant degree with calcium, total protein, creatinine and phosphorus, and ultracentrifugation reduced or removed that interference; a later study found high-speed spinning in a micro-centrifuge a practical and cheaper substitute for several analytes. Potassium, LDH, AST and bilirubin make up the hemolysis set, not the lipemia one.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Glucose screening tests during pregnancy (007562), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Gestational OGTT sampling · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.G timed draws · CCMA 3E k139 timed specimens
preguntas.pregunta: How many blood samples does the 3-hour, 100 g gestational glucose tolerance test require, and when are they drawn?
opciones: Four: one before the drink and one every 60 minutes for 3 hours
Three: one before the drink and one every 60 minutes for 2 hours
Five: one before the drink and one every 30 minutes for 2 hours
Two: one before the drink and one at the end of the 3 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Blood is drawn before the 100 g drink and three more times, 60 minutes apart, so the appointment takes at least three hours and yields four values: fasting, 1 hour, 2 hours and 3 hours. The three-sample version is the one-step test, drawn fasting and every 60 minutes for two hours after a 75 g load. Nothing may be eaten during either test.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A processor holds a separated serum tube up to the light and records it as clear. Below roughly what free hemoglobin concentration will hemolysis escape the naked eye?
opciones: About 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, below which separated serum still looks normal
About 0.5 to 0.6 g/L, the level taken as significant interference at the bench
About 1.0 to 1.5 g/L, the level at which potassium begins to climb
About 0.05 to 0.1 g/L, roughly the detection limit of the analyser
preguntas.explicacion: Once the serum has been separated, hemolysis becomes visible at a free hemoglobin of about 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, while the concentration accepted as clinically significant interference is 0.5 g/L. A tube that looks clean can therefore already be carrying interference, which is the whole argument for measuring an index on the analyser instead of trusting the eye.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014), Which sampling container is preferable?
preguntas.subtema: Purpose of clean-catch · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 / V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the midstream clean-catch technique used instead of simply voiding into a cup?
opciones: To keep germs from the penis or vagina out of the sample, so contaminants and formed particles are minimized
To obtain the most concentrated urine of the day, which shows the kidneys' ability to concentrate
To bypass the urethra entirely, which is the only way to get a sample free of periurethral flora
To capture the first portion of the stream, where epithelial cells and leukocytes are most numerous
preguntas.explicacion: The clean-catch method exists to keep organisms from the vagina or the penis out of the urine. A multicentre comparison found first-voided samples carrying more epithelial cells, red cells and leukocytes than midstream ones, which is what confirmed midstream as the sample of choice. Concentration is the reason for a first-morning specimen, and bypassing the urethra describes suprapubic aspiration, not a voided sample.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(2)(i) and (c)(2)(ii), Exposure Determination
preguntas.subtema: Exposure determination · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: When the employer decides which jobs involve occupational exposure, how must protective equipment be treated?
opciones: Ignored: the determination is made as if no protective equipment were worn
Counted: a job is exposed only if PPE cannot fully block the anticipated contact
Counted: the determination lists the PPE provided and excludes tasks it covers
Deferred: PPE is assessed later, in the annual review of safer medical devices
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(2)(ii) has the exposure determination drawn up as though no protective equipment existed. What is being asked is whether contact with blood or OPIM is reasonably anticipated in that job, not whether gloves or a gown would stop it. That is why the lists in (c)(2)(i) are built from job classifications and tasks. The annual review in (c)(1)(iv) looks at technology and safer devices; it is no substitute for the determination.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Hematoma · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: As the needle is advanced, a swelling rises quickly at the site. What has most likely happened?
opciones: The needle went beyond the lumen of the vein and blood is pooling under the skin
The vein has collapsed under the vacuum of the tube and blood is backing up into it
The tourniquet has occluded the artery and the limb is becoming congested
The alcohol was not dry, and the irritated skin is swelling around the needle
preguntas.explicacion: Inserting the needle beyond the lumen of the vein causes a hematoma, the pooling of blood under the skin. A hematoma can also form when too little pressure is kept up during the draw and after it. A collapsed vein is not described in these sources, and wet alcohol raises contamination risk, not swelling.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory measuring its rate of misidentified samples wants a benchmark to judge itself against. Which figure marks optimum performance in the published specifications?
opciones: Under 0.4 % of samples misidentified
Under 2 % of samples misidentified
Under 0.01 % of samples misidentified
Under 5 % of samples misidentified
preguntas.explicacion: The preliminary quality specifications drawn from laboratories in Europe, the United States and the Asia-Pacific region place three figures at the optimum level: fewer than 0.4 % of samples misidentified, an average time under 50 minutes to communicate a critical result, and more than 96 % of critical results communicated at all. Laboratories already past those should aim higher.

preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: When several tubes are collected in one venipuncture, which tube is filled first?
opciones: The blood culture bottle
The light blue citrate tube
The non-additive tube
The gray fluoride tube
preguntas.explicacion: Tubes are filled in a fixed sequence so that the additive of one tube is not carried into the next. In the order the WHO reproduces from the United States laboratory standards consensus, the blood culture bottle is number 1 and the fluoride/oxalate tube is number 10, the last one used. Summarized in four groups, the same sequence runs sterile containers first, coagulation tubes next, plain and gel tubes after them, and the remaining additive tubes last. Color codes can differ between manufacturers, so the WHO tells you to check with the local laboratory.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 9: Address Language Differences, Assess language preferences
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA I.A.3 / 2027 A.3.c · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: How should a practice assess each patient's language needs?
opciones: Ask every patient which language they prefer to speak and to read, and record it
Ask patients how well they speak English, and note the answer in the record
Note the preferred language only for patients who visibly struggle to speak English
Infer the language from the patient's surname or country of birth on the form
preguntas.explicacion: Every patient is asked which language they prefer for speaking and which for reading, the answer goes into the medical record, and an 'I Speak' card is used where the patient cannot answer. The reason preference is asked rather than proficiency is spelled out: people lose their English when sick or frightened, and may be too embarrassed to admit that it is limited.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Blood Volume", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Blood volume · CPT D4 4E k83 volume requirements · PBT I.C blood composition
preguntas.pregunta: Roughly how much blood circulates in an average adult, and how is it divided?
opciones: About 5 liters, roughly 60% plasma and 40% red cells with the other cells
About 5 liters, roughly 40% plasma and 60% red cells with the other cells
About 3 liters, roughly 60% plasma and 40% red cells with the other cells
About 8 liters, roughly 50% plasma and 50% red cells with the other cells
preguntas.explicacion: Blood volume is all the fluid held at a given moment in the heart chambers, the arteries, the veins, the venules and the capillaries, and the average adult carries close to 5 liters of it. About 60% of that is plasma and about 40% erythrocytes, with leukocytes and platelets in the mix. How much there is depends on size and weight, which is why an estimate for one patient needs a formula, not an average.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(g)(2)(ii) and (g)(2)(iv), Information and Training
preguntas.subtema: Training frequency · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.e · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: When must bloodborne pathogens training be given to an employee with occupational exposure?
opciones: At initial assignment to exposure tasks and at least once a year afterward
At initial assignment only, with a refresher when an exposure incident occurs
Within 10 working days of hire and again whenever the sharps log is updated
Once every three years, matching the retention period for the training records
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(2)(ii) puts training at the moment the employee is first assigned to tasks that may bring exposure, and at least once a year after that; (g)(2)(iv) adds that each annual session must fall inside a year of the last one. An exposure incident triggers follow-up for the employee, not a training cycle. Ten working days is the vaccine deadline of (f)(2)(i), and three years is how long the training records are kept, not how often training happens.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 6
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A preanalytical slip makes a molecular test report a false negative in a patient with sepsis. What is named as the danger that follows?
opciones: Treatment the patient needs is delayed or withheld, which in sepsis can end in death
Treatment the patient does not need is started, with resistance among its later effects
The event has to go to the state health agency as a reportable laboratory incident
The report has to be corrected once the error surfaces, and the physician notified again
preguntas.explicacion: A falsely negative result endangers the patient because it delays or denies treatment that is appropriate and often life-saving, and holding antibiotics back in adults and children with sepsis can end in death. The mirror error, a false positive, exposes the patient to treatment nobody needed, resistance among its long-term effects. Both distort the disease reporting public health rests on.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Blood Alcohol Level, What happens during a blood alcohol test? and What do the results mean?
preguntas.subtema: Blood alcohol testing · CPT D4 4I k85 · PBT III.A.4 alcohol · PBT II.D patient preparation
preguntas.pregunta: For roughly how long after the last drink can a blood alcohol test still detect alcohol, and what preparation does the patient need?
opciones: About 12 hours, and no special preparation is needed
About 12 hours, and an 8-hour fast is needed beforehand
About 48 hours, and no special preparation is needed
About 3 hours, and the patient must avoid mouthwash first
preguntas.explicacion: A blood alcohol test can detect alcohol in the system for up to about 12 hours after the last drink, which is why the timing of the draw affects the accuracy of the result, and no special preparation is required of the patient. Hair testing shows use over a much longer period, and urine, saliva and sweat are the other matrices employers or legal officials sometimes use.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Health Topic: Patient Rights, Where can I get help; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Who Monitors; 45 CFR 164.530(d) and (g)
preguntas.subtema: Privacy complaints · CPT D1 k13 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: Where can a patient file a complaint about a violation of their health information privacy rights?
opciones: With the HHS Office for Civil Rights
With the state insurance oversight agency
With the hospital's patient advocate only
With the long-term care ombudsman office
preguntas.explicacion: The Office for Civil Rights, at the federal Department of Health and Human Services, takes complaints from people who believe their health information privacy rights were violated, or who were discriminated against in their medical care; it investigates, audits, and may pass criminal matters to the Department of Justice. Patient advocates, state health departments, insurance oversight agencies and long-term care ombudsman offices handle other kinds of problem. A covered entity must also run its own complaint process and may not retaliate against anyone who files.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, sections First Aid and DO NOT
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural complications · CPT D3 k69 k74 · D1 1M k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether the swollen bruise on the arm can be drained with a needle at home. What is the advice?
opciones: Do not drain it, and rest the bruised part rather than using it
Drain it only with a sterile lancet after cleaning the skin first
Drain it once the color has turned bluish, but not before that
Do not drain it, but keep exercising the arm to disperse the blood
preguntas.explicacion: The instructions are explicit: a bruise is not drained with a needle, the painful part is rested rather than worked, and pain and swelling are not ignored. What does help is ice wrapped in a clean towel and keeping the bruised area raised above heart level where that is possible.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Caring for Older Patients With Cognitive Impairment, Tips for communicating with a patient who has cognitive impairment
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 k49 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(6) / 2027 F.1.d(6) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with cognitive impairment hears you but does not understand the instruction. What should you do?
opciones: Rephrase the statement, without speaking any faster or louder
Repeat it word for word until it finally registers with him
Speak much louder, since hearing is usually the underlying problem
Ask the caregiver to answer so the visit stays on schedule
preguntas.explicacion: Where the patient can hear but does not understand, the clinician rephrases rather than repeats, and does not speak faster or louder. Tell the patient plainly that no one is judging their answers, and keep addressing the patient directly rather than only the caregiver.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Actinic Purpura", sections Introduction, Etiology and History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k49 age and physical condition, k48 variables · PBT II.I complications and considerations
preguntas.pregunta: A 78-year-old has large purple patches on the backs of both hands and forearms. What is this and what causes it?
opciones: Actinic (senile) purpura: sun-damaged, atrophic dermis lets capillaries rupture with minor trauma; it fades in 1 to 3 weeks
Thrombocytopenic purpura: a low platelet count lets blood leak from intact vessels, and it needs an urgent platelet transfusion
Vasculitis: inflamed vessel walls leak blood into the dermis; the patches are tender and last for several months
Medication bruising: anticoagulants thin the blood so that every venipuncture leaves a spreading hematoma
preguntas.explicacion: Actinic purpura, also called senile or Bateman purpura, consists of purpuric macules and patches on sun-exposed skin, most often the dorsal hands and extensor forearms of older adults, caused by dermal atrophy and vascular fragility so that minor trauma ruptures capillaries. The lesions are painless, without inflammation, and resolve in 1 to 3 weeks; about 30% of people aged 75 or older are affected.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Recommendations for Workers
preguntas.subtema: Planning disposal first · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which habit is recommended to workers so that a used needle never becomes a hazard in the room?
opciones: Plan how the needle will be handled and discarded before the procedure starts
Recap the needle with one hand until a container can be brought to the room
Set the used needle on the tray until the tubes have been labeled correctly
Carry the needle to the container at the end of the round of draws
preguntas.explicacion: The advice to workers is a short list: avoid needles wherever a safe alternative exists; help evaluate the safety devices and then use them; do not recap; before a procedure with needles starts, plan how they will be handled and disposed of; get them into the proper container promptly; report every injury without delay; point out hazards; and take part in training and in hepatitis B vaccination. Leaving a used sharp on a tray, or carrying it around, is exactly the delay this list exists to remove.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Combined Nasal and Throat Swab; and CDC, Information on Collection of Respiratory Specimens for Influenza Virus Testing, Outpatients
preguntas.subtema: Avoid the tongue · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.C.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.iii · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: A combined nasal and throat swab is being collected for influenza. Which area does the throat swab deliberately miss?
opciones: The tongue, while the posterior pharynx and the tonsillar areas are swabbed
The tonsillar areas, while the posterior pharynx and the tongue are both swabbed
The posterior pharynx, while the tonsillar areas and the tongue are swabbed
The soft palate, while the posterior pharynx and the tongue are swabbed
preguntas.explicacion: For the throat half of a combined specimen, a second dry polyester swab goes into the mouth and collects from the posterior pharynx and the tonsillar areas, and the instruction is to avoid the tongue. Its tip then goes into the same transport tube as the nasal swab and the applicator is cut off. Combining nasal and throat in one specimen detects influenza better than either alone.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C k42 · PBT II.A · CCMA 3E2 k124
preguntas.pregunta: Which set matches the identification data a center may record with each blood sample?
opciones: Ordering provider, patient's full name and DOB, address, collection date and time, and collector
Ordering provider, insurance plan, copayment collected, and the color of each tube drawn
Patient's full name, room number, bed location, and the nurse on duty at the time
Patient's full name and DOB, the test priority, and the date the results are due
preguntas.explicacion: Depending on the center's policy, the record may hold the identity of the provider who requested the tests, the patient's full name, middle name included, the date of birth and the full address, the sample's own identifying characteristics, the exact date and time of collection, and the identity of whoever drew it. Billing items and bed locations are not on that list.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Low blood sugar", Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.f · 2027 I.B.8.f · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15 · CPT 1M k37
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes becomes shaky, sweaty and confused while waiting, but can swallow and follow directions. What is offered?
opciones: Juice, a sugary drink or glucose tablets, and then the provider is told
An injection of glucagon into the muscle of the outer part of the thigh
A glass of water and a rest in a cool room until the shaking settles
No food or drink, because the glucose must be measured in the lab first
preguntas.explicacion: A patient who is awake and able to swallow is given fast sugar: juice or another sugary drink, food, or glucose tablets. Glucagon, a medicine that raises blood sugar, is the route when the patient cannot take sugar by mouth. If the signs do not improve after a snack with sugar, the patient goes to the emergency room and does not drive.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1241(d), Standard: Test request
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F k92 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E k146
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital laboratory uses the patient's electronic chart, rather than a separate form, as the test requisition. When is this acceptable under CLIA?
opciones: When the laboratory has the chart on hand while testing and can show it to CMS on request
When the ordering physician signs a paper copy of the chart entry within 30 days of the order
When the chart is used only for waived tests performed at the point of care
When the laboratory also keeps a duplicate paper requisition for every order
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1241(d) allows the patient's chart or medical record to serve as the requisition or authorization, on two conditions: it must be available to the laboratory when the test is performed and available to CMS or its agent upon request. No paper duplicate, signature deadline or restriction to waived testing is imposed; the 30-day rule concerns oral requests.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 5 Specimen processing
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5D k89 · PBT III.C
preguntas.pregunta: A specimen carrying a biosafety level 4 pathogen is being processed for a molecular test. Why is containment and thorough disinfection insisted on at that bench?
opciones: Because the organism may still be alive: the testing process does not necessarily inactivate it
Because the extraction reagents inactivate the organism only once amplification has finished
Because the amplicons the reaction produces are themselves infectious when a tube is opened
Because the process does inactivate the organism, so only the residue left behind carries risk
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratories handling biosafety level 3 and especially level 4 organisms work under strict engineering controls: ventilation that is separate or controlled, separate areas for transferring the sample, for extraction and for analysis, access limited to authorized staff, and full-body air-supplied suits. Containment and disinfection matter during processing because the organism may not be inactivated before the molecular test is run.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview of the Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", Sputum Specimens; and StatPearls, "Sputum Analysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Sputum for tuberculosis · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.B.3 / V.D.3 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(4) · RMA III.C.4.a.v
preguntas.pregunta: Tuberculosis is suspected. How does the sputum collection differ from a routine sputum culture?
opciones: A series of 3 early morning specimens of 8 to 10 mL is collected on separate days
A single early morning specimen of 8 to 10 mL is collected and sent the same day
A series of 3 specimens is collected 2 hours apart on the same morning and pooled
A series of 3 specimens is collected on separate days and kept at room temperature
preguntas.explicacion: For Mycobacterium tuberculosis a series of three early morning specimens of 8 to 10 mL each is collected on consecutive days, refrigerated and returned to the laboratory daily; the refrigerator is where each one waits, not the bench. A routine culture takes a single specimen sent in the same day. In an uncooperative patient the organism can also be recovered from gastric contents by stomach aspiration.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2E k41 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3A2 k43 · NCMA 2B.1 · CMA III.H.2.a / 2027 III.H.2.a patient verification
preguntas.pregunta: For admitted hospital patients, which set of identifiers is the widely accepted one to ask for and record before a draw?
opciones: Date of birth and first and last name, plus one extra identifier such as SSN or address
First and last name and room number, confirmed against the card on the bed
First and last name, read aloud by the phlebotomist for the patient to confirm
The ID bracelet number on its own, cross-checked against the laboratory form
preguntas.explicacion: Every admitted patient planned for phlebotomy carries an ID bracelet; name and date of birth are asked and recorded, and the accepted consensus is first and last name plus date of birth plus one extra general identifier, such as the social security number or the address. The WHO wants the patient to state the full name rather than confirm one read to them.

preguntas.pregunta: At what angle does the WHO guideline say the needle should enter the vein?
opciones: Swiftly, at 30 degrees or less, then along the vein at the easiest angle
At 30 degrees or more, steepening the angle as the needle advances along the vein
At 90 degrees, straight down, as when piercing a tube stopper directly from above
At 30 degrees or less, with the thumb anchoring the vein just ABOVE the puncture site
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 says to enter the vein swiftly at an angle of 30 degrees or less and then keep advancing the needle along the vein at whatever angle gives the easiest entry: the angle does not steepen. The step pairs this with anchoring the vein first, holding the patient's arm with a thumb placed BELOW the puncture site, not above it, and asking the patient to make a fist so the veins stand out. Piercing straight down from above is how Step 7 fills a tube through its stopper, not how the needle enters a vein.

preguntas.pregunta: How often may a healthy donor give whole blood, and what changes after a double red cell collection?
opciones: Once in 8 weeks, extended to 16 weeks after a double red cell collection
Once in 8 weeks, extended to 24 weeks after a double red cell collection
Once in 4 weeks, extended to 8 weeks after a double red cell collection
Once in 16 weeks, shortened to 8 weeks after a double red cell collection
preguntas.explicacion: No more than one donation in any 8 weeks, which blood centers count as 56 days, for a single unit of whole blood or red cells; after an apheresis collection that yields two units of red cells the wait is 16 weeks. Even 56 days may not rebuild the iron lost, part of why repeat donors get deferred for low hemoglobin.

preguntas.pregunta: A 5-month-old infant who weighs 6 kg needs a capillary blood sample. Where is the lancet placed?
opciones: On the medial or lateral plantar surface of the infant's heel
On the side of the middle or ring finger, across the print
On the posterior curve of the heel, where the tissue is deepest
On the great toe, which has more tissue over bone than the heel
preguntas.explicacion: The capillary site is chosen by age and weight: heel-prick from birth to about 6 months and roughly 3 to 10 kg, finger-prick over 6 months and above 10 kg. On the heel the lancet goes on the medial or lateral plantar surface. In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance is 3.32 mm there, only 2.33 mm at the posterior heel, which is to be avoided, and 2.19 mm at the toe.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's veins are small and hard to see. Which measures can improve the chance of success before the puncture?
opciones: Tapping the skin over the vein and applying a warm compress or briefly soaking the limb in warm water
Applying an ice pack for up to 15 minutes each hour so the vein wall becomes firmer
Keeping the tourniquet in place for two to three minutes so the veins fill completely
Asking the patient to fast for 12 hours and avoid alcohol for 24 hours before the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Measures that help include ballotting or tapping the skin over the vein, then the antiseptic preparation, and a warm compress or a brief soak of the limb in warm water, along with good positioning and lighting. Ice is first aid for a bruise, a two-to-three-minute tourniquet exceeds both the WHO and StatPearls limits, and the fasting rules concern the tests, not vein visibility.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient brings in a 24-hour urine container that he kept on the kitchen counter for the whole collection day. What was wrong?
opciones: The container should have been kept refrigerated or in a cool place throughout the collection period
The container should have been kept frozen, since freezing preserves urine better than refrigeration
The urine should have been carried to the laboratory after each void instead of being pooled at home
The container should have been kept at body temperature and delivered within 30 minutes of the last void
preguntas.explicacion: During a 24-hour collection the capped container stays in the refrigerator or a cool place, and the sample is kept refrigerated throughout the period; a preservative may be added by the laboratory to stabilize it. Freezing is not an accepted replacement for refrigeration in urine preservation, the urine is pooled at home rather than delivered void by void, and body-temperature delivery within 30 minutes is the semen instruction.

preguntas.pregunta: In which situation is the ear lobe used as a capillary sampling site?
opciones: Rarely, in mass screening or research studies
Routinely, as the preferred adult capillary site
In neonates, as the alternative to the heel
In children who walk and have callused feet
preguntas.explicacion: Capillary blood comes from a finger, a heel or, now and then, an ear lobe. In adults the finger is the usual choice; the sides of the heel belong to babies and small children; and the ear lobe turns up mainly in mass screening work or in research. The AAMA outline names those same three sites for dermal puncture.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is about to take a breath alcohol test and has just finished a cigarette. What waiting rule applies?
opciones: Wait 1 minute after smoking, and 15 minutes after an alcoholic drink
Wait 15 minutes after smoking, and 1 minute after an alcoholic drink
Wait 15 minutes after smoking, and 15 minutes after an alcoholic drink
Wait 2 hours after smoking, as for a hydrogen breath test
preguntas.explicacion: The instruction is to let 15 minutes pass after any alcoholic drink, and 1 minute after a cigarette, before the breath test begins; the alcohol in exhaled air mirrors the alcohol in blood accurately, so mouth alcohol has to clear first. Two hours without smoking is a condition of hydrogen breath testing for lactose, a different test with a different reason behind the rule.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient denies any latex allergy but says bananas and avocados make her mouth itch. How should that be handled?
opciones: Treat her as at risk for a latex reaction and ask further before using latex items
Fruit allergies are unrelated to latex; proceed with the standard latex gloves
Only a chestnut allergy is linked with latex, so no precaution is needed here
She must have a skin prick test for latex before any draw can take place
preguntas.explicacion: Some people with latex allergy also react to foods whose proteins resemble those in latex, the latex-fruit syndrome; bananas, avocado and chestnuts are the most strongly linked, with kiwi, peaches, nectarines, celery and melons less so, and the association runs in both directions. Skin prick testing for latex is not available in the United States for lack of an approved reagent.

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn needs a heel-prick. Which antiseptic does the WHO say must NOT be used for a skin puncture in a newborn or a small child?
opciones: Povidone iodine
70% isopropyl alcohol
Chlorhexidine
Soap and water
preguntas.explicacion: Chapter 7 states plainly that povidone iodine is not for a capillary skin puncture in a pediatric or a neonatal patient and that alcohol is used instead, as in the adult instructions. For adults, Step 5 already prefers 70% alcohol over iodine because of its effect on potassium, phosphorus and uric acid results. Soap and water is the WHO's hand hygiene method, not a skin antiseptic for the puncture site.

preguntas.pregunta: A portable hemoglobin analyzer is carried from the clinic to a community screening event. Before the first patient there, what does the pretesting checklist recommend?
opciones: Perform control testing or a calibration check after moving it, even if the manufacturer does not require it
No extra step; a waived analyzer needs controls only with each new lot or shipment, wherever it is used
Recalibrate it at the event using a patient sample of known value brought along from the clinic
Run it for 30 minutes without samples at the event so its internal temperature stabilizes
preguntas.explicacion: Portable equipment that has been moved may give inaccurate results, so the checklist advises verifying proper function with control testing or a calibration check after the move, even when the current manufacturer's instructions do not demand it. Calibration checks in general follow the insert, and equipment and electrical connections are inspected before use. Patient samples are not calibration materials.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic laboratory forwards a specialized assay to a distant laboratory and passes the result on to the ordering physician. What else must the referring laboratory tell that physician?
opciones: The name and address of the laboratory that actually performed the test
The reason the assay could not be performed on its own premises
The date on which the specimen was dispatched to the other laboratory
The name of the courier service that carried the specimen there
preguntas.explicacion: When specimens are referred, three rules apply at once: the referring laboratory may not revise the results or their interpretation, it may let the testing laboratory report straight to the ordering person provided it can produce an exact duplicate of that report, and it must tell whoever ordered the test the name and address of every laboratory location where the testing was done.

preguntas.subtema: Fill level · CPT D3 k9 k51 k59 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: An ESR tube is filled only two thirds of the way. What effect does the short fill have on the reading?
opciones: Air bubbles are introduced and the measured value comes out higher
Air bubbles are introduced and the measured value comes out lower
The citrate is diluted and the red cells stop stacking altogether
The plasma layer disappears and no reading at all can be taken
preguntas.explicacion: Filling the tube inadequately lets air bubbles into the column, and that raises the value measured. It sits alongside the other physical faults that push the reading up: a tilted tube and vibration. Delay in testing works the other way and lowers the result.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient admits she ate a biscuit two hours ago before a fasting panel. What does the guidance say happens next?
opciones: She tells the provider, and the test may be rescheduled for another time
She waits in the department for two more hours and is then drawn
She is drawn now, and the result is reported with a comment on diet
She is drawn now, since one biscuit adds no sugar to the bloodstream
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are told to say so if they ate or drank before the test, and that it may need to be rescheduled for a time when they can fast, so the results come out accurate. Eating and drinking are listed among the common factors that affect accuracy, since the bloodstream takes up sugar, fat and protein from whatever is consumed.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient describes himself as 'queer'. May staff use that word to describe him?
opciones: Follow the patient's lead, but staff should not use such terms to describe him
Use the same word in the chart, since the patient chose it himself
Correct the patient and suggest the clinical term 'homosexual' instead
Avoid noting any description of the patient's orientation in the record
preguntas.explicacion: Members of the LGBTQ community may use words like queer or gay for themselves, but the same words are considered derogatory when a provider uses them to describe a patient; staff listen, follow the patient's lead, and ask how the patient and partner should be described, then record the agreed terms. 'Homosexual' is listed as a term that has been replaced.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with no insurance arrives at an emergency department in crisis. Which federal law applies?
opciones: The one requiring an attempt to stabilize, whatever the ability to pay
The one requiring a written estimate before any care is given
The one requiring transfer to a public hospital within the hour
The one requiring the plan to be billed before treatment begins
preguntas.explicacion: The Emergency Medical Treatment and Active Labor Act, passed inside a budget reconciliation law, obliges an organization that devotes at least a third of its services to emergency care to attempt to stabilize an emergency condition whether or not the person is able to pay for it. It exists because patients known or suspected to be unable to pay were being turned away. What counts as an emergency, and when a patient is stable enough to stop, is left to each organization to interpret.

preguntas.subtema: Labeling · CPT D3 3R k22 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: A coagulation specimen is about to leave the ward. Which details are required on the tube and on the request slip?
opciones: The name, a medical record number or birth date, the date drawn and the specimen source
Name, insurance policy number, ordering clinic and the room where blood was drawn
Name and medical record number only, since the laboratory time-stamps arrival itself
Name, date of birth and the phlebotomist's initials, with no need for the collection date
preguntas.explicacion: Results depend on specimen quality, and the labeling asked for on both the tube and the slip is the patient's name, the medical record number or date of birth, the date of collection and, where it applies, the source of the specimen. Arrival time in the laboratory does not replace those fields.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a central venous catheter is suspected of having a catheter-associated bloodstream infection. How should the blood cultures be obtained?
opciones: One set by peripheral venipuncture and one set through the catheter
Only through the catheter, since that is where the infection is suspected
Only by peripheral venipuncture, because catheters are never used for cultures
Two sets through the catheter, one from each lumen
preguntas.explicacion: Peripherally drawn cultures are preferred over catheter-drawn ones because they are contaminated less often, with one exception: when a catheter-associated bloodstream infection is suspected, both a peripheral draw and a catheter draw are indicated. Drawing only from the catheter loses the comparison, and ruling catheters out altogether ignores the exception the CDC states.

preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E k125 k128 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for fasting blood work asks the phlebotomist whether to skip the morning blood-pressure pill. What is the right guidance?
opciones: Take usual medicines unless the provider said to stop, and tell the provider of every medicine, vitamin and supplement
Skip all medicines on the morning of a fasting test, since swallowing any pill counts as breaking the fast
Take prescription medicines but stop vitamins and supplements, which are the only products that alter results
Take the pill only if it can be swallowed without water, because liquids are not allowed during the fast
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are told to ask their provider whether the prescription and over-the-counter medicines they take may be continued, and never to stop one unless the provider says so; for certain tests the provider will have them hold a drug, and that call is not the phlebotomist's. Vitamins and supplements get reported too, since a medicine can push blood glucose up or down and change a result drawn too soon after a dose. Plain water is allowed all through the fast.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.3 Modes of Disease Transmission, Healthcare-Associated (Nosocomial) Infections
preguntas.subtema: Nosocomial infections · CPT D1 1K k11 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C k98 · CMA I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: For an infection to be classified as healthcare-associated (nosocomial), which condition must be met?
opciones: The patient was admitted for a reason other than that infection
The infection was acquired from a healthcare worker rather than from equipment
The infection appeared within 24 hours of admission to the facility
The infection is caused by a multidrug-resistant organism
preguntas.explicacion: A healthcare-associated infection is one picked up inside a health-care facility, and what defines it is that the patient was admitted for some other reason. They are often tied to surgery or to invasive procedures that open a portal of entry, and to contaminated equipment such as catheters and ventilators; in 2011 more than 720,000 occurred in U.S. hospitals, surgical sites and pneumonia accounting for about 22 percent each. The source may be equipment, staff or the environment, the organism need not be resistant, and the definition sets no 24-hour cutoff.

preguntas.pregunta: Which disadvantage of the evacuated tube system arises after the draw rather than during it?
opciones: Reusing the tube holder risks a needle-stick while it is taken apart
Reusing the tube holder risks a hemolyzed specimen in the next tube

preguntas.explicacion: Among the drawbacks listed for vacuum systems is that reuse of the needle holder creates a needle-stick risk during disassembly, which happens once the blood is already drawn. Skill in use, mixing components from different makers and higher cost are the other entries on that list.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 k78 · CMA I.B.9.a · 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 15 · CPT 1M k37
preguntas.pregunta: Blood soaks through the gauze being held on a bleeding wound. What should be done?
opciones: Lay another cloth over the first one and keep up the pressure
Lift the gauze to look at the wound and then press again harder
Replace the soaked gauze with dry gauze and press on the artery
Loosen the pressure for a moment so that a clot can start to form
preguntas.explicacion: A soaked dressing is not taken off: another one is placed on top and pressure continues until bleeding stops, and then the dressing is wrapped firmly in place. Peeking disturbs the wound and makes control harder. Bleeding that keeps seeping through calls for medical attention right away.

preguntas.pregunta: A barcode scanner at the accessioning desk misreads a patient identification label. What did the emergency laboratory identify as the cause of such misreads?
opciones: A mismatch between the scanner settings and the print area size or symbology of the barcode on the wristband
Barcodes printed more than 30 minutes before collection, which fade beyond the reading threshold of the scanner
Labels printed with more than two identifiers, which overload the nine-digit internal code the scanner expects
Heat from the centrifuge, which distorts the code 39 bars so that the digits no longer match the record
preguntas.explicacion: Barcoding carries an evidence-based recommendation behind it, since it cuts identification errors in specimens and in testing, yet this laboratory still saw scanners misread patient barcodes when the symbology or the print area on a wristband or specimen label did not match the scanner's settings. Its own nine-digit code 39 barcode carries name, sex, age, tube and sample type, print and collection times, collection site, the tests, the ordering doctor and the phlebotomist.

preguntas.pregunta: A used needle really has to come off its syringe. How is the one-hand scoop performed?

Hold the cap in one hand and push the needle into it with the other hand
Pinch the cap between two fingers and twist the syringe until it is covered

preguntas.pregunta: How much blood should one adult blood culture set contain per venipuncture, according to the CDC?

40 to 60 mL, which requires four bottles in all

preguntas.explicacion: An adult set should hold 20 to 30 mL of blood collected by venipuncture, and depending on the culture system and the institution's policy that can take more than two bottles. preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urea Breath Test", Procedures (Urea Breath Test)
preguntas.subtema: UBT medication holds · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.C.3 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient on omeprazole and a recent course of antibiotics is booked for a urea breath test. What has to happen first?
opciones: Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 4 weeks and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 2 weeks
Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 2 weeks and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 4 full weeks
Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 4 days and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 2 days
Only the antibiotic has to stop, for 4 weeks; acid suppressants do not interfere
preguntas.explicacion: Antibiotics and bismuth compounds are stopped at least 4 weeks ahead, and proton pump inhibitors and sucralfate at least 2 weeks ahead, because all of them suppress the urease activity the test measures and produce a false negative. Histamine-2 blockers are ideally held 24 to 48 hours beforehand. Plain antacids are allowed and do not interfere.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5: Disinfect the entry site
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation · CPT D3 3G k63 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E5 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: After cleaning the site, a phlebotomist palpates the vein once more with a gloved finger to confirm its position. What does the WHO require now?
opciones: Repeat the disinfection, because the cleaned site was touched
Proceed at once, since the glove was clean and the alcohol has dried
Wipe the fingerprint with dry gauze and proceed without delay
Apply povidone iodine over the alcohol before inserting the needle
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 says not to touch the cleaned site and, in particular, not to place a finger over the vein to guide the exposed needle; if the site is touched, the disinfection is repeated. A clean glove does not change the rule. The same step prefers alcohol to povidone iodine, which can falsely raise potassium, phosphorus or uric acid results.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, key communication tips and Families and caregivers
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k40 patient communication, k49 age considerations · PBT II.B age-specific needs
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist greets an 80-year-old as 'dear' and starts explaining quickly. Which recommendations for older patients does this ignore?
opciones: Use formal address such as Mr. or Ms. unless told otherwise, and do not hurry the patient
Use first names to build trust, and keep the explanation brief so as not to overload them
Address the accompanying relative first, since older patients defer to their family
Use medical terminology, since older patients expect a professional register from staff
preguntas.explicacion: Speak to the patient as a fellow adult, defaulting to formal terms such as Mr. or Ms. and avoiding familiar words like 'dear', which can be perceived as disrespectful. Do not hurry: speak more slowly, do not interrupt, and use plain language rather than medical terminology. A companion's role is checked with the patient first, to protect privacy.

opciones: A black symbol on a white background inside a red square frame set on a point
A black symbol on a fluorescent orange background with the legend BIOHAZARD
A red symbol on a white background inside a black diamond used for transport
A black symbol inside a red square frame that may be left empty as a design element
preguntas.explicacion: A pictogram on a shipped container is a red square frame standing on one point, with a black symbol for the hazard set on white inside it, drawn wide enough to be seen clearly. A red frame left empty, with no symbol in it, is not a pictogram and has no place on the label. The fluorescent orange label carrying the BIOHAZARD legend belongs to the bloodborne pathogens standard, and the diamond-shaped transport labels are what the Department of Transportation requires for shipping, which the OSHA pictograms do not replace.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling; and "Prothrombin Time", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k59 k9 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A new phlebotomist shakes a filled citrate tube hard to be sure the blood mixes. What is the consequence?
opciones: Frothing or hemolysis that makes the coagulation results inaccurate
Small clots in the tube, the result the review links to under-mixing
A rise in the citrate-to-blood ratio, as happens with a short draw
Loss of the vacuum, so the next tube in the sequence will not fill
preguntas.explicacion: Both the coagulopathies review and the prothrombin time chapter say the citrate tube is inverted gently and never shaken, because vigorous agitation causes frothing or hemolysis and the coagulation results become unreliable. Small clots are the opposite problem, inefficient mixing, in the tube collection review; the citrate ratio changes with underfilling, not with shaking.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(iv)(A) and (d)(3)(iv), Laundry and PPE
preguntas.subtema: Contaminated laundry · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.6.a / 2027 I.B.5.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A lab coat is soaked with blood after a difficult draw. How do the standard's laundry rules apply?
opciones: Bag it where it was used, without sorting or rinsing, in a container that prevents soak-through
Rinse it in the nearest sink first, then bag it, so the laundry service is not exposed
Take it home to wash separately, since the employer is not responsible for laundering
Sort it with other soiled coats at the laundry, where staff wear gloves and gowns
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(iv)(A) requires contaminated laundry to be handled as little as possible and with minimal agitation, bagged or containerized at the location of use, and never sorted or rinsed there; when it is wet enough to soak through, the bag or container must prevent leakage to the outside. The employer, not the employee, cleans and launders required PPE at no cost under (d)(3)(iv), so taking the coat home is not an option, and the gloves worn by laundry staff under (d)(4)(iv)(B) do not permit sorting at the point of use.

preguntas.pregunta: How should the lancet be oriented on the fingertip in a capillary puncture?
opciones: On the side of the finger pad, crossing the fingerprint lines at a right angle
On the center of the fingertip pad, running along the fingerprint lines
On the side of the finger pad, running along the fingerprint lines instead
Over the very tip of the finger next to the nail, at a right angle to the nail bed
preguntas.explicacion: A finger puncture is made on the side of the pad, with the lancet crossing the print lines instead of following them; on the heel the spot is the medial or lateral plantar surface. One quick, firm stroke carried through gives a flow good enough that the patient need not be stuck again.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fasting", section Issues of Concern; and MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, How long do I have to fast before the test?

preguntas.pregunta: A patient fasting since midnight reports a dull headache. Which mechanisms are proposed for it?
opciones: Low blood sugar, dehydration and caffeine withdrawal
Low blood sugar, high potassium and a raised cortisol
Dehydration, low iron stores and a raised cortisol
Caffeine withdrawal, high potassium and low iron stores
preguntas.explicacion: A tension-type headache is described as a notable effect at the beginning of a fast. Its precise cause has not been identified, and the mechanisms proposed for it are hypoglycaemia, dehydration and caffeine withdrawal. That is one more reason a fasting draw is scheduled early in the morning, so most of the fasting time passes during sleep.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Location of the Heart; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Structure of the Heart
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the heart sit in the body?
opciones: In the mediastinum between the lungs, with the apex pointing to the left
In the mediastinum, with two thirds of its mass to the right of the midline
In the left pleural cavity behind the sternum, with the apex pointing right
In the pericardial cavity below the diaphragm, at the level of the third rib
preguntas.explicacion: The heart lies in the chest between the two lungs, in the space called the mediastinum, wrapped in its own pericardial sac; the base reaches the level of the third costal cartilage and the apex points a little to the left of the sternum, between the fourth and fifth ribs, with roughly two thirds of the mass left of the midline. That position decides where the stethoscope goes.

preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: The superficial veins on the back of the hand arise from which structure, and where do they drain?
opciones: From the dorsal venous arch, into the cephalic and basilic veins
From the dorsal venous arch, into the radial and ulnar deep veins
From the deep palmar arch, into the cephalic and basilic veins
From the median cubital vein, into the dorsal venous arch below it
preguntas.explicacion: On the dorsum of the hand the superficial veins spring from the dorsal venous arch, which drains into the cephalic and the basilic, the two main superficial channels of the limb. The palmar arches belong to the deep system and drain into the ulnar and radial veins instead.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: Labeling · CPT D3 3R k22 · D2 2E k41 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: Beyond first and last name and date of birth, which further identifier is described as accepted for matching a patient to a specimen?
opciones: The social security number or the patient's address
The name of the insurance plan covering the visit
The color of the identification bracelet in use
The number of the room where the draw took place
preguntas.explicacion: Identification is built on the patient's first and last name and date of birth plus one further general identifier, and the examples given are the social security number or the address. Extra data of that kind lowers the risk of preventable error, which is why more than one item is used.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.3, footnote b
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k57 k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic decides that stopper color alone will tell staff in what sequence to fill tubes. What problem remains?
opciones: The sequence still has to be followed; color by itself does not enforce it
Stopper colors are identical between manufacturers, so the risk is covered
Color tells the phlebotomist how many inversions each tube will need
Color identifies the additive, so carry-over between tubes cannot happen
preguntas.explicacion: Color coding makes the tubes easy to tell apart, but an incorrect collection still follows when the sequence is not respected, which is why training matters. Color codes can also differ from one laboratory to another, so they should be checked locally rather than assumed.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(xii), Personal Protective Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Caps and shoe covers · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Surgical caps or hoods and shoe covers are required by the standard in which situation?
opciones: Where gross contamination is reasonably anticipated, autopsies for instance
When a patient is uncooperative and may pull away during the venipuncture
Whenever blood may splash onto the face during a routine venipuncture
Whenever a patient is on Contact Precautions for a resistant organism
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(xii) reserves caps, hoods, shoe covers and boots for situations where gross contamination is reasonably anticipated, and gives autopsies and orthopedic surgery as the examples. An uncooperative patient is the example the standard uses in (d)(3)(ix)(D)(4)(ii) for when a blood donation center must require gloves; splashes to the face trigger masks and eye protection under (d)(3)(x); and Contact Precautions call for gown and gloves under the CDC recommendations, not for head or shoe covering.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 8: Draw samples in the correct order
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A trainee asks why the tubes cannot simply be filled in whatever order is convenient. What reason does the WHO give in Step 8 for a fixed order of draw?
opciones: It prevents the additive in one tube from being carried over into the next tube
It ensures the tubes that need a full draw are filled while the tourniquet is still on
It gives the serum tubes 10 to 15 minutes to clot before the last tube is filled
It minimizes platelet clumping, which is the reason given for the capillary sequence
preguntas.explicacion: Step 8 states the purpose in one line: draw the tubes in the right order so that additives are not carried across from one tube to the next. The clotting time of 10 to 15 minutes is a processing detail for red tubes, not a reason for the order; and platelet clumping is the reason Chapter 7 gives for the reversed skin-puncture order, not for venipuncture.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: The same hospital had earlier published rejection figures for its routine core laboratory rather than the emergency one. Which reason topped that list?
opciones: Clotted specimens, followed by inadequate volume
Hemolysed specimens, followed by clotted ones
Misidentified specimens, followed by lipemic ones
Improper containers, followed by delayed transport
preguntas.explicacion: In the core laboratory clotted specimens accounted for 55.8 % of all rejections and inadequate volume for 29.3 %, a pattern the authors read as much like what the emergency laboratory saw. Most of those clotted tubes came from adult inpatient services, 54.3 %, and then from pediatric inpatient services, 26.8 %, which aims the training effort at the wards rather than at the laboratory.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Does Pneumatic Tube System Transport Contribute to Hemolysis in ED Blood Samples?" (West J Emerg Med 2016, PMC5017839), Introduction and Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: An emergency department reports that 15 % of its blood samples are hemolysed. How does that compare with published figures?
opciones: It sits inside the 6 to 30 % range reported for emergency departments, far above the 2 % ASCP benchmark
It is below the 20 % benchmark set by the ASCP for samples drawn during intravenous placement
It is unusually high, since emergency departments typically report hemolysis in fewer than 3 % of samples
It matches the 13 to 14 % rate expected for any sample sent through a pneumatic tube system
preguntas.explicacion: The American Society for Clinical Pathology sets 2 % as the benchmark, yet blood drawn in the emergency department hemolyses at 6 to 30 %; in the pneumatic tube study the ED figure was about 13.5 % against roughly 3 % elsewhere in the hospital, a gap the authors trace to blood taken during IV placement instead of by straight stick. The 13 to 14 % figure was that hospital's rate, not something the tube system caused.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 lancet depth · PBT II.J lancets · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.5 equipment for the test ordered
preguntas.pregunta: When preparing a lancing device for a fingerstick glucose test, what depth setting is advised?
opciones: No deeper than 2.0 mm, so the tip cannot reach and injure bone
No deeper than 3.0 mm, so the tip cannot reach and injure bone
At least 2.4 mm, to guarantee a drop large enough for the strip
The deepest setting on the first finger, then shallower on repeats
preguntas.explicacion: For a capillary glucose reading the device is set no deeper than 2.0 mm, which keeps the tip clear of bone; newer lancing devices also hurt less than the older systems. A modern meter runs on 0.3 to 1 microlitre, so there is nothing to gain from a deep stick. For finger punctures in general the ceiling is 2.4 mm.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F.3 Specimen shipping, DOT Category B · CPT D5 k89 handling and transportation
preguntas.pregunta: A liquid Category B specimen is being packed for shipment. Where does the absorbent material go, and how much is needed?
opciones: Between primary receptacle and secondary packaging, enough to absorb all of it
Between secondary packaging and outer box, enough to absorb the whole contents
Between primary receptacle and secondary packaging, enough to absorb about half
Inside the primary receptacle alongside the specimen, enough to absorb the whole contents
preguntas.explicacion: For liquids both the primary receptacle and the secondary must be leakproof, with absorbent material between them in a quantity able to take up everything the primary receptacles hold, without spoiling the cushioning or the outer packaging. Several fragile primary receptacles in one secondary have to be wrapped or separated. Ice and dry ice ride outside the secondary, or else in an overpack.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(1)(ii) and (h)(1)(iv), Medical Records
preguntas.subtema: Employee medical record retention · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: How long must an employer keep the medical record it maintains for a phlebotomist with occupational exposure?
opciones: For the duration of employment plus 30 years
For 3 years from the date of the last entry
For 6 years from the date of the last entry
For the duration of employment plus 5 years
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(1)(iv) requires the records of paragraph (h) to be kept at least for the length of employment plus 30 years, following 29 CFR 1910.1020. The record itself holds the employee's name, hepatitis B vaccination status and dates, results of examinations and follow-up, the employer's copy of the written opinion and the information sent to the healthcare professional. Three years is the retention of training records in (h)(2)(ii); six years is the HIPAA documentation period in 45 CFR 164.530(j), a different regulation.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Thrombocytopenia", section Evaluation (peripheral smear and pseudothrombocytopenia)
preguntas.subtema: Additives and pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k57 k9 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A CBC drawn in EDTA reports a very low platelet count, but the smear shows the platelets stuck together in clumps. What is this called, and what causes it?
opciones: Pseudothrombocytopenia, from in vitro platelet clumping caused by EDTA-dependent agglutinins
True thrombocytopenia, from platelet destruction that had already begun before the blood was drawn
Hemoconcentration, from a tourniquet left in place for more than one minute
Platelet satellitism, from the sodium fluoride in a gray tube drawn before the EDTA
preguntas.explicacion: Platelet clumping can occur when EDTA is the anticoagulant, producing pseudothrombocytopenia, a falsely low count due to in vitro aggregation from EDTA-dependent agglutinins. It is an artifact of the tube, not a disease of the patient. Platelet satellitism is a different smear finding, and hemoconcentration is the tourniquet effect described in the phlebotomy chapter.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 6.2.2 and 7.2.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4B assisting with pediatric collection · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E8 k130 wrapping · NCMA 2C.10
preguntas.pregunta: Blood is flowing poorly from a heel-prick in a cold, fussy infant. Which measure improves flow?
opciones: Keep the child warm and swaddled, with only the sampling limb bare; warmth can raise flow sevenfold
Lower the heel well below the level of the heart for two minutes so gravity fills the capillary bed
Squeeze the heel rhythmically at the puncture itself until a steady stream of blood appears there
Switch to a 25-gauge butterfly on the dorsal hand, which the WHO prefers when a heel-prick fails
preguntas.explicacion: The baby is kept warm: as few clothes off as possible, wrapped in a blanket, held by a parent with only the limb being sampled left out, and warm cloths on the site. Warmth can multiply the flow by as much as seven. Squeezing hemolyses the sample, and needles of 25 gauge or finer are the ones to keep away from.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, footnote d
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is worried that tissue fluid from a difficult puncture could contaminate a coagulation specimen. What does the WHO table allow in that situation?
opciones: Collecting a non-additive tube before the light blue citrate tube
Collecting the light blue tube first and then a second one for the test
Collecting a purple EDTA tube before the light blue citrate tube
Collecting the citrate tube last, after all the additive tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Footnote d of Table 2.3 addresses this exact worry: if tissue fluid or thromboplastin could contaminate the specimen, a tube without additive can be drawn ahead of the additive tube. That keeps the sequence of the table intact, because the plain tube is position 2 and citrate is position 3. EDTA is far down the list at position 8, and citrate never moves to the end.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 2 and section 5
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A sputum specimen for molecular bacterial testing is too thick to pipette and cannot be run today. Which pair of handling points applies?
opciones: Thin it with acetylcysteine or dithiothreitol; hold it at 4 to 8 °C for up to a week
Thin it with sterile saline; hold it at room temperature for up to a week
Thin it with acetylcysteine or dithiothreitol; freeze it at −20 °C the same day
Thin it with buffered glycerol; hold it at 4 to 8 °C for up to three days
preguntas.explicacion: Sputum is one of the viscous specimen types that jam automated pipetting, and the additives named for it are N-acetyl l-cysteine and dithiothreitol; homogenisation with inert beads in sterile buffer is the physical alternative. For storage the general guideline is 4 to 8 °C for up to seven days, with below −70 °C reserved for keeping it as long as twelve months.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.1 Structure and Function of Blood Vessels, Table 20.2 Comparison of Arteries and Veins; and 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Pulse
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 k7 (applied D3 k61 palpation, k62) · PBT I.A.2 I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: While palpating for a venipuncture site you feel a vessel that pulses. Which set of features identifies an artery rather than a vein?
opciones: Thick wall, small rounded lumen, high pressure, no valves
Thin wall, large flattened lumen, low pressure, valves in the limbs
Thin wall, large lumen, high pressure, valves present in the limbs
Thick wall, small lumen, low pressure, valves present in the limbs
preguntas.explicacion: Arteries have thick walls, a rounded appearance, high pressure and no valves; veins have thin walls, irregular often collapsed lumens, low pressure and valves, mostly in the limbs and below the heart. The pulse itself is the expansion and recoil of an artery as blood is ejected from the heart, so a pulsing vessel is an artery.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Examples of Safety Device Designs
preguntas.subtema: Self-blunting needles · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: How does a self-blunting phlebotomy needle protect the person drawing the blood?
opciones: A blunt cannula inside it is pushed past the tip before the needle leaves the vein
A spring pulls the needle back into the tube holder once the vein has been entered
A hinged shield snaps over the tip as the tube is pushed onto the holder
A blunt cap is screwed onto the tip once the needle has left the vein
preguntas.explicacion: In a self-blunting phlebotomy or winged-steel needle, a blunt cannula sits inside the needle and is pushed past the tip while the needle is still in the vein, so what finally leaves the patient is no longer sharp. Retracting needles and hinged or sliding shields are separate designs on the same list, and each works at a different moment; the blunting one is the only one that acts while the needle is still in the vein.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: When Can Information Be Shared?; Issues of Concern: Selective Access
preguntas.subtema: How much to tell a colleague · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A physician asks a phlebotomist to place an IV line for a patient's chemotherapy. How much of the history should the request carry?
opciones: Only what the task needs; the reason for the therapy is not required
The full oncology history, so the phlebotomist can judge the vein
The diagnosis and the stage, since both work for the same employer
No history at all, since treatment details may not be shared
preguntas.explicacion: Providers are not restricted from talking to one another about treatment, and a patient's care would stall if they were. The caution is about how much: asking someone to place a line does not require telling them why the therapy was prescribed. That is the same minimum necessary thinking behind selective access to records, where a laboratory worker needs the laboratory record and not the whole medical history.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the light blue coagulation tube fall in relation to the serum tubes and the other additive tubes?
opciones: Ahead of all of them: before the clot activator, separator, heparin and EDTA tubes
After the serum tubes, but still ahead of the heparin and EDTA tubes
Last of all, because it is one of the tubes that requires a full draw
Immediately before the fluoride tube, since both of them require a full draw
preguntas.explicacion: The numbered table gives the citrate tube position 3, the clot activator 4, the serum separator 5, the heparin tubes 6 and 7, EDTA 8, ACD 9 and the fluoride/oxalate tube 10. The four-group summary used in the coagulopathy review says the same thing in fewer words: sterile containers first, coagulation tubes next, plain and gel tubes after them, and the remaining additive tubes last. Both put the coagulation tube ahead of every serum and additive tube, and the full-draw requirement, which the citrate, EDTA and fluoride tubes share, says nothing about position.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Time Pressures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is asked to sign for a procedure while already medicated in the holding area. Why is that criticised?
opciones: Consent should be a two-way talk with time to ask questions and reflect
Consent signed outside a clinic has to be witnessed by a second nurse
Consent is not valid unless the same clinician performs the procedure
Consent in writing takes the place of discussing risks and benefits
preguntas.explicacion: The improper methods singled out are these: discussing the procedure shortly before it happens; taking consent in the holding area just before surgery; and taking it while the patient is medicated or on the point of falling asleep. What is called for instead is a structured two-way dialogue in a clinic or an office, leaving the patient time to ask questions and to think.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.E · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Under ISO 15189, at what point does the preanalytical phase end?
opciones: When the analytical examination begins
When the laboratory receives the specimen
When the specimen has been centrifuged
When the request is entered into the LIS
preguntas.explicacion: The ISO 15189 definition walks the preanalytical phase in chronological order: it opens with the clinician's request, takes in identifying and preparing the patient, the collection of the primary sample and its transport to the laboratory and inside it, and closes the moment the analytical examination starts. Receipt, centrifugation and order entry all fall inside that span, not at its edge.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Indications: Five Moments for Hand Hygiene
preguntas.subtema: Moments for hand hygiene · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist has greeted the patient and is about to clean the skin for the puncture. Which moment for hand hygiene is that?
opciones: Before a clean or aseptic procedure
After contact with the patient nearby
After exposure to any body fluid
After leaving the patient's own room
preguntas.explicacion: There are five moments, two of them before and three of them after. The two before are touching a patient and beginning a clean or aseptic procedure; the three after cover body fluid exposure or glove removal, patient contact, and contact with the patient's immediate surroundings. Cleaning the skin for a puncture is the aseptic procedure itself, so hands are done again right before it and not only on arrival.
