preguntas.pregunta: Which organization created the first patient bill of rights, in 1973?
opciones: The American Hospital Association (AHA)
The American Medical Association (AMA)
The American Cancer Society (ACS)
The Joint Commission (TJC)
preguntas.explicacion: The American Hospital Association produced the first patient bill of rights in 1973, a document about relationships between patients, professionals and organizations that carried little enforceability. The American Cancer Society also produced one in the same decade, and the AMA did not publish a list of patient rights until 2017. Such bills remain non-enforceable.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3, "1) Joint Commission International", IPSG 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5E 5G · PBT VI.D · CCMA 3E13
preguntas.pregunta: A technologist telephones a critical potassium result to a nurse. According to the Joint Commission International communication goal, what must the receiver do?
opciones: Write down the result, read it back, and confirm that what was written is accurate
Repeat the result aloud once and hang up so the physician can be notified as quickly as possible
Enter the result in the chart and ask the laboratory to send a written copy later
Ask a second nurse to listen in on the call as a witness to the reported value
preguntas.explicacion: The second international patient safety goal requires a procedure for verbal and telephone orders and for critical results: the receiver writes down or enters the complete result, reads it back, and both parties confirm that the written value and the read-back are accurate. A single repetition, a later written copy or a second listener do not complete the write-down / read-back / confirm sequence that surveyors look for.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, section When to Contact a Medical Professional
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural complications · CPT D3 k69 k74 · D1 1M k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports extreme pressure and severe pain in a large bruised area of the forearm. Why does that need urgent care?
opciones: It may be compartment syndrome, which can threaten the limb and life
It may be a periosteal bruise, which heals only after several months
It may be thrombophlebitis, which resolves once the arm is elevated
It may be simple swelling, which settles with ice applied every hour
preguntas.explicacion: A feeling of extreme pressure in a bruised part, especially when the area is large or very painful, can mean compartment syndrome, in which rising pressure cuts the blood and oxygen supply to the tissues. It is described as life-threatening and needing emergency care, sometimes surgery.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT VI.A · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Having measured an overall specimen rejection rate of 6 %, a laboratory sets itself a target below 2 %. Which two measures did it adopt to get there?
opciones: Monthly documentation of rejected samples and training where rejection is worst
Automatic acceptance of borderline samples and a monthly report to the medical director
A separate set of rejection criteria for the night shift and longer storage of rejects
Weekly rotation of the accessioning secretaries and a stricter barcode reading policy
preguntas.explicacion: The plan to bring 6 % down below 2 % rested on two things: enhanced documentation of every rejected sample, reviewed monthly, and periodic training organized for the departments with the highest rejection rates. Identifying and documenting the problem is described as the first step in improving quality; loosening the criteria would only move the error further down the line.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Cerebrospinal Fluid Samples)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k89 · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15
preguntas.pregunta: A lumbar puncture yields three numbered sterile tubes. Which tube is routinely designated for microbiological culture and sensitivity?
opciones: Tube 2, with tube 1 going to chemistry and serology and tube 3 to cytology
Tube 1, with tube 2 going to chemistry and serology and tube 3 to cytology
Tube 3, with tube 1 going to chemistry and serology and tube 2 to cytology
Tube 1, with tube 2 going to cytology and tube 3 to chemistry and serology
preguntas.explicacion: Cerebrospinal fluid collected under strict asepsis, usually between L3-L4 or L4-L5, is distributed into three sterile tubes: the first for chemistry and serology, the second for culture and sensitivity, and the third for cytological examination. Processing has to be immediate, because delay degrades the cells and shifts the biochemical values, glucose in particular, so a mis-sent tube costs time the specimen does not have.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Test!: Recording Results
preguntas.subtema: Recording qualitative results · CPT D5 k94 · PBT VI.A · CCMA 3D3 · CMA I.C.9.a · RMA III.C.3.b
preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant records a rapid strep result in the log as '+'. What does the record-keeping guidance say?
opciones: Qualitative results are recorded in words or abbreviations, such as 'Positive' or 'Pos', not as symbols
A '+' is acceptable as long as the cover page of the log has a key that explains what each symbol means
Symbols are preferred for qualitative results because they save space and they cannot be misspelled
Only the final result is recorded; a first result that was invalid is omitted so that the log stays clean
preguntas.explicacion: Results are recorded accurately and kept as a permanent record with enough detail to be retrieved. Quantitative results carry the units of measurement given in the manufacturer's instructions, and qualitative results are written as words or abbreviations rather than symbols: 'Positive' or 'Pos', 'Negative' or 'Neg', 'Reactive' or 'R', 'Non-reactive' or 'NR'. Invalid or unacceptable results are recorded too; the test is repeated and only the final acceptable result is reported.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP), What is a comprehensive metabolic panel?; and Lab Tests: Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP), What is a basic metabolic panel?
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · CPT D3 k57 D2 k47 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: An order is changed from a basic metabolic panel to a comprehensive one. Which measurements does the comprehensive panel add to the eight of the basic?
opciones: Albumin, total protein, ALP, ALT, AST and bilirubin
Phosphate, uric acid, lactate and blood ammonia
Cholesterol, triglycerides and the calcitonin level
Hemoglobin, hematocrit, platelets and the white count
preguntas.explicacion: The basic panel reports eight substances: glucose, calcium, the four electrolytes, and the two waste products BUN and creatinine. The comprehensive panel reports fourteen, adding albumin and total protein, the enzymes ALP, ALT and AST, and bilirubin, which is what lets it speak for the liver as well as the kidneys. Lipids and blood counts are ordered as separate tests.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Endocervical culture (003754), How to Prepare for the Test and How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Endocervical culture preparation · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.C · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(e) 2027
preguntas.pregunta: What is a patient told in the 2 days before an endocervical culture?
opciones: No vaginal creams or medicines, no douching and no intercourse, and empty the bladder and bowel
No vaginal creams or medicines, no douching and no intercourse, and drink water to fill the bladder
No tub baths and no tampons, and take a dose of an antifungal cream the night before
No solid food after midnight, and empty the bladder and bowel just before the examination
preguntas.explicacion: For the 2 days ahead the patient avoids creams or medicines in the vagina, douching and intercourse, and she empties bladder and bowel before the examination. The provider then uses a speculum to see the cervix and swabs mucus and cells from the endocervix, the part at the opening of the uterus. Douching is discouraged in general because it can cause infection.

preguntas.fuente: NCBI Bookshelf, Understanding Genetics (Genetic Alliance), Newborn Screening chapter (NBK132148), unacceptable results
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4C metabolic screening · PBT III.A.4 newborn screening acceptability
preguntas.pregunta: A state laboratory reports a newborn screening specimen as unacceptable. Who is responsible for repeating it?
opciones: The submitting hospital, which contacts the parents and repeats it
The state laboratory, which sends a mobile collector to the family's home
The parents, who must return to any clinic within 30 days of the report
The pediatrician of record, who is billed for the second card and collects it
preguntas.explicacion: Program rules put the repeat on the hospital that sent the card: the laboratory calls that hospital to ask for another screen, and the hospital contacts the parents and collects it, sending the second card in before the baby is a week old. The state children's program is told of the unacceptable result and writes to the parents within 48 hours.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(g)(1)(i)(A), (F), (G) and (I), Labels
preguntas.subtema: Labeling exemptions · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which container is exempt from the biohazard labeling requirement of the standard?
opciones: A unit of blood labeled as to contents and released for transfusion
A refrigerator that stores specimens of blood awaiting testing
A sharps container that is only one-quarter full
A bag of regulated waste that is going to an off-site incinerator
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(1)(i)(F) lets a unit go unlabeled when its container already states what is inside and it has been released for transfusion, or for another clinical use; (g)(1)(i)(G) does the same for individual containers placed inside a labeled one, and (g)(1)(i)(I) for waste that has been decontaminated. Refrigerators holding blood and containers of regulated waste are named in (g)(1)(i)(A) as needing the label, and a sharps container carries a label or color coding from the moment it goes into service under (d)(4)(iii)(A)(1)(iv), whatever its fill level.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urine Culture", Procedures (Specimen Preservation and Processing); and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine culture (003751), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Culture turnaround · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how soon a urine culture will tell which organism is growing. What is the usual answer?
opciones: In 24 to 48 hours, the incubation time the plates need before organisms can be identified
In 2 to 4 hours, the incubation time the plates need before organisms can be identified
In 48 to 72 hours, the incubation time the plates need before any organism can be identified
In about a week, the incubation time the plates need before organisms can be identified
preguntas.explicacion: Urine is plated with a calibrated loop on media such as blood agar and MacConkey agar, held at 35 to 37 degrees Celsius, and read after 24 to 48 hours; that is also how long the laboratory tells the patient the culture takes. Susceptibility testing follows from the isolated colonies. A few unusual organisms, such as Oligella urolytica, need longer than 48 hours, which is the exception rather than the routine.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Discussion; PMC, "Preanalytical phase - a continuous challenge for laboratory professionals" (Biochem Med 2012, PMC4062337), Preanalytical phase studies recently published
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5G k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E13 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A preterm infant on oxygen has a moderately hemolysed serum sample with an LDH ordered for monitoring. What approach did the neonatal laboratory and the surveyed neonatologists favor?
opciones: Report the approximate LDH with a comment that moderate hemolysis affects it, rather than rejecting it outright
Reject the LDH and every other analyte on the sample, since LDH is the analyte most sensitive to hemolysis
Correct the LDH with a formula based on the hemolysis index and report the adjusted value without a comment
Report the LDH only after a repeat heel sample, since a moderate index in a newborn always means in vivo hemolysis
preguntas.explicacion: LDH is a basic monitoring test in premature babies receiving supplementary oxygen and is very sensitive to hemolysis, so the laboratory may be slightly more permissive in them: raise the hemolysis borderline a little and report the approximate LDH with a note that moderate hemolysis affects it. That matches a survey in which neonatologists preferred receiving the result with a qualitative comment on the interference over having the LDH rejected. Correction formulas, by contrast, have been shown to be unreliable.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Desirable Characteristics of Devices with Safety Features
preguntas.subtema: Activating the safety feature · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: When a safety feature has to be activated by the user rather than working on its own, how should that be done?
opciones: With one hand, and with the worker's hands staying behind the exposed tip
With both hands, so the shield is seated squarely over the used needle
After the needle is in the container, where the tip can hurt no one
By the coworker who receives the device, before the tube is removed
preguntas.explicacion: A passive feature, one that needs nothing from the user, is preferred. Where the user does have to activate it, the recommendation is a single-handed technique that keeps both hands behind the exposed sharp, and a feature the user can plainly see has engaged. Waiting until the device is inside the container defeats the purpose, since injuries also happen during disposal, and passing an unprotected device to another worker adds a second person to the risk.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 3F k62 k9 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which devices placed for venous access rule out a site for a routine draw?
opciones: A venous port, a central catheter or an intravenous catheter
A venous port only, since catheters can be drawn through safely
An intravenous catheter only, when fluids are actually running
A central catheter only, when the line was placed within a week
preguntas.explicacion: The contraindication is written broadly: any device used for venous access, and the three examples given are a venous port, a central catheter and an intravenous catheter. Blood taken from an existing peripheral access can be hemolyzed, contaminated, or diluted by fluid and medication.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", sections Introduction and Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Post-prandial glucose · CPT D4 4H 2-hour post-prandial · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139
preguntas.pregunta: A provider asks the laboratory about a 5-hour oral glucose tolerance test to work up hypoglycemia that appears a few hours after meals. What is the standing view of that test?
opciones: It is generally not recommended, because false-positive results are common
It is the standard workup, and the only way to confirm the diagnosis
It is recommended only when the ordinary 2-hour test comes back normal
It is recommended only in pregnancy, once the 3-hour test is abnormal
preguntas.explicacion: Reactive, or postprandial, hypoglycemia means glucose falling 2 to 5 hours after a meal heavy in carbohydrate, early when it comes between 2 and 3 hours and late between 3 and 5. A 5-hour oral glucose tolerance test can be used to look into it, but clinical practice generally advises against it for diagnosing reactive hypoglycemia, because of the false positives.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Clinical Note: Capillary versus Venous Glucose Measurements
preguntas.subtema: Capillary vs venous glucose · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.4 · CCMA 3D3 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.ii
preguntas.pregunta: One hour after lunch, a patient's fingerstick meter reads 205 mg/dL while a venous sample drawn at the same time gives 186 mg/dL in the laboratory. What does this pattern reflect?
opciones: Capillary values run slightly higher than venous ones after meals; discrepant results are confirmed by the laboratory venous test
The meter is out of calibration and must be taken out of service until two levels of liquid control material have been run and passed
The venous sample was falsely low because it was drawn from an arm that was receiving an intravenous glucose infusion at the time
Capillary values run lower than venous ones after meals, so the laboratory value should be reported instead of the meter
preguntas.explicacion: Capillary blood glucose and venous or arterial plasma differ by a clinically relevant margin: the capillary reading runs slightly higher after a meal. What comes off a capillary point-of-care test should not be casually mixed with laboratory venous values, and a discrepant capillary result is confirmed by venous testing in the laboratory, in hospital above all. A postprandial gap of that kind does not by itself mean the meter has failed.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Characteristics of Leukocytes
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A CBC report lists white cells at 7,000 per microliter. How do leukocytes differ from the other formed elements?
opciones: They are complete cells with a nucleus, some 5,000 to 10,000 per µL
They are anucleate biconcave discs, numbering about 5 million per µL
They are cell fragments only 2 to 4 µm across, made in the marrow
They are complete cells that never leave the vessels, unlike erythrocytes
preguntas.explicacion: Among the formed elements only the white cells are complete cells, with a nucleus and organelles, and there are far fewer of them than red cells, about 5,000 to 10,000 per microliter, so 7,000 is in range. Red cells stay inside the vessels, while white cells cross the wall to work in the tissues. The anucleate discs are the red cells, and the fragments 2 to 4 micrometers across are the platelets.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, Blood alcohol concentration in the clinical laboratory: a narrative review, Biochemia Medica 2024 (PMC10564119), sections Microbial contamination and Sample container
preguntas.subtema: Blood alcohol specimen · CPT D4 4I k85 · PBT III.A.4 alcohol · PBT II.J additives
preguntas.pregunta: Is sodium fluoride required as a preservative for a forensic blood alcohol specimen?
opciones: No, provided a sterile pre-evacuated tube is used and handled correctly
Yes, because without it the concentration climbs during storage
Yes, but only when the specimen will be stored for more than 24 hours
No, because the ordinary glucose tube already carries enough of it
preguntas.explicacion: With sterile pre-evacuated tubes filled, mixed and kept closed, a forensic result needs no specific preservative, and fluoride brings complications of its own. Contamination is expected to bias the result downward rather than upward, and the fluoride in an ordinary glucose tube, 2.5 mg per mL of blood, is too little to hold microbial growth back anyway.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Plasma Proteins
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.2 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which plasma protein is the most abundant and contributes most to the osmotic pressure of blood?
opciones: Albumin, about 54 percent of plasma protein
Fibrinogen, about 7 percent of plasma protein
Gamma globulin, the antibody fraction
Alpha globulin, which carries iron and lipids
preguntas.explicacion: There are three groups of plasma proteins. Albumin, made by the liver, is the largest share at about 54 percent (3.5 to 5.0 g/dL); it binds fatty acids and steroid hormones and is the main protein holding water inside the vessels, which helps keep blood volume and pressure. Globulins are second at about 38 percent, and the gamma fraction is the antibodies. Fibrinogen is about 7 percent and is needed for clotting.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Critical Limits of Laboratory Results for Urgent Clinician Notification" (EJIFCC 2003, PMC6178782), introductory text; PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3, "3) ISO 15189: 2007"
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT VI.D · CCMA 3E13
preguntas.pregunta: A new outpatient clinic asks the laboratory for the official national list of critical values. What is the correct reply?
opciones: There is no single list: the parameters and limits are agreed between the treating physicians and the laboratory, and depend on the diseases that practice expects to see
The list is fixed by CLIA in 42 CFR 493.1291, which names the analytes and the limits that every certified laboratory must apply without local changes
The list is the one published by the analyzer manufacturer, since limits are method-dependent and cannot be changed by the laboratory or the clinicians
The list is set by the accreditation body at each inspection cycle and applies unchanged to every client the laboratory serves
preguntas.explicacion: Before the laboratory can call a critical result out immediately, the clinician and the laboratory have to have agreed between them on what counts as critical, and which parameters and limits to set depends on the diseases that clinic or practice expects to meet; ISO 15189 likewise wants critical results defined locally, with the clinicians who use the laboratory. CLIA requires immediate alerting for life-threatening and panic values but puts no numbers on them.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Skin Care and Aging, How does skin change as you age? and Bruises
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k49 age and physical condition · PBT II.B II.I age-specific needs · CCMA 3E4 site by age and condition, k131 skin integrity
preguntas.pregunta: An 84-year-old with paper-thin skin bruises after a routine draw. What age changes explain this?
opciones: Thinner, paler, less elastic outer skin and more fragile blood vessels, so older adults bruise more easily
The skin thickens with keratin and the veins sink deeper, so the needle tears more tissue on the way in and out
The skin loses its sweat and oil glands, so the alcohol cannot dry and irritates the puncture site
The platelet count falls sharply after 80, so every puncture bleeds under the skin
preguntas.explicacion: As the years pass the outer skin turns thinner, paler and less springy, and the vessels underneath grow fragile, so an older adult bruises on less and takes longer to clear the mark. The loss of elastin and collagen leaves the skin easier to damage. Adhesive strips used again and again can break down very elderly skin.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 3186, Model Exposure Control Plan, Recordkeeping: Sharps Injury Log; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(5)(i) and (h)(5)(iii)
preguntas.subtema: Keeping the sharps log · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA II.B.5.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: How long is the sharps injury log kept, and what happens when someone asks for a copy of it?
opciones: At least five years after the end of the year it covers, with identifiers removed
Three years after the training it documents, with the trainer's name removed
Thirty years after the employee leaves, with the device brand taken out
Five years, and copies go only to the Assistant Secretary who asks for them
preguntas.explicacion: The standard sends the log's retention to 29 CFR 1904.33, and the model plan spells out what that comes to: five years at minimum, counted from the close of the calendar year the log covers. The model adds that any copy handed out has the personal identifiers stripped, which matches the demand in (h)(5)(i) that the record keep the injured worker's identity confidential. Three years is the training record; employment plus thirty years is the medical record.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Blood Plasma and Plasma Proteins
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.2 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: What proportion of blood plasma is water?
opciones: About 92 percent
About 55 percent
About 45 percent
About 7 percent
preguntas.explicacion: Plasma is about 92 percent water. Nearly all the rest, about 7 percent, is protein, and the electrolytes, gases, nutrients and wastes together add up to roughly 1 percent. The other figures belong to different measures: about 45 percent of whole blood is red cells (the hematocrit), and plasma is a little over half of whole blood, which is where a 55 percent figure comes from.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, section Causes
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural complications · CPT D3 3C k69 k74 · D2 2L k48 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which medicines make a patient more likely to bruise at a puncture site?
opciones: Aspirin, warfarin, apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran or clopidogrel
Aspirin, insulin, metformin, levothyroxine, warfarin or amoxicillin
Warfarin only, since the other blood thinners act on platelets alone
Clopidogrel only, since aspirin is taken at too low a dose to matter
preguntas.explicacion: Patients taking a blood thinner are described as likely to bruise more easily, and the drugs listed are aspirin, warfarin, dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban and clopidogrel. It is a fair thing to ask about before a draw, since firm pressure afterwards matters more in those patients.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Safely Using Sharps (Needles and Syringes) at Home, at Work and on Travel; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.2
preguntas.subtema: Exposure response · CPT D1 1H k33 · D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A worker is stuck by another person's used needle. What are the first two actions?
opciones: Wash the area with soap and water or antiseptic, then seek medical care
Squeeze the wound to bleed it, then report the incident at end of shift
Cover the wound with a dressing, then wait for the source result to arrive
Apply an alcohol swab for thirty seconds, then finish the current draw
preguntas.explicacion: The exposed area is washed straight away with water and soap, or cleaned with a skin antiseptic, rubbing alcohol or hand sanitizer, and medical attention is sought at once. The same instructions apply to blood reaching the eyes, nose, mouth or skin, and prophylaxis is not delayed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 · CCMA 6 k199 k202 · CMA F.1.g / 2027 F.1.d · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Staff say there is no time to answer a frightened patient's worry. What did an observational study find?
opciones: Empathic responses lengthened the consultation by about 21 seconds
Empathic responses lengthened the consultation by about 21 minutes
Empathic responses shortened the consultation by roughly one third
Empathic responses made no measurable difference to the anxiety
preguntas.explicacion: The worry that there is no time to address emotional concerns is not what the literature shows. Studies of physicians found only a marginal change in the length of a consultation when an empathic response was given, and better communication skills were not associated with longer consultations. One observational study put the average increase at 21 seconds.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", HIPAA and Communication With Patients, Contents and Authorizations; StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Relative disclosure
preguntas.subtema: Family and caregivers · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: May a phlebotomist tell a patient's spouse, who is present and involved in the patient's care, about the draw and the follow-up?
opciones: Yes, if the patient is informed and does not object; ask when others are present
No; disclosure to any family member requires a signed written authorization
Yes, and the same applies to any relative who telephones the clinic asking about results
No, unless the spouse holds a medical power of attorney on file at the clinic
preguntas.explicacion: The Privacy Rule lets information reach a spouse, a parent, a guardian or another caregiver who takes part in looking after the patient, and no formal agreement is needed for it. The practical move is to ask the patient whether they mind before discussing something specific with others in the room. Patients may also put limits on that sharing, for instance asking that no relative collect medications or be told about their condition. A relative on the telephone is a different case: a hospital may not disclose over the phone to a caller who says they are family.

preguntas.pregunta: Why does the WHO recommend closed vacuum-tube systems over open needle-and-syringe collection?

They are the cheapest devices and need no special training to use
They give better precision on small or difficult veins than any other collection device
They can be heparinized and used for arterial as well as venous sampling
preguntas.explicacion: Chapter 3 says closed systems have proven safer than open systems, and that vacuum extraction systems reduce the risk of direct exposure to blood and make several samples from one venepuncture easier to take, though they require training and skill. The other three statements are advantages that Table C.1 gives to the hypodermic syringe (cheap, no special training, heparinized for arterial blood) and to the winged needle (precision on small veins).

preguntas.pregunta: Four patterns are described for the superficial veins at the elbow. Which of them is the most common?
opciones: Type II, in which the median cubital vein joins the cephalic and basilic veins (the M pattern)
Type I, in which a dominant median antebrachial vein joins both veins (the N pattern)
Type III, in which the brachial cephalic vein is poorly developed or missing
Type IV, in which there is no communicating branch between cephalic and basilic
preguntas.explicacion: Type II, with the cephalic and the basilic joined by the median cubital vein, also called type M, is the most common pattern, followed by type I, the N type with a dominant median antebrachial vein. It adds that because of this variation, bruising, hematoma and sensory changes from mispuncture have been reported across health systems.

preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 k48 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA I.A.3 / 2027 A.3.c · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: What does the guidance suggest an older patient bring so that their medicines can be checked?
opciones: A list with dose and frequency, or everything in a bag
Only the prescriptions written since the last appointment
The pharmacy receipts covering the past twelve months
A note from the pharmacist listing the interactions
preguntas.explicacion: Older people often take many medicines, prescribed by more than one doctor, and some of those combinations end in serious complications. The patient is asked to bring a list of it all, what is prescribed, what is bought over the counter, the vitamins and the dietary supplements, with the dose and frequency of each, or simply to bring the lot along in a bag.

preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 k93 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D k111 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: What do the letters H, I and L stand for in the serum indices that conventional laboratory analyzers measure, and how are the same problems detected at the point of care?
opciones: Hemoglobin, icterus and lipemia; at the point of care only by visual inspection of a centrifuged aliquot
Heparin, infusion and light; at the point of care by a built-in spectrophotometric check on every strip
Hemoglobin, icterus and lipemia; at the point of care by an automatic index reported with each result
Hematocrit, ionic strength and lactate; at the point of care by running a control before each sample
preguntas.explicacion: Conventional laboratories add a step that measures the serum index for hemoglobin (H), icterus (I) and lipemia (L), usually spectrophotometrically, because all three can make results inaccurate or incalculable, potassium being especially vulnerable. Point-of-care devices have no such index, so hemolysis, icterus and lipemia can be recognized there only by looking at a centrifuged aliquot; dilution may fix excess bilirubin and ultracentrifugation excess lipids.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", section Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: OGTT conditions · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.G II.B · CCMA 3E k139
preguntas.pregunta: Between the fasting and 2-hour samples of an OGTT, the patient asks to step outside for a cigarette. What is the correct response?
opciones: No; the patient must stay seated and must not smoke during the test
Yes, as long as the patient is back within 5 minutes of the draw
Yes, but the walk must be recorded because exercise lowers glucose
Yes, but only after the 1-hour sample has been collected
preguntas.explicacion: During the OGTT the patient remains seated and smoking is avoided; those are stated conditions of the test, alongside the fast, the morning start and the three-day diet. Vigorous exercise is something to avoid in the days before, not something to log and allow. The five minutes in one option is the time over which the glucose drink is swallowed, not a grace period for leaving the chair.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 6.2.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2E k41 k49 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3E1 k124 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: A 4-year-old is on the ward with his father. How does the WHO guidance say the child should be identified before a draw?
opciones: Ask the father for the child's first and last names, then match the form
Ask the child to state his own first and last names, then match the form
Read the name off the band tied to the cot rail, then match the form
Ask the nurse who admitted the child, then match her answer to the form
preguntas.explicacion: For pediatric patients a band counts only when it is on the child, never one fixed to the bed or cot, and where a parent or legal guardian is there, that adult is asked for the child's first and last names. The form is then checked against the patient for the hospital or file number, the date of birth and the name.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, Blood alcohol concentration in the clinical laboratory: a narrative review, Biochemia Medica 2024 (PMC10564119), Table 1 and Sample container
preguntas.subtema: Blood alcohol site preparation · CPT D4 4I k85 skin preparation · PBT III.A.4 alcohol
preguntas.pregunta: How should the venipuncture site be prepared when a blood alcohol concentration is ordered?
opciones: With a non-alcoholic antiseptic
With 70% isopropyl alcohol
With a povidone-iodine swab and alcohol
With chlorhexidine in 70% alcohol
preguntas.explicacion: First of the seven pillars of a forensically defensible blood alcohol collection: clean the skin with an antiseptic that contains no alcohol. Isopropyl and chlorhexidine preparations both carry alcohol, and so does the povidone-iodine option offered here. Official laboratory guidance does not ban alcoholic antiseptics but asks that they dry off first; the non-alcoholic rule reinforces that so the step stays error-proof in a busy emergency room, at no meaningful extra cost.

preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Code of Ethics
preguntas.subtema: Codes of ethics · CPT D1 k26 · CCMA 7C · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: Which duty does the code of ethics for NHA-certified professionals state?
opciones: To respect and safeguard every patient's dignity, privacy and safety
To report any colleague suspected of an error to the state licensing board
To accept any assignment the employer gives while the shift is under way
To keep patient information from the patient's own family in every case
preguntas.explicacion: The code lists six duties a certified professional takes on, and one is safeguarding every patient's dignity, privacy and safety. The others cover working for the betterment of society and the profession, professionalism and honesty, continued learning, taking part in activities that improve health and the allied health field, and acting in the public's best interest.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003); WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Follow-up
preguntas.subtema: Precautions during follow-up · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: During the HIV follow-up period after an exposure, what does the CDC advise the worker to avoid?
opciones: Donating blood, semen or organs and unprotected sex, mostly in the first 6 to 12 weeks
Patient care duties of any kind until the 6-month antibody test comes back negative
Close contact with household members until the 12-week antibody test is negative
Any other medication, since it would interfere with the antiretroviral regimen
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC brochure asks exposed workers, especially during the first 6 to 12 weeks when most infected persons show signs of infection, to follow HIV prevention recommendations: no donation of blood, semen or organs, no sexual intercourse or consistent condom use, and consideration of not breastfeeding. WHO's annex adds no blood or organ donation for up to 6 months. Neither source restricts patient care or household contact, and the CDC asks workers to tell the treating provider about other medications, not to stop them.

preguntas.pregunta: Besides reading the number, what does the daily temperature routine ask staff to look at on the thermometer itself?

Whether the probe still sits in the middle shelf of the compartment
Whether the calibration sticker is still inside its expiry period
Whether the minimum and maximum display has been reset since the last read
preguntas.explicacion: The recording instructions add a physical check to the daily reading: each time the thermometer is read, look for a separated column, for gas bubbles and for cracks, where those apply. Resetting the minimum and maximum display belongs to the optional data logger used over weekends and closures, and it is done after the reading rather than instead of the inspection.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(5), Healthcare Professional's Written Opinion
preguntas.subtema: Post-exposure written opinion · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: After a post-exposure evaluation, how soon must the employer hand the employee a copy of the evaluating professional's written opinion?
opciones: Within 15 days of completing the evaluation
Within 10 working days of the exposure incident
Within 30 days of the exposure incident
Within 90 days, once the baseline sample is tested
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(5) makes the employer obtain the evaluating professional's written opinion and put a copy in the employee's hands no more than 15 days after the evaluation is finished. The other periods sit elsewhere in the standard: 10 working days is the window for offering the hepatitis B vaccine after initial assignment, and 90 days is how long a baseline blood sample is kept when the employee consents to the draw but not yet to HIV testing. Thirty days is no deadline in this standard.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, introduction and Sections 12-15
preguntas.subtema: SDS structure · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: How many sections does a GHS-format Safety Data Sheet have, and which of them does OSHA not enforce?
opciones: 16 sections; OSHA does not enforce sections 12 through 15
16 sections; OSHA does not enforce sections 9 through 11 and 16
12 sections; OSHA does not enforce the last two, transport and regulatory
8 sections, one per required pictogram; all are enforced by OSHA
preguntas.explicacion: A safety data sheet under the Hazard Communication standard has 16 numbered sections in a fixed order. Sections 12 through 15, ecological information, disposal, transport and regulatory information, must be present to match the GHS, but OSHA does not enforce their content because other agencies handle those matters. Sections 9 through 11 and 16 hold technical data such as physical properties, reactivity, toxicology and the date of preparation, and they are enforced. Eight is the number of pictograms OSHA requires, not of SDS sections.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Information on Collection of Respiratory Specimens for Influenza Virus Testing, Outpatients; and CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Considerations
preguntas.subtema: Timing after onset · CPT D2 k45 timing · PBT V.C.2 / V.D.2 · CCMA 3D k117 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with influenza symptoms asks whether it matters how soon the swab is taken. What is the answer?
opciones: Yes: shedding in the upper airway falls off about 3 to 4 days after onset, so earlier is better
No: the amount of virus in the upper airway stays steady for about two weeks after onset
Yes: the virus is undetectable in the first 3 to 4 days, so waiting improves the yield
No: a negative rapid test rules out influenza whenever the swab happens to be taken
preguntas.explicacion: Influenza shedding in the upper respiratory tract drops substantially around 3 to 4 days after illness begins, so specimens are collected as close to onset as possible, ideally within four days. Infants and immunosuppressed patients may shed longer. A negative rapid antigen test never rules the infection out and should not stop further testing by molecular assay or empiric treatment.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3, "2) College of American Pathologists Laboratory Accreditation Program", item GEN.20365
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5E · PBT VI.A · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15
preguntas.pregunta: An accreditation program asks a laboratory to show how it addresses its four patient safety goals. Which of these is one of them?
opciones: Coordinating the laboratory's patient safety role across the organization
Verifying the calibration of every analyser at each change of reagent lot
Reviewing the appropriateness of the tests that clinicians order each month
Confirming the competency of each testing employee twice in the first year
preguntas.explicacion: The four goals all sit outside the analysis itself: better identification of patient and sample at collection, at analysis and at reporting; better verification and communication when the information is life-threatening or life-altering; errors spotted, reported and put right sooner; and a laboratory whose part in patient safety is coordinated better with the rest of the organization.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the Teach-Back Method
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.D Interpersonal Relations · CPT D2 2B k40 · CCMA 6 k199 · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods
preguntas.pregunta: A patient cannot say back what he has to do before a glucose tolerance test. What comes next?
opciones: Explain it another way and ask again, until he can describe the plan in his own words
Hand him the printed instruction sheet and ask him to read the relevant lines out loud
Document that the teaching was offered and refused, and tell the ordering provider later
Repeat the same explanation word for word but more slowly, and move on once he nods
preguntas.explicacion: When teach-back uncovers a misunderstanding, the cycle repeats: explain it using a different approach, ask for the teach-back again, and keep going until the patient describes the information correctly in his own words. Words repeated back verbatim are a warning sign rather than a pass, and a nod proves nothing at all.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Diversity and Discrimination in Health Care", sections Introduction and Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6 k193 · CMA F.2.b / 2027 F.1.c · RMA I.D.1.e
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about discrimination in health care is correct?
opciones: It can rest on perceived group membership, and no harm needs to have occurred
It requires proof that the patient was harmed by the action or omission
It requires that the patient actually belong to the group in question
It is limited to the overt acts that Title VII and the ADA prohibit
preguntas.explicacion: Discrimination in health care is negative actions or lack of consideration based on preconceived notions about identity, adding that it can occur on perceived membership, that a person need not belong to the group, and that harm does not have to occur. Title VII and the ADA reduced overt racism, after which awareness shifted to the subtler microaggressions.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 4: Communicate Clearly, Actions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2M k15 · PBT II.B · CCMA 4 k160 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: When explaining fasting instructions, which approach follows the health-literacy principles for communicating clearly?
opciones: Give one to three need-to-know points in plain words, and repeat them
Cover every instruction once, quickly, so that none of them is left out
Use the precise medical terms so the patient learns them for next time
Hand over the printed sheet and skip the spoken explanation entirely
preguntas.explicacion: Keep it to one, two or at most three things the patient needs to know or to do, press each of them more than once, slow down, and use plain non-medical language, since jargon shuts patients out. Kessels found that up to 80% of what patients are told is forgotten at once, and that nearly half of what stays is wrong, which rules out a fast, exhaustive or paper-only approach.

preguntas.pregunta: Which item is listed for the case where a large quantity of blood has to be collected?

A set of four pediatric microtubes in a rack
A second tube holder with a wider barrel fitted
A pair of gray fluoride tubes drawn back to back
preguntas.explicacion: Alongside the ordinary sample tubes, the equipment list names a sterile glass or collapsible bleeding pack for occasions when large quantities of blood are taken. Donation is also the setting for the widest needles on the gauge table, sixteen to eighteen.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antiepileptic Drug Monitoring", section Trough Versus Free Levels
preguntas.subtema: Trough timing · CPT D2 k45 high and low levels · PBT II.G common tests · CCMA 3E k139 medication levels · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2 pre-test conditions
preguntas.pregunta: A trough level is ordered for a patient on an antiepileptic drug. When is the sample drawn?
opciones: At the lowest point of the dosing interval, just before the next dose
At the highest point of the dosing interval, just after the next dose
Halfway between two doses, when the concentration is most stable
At the same hour each morning, independently of the dose times
preguntas.explicacion: A trough is the concentration of the drug in blood at its lowest point, which falls just before the next dose is due; it matters most for drugs with short half-lives. The value shows the minimum concentration reached between doses, so it tells the prescriber whether the level stayed inside the therapeutic range all the way through the interval and, for seizure drugs, whether breakthrough seizures are likely.

preguntas.subtema: Donor identification and consent · CPT D4 4D k82 complete screening
preguntas.pregunta: Besides proof of identity, what must be obtained from a donor on the day of donation?
opciones: A postal address where the donor can be reached for 8 weeks afterwards
A postal address where the donor can be reached for 16 weeks afterwards
A photograph of the donor, kept with the unit's identification number
The name of a physician who can be contacted about abnormal results
preguntas.explicacion: On the day of donation two things are required: proof of identity, and a postal address good for reaching the donor over the 8 weeks that follow. The donor also acknowledges having reviewed the educational material, agrees not to donate if it would put recipients at risk, and is told a sample will be tested and that any deferral would be notified. That acknowledgement may carry no exculpatory language.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Stool guaiac test (003393), How to Prepare for the Test; and StatPearls, "Fecal Occult Blood Test", Interfering Factors; and StatPearls, "StatPearls — Urinalysis" (NBK557685)
preguntas.subtema: gFOBT dietary restrictions · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · RMA III.C.4.a.iv · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: Which foods are patients told to avoid before a guaiac-based fecal occult blood test?
opciones: Red meat, cantaloupe, raw broccoli, turnip, radish and horseradish
Beets, blackberries, rhubarb, carrots and other strongly colored foods
Onions, garlic and asparagus, which change the odor of the specimen
Cranberry juice and a high-protein diet, which acidify the specimen
preguntas.explicacion: Red meat carries heme with peroxidase activity, and raw produce such as turnip, broccoli, horseradish, radish and cantaloupe is rich in plant peroxidases; either can turn a guaiac card falsely positive, and about 3 days of avoidance is advised. The other lists are urine interferences: colored foods alter urine color, onions and asparagus its odor, and cranberry juice or a high-protein diet its pH. Immunochemical kits need no diet.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet removal · CPT D3 3E k60 k70 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist withdraws the needle and only then reaches for the tourniquet. Which instruction was missed?
opciones: The band comes off before the needle is withdrawn, not after
The band comes off once pressure has been applied with gauze
The band comes off before the first tube is pushed on the needle
The band comes off as soon as the needle has entered the vein
preguntas.explicacion: Once enough blood has been collected, the band is released before the needle is withdrawn; some guidance puts it earlier still, as soon as flow is established, and in every version before two minutes have passed. Pressure with clean gauze belongs to the step that follows the withdrawal.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Fecal Occult Blood Test (FOBT), Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?; and StatPearls, "Fecal Occult Blood Test", Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Vitamin C false negative · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.2 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · RMA III.C.4.a.iv · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient takes 1,000 mg of vitamin C daily and is about to do a guaiac stool test. What effect should be expected if she continues?
opciones: A false-negative result, because ascorbic acid blocks the guaiac color reaction
A false-positive result, because ascorbic acid has peroxidase activity
An unchanged result, because only vitamin C above 2,000 mg a day interferes
A false-negative result, because ascorbic acid stops intestinal bleeding for 3 days
preguntas.explicacion: Vitamin C is a reducing agent that interferes with the oxidation the guaiac reaction depends on, so it hides blood that is really there. Patients are told to avoid more than 250 mg a day from supplements, juice or fruit, and high amounts for the 3 days before the test can cause a false negative; 1 to 2 grams daily has produced false negatives in studies. It does not stop bleeding and has no peroxidase activity.

preguntas.pregunta: A moderately hemolysed serum is tested anyway because the patient cannot be redrawn, and the physician wants the figure. What must the printed report carry?

The name of the person who decided to accept the flawed specimen
A recommendation that the ordering provider repeat the collection
The measured hemolysis index alongside every affected analyte
preguntas.explicacion: The test report standard lists what has to appear on the report, and among those items is whatever is known about the state of specimens that fall short of the laboratory's acceptability criteria and about what was done with them. Naming the decision maker, advising a redraw or printing the index may all be local practice, but the federal requirement is that the report say what was wrong with the specimen.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Materials and Methods; Results and Table 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's CRP is ordered to monitor for perinatal infection and the serum returns a hemolysis index of about 800 mmol/L. What does the laboratory do with the CRP?
opciones: Rejects it and asks for a repeat sample, since an index above 622 mmol/L can underestimate CRP
Reports it, since specific proteins such as CRP are immune to hemolysis interference at any index
Reports it with a note, since only indices above 2,000 mmol/L count as severe in newborns
Dilutes the serum to bring the index below 31 mmol/L and reports the CRP from that dilution
preguntas.explicacion: Specific proteins are less sensitive to hemolysis than many chemistry tests, but severe in vitro hemolysis can still interfere: over a hemolysis index of 622 mmol/L the CRP is underestimated, and in that series 199 newborn CRP requests were rejected for severe hemolysis, the highest being 1,997. Each rejected CRP became reliable after the blood sampling was repeated two to five hours later. The figure 31 mmol/L is merely the index equivalent of 0.5 g/L free hemoglobin, the threshold that defines a hemolysed sample.

preguntas.subtema: Anchoring the vein · CPT D3 3H k64 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9

opciones: The hand that is not holding the needle
The hand that is holding the needle itself
Either hand, whichever reaches the site first
The patient's own free hand, guided by the worker
preguntas.explicacion: The hand not being used for the draw is the one that tightens the skin above the vein, with the thumb pulling the skin down and slightly away from the site. The other hand then inserts the needle slowly at fifteen to thirty degrees to the surface of the arm.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic drug levels (003430), Why the Test is Performed; MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, What do the results mean?
preguntas.subtema: Timed draws · CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139 timed specimens · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: Why does a therapeutic drug level have to be drawn at the scheduled time rather than whenever the patient arrives?
opciones: The useful range is narrow: too high is harmful and too low does not work
The tube additive breaks down if the specimen is collected off schedule
The laboratory only runs drug levels in fixed batches during the day
A late sample would need a larger volume to reach the same sensitivity
preguntas.explicacion: For most medicines a certain level in the blood is needed for the proper effect: some are harmful if the level climbs too high and useless if it falls too low, so monitoring keeps the drug inside its therapeutic range. The published ranges assume a set moment in the dosing interval, such as 12 hours after the dose, which is why the clock, not the workload, sets the draw time.

preguntas.pregunta: How long does a patient usually need to fast before a blood test, and who sets the exact time?
opciones: Usually 8 to 12 hours; the provider sets it according to the test ordered
Usually 4 to 6 hours; the laboratory sets it according to the tube type
Usually 24 hours; the provider sets it according to the patient's body weight
Usually 12 to 16 hours; the phlebotomist sets it at check-in
preguntas.explicacion: The usual fast is 8 to 12 hours, and the provider states exactly how long, depending on the test, sometimes with extra instructions such as avoiding alcohol for longer. Scheduling the draw early in the morning lets most of the fast happen during sleep. The 24-hour figure in the sources is the alcohol-free window before sampling, not a fast.

opciones: Nature, risks and benefits, alternatives, their risks and benefits, and the patient's understanding
Nature, risks and benefits, alternatives, and the patient's signature with a staff witness
Disclosure of the information, the patient's competency, and a voluntary decision
Nature, risks, benefits and alternatives, documented only on the printed consent form
preguntas.explicacion: Five elements are documented: what the procedure is, the risks it carries and the benefits it offers, the alternatives that are reasonable, what each of those would risk and offer in turn, and a check on how far the patient has understood; the record may be a form, a progress note or another part of the chart. The three-part list belongs to research consent, and Bottrell's four leave out the understanding check.

preguntas.explicacion: Latex turns up in hospital items such as surgical and exam gloves, in catheters and tubing, in tourniquets and medicine vials, and in elastic bandages and wraps; sticky tape and electrode pads are now often latex-free but should be checked. preguntas.pregunta: A patient with limited English insists that her sister interpret for her. What is the correct course?
opciones: Respect the request, and also bring in a qualified interpreter to confirm accuracy
Refuse the sister and proceed only once a telephone interpreter is on the line
Accept the sister alone, because the patient has the right to choose her
Accept the sister, or her 12-year-old son if the sister has to step out
preguntas.explicacion: Where a patient insists that a relative interpret, the request is respected, and a qualified interpreter is brought in as well so that the information travels accurately, since a relative may voice her own views and privacy goes with it. The toolkit is flat about one thing: a child is never used as an interpreter.

preguntas.pregunta: When taking a manual blood pressure, where is the stethoscope placed, and which artery is being heard?
opciones: In the antecubital fossa, listening over the brachial artery
At the wrist, listening over the radial artery
At the neck, listening over the common carotid artery
In the antecubital fossa, listening over the median cubital vein
preguntas.explicacion: The cuff goes around the arm at heart level, and the stethoscope is placed on the antecubital region while the cuff deflates, to hear the Korotkoff sounds as blood returns through the brachial artery; the first sound marks the systolic pressure and the last the diastolic. The radial and carotid arteries are pulse sites, not where the cuff is read.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, opening paragraph; and Fibrinolysis
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k74) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In what order do the three steps of hemostasis occur after a vessel is punctured?
opciones: Vascular spasm, platelet plug, coagulation
Platelet plug, vascular spasm, coagulation
Coagulation, fibrinolysis, platelet plug
Vascular spasm, coagulation, fibrinolysis
preguntas.explicacion: Hemostasis is the sealing of a ruptured vessel, in three steps: first the smooth muscle of the vessel wall contracts (vascular spasm), then platelets stick to the exposed collagen and to each other (platelet plug), and finally a fibrin clot forms (coagulation). Fibrinolysis is not one of the three; it is the later breakdown of the clot as the vessel heals. Failure of any step leads to hemorrhage.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D2 k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: The dorsum of the hand is the preferred location for what?
opciones: Establishing an intravenous site
Routine venous blood sampling in adults
Arterial blood gas sampling
Capillary sampling in infants
preguntas.explicacion: The median cubital vein is the common site for drawing blood; the dorsum of the hand, by contrast, is the site of choice for starting an IV line. Arterial sampling is indicated for blood gases and is done on arteries, and the capillary site the chapter names for infants is the lateral plantar surface of the heel.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3: Select the site
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D2 2O k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: The only clearly visible vein in a patient's antecubital fossa forks into two branches right at the point that would be easiest to reach. What does the WHO's Step 3 say about that spot?
opciones: Do not insert the needle where veins diverge, because it raises the chance of a hematoma
Insert the needle at the fork, because two branches give the best blood flow
Insert the needle just below the fork only if the tourniquet has been on for less than a minute
Use the fork, since the biceps aponeurosis beneath it prevents hematoma formation
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 instructs the phlebotomist not to put the needle in where the veins divide, precisely because that raises the chance of a hematoma, and to look for a vein of decent calibre, plainly visible, straight and unobstructed. The protective role of the biceps aponeurosis applies to the median cubital vein in general, not as a license to puncture a branching point.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Disorders of Clotting
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 3C bleeding disorders) · PBT I.C · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: A male patient bleeds into his joints after exercise and lacks functional factor VIII. Which disorder is this, and how common is it among hemophilias?
opciones: Hemophilia A, roughly 80 percent of cases
Hemophilia B, roughly 20 percent of cases
Hemophilia C, the rare autosomal form
Thrombocytopenia, a shortage of platelets
preguntas.explicacion: Hemophilia is a group of inherited disorders in which one or more clotting factors are not produced in functional amounts. Hemophilia A, a deficiency of factor VIII, accounts for about 80 percent of cases; hemophilia B, a deficiency of factor IX, about 20 percent. Both are X-linked and typically passed from carrier mothers to sons. Hemophilia C is a rare autosomal defect of factor XI.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Antiretroviral drugs for PEP; CDC, Clinical Guidance for PEP, Exposure to HIV is a medical emergency
preguntas.subtema: Starting PEP before results · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: The rapid HIV test on the source patient will not be back for hours. What do the WHO and CDC guidance say about starting PEP?
opciones: Start it without waiting for results; stop it later if the source proves negative
Wait for the result, since PEP is only prescribed once the source is confirmed positive
Start it only if the worker's own baseline test is negative and the 72-hour window has closed
Skip it and rely on follow-up testing at 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months
preguntas.explicacion: A health worker should not wait for test results before taking or giving PEP, and the prophylaxis can be stopped if the source turns out negative. The CDC says the same about the exposed person's own rapid test: when it has not come back and prophylaxis is indicated, the first dose goes in immediately, to be stopped later if the person has HIV or the source proves not to. The 72-hour window is the deadline for starting, not a period to wait out, and follow-up testing complements PEP rather than replacing it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antiepileptic Drug Monitoring", section Function, Patient-Specific Antiepileptic Drug Levels; and section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: Why may a level be drawn while a patient on an antiepileptic is entirely seizure-free?
opciones: It sets a benchmark to compare against if control or symptoms change
It confirms the diagnosis of epilepsy without an electroencephalogram
It takes the place of the clinical assessment of how the drug is working
It is required before any brand may be exchanged for a generic
preguntas.explicacion: A single level can reasonably be taken while the patient is seizure-free, and it then serves as a benchmark for future reference should seizure control deteriorate or symptoms of toxicity appear. Assessment of efficacy should itself be clinical, with level monitoring used as a complementary tool; epilepsy is assessed clinically with electroencephalograms and imaging.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urethral discharge culture (003750), How the Test is Performed and How to Prepare for the Test
preguntas.subtema: Urethral swab preparation · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.C · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(e) 2027
preguntas.pregunta: A man is having a urethral discharge culture collected. Which instruction protects the result?
opciones: Do not urinate for 1 hour before the test, and ideally wait 2 hours after voiding
Urinate right before the test, so the urethra is clear of any residual urine
Do not urinate for 8 hours before the test, and take no fluids at all during that time
Urinate a small amount into the toilet first, then hold the rest for the swab
preguntas.explicacion: Voiding washes away the very organisms the swab is meant to pick up, so the patient is asked not to urinate for an hour before the test and the swab is best taken at least 2 hours after the last void. The tip of the penis is cleaned with sterile cotton or gauze, and the swab goes about three-fourths of an inch, roughly 2 cm, into the urethra and is turned.

preguntas.pregunta: In a finger-prick on a small child, what can the parent be asked to do with the child's wrist to help blood flow?
opciones: Tighten and release the wrist in a steady rhythm
Hold the wrist tightly throughout, as a tourniquet
Shake the whole hand downward between the drops
Press the wrist flat, palm up, on the chair arm
preguntas.explicacion: In a child's finger-prick the parent can squeeze and let go of the wrist in a rhythm, which keeps enough blood coming. On the lap the wrist is held palm down; the palm-up hold belongs to the table position for venepuncture, where the grip on the wrist works as a tourniquet of sorts. Rubbing the finger itself is out.

preguntas.pregunta: A basic metabolic panel was drawn after the skin was prepared with povidone iodine. Which results does the WHO warn may be falsely raised?
opciones: Potassium, phosphorus and uric acid
Sodium, chloride and bicarbonate
Glucose, BUN and creatinine
Albumin, bilirubin and total protein
preguntas.explicacion: The note to Step 5 explains why alcohol is preferred over povidone iodine: blood contaminated with iodine may show falsely increased potassium, phosphorus or uric acid. The other groups are real components of the metabolic panels (electrolytes, kidney waste products, liver proteins), but the WHO does not link them to iodine contamination.

preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which two mechanisms does the WHO describe in some vacuum-tube systems for dealing with the used needle?
opciones: One retracts the needle into the barrel and snaps shut; another releases it into the sharps container
One shears the needle from the hub with a small blade; another bends it so it cannot be used a second time
One recaps the needle automatically; another sterilizes it in place for reuse on the same patient
One dissolves the needle in disinfectant; another seals it inside the last tube that was filled
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.1.1 says some systems have a mechanism that, once the needle has been used, retracts it into the barrel and snaps it shut, while others have a quick-release mechanism that dislodges the used needle straight into the sharps container. Shearing a contaminated needle, or breaking it, is forbidden by OSHA, and no source describes automatic recapping, dissolving or sealing a needle in a tube.

preguntas.subtema: Drug screen site preparation · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 · CCMA 3E k127 witness · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: Why is a bluing agent placed in the toilet before a federal drug test collection?
opciones: To keep toilet water from being used to dilute the specimen
To preserve the drug metabolites until the specimen reaches the laboratory
To disinfect the bowl between one donor and the next donor
To mark the temperature strip so the reading can be seen clearly
preguntas.explicacion: Preparing the collection area means putting a bluing agent in the toilet and, where none is available or an automatic flush is fitted, turning off the water and flushing to empty the bowl. Water sources inside the restroom are turned off or secured, soap and disinfectant are removed as potential adulterants, and places where something could be hidden are inspected. The donor is also told not to flush.

preguntas.pregunta: What does that code say about a certified professional's knowledge over time?
opciones: That learning continues and that the person keeps up with current research
That the original training is sufficient until the credential is renewed
That new techniques are learned only through the employer's own program
That research is followed only when the employer pays for the coursework
preguntas.explicacion: One of the six duties is to keep learning, applying and advancing knowledge and skills, practical and scientific alike, and to stay current with the latest research and how it is used in practice. Nothing ties that duty to who pays or who provides the course, and the very purpose of renewing the credential is to show that the holder stays current.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Lavender; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.3
preguntas.subtema: Additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: By what mechanism does the EDTA in a purple top tube keep the blood from clotting?
opciones: It binds the calcium in the sample so the coagulation cascade cannot proceed
It inhibits the formation of thrombin, as the heparin in a green tube does
It activates clotting on contact so the cells can be spun away from the serum
It blocks the breakdown of glucose, which also keeps the cells from clumping
preguntas.explicacion: EDTA works by chelating the calcium ions in the blood, and the WHO table describes the same action as forming calcium salts to remove calcium. Because the blood never clots, the liquid left after spinning is plasma. Thrombin inhibition is how heparin works, contact activation is the plain red tube, and blocking glycolysis is the sodium fluoride of the gray tube.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", section Evaluation; and MedlinePlus, Latex allergies - for hospital patients, Diagnosis
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D II.J · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: For a type I hypersensitivity to latex, which test carries the gold-standard label?
opciones: The skin prick test, though it is not available in the United States
The serum assay for bound IgE, which rarely gives a false positive
A trial of exposure to latex, run as the first step by an allergist
The blood test for latex antibodies, which is the in-vivo assay
preguntas.explicacion: Skin prick testing, an in-vivo assay that applies a non-ammoniated latex extract and watches for a wheal, is considered the gold standard for type I hypersensitivity to latex, yet it is not available in the United States for want of an approved reagent. The common serum test detects bound IgE in vitro and had significant false positives; a supervised exposure trial only confirms.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Common Pitfalls), Providing false reassurance
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 · CCMA 6 k199 k202 · CMA F.1.c / 2027 F.1.d · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: 'Don't worry, this won't hurt a bit and I never miss.' Which communication pitfall is this?
opciones: Giving false reassurance
Unsolicited advice
Changing the subject abruptly
Responding defensively
preguntas.explicacion: The pitfalls table warns that false reassurance can cause a severe rupture in the relationship, especially when the promised outcome does not happen, which a missed vein would make obvious. Unsolicited advice feels intrusive unless asked for, an abrupt change of subject reads as dismissive, and defensive replies leave the patient less room to voice frustration.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003), Risk of Infection After Exposure: HBV
preguntas.subtema: HBV transmission risk · CPT D1 k31 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C k97 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: For a susceptible worker, the CDC puts the risk of HBV infection from a single needlestick with HBV-positive blood at which figure?
opciones: 6 to 30 percent, depending on the source's HBeAg status
0.3 percent, the same figure the CDC gives for HIV
About 1.8 percent, the same as for hepatitis C
Under 0.1 percent, since most workers are vaccinated
preguntas.explicacion: A susceptible person stuck or cut with HBV-infected blood faces a 6 to 30 percent chance of infection, and where in that range depends on the source's hepatitis B e antigen status: HBsAg-positive individuals who are also HBeAg-positive carry more virus and transmit more readily. Workers who were vaccinated and developed immunity are at virtually no risk, which is why the question specifies a susceptible worker. There is no known risk from intact skin. The 0.3 and 1.8 percent figures are for HIV and HCV.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k135 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c)
preguntas.pregunta: A lavender EDTA tube for a CBC arrives with a visible red-cell clot. Which handling error is the most likely cause according to the rejection study?
opciones: Poor mixing after collection and leaving the tube lying horizontally instead of upright
Centrifuging the tube too soon, before the anticoagulant had time to dissolve
Transporting the tube in a padded holder, which stops the additive from circulating
Filling the tube above its nominal volume so that the EDTA was diluted by excess blood
preguntas.explicacion: Visible clots in anticoagulated tubes, whether red-cell clots in whole blood or fibrin in plasma, are attributed mainly to poor mixing after the draw and to tubes left horizontal rather than vertical; manufacturers and CLSI ask for gentle inversion several times to bring blood and additive into contact. Anticoagulated tubes are not centrifuged for a CBC, and racks or padded holders are the recommended way to carry tubes.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(g)(6)(i) and (g)(6)(iii), Safety data sheets
preguntas.subtema: A shipment with no SDS · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A shipment of a hazardous disinfectant arrives at a laboratory with a label but no safety data sheet. What must the employer do?
opciones: Obtain one as soon as possible from the manufacturer or the importer
Return the shipment unopened, since the sheet travels with the label
Write one from the label, which carries the same hazard information
Wait for the next shipment, which must include the updated sheet
preguntas.explicacion: Manufacturers and importers have to provide a safety data sheet with the first shipment and with the first shipment after the sheet is updated, either with the containers or beforehand. When a shipment labeled as a hazardous chemical turns up without one, the duty falls on the distributor or the employer to get one from whoever made or imported the chemical, as fast as they can, and those parties must also supply a sheet on request. A label alone is no substitute: it carries a fraction of what the sheet holds.
