preguntas.subtema: Sharps and waste disposal · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: After a routine draw, which used item does the WHO say may go into the general waste (unless local rules differ), and which must go into a puncture-resistant container?
opciones: Gloves that would not drip blood if they were squeezed may go to general waste; the needle to the sharps container
The gauze pressed on the puncture site may go to general waste; the gloves go to the sharps container
The needle may go to general waste once its safety feature is activated; the gloves go to the sharps container instead
Every item from a blood draw, gloves included, goes to the sharps container
preguntas.explicacion: Step 9 drops the used needle and syringe, or the sampling device, into a sharps container a needle cannot pierce, and places the other items in their waste category: items that would not drip blood if they were squeezed, gloves being the example, can go to the general waste unless local rules say otherwise. An activated safety feature does not turn a needle into general waste.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins" (2023), sections Structure and Function, and Physiologic Variants
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k7 (applied D2 k53 hand) · PBT I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Where does each of the two main superficial veins of the arm end once it has climbed past the shoulder?
opciones: The cephalic pierces the deep fascia at the axilla into the subclavian; the basilic joins the brachial or axillary
The basilic pierces the deep fascia at the axilla into the subclavian; the cephalic joins the brachial or axillary
Both stay superficial the whole way and empty together into the subclavian vein above the collarbone
The cephalic joins the median cubital at the elbow; the basilic runs on alone as far as the superior vena cava
preguntas.explicacion: The two superficial veins part company at the top of the arm. The cephalic goes through the deep fascia around the axilla and ends in the subclavian vein. The basilic ends earlier and less predictably: it may empty into the brachial vein or into the axillary vein, and which of the two it picks varies from person to person. Nothing of this is fixed by rule — the venous pattern of the limb is one of the most variable in the body, the basilic is usually the wider of the pair though sometimes the cephalic is, and the only constant is that everything comes back to the superior vena cava by way of the subclavian.

preguntas.pregunta: How far should an isolation gown reach when it is put on correctly?

From the neck to the ankles, with the ties left loose at the neck
From the chest to the knees, over the uniform but under the badge
preguntas.explicacion: In the donning sequence the gown goes on first, outside the patient room, and it has to cover the body from neck to knees and the arms to the wrists, and wrap around the back, with the neck and waist ties fastened if the gown has them. Gloves go on last and are pulled over the cuff of the gown, so that no skin or sleeve is left showing between the two. A gown left open at the back is not covering what it was chosen to cover.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 5 Specimen processing
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k88 · PBT III.C
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory that pipettes by robot keeps running into trouble with saliva and swab specimens that arrive thick. What goes wrong, and what is done about it?
opciones: They cause pipetting errors and contamination; they are thinned chemically or broken up with beads
They cause pipetting errors and contamination; they are diluted with the patient's own plasma
They block the extraction column alone; they are spun and only the supernatant is carried forward
They cause pipetting errors and contamination; they are pooled so one aspiration serves several
preguntas.explicacion: Sputum, saliva and swabs can arrive highly viscous, and that is where automated liquid handlers struggle: viscous material causes pipetting errors and can lead to contamination. Laboratories pretreat such specimens, either liquefying the mucus with an additive such as acetylcysteine or Sputasol, or homogenising it physically with inert beads in a sterile medium such as PBS.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet application · CPT D3 3E k60 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: When placing a peripheral IV line, how far proximal to the intended site is the tourniquet applied, and how tight?
opciones: 5 to 10 cm proximal, tight enough to swell the veins while the arterial flow continues
2 cm proximal, tight enough to abolish the radial pulse for the duration of the draw
15 to 20 cm proximal, loose enough that the veins remain flat until the fist is made
5 to 10 cm distal, tight enough to swell the veins while the arterial flow continues
preguntas.explicacion: For a peripheral line the tourniquet sits roughly 5 to 10 cm above the intended site, tight enough to swell the veins but not so tight that arterial flow stops, since engorgement is what makes the vein easy to identify and cannulate. Distal placement is the wrong side, abolishing the pulse means arterial occlusion, and 2 cm is the WHO's swab area, not a tourniquet distance.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(ii)(D), Housekeeping; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex F
preguntas.subtema: Broken glass and spills · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C5 k108 · CMA I.B.6.b / 2027 I.B.5.b · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: A tube of blood shatters on the floor of the draw room. How must the broken glass be picked up?
opciones: By mechanical means only: dust pan and brush, tongs or forceps, never by hand
With gloved hands, since gloves are the barrier the standard requires for contaminated items
With paper towels soaked in disinfectant, so the glass is decontaminated as it is lifted
With a reusable sharps container held open, so the pieces can be swept directly into it
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(D) is explicit: glassware that has broken and may carry contamination is never picked up directly with the hands, gloved or not; it is lifted mechanically, with a dust pan and brush, or with tongs or forceps. The WHO spillage annex describes the same sequence, tongs or pan and brush for the glass, which then goes into a sharps container, followed by absorbing the fluid, cleaning with detergent and applying 0.5 percent hypochlorite. Reusable sharps containers are never opened or emptied by hand under (d)(4)(iii)(A)(4).

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Clinical Guidance for PEP, Exposure to HIV is a medical emergency; CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003)
preguntas.subtema: Timing of HIV PEP · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Why does the CDC describe an HIV exposure as a medical emergency?
opciones: Infection often takes hold within 24 to 36 hours, so PEP works best when begun within hours
Antibodies appear within 24 to 36 hours, so a rapid test must be done before any PEP
PEP is only effective if started before the source patient's viral load is known
The exposed worker becomes infectious to others within 24 to 36 hours
preguntas.explicacion: HIV takes hold fast, usually 24 to 36 hours after the exposure, which is why the patient is evaluated at speed and the first dose given immediately where a rapid test result is not yet to hand and PEP is indicated. The older CDC brochure makes the same point: treatment should begin preferably within hours rather than days, since animal studies suggest the benefit falls off after 24 to 36 hours. Antibodies and infectiousness take far longer to appear, which is why follow-up testing runs on for months.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Amputation - traumatic", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k78 · CMA I.B.9.m · 2027 I.B.8.m · RMA III.I.1.b · CPT 1M k37
preguntas.pregunta: What is done first for the patient in a traumatic amputation, before the severed part is dealt with?
opciones: Airway, breathing and circulation are checked and the bleeding is controlled
The stump is rinsed with sterile saline and wrapped in a bulky dressing
The patient is walked to a chair so the injured limb can be raised
The part is searched for, since reattachment depends on finding it early
preguntas.explicacion: The patient comes before the part: airway, breathing and circulation are checked, rescue breathing, CPR or bleeding control is started if needed, and help is called. Bleeding is controlled with direct pressure and elevation, and a tight bandage or tourniquet is easier than direct pressure when the bleeding threatens life.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: Preventing syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who faints at every blood test asks what can be done between visits. Which conservative advice fits?
opciones: Lie down at the first warning sign, drink more fluid, change position slowly
Stand up quickly at the first warning sign, drink less fluid, keep the arm raised
Lie down after the test only, restrict salt intake, and avoid all morning draws
Sit upright through the warning signs, drink more fluid, and hold the breath in
preguntas.explicacion: Management of these episodes is conservative: avoid known triggers, take more fluid to improve filling, and change position slowly. Patients are taught the warning signs and told to get themselves supine when one starts, which often stops the faint and prevents a fall.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 k62 · PBT II.F II.I · CCMA 3E7 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.11
preguntas.pregunta: A prothrombin time drawn through an indwelling line comes back markedly prolonged although the patient takes no anticoagulant. What is the likely cause?
opciones: Contamination of the sample by the heparin or saline used to flush the line
Contamination of the sample by the alcohol used to disinfect the skin surface
Excess citrate from a tube that was filled well beyond its stated volume line
Loss of citrate from a tube that was inverted more than six times after filling
preguntas.explicacion: Samples taken from indwelling catheters can pick up the heparin or other solutions used to flush the line, and that artificially lengthens clotting times. Overfilling is not the recognized fault: the problem described for citrate tubes is a short draw, which leaves too much anticoagulant for the plasma.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(iii), (d)(2)(iv) and (b), Definitions: Handwashing Facilities
preguntas.subtema: Handwashing facilities · CPT D1 k33 k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What does the standard require of employers regarding handwashing facilities?
opciones: The employer must provide facilities that are readily accessible to employees
Employees may substitute alcohol hand rub at any time, even when sinks are available
A sink is required only where research or production work involves HIV and HBV
Facilities must be foot- or elbow-operated and located near the exit door of every draw room
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(iii) has the employer provide handwashing facilities that are readily accessible, and paragraph (b) says what one is: potable water that runs, soap, and either single-use towels or an air dryer. Only where such facilities are not feasible does (d)(2)(iv) allow antiseptic hand cleanser or towelettes, and even then the hands still have to reach soap and running water as soon as that becomes feasible. Foot- or elbow-operated sinks by the exit door are what (e)(4)(iii) requires of HIV and HBV production facilities, not of an ordinary draw room.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(xii), Engineering and Work Practice Controls
preguntas.subtema: Prohibited work practices · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which practice does the standard prohibit outright in areas where blood is handled?
opciones: Drawing blood or OPIM up by mouth, whether by pipette or by suction
Using a mechanical device to remove a contaminated needle when a procedure requires it
Decontaminating utility gloves for reuse when the glove is still intact
Keeping a sharps container upright and replacing it before it overfills
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xii) bans mouth pipetting and mouth suctioning of blood or OPIM with no exception. The other three are things the standard permits or requires: (d)(2)(vii)(B) allows needle removal by mechanical device or one-handed technique when the (d)(2)(vii)(A) exception applies; (d)(3)(ix)(C) allows utility gloves to be decontaminated and reused while their integrity holds; and (d)(4)(iii)(A)(2) requires sharps containers to be kept upright and replaced routinely.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Medial Antebrachial Cutaneous Nerve", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Nerve injury · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: What symptoms result from accidental damage to the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve during a venipuncture?
opciones: Painful tingling, altered sensation and numbness
Pinpoint non-blanching spots smaller than 2 mm
Pooling of blood under the skin with swelling
Lightheadedness, sweating and a brief loss of consciousness
preguntas.explicacion: The medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve is prone to injury during venipuncture, and accidental damage brings painful tingling, altered sensation and numbness; the phlebotomy chapter adds loss of sensation over the medial forearm. Pinpoint spots are petechiae, pooled blood under the skin is a hematoma, and lightheadedness, sweating and a brief loss of consciousness describe vasovagal syncope.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", Introduction; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Engineering controls
preguntas.subtema: Double gloving · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: What does wearing two pairs of gloves do for a worker who suffers a sharps injury?
opciones: It cuts the volume of blood transferred, without stopping the puncture
It stops the needle from reaching the skin when the gauge is small
It removes the need to wash hands once the outer pair comes off
It counts as an engineering control under the bloodborne standard
preguntas.explicacion: Double gloving may reduce the volume of blood that gets through during a sharps injury, but it does not stop the needle from puncturing the skin, so it is a way of lessening an exposure and not of preventing one. Hand hygiene after removing gloves is required either way, and controls that isolate or remove the hazard, such as safer needles and sharps containers, are what the standard calls engineering controls; gloves are personal protective equipment.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lactose tolerance tests (003500), How to Prepare for the Test; StatPearls, "Lactose Intolerance", section Proper Performance of Hydrogen Breath Testing
preguntas.subtema: Lactose test preparation · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.D patient preparation · CCMA 3E k139 fasting · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2 pre-test conditions
preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for lactose tolerance testing asks how to get ready. What are the instructions?
opciones: No food and no heavy exercise for the 8 hours before the test
No food for 8 hours, but light meals are allowed up to the test
No food for 12 to 16 hours and no exercise for 24 hours before
No dairy for 3 days, then a normal breakfast on the morning of the test
preguntas.explicacion: The instruction is not to eat and not to exercise heavily for eight hours before lactose tolerance testing. For the breath version the fast is at least eight hours for children and adults and at least four for infants, with no smoking for two hours before and during, and physical activity kept down for two hours to prevent hyperventilation. Dropping dairy for days beforehand is not part of the preparation.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, The ABO Blood Group; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia 003345 Blood typing, How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k5 (applied D4 4D donation) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is blood type A. Which antigen is on the red cells and which antibody circulates in the plasma?
opciones: A antigen on the red cells; anti-B antibodies in the plasma
A antigen on the red cells; anti-A antibodies in the plasma
B antigen on the red cells; anti-A antibodies in the plasma
Neither antigen; both anti-A and anti-B in the plasma
preguntas.explicacion: ABO typing looks at two glycoprotein antigens, A and B. Type A cells carry the A antigen, and because people are exposed to A and B antigens in food and microbes early in life, a type A person has naturally formed anti-B antibodies. Type B has the B antigen with anti-A, type AB has both antigens and neither antibody, and type O has no antigens but both antibodies.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 3, Hospitalized patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 k49 · PBT II.D II.I · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: An inpatient has a running peripheral IV in the left forearm. What does the WHO guidance say about drawing from it?
opciones: Do not draw from the existing access; IV fluid and hemolysis can alter results
Draw through the IV, because it spares the patient a second needle stick
Draw from the IV only if a nurse disconnects the fluids for the sample
Drawing from the IV is acceptable, though not ideal, at any time
preguntas.explicacion: In a hospitalized patient, an existing peripheral line is not used as the draw site: hemolysis, contamination, and the intravenous fluid and medication running through it can all falsify results. Nurses and physicians may sample central lines under protocol, with a contamination risk attached, and the case called acceptable but not ideal is drawing as the device is first inserted, before the fluids are connected.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(vi) and (d)(3)(i), Personal Protective Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Penetrated garments · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Blood soaks through a phlebotomist's gown to the scrubs underneath. When must the gown come off?
opciones: Immediately, or as soon as feasible
Once the procedure has been completed
At the end of the shift, with other coverings
After hands are washed and gloves changed
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(vi) says that a garment penetrated by blood or OPIM is removed immediately or as soon as feasible. The standard defines appropriate PPE in (d)(3)(i) as equipment that does not let blood reach work clothes, street clothes, undergarments or skin under normal conditions of use, so a gown that has been soaked through has stopped being appropriate. End of shift is the timing given for surfaces and protective coverings in (d)(4)(ii), not for garments; handwashing follows removal, it does not precede it.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Caring for Older Patients With Cognitive Impairment, Tips for communicating with a patient who has cognitive impairment
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 k49 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(6)(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(6)(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dementia looks lost when asked, 'Have you eaten, taken your pills, or had any coffee since midnight?' How should the questioning be reworked?
opciones: Ask one thing at a time, in yes-or-no form, and re-explain who you are
Repeat the whole question more loudly and quickly to hold his attention
Switch to open-ended questions so that he can tell the story in his own words
Put every question to the caregiver, since he cannot answer reliably
preguntas.explicacion: With cognitive impairment: address the patient directly with simple wording, one idea at a time, using yes-or-no or multiple-choice questions; help orient the patient by explaining or re-explaining who you are and what you will do; and avoid speaking too quickly or loudly. Yes-or-no questions also help when the patient struggles with open ones.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: CPR - adult and child after onset of puberty, Considerations and First Aid
preguntas.subtema: Compression depth and time · CPT D1 1L k38 · CMA I.B.9.c / 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10
preguntas.pregunta: How deep are adult chest compressions, and how soon can permanent brain damage begin once blood flow stops?
opciones: About 2 inches (5 cm); damage can begin in as little as 4 minutes
About 1 inch (2.5 cm); damage can begin after 10 minutes
About 3 inches (7.5 cm); damage can begin after 2 minutes
About 2 inches (5 cm); damage can begin only after 15 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: Compressions press the adult chest down about 2 inches, 5 centimeters, hard and fast without pausing, and the chest is allowed to rise all the way between them. Time is why CPR cannot wait: four minutes without blood flow is enough for permanent brain damage, or for death, and death may follow 4 to 6 minutes after that, so compressions continue until heartbeat and breathing return or trained help takes over. Where the person is breathing normally, coughing or moving, compressions are not started.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 4.1 Time, temperature and freeze-thaw cycles
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k88 · PBT III.C III.D.1 · CCMA 3E11 k140 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: Whole blood for a PCR assay cannot be extracted until next week. Which storage plan follows the recommendations?
opciones: Separate the plasma or serum from the red cells and store it at −20 °C or colder
Freeze the whole blood tube at −20 °C or colder until the extraction can be done
Keep the whole blood tube at 2 to 8 °C, where it stays stable indefinitely for DNA
Keep the whole blood tube at room temperature, since cold storage lyses the white cells
preguntas.explicacion: Whole blood is not stored below 0 °C: when a frozen sample thaws, heme is released, and heme inhibits the polymerase and quenches the fluorophores used to detect the product. If extraction cannot happen within an acceptable time the erythrocytes are removed and the plasma or serum is frozen at −20 °C or colder. There is no absolute limit for whole blood at room temperature or 2 to 8 °C, but prolonged storage there raises the risk of hemolysis and of nucleic acid degradation from white cell lysis.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Fill level · CPT D3 k59 k51 k9 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A gray top tube for glucose is drawn short and the laboratory reports the sample as hemolyzed. What does the WHO table say about this tube?
opciones: It requires a full draw, because a short draw may cause hemolysis
It requires a half draw, because its additive is concentrated for small volumes
It needs no fill requirement, since fluoride keeps glucose stable for five days
It should be filled last only when a hemolyzed sample is expected
preguntas.explicacion: In the uses column for the oxalate/fluoride tube, Table 2.3 states that glucose specimens require a full draw and that a short draw may cause hemolysis. The five-day glucose stability is a separate property of the antiglycolytic agent and does not remove the fill requirement. The gray tube is drawn last (position 10) in every case, not only when hemolysis is suspected.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.3
preguntas.subtema: Specimen preparation · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A test must be run on plasma. Which tubes will supply it?
opciones: The heparin tubes, the EDTA tube and the citrate tube
The clot activator tube and the serum separator tube alone
The clot activator tube, the citrate tube and the EDTA tube
The serum separator tube and the light green separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: Plasma comes from tubes whose additive stops the blood from clotting: heparin in the green tubes, EDTA in the purple tube and citrate in the light blue tube, which is why coagulation testing uses plasma. The red clot activator tube and the gold separator tube are the ones that yield serum.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 9: Address Language Differences, Never use unacceptable language access services; and Finance language access services
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A bilingual receptionist offers to interpret the pre-draw questions. Why are staff untrained as healthcare interpreters ruled out?

Their interpreting time cannot be reimbursed by any state Medicaid program
They cannot be listed in the practice directory of bilingual clinicians
They are barred from signing the practice's interpreter ethics statement
preguntas.explicacion: The unacceptable services include a clinician or a staff member whose command of both languages falls short, and anyone not trained or certified as a healthcare interpreter, because research shows that people untrained in interpreting make more clinically significant mistakes. Medicaid reimbursement for interpreters is in fact available in a number of states.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, How to Obtain a CLIA Certificate, What are the different CLIA certificate types?
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F Laboratory Regulations, CLIA · CPT D5 k90 laboratory requirements · RMA III.C.1 CLIA '88
preguntas.pregunta: How long is a CLIA certificate valid, and how many certificate types does the CLIA program have?
opciones: Two years, and the program has five certificate types in all
Two years, and the program has three certificate types in all
One year, and the program has five certificate types in all
Three years, and the program has four certificate types in all
preguntas.explicacion: Every certificate type runs for two years, and there are five of them: waiver, provider-performed microscopy, registration, compliance and accreditation. The one held has to match the highest complexity of testing performed. Registration is the temporary one and it is not chosen on the application: it goes to whoever applies for compliance or accreditation, and it lasts until the survey is done.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014); and StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Specific Gravity)
preguntas.subtema: Refrigeration and crystals · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.3 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.8.c.(1)
preguntas.pregunta: Which urine examination is disturbed when the specimen is refrigerated before it is examined?
opciones: Crystal identification, because cold precipitates phosphates and urates in the sediment
Leukocyte esterase, because cold destroys the enzyme within 1 hour of refrigeration
Bacterial culture, because cold stops growth so the colony count becomes falsely low
Specific gravity, because cold urine reads falsely high on the refractometer
preguntas.explicacion: Refrigeration is the preferred way to hold urine, but it makes phosphates and urates precipitate, which can confuse the analysis of those analytes; when crystal differentiation is requested a separate aliquot is kept unrefrigerated. Refrigeration preserves, rather than lowers, the colony count for culture, and the documented false elevations of specific gravity are from dextran, intravenous contrast and proteinuria, not cold.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Section 9: Physical and Chemical Properties
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 9 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which information belongs to section 9 of a safety data sheet, Physical and Chemical Properties?
opciones: Appearance, odor, pH, flash point, boiling range and vapor pressure
Signal word, pictograms, hazard statements and the classification
Permissible exposure limits, ventilation advice and glove material
Symptoms of exposure, the LD50 figure and any carcinogen listing
preguntas.explicacion: Section 9 is the list of measurable properties: appearance and physical state, odor and odor threshold, pH, melting and freezing point, initial boiling point and range, flash point, evaporation rate, flammability, upper and lower flammability limits, vapor pressure and density, relative density, solubility, partition coefficient, auto-ignition and decomposition temperatures, and viscosity. When an item is not relevant or not available, the sheet has to say so rather than leave a blank.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, Clinical Safety guidance, duration; StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Technique
preguntas.subtema: Duration of hand hygiene · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 k102 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How long should an alcohol hand rub take, and how long should hands be rubbed with soap and water, according to the CDC?
opciones: About 20 seconds for the rub; at least 15 seconds of rubbing for the wash
About 2 to 6 minutes for the rub; at least 20 seconds for the wash
About 10 seconds for the rub; at least 60 seconds for the wash
About 30 seconds for the rub; at least 30 seconds for the wash
preguntas.explicacion: Rubbing sanitizer over every surface of the hands until they dry takes around 20 seconds; with soap and water the hands are scrubbed briskly against each other for 15 seconds at the least. Either duration is acceptable. StatPearls gives the same numbers: 3 to 5 mL of rub for some 20 seconds, and a wash of at least 15 to 20 seconds covering palms, backs, wrists, between the fingers, the thumbs and under the nails. Two to six minutes is a surgical scrub, not routine hand hygiene.

They may be renewed indefinitely without a new assessment
They may be issued by any staff member trained in restraint use
preguntas.explicacion: Restraint or seclusion may be used only to secure the patient's immediate physical safety, or that of staff or of others, never as coercion, as discipline, for the convenience of staff or as payback, and only once less restrictive measures have failed, on the order of a physician or another licensed practitioner responsible for that patient. Such an order is never written as a standing order, nor on a PRN basis. For violent behavior each order runs at most 4 hours for adults, 2 hours from ages 9 to 17 and 1 hour under 9, to a total of 24 hours, with a face-to-face evaluation inside 1 hour, and the intervention stops as soon as it can.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L 2N k48 k52 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k126 k128 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports that he fainted during his last two blood draws. What is the correct preparation?
opciones: Have him lie down if possible, reassure him, and be ready for a syncope
Draw quickly while he stands, so that he can walk the dizziness off afterwards
Ask him to watch the needle closely so that he stays alert throughout
Postpone the draw until he returns with a signed consent form
preguntas.explicacion: Patients who fear blood tests or have a history of vasovagal attacks during earlier draws are identified specifically so the team is prepared to act on a syncope; with a severe history of panic the patient may be asked to lie down, and the WHO step 2 asks about previous fainting and tells the phlebotomist to reassure an anxious patient. Supine positioning is the WHO default where possible.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Iron Tests, sections What are they used for, and Will I need to do anything to prepare
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k45 k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: Why are iron tests usually done in the morning, often after a 12-hour fast?
opciones: Blood iron varies through the day and may be higher in the morning
Blood iron peaks around 4 p.m., so the morning gives a trough value
Blood iron is stable in serum for only two hours after waking
Blood iron falls once the 24-hour glycogen stores have been used up
preguntas.explicacion: How much iron is in the blood shifts across the day, and the morning figure may be the higher one, so the test is usually done in the morning and the provider may ask for a 12-hour fast beforehand. The 4 p.m. low point describes cortisol, and the 24-hour glycogen figure comes from the physiology of fasting rather than from iron testing.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 lancet depth · PBT II.J lancets · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.5 equipment by age · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: What is the maximum puncture depth for a heel-prick?
opciones: 2.4 mm
1.5 mm
3.3 mm
preguntas.explicacion: A heel-prick goes no deeper than 2.4 mm, and a 0.85 mm lancet exists for premature neonates. The 1.5 mm figure is the recommended finger-prick depth for a child over 6 months and under 8 years, and 3.32 mm is the skin-to-bone distance at the medial and lateral heel of a 3 kg baby, not a puncture depth.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Blood Specimens); PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5B · PBT III.A.2 III.D.1 · CCMA 3E10 3E14 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d)
preguntas.pregunta: Blood for serological testing is drawn at a rural clinic in midsummer and sent by car to the laboratory. Which two handling points apply to that specimen?
opciones: Let the blood clot before processing, and protect the sample from extreme temperatures during transport
Centrifuge the tube immediately after the draw, and keep the sample frozen at −20 °C during transport
Mix the tube by five inversions to prevent clotting, and keep the sample at 37 °C during transport
Let the blood clot before processing, and keep the sample on wet ice during the whole transport
preguntas.explicacion: For serological testing the blood is allowed to clot before it is processed, the specimen goes into properly labeled containers, and during transport it is protected from extreme temperatures; serum for prompt serology is then stored at 2 to 8 °C, and only long-term storage or delayed transport calls for freezing at −20 °C or lower. Spinning before the clot has formed is what produces fibrin in the serum, and wet ice is the transport rule for other specimen types.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Infection Control in Healthcare Personnel (2019), section 7, Reporting HCP exposures and illnesses; OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Recordkeeping
preguntas.subtema: Reporting device problems · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k96 · CMA I.B.11.c / 2027 I.B.10.c · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: A safety needle's shield failed to activate and caused a needlestick. Besides the internal report, where can the device problem be reported, according to the CDC?
opciones: To the FDA MedWatch database, voluntarily, so device hazards can be identified
To the state health department, which requires reports of all device failures
To the Ryan White notification system for emergency response personnel
To OSHA within 24 hours, as with work-related hospitalizations
preguntas.explicacion: Adverse events involving medical devices can expose personnel to infection, and devices involved because of a quality problem can be reported to the FDA MedWatch database; the reporting is voluntary but helps identify device hazards that may warrant review. State reporting requirements concern notifiable infections in persons, not device failures. The Ryan White Act covers notification of emergency responders exposed to selected diseases, and the 24-hour OSHA report is for inpatient hospitalizations, amputations and eye loss.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, rows 5, 6 and 10
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A gold serum separator tube, a dark green heparin tube and a light gray fluoride tube are all ordered. In which sequence are they filled?
opciones: Gold separator tube, then dark green heparin, then light gray fluoride
Dark green heparin, then gold separator tube, then light gray fluoride
Light gray fluoride, then gold separator tube, then dark green heparin
Gold separator tube, then light gray fluoride, then dark green heparin
preguntas.explicacion: The gold or tiger top separator tube holds position 5, the dark green heparin tube position 6 and the fluoride/oxalate tube position 10, the last one used. The sequence therefore runs separator tube, heparin tube, fluoride tube, and the fluoride tube is always the one left for the end.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: Of the ten tube types listed in the WHO order of draw, which one is drawn last when it is needed?
opciones: The light gray oxalate/fluoride tube
The purple EDTA hematology tube
The pale yellow acid-citrate-dextrose tube
The light green plasma separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: Position 10 of Table 2.3 belongs to the light gray tube with sodium fluoride and potassium oxalate, used for glucose. The purple EDTA tube is number 8, the pale yellow ACD tube for HLA typing and DNA studies is number 9, and the light green PST with lithium heparin and gel is number 7. Footnote a explains that 1 means draw first and 10 means draw last, if that tube is used at all.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Semen analysis (003627), How the Test is Performed; and StatPearls, "Semen Analysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Semen transport · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient collects a semen sample at home. What should he be told about getting it to the laboratory?
opciones: Bring it within 30 minutes, carried in an inside coat pocket so it stays at body temperature
Bring it within 30 minutes, carried in an insulated bag with a cold pack so that it stays chilled
Bring it within 6 hours, carried in an inside coat pocket so it stays at body temperature
Bring it whenever convenient, since the laboratory warms every specimen to 37 degrees anyway
preguntas.explicacion: A home-collected specimen should reach the laboratory inside 30 minutes, kept warm in an inside coat pocket at body temperature, and a specialist has to examine it within 2 hours of collection; the sooner it is read, the more reliable the result. Chilling is the wrong direction, since the container is meant to stay between 20 and 37 degrees Celsius so that dehydration and temperature swings do not damage the sperm.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Cubital Fossa" (2023), section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k7 (applied D2 k53) · PBT I.A.2 I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In the cubital fossa, where does the brachial artery run relative to the biceps tendon, and where is the median nerve?
opciones: The artery just medial to the tendon; the median nerve most medial of all
The artery just lateral to the tendon; the median nerve most lateral of all
The artery deep to the median cubital vein in the roof; the nerve lateral
The artery only at the apex of the fossa; the radial nerve most medial
preguntas.explicacion: The contents of the fossa run from lateral to medial: the radial nerve near the brachioradialis, the biceps tendon, the brachial artery just medial to that tendon, and the median nerve, the most medial structure, usually passing between the two heads of pronator teres. The artery divides into radial and ulnar arteries at the apex. The median cubital vein is not inside the fossa but in its roof.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, How to Understand Your Lab Results, What is a reference range?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2M k15 · PBT II.B · CCMA 4 k160 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why her cholesterol figure cannot be set beside the one another laboratory gave her last year. Why not?
opciones: Laboratories use different methods, so their reference ranges differ
Laboratories report in different units, and only the units differ
Laboratories keep results on file for a single calendar year only
Laboratories round the figures differently when they issue reports
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratories often work with different testing methods, and so they describe a normal result against different reference ranges. A figure therefore has to be read against the range printed on its own report, and results from two laboratories cannot be set side by side. Anyone looking for a trend over time is told to try to use the same laboratory each time.

preguntas.fuente: eCFR, 21 CFR 862.1675, Blood specimen collection device, paragraphs (a) and (b)
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Under 21 CFR 862.1675, how does the FDA define and classify a blood specimen collection device?
opciones: A device to collect and handle blood specimens and separate serum from cellular components; Class II
A device to collect and handle blood specimens and separate serum from cellular components; Class I device
A device carrying a feature that retracts or shields the needle after use; Class III
A device to transfer blood between tubes without additive carry-over; Class II
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation identifies a blood specimen collection device as one meant to collect and handle blood specimens, and to part the serum from the cellular components before testing, and says the type takes in tubes, vials, whole systems, serum separators, collection trays and vacuum sample tubes. Paragraph (b) assigns it to Class II. Sharps injury prevention features are covered by a separate FDA guidance.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sputum Analysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Sputum mouth rinse · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.3 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(4) · RMA III.C.4.a.v · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: What should a patient do just before coughing a sputum specimen into the container?
opciones: Rinse the mouth with plain water for 10 to 15 seconds and spit the saliva out
Rinse the mouth with an antiseptic mouthwash and spit the rinse out completely
Eat a light breakfast so the cough reflex is stronger and the sputum comes up
Hold the breath for 10 to 15 seconds, which loosens secretions from the airway
preguntas.explicacion: Rinsing with clear water for 10 to 15 seconds clears contaminants out of the mouth, and the saliva is spat out before the patient takes three deep breaths and coughs at roughly two-minute intervals until sputum arrives. The best time for a deep-cough sample is first thing in the morning, before anything is eaten or drunk. Antiseptic mouthwash is what is specifically avoided before a throat swab.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Blood Specimens)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5B · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3 · CCMA 3E14 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: Serum for hepatitis serology will not reach the reference laboratory for another six days. How should it be stored in the meantime?
opciones: Frozen at −20 °C or lower, the rule for long-term storage or delayed transport
Refrigerated at 2 to 8 °C, the rule for serum awaiting prompt serological testing
At room temperature away from extremes, the rule for specimens while in transit
Frozen at −70 °C, the rule for specimens that must keep the virus intact for culture
preguntas.explicacion: Serum meant for prompt serological testing waits at 2 to 8 °C, but when transport is delayed or storage will be long the specimen is frozen at −20 °C or lower. Protection from temperature extremes applies while the sample travels, and −70 °C is the transport temperature for viral culture specimens, so each distractor is a real instruction attached to the wrong situation. The blood must also have clotted before the serum is processed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Interfering Factors (preservatives)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: A ward sends a preserved 24-hour urine and asks for a dipstick from the same jug. Which pairing of preservative and false result is correct?
opciones: Thymol reads as albumin; mercury salts read as no leukocyte esterase
Thymol reads as glucose; mercury salts read as no urobilinogen present
Thymol reads as no albumin; mercury salts read as leukocyte esterase
Thymol reads as nitrite; mercury salts read as no bilirubin present
preguntas.explicacion: A preservative keeps the collection usable and distorts the strip at the same time. Thymol fakes a positive albumin and mercury salts push leukocyte esterase falsely negative. Formaldehyde is the broad offender, faking positives for glucose, urobilinogen, the peroxidase reaction and leukocyte esterase alike; hydrochloric acid moves the pH, and boric acid blunts the leukocyte pad.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.4, Availability of appropriate supplies
preguntas.subtema: Safety-engineered devices · CPT D3 3A k54 k66 · D1 1A k24 · PBT II.J VI.G · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomy service is choosing safety-engineered devices for the first time. What is asked of it before the purchase?
opciones: Investigate their use, fit with current practice and protective value
Buy whichever device the largest hospital in the region already uses
Buy the cheapest device available, since all are cleared for the task
Trial each device on staff volunteers before any patient is drawn
preguntas.explicacion: Safety-engineered devices cut exposure to blood and injuries, but not every one of them suits phlebotomy. Users are asked to investigate the devices available thoroughly, looking at how they are meant to be used, how they fit current practice and how well they protect staff and patients.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Ready?: What are the Types of Controls? (internal controls)
preguntas.subtema: Internal (procedural) controls · CPT D1 1F · PBT IV.B.3 · CCMA 3D k115 · CMA I.C.9.c · RMA III.C.1.a.ii · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: On a rapid pregnancy cassette, what does the built-in control line tell the operator?
opciones: That the device worked and enough sample migrated through the strip; not whether the result is right
That the whole process, from applying the sample through to interpreting it, was carried out correctly
That the result is positive, because a control line only develops in the presence of the analyte
That the kit lot has passed the manufacturer's quality control and is within its expiration date
preguntas.explicacion: Internal, procedural or built-in controls check that the test itself is functioning: the sample volume was adequate, the fluid moved through the strip, and any electronic functions worked. They do not prove the operator handled the whole process correctly; that is what an external control, run like a patient sample, is for. A missing control line means an invalid test, whatever the result window shows.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings; Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Critical value vs STAT · CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT IV.C · CCMA 3D3 k116 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement correctly distinguishes a critical value from a STAT test result?
opciones: A critical value is defined only by how far it lies outside the normal range; a STAT test is designated by the ordering clinician
A critical value is designated by the ordering clinician; a STAT result is any value that falls outside the reference range
A critical value is any result outside the reference range; a STAT result is one that was reported within an hour of collection
A critical value is a result the instrument flags as invalid; a STAT test is one that must be confirmed by a second method
preguntas.explicacion: A critical value sits so far outside the normal range that it flags possible pathology, and the definition rests on that distance alone, whatever state the patient is in. A STAT or urgent test is the other thing entirely: the ordering clinician designates it, usually already knowing how the patient is doing. Both are handled post-analytically, when findings go to the treatment team.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003), Follow-up After an Exposure: HIV; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Testing and counselling
preguntas.subtema: HIV follow-up schedule · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: How long is an exposed worker followed with HIV antibody testing after an occupational exposure?
opciones: Baseline, then periodically for at least 6 months, for example at 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months
Baseline and one repeat at 7 days, when the 28-day PEP course is one quarter done
Baseline and one repeat at 1 to 2 months, the schedule used after the hepatitis B series
Baseline only, since a negative rapid test rules out infection from that exposure
preguntas.explicacion: HIV antibody is tested as soon as possible after exposure and periodically for at least 6 months, typically at 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months; WHO's annex uses baseline, 6 to 12 weeks and 6 months. Workers on PEP also have blood counts and kidney and liver tests before and 2 weeks after starting. The 1-to-2-month test is the anti-HBs check after hepatitis B vaccination, and a baseline test only shows the worker's status at the time of exposure.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, PEP not indicated; CDC, Exposure to Blood (2003), Risk of Infection: HIV; CDC, Clinical Guidance for PEP
preguntas.subtema: When PEP is not indicated · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: For which of these exposures do the CDC and WHO guidance say HIV post-exposure prophylaxis is NOT indicated?
opciones: A few drops of blood on intact skin
A splash of blood into the eye
A needlestick with a hollow-bore needle
Blood contact with a fresh abrasion on the hand
preguntas.explicacion: When a potentially infectious fluid meets skin that is intact, there is no indication for HIV or hepatitis B prophylaxis; the same holds for fluids not known to transmit HIV, such as feces, saliva, urine or sweat. The CDC adds that a few drops of blood landing on skin that is whole most likely carry no risk, and that no such transmission has ever been documented; its PEP guidance keeps mucous membranes, non-intact skin and perforated skin as the routes worth considering. An eye splash, a hollow-bore needlestick and an abrasion are all on that list.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.4 and Table 7.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k49 age as a special consideration · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 site by age
preguntas.pregunta: Why are finger-pricks not performed on neonates?
opciones: Puncturing the fingers of a neonate can leave nerve damage behind
Neonatal fingers have no capillary bed close to the skin surface
The fingerprint lines are not formed, so the lancet cannot be oriented
Neonatal fingers are callused from grasping, so the flow is poor
preguntas.explicacion: Puncturing a neonate's fingers is listed among the complications of capillary sampling, on account of nerve damage. That fits the site table, which gives the heel-prick from birth to about 6 months and 3 to 10 kg, and the finger-prick only above 6 months and 10 kg. Calluses are the concern for the feet of children already walking.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2L k48 · PBT II.B II.D · CCMA 3E1 k126 · CMA F.1.c / 2027 F.1.d · RMA I.D.1.c · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says 'I hate needles' and begins to tremble. What does WHO step 2 direct?
opciones: Reassure her, and ask what would help her feel more comfortable
Tell the patient firmly that it will not hurt at all this time
Proceed as quickly as possible before the anxiety builds further
Ask a colleague to hold the arm firmly while you perform the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 says that where the patient is anxious or afraid, the health worker gives reassurance and asks what would help them feel more at ease. Promising that it will not hurt is the false reassurance listed among therapeutic communication pitfalls, rushing ignores the patient, and holding somebody down is a pediatric immobilization technique, not a response to an anxious adult.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Injection Safety: Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices, Key points for medication preparation
preguntas.subtema: Aseptic medication preparation · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C7 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A colleague leaves a needle inserted in a medication vial's septum between doses. Why does the CDC object?
opciones: It opens a direct route for microorganisms into the vial and its contents
It counts as recapping, which the bloodborne pathogens standard prohibits
It exposes the drug to light and reduces its potency within minutes
It is acceptable in a clean medication area away from patient treatment
preguntas.explicacion: A needle is never parked in a vial septum between doses, because it leaves microorganisms an open road into the vial and into what it holds; any vial whose sterility is compromised or in doubt is discarded. The same section asks that medications be drawn up in a designated clean area away from sinks, as near to administration time as possible. Recapping is a sharps rule about the cap of a used needle, a different hazard, and none of this has to do with light.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 7.1.3 and 6.1.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3P k72 · PBT II.H.2 II.I · CCMA 3E4 site by condition · NCMA 2C.5
preguntas.pregunta: An order for a child calls for four different specimen types by skin puncture. What is the best approach?
opciones: Consider venipuncture, which may give more accurate results when more than two specimens are needed
Collect all four by skin puncture, starting with blood bank so the largest volume comes first
Collect two by heel-prick and two by finger-prick, so that no single site is over-punctured
Collect all four from one puncture, squeezing gently between specimens to keep the flow going
preguntas.explicacion: Where a skin puncture would have to yield more than two specimens, the laboratory result is likely to be more accurate from a venepuncture. Capillary blood also serves only a limited range of tests, both because skin flora contaminate it and because there is so little of it. Squeezing dilutes the specimen with tissue fluid and makes hemolysis likelier.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A red top tube is sent to the laboratory for a prothrombin time. Why will it be rejected?
opciones: Coagulation tests need plasma; serum has lost its clotting factors
Coagulation tests need serum; the red tube gives plasma instead
The red tube clots too slowly, beyond the 60 minutes the test allows
The clot activator in the red tube binds the calcium the test measures
preguntas.explicacion: Coagulation testing is done on plasma, never on serum, because the clotting factors are removed when serum forms. The correct specimen is a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate, which chelates calcium and holds the sample in stasis until calcium chloride is added in the laboratory. The clot activator does not bind calcium; it does the opposite, it lets the blood clot.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Engineering Controls, Work Practice Controls; NIOSH, Bloodborne Infectious Disease Risk Factors, Hierarchy of Controls
preguntas.subtema: Engineering vs work practice controls · CPT D1 k12 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A self-sheathing needle is an example of which type of control under the standard?
opciones: An engineering control, which isolates or removes the hazard from the workplace
A work practice control, which changes the way a task is performed
Personal protective equipment, which is used when exposure remains after controls
An administrative control, such as the annual review of the Exposure Control Plan
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b) lists self-sheathing needles, sharps disposal containers and sharps with engineered injury protections as engineering controls: devices that wall off the bloodborne pathogen hazard or take it out of the workplace. A work practice control changes how the task is done, and the example the standard itself gives is the ban on two-handed recapping. PPE is specialized clothing or equipment the employee wears. NIOSH's hierarchy puts elimination and substitution first, then work practices and administrative controls, then engineering controls, with PPE last.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.3 Modes of Disease Transmission, Reservoirs and Carriers
preguntas.subtema: Asymptomatic carriers · CPT D1 1K k11 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C k94 · CMA I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which pathogens are named as often being passed on by carriers who show no symptoms?
opciones: HIV, hepatitis B virus and herpes simplex virus
Salmonella typhi, Clostridium tetani and hantavirus
Influenza virus, measles virus and Bordetella pertussis
Clostridioides difficile, norovirus and scabies mites
preguntas.explicacion: An active carrier who shows no sign or symptom despite being infected is an asymptomatic carrier, and HIV, hepatitis B virus and herpes simplex virus are the three the microbiology text names as often spread that way; Typhoid Mary is the historical example, for Salmonella typhi. It is one reason blood is handled under Universal and Standard Precautions whatever the chart says. Clostridium tetani is the example of a pathogen persisting in a nonliving reservoir, and hantavirus the example of dust-borne vehicle transmission.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Health Topic: Patient Rights, Summary; 42 CFR 482.13(b)(2)
preguntas.subtema: Federal patient rights · CPT D1 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k215 · CMA II.E.1.d · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: Which patient right is guaranteed by federal law, as opposed to a facility's own bill of rights?
opciones: The right to a copy of one's medical records and to keep them private
The right to receive any treatment the patient requests, regardless of medical necessity
The right to free care in any hospital that accepts Medicare
The right to choose which staff member performs each procedure
preguntas.explicacion: Some patient rights are guaranteed by federal law, notably the right to get a copy of one's medical records and to have them kept private and secure; many states add protections, and insurers, medical organizations and facilities publish their own non-enforceable bills of rights. Other common rights are respectful treatment, freedom from discrimination, the right to refuse treatment and informed consent. The CMS condition adds that the right to make informed decisions is not a mechanism to demand treatment that is medically unnecessary.

preguntas.subtema: Common tests · CPT D3 k57 D2 k47 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient on warfarin comes in for routine monitoring. Which test and tube are expected?
opciones: A PT/INR in a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate
A PTT test in a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate
A PT/INR in a lavender tube with EDTA
A CBC with differential in a lavender tube with EDTA
preguntas.explicacion: The PT/INR is used most often to check how well warfarin (Coumadin) is preventing clots, with the INR letting providers compare results from different laboratories, and the specimen goes in a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate. The PTT is the test linked to monitoring heparin, and EDTA is the hematology anticoagulant.

preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient loses consciousness during a draw. Which set of findings fits a vasovagal episode while it is happening?
opciones: Slow pulse, low blood pressure, pallor and heavy sweating
Fast pulse, high blood pressure, flushing and dry warm skin
Slow pulse, high blood pressure, flushing and heavy sweating
Fast pulse, low blood pressure, pallor and a bitten tongue
preguntas.explicacion: During the event the patient is typically bradycardic and hypotensive, pale and diaphoretic, and consciousness returns without help. A bitten tongue points instead towards a seizure, which is why it is looked for afterwards along with any sign of injury from a fall.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", sections Testing Procedures and Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings; MedlinePlus, Glucose tolerance test (003466), Normal Results
preguntas.subtema: OGTT samples · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139 timed specimens
preguntas.pregunta: Which two plasma glucose measurements define a standard 75-g OGTT for diagnosing type 2 diabetes?
opciones: Fasting and 2 hours after the load
Fasting and 1 hour after the load
1 hour and 3 hours after the load
30 minutes and 2 hours after the load
preguntas.explicacion: Venous plasma glucose is measured fasting and two hours after the oral load, and the 2-hour value is the one that makes the diagnosis: under 140 mg/dL is normal, 140 to 199 is impaired glucose tolerance and 200 or more is diabetes. Some protocols draw every 30 to 60 minutes for up to three hours, and a 1-hour reference (under 200) exists, but the diagnostic pair is fasting plus 2 hours.

preguntas.pregunta: In a published table of critical limits for urgent clinician notification, which adult glucose values require the physician to be notified immediately?
opciones: Below 45 mg/dL (2.5 mmol/L) or above 500 mg/dL (27.8 mmol/L)
Below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) or above 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L)
Below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L) or above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L)
Below 25 mg/dL (1.3 mmol/L) or above 600 mg/dL (33.3 mmol/L)
preguntas.explicacion: The table of adult and pediatric critical limits sets glucose at below 45 mg/dL (2.5 mmol/L), where neuroglycopenic symptoms up to loss of consciousness occur, and above 500 mg/dL (27.8 mmol/L), the range of diabetic coma with osmotic diuresis and ketoacidosis; the limits apply after confirmation by repeat measurement in the same sample. The other pairs mix thresholds from elsewhere: 70 and 54 mg/dL mark hypoglycemia levels, 25 mg/dL is the neonatal limit, and 600 mg/dL characterizes the hyperosmolar state.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Please sit down and make yourself comfortable; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia (patient instructions): Latex allergies - for hospital patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: The WHO pre-draw interview asks specifically about allergies to which three items?
opciones: Latex, povidone iodine and tape
Latex, alcohol and chlorhexidine
Bananas, avocado and kiwi
Vinyl, silicone and neoprene
preguntas.explicacion: The Annex C interview asks whether the patient is allergic to anything, and it names three items to raise explicitly: latex, povidone iodine and tape. Bananas, avocado and kiwi are the fruits of the latex-fruit syndrome, a reason to probe further rather than the question itself, and vinyl, silicone and neoprene are the latex alternatives used once an allergy is known.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding, Symptoms and First Aid
preguntas.subtema: Shock position · CPT D1 1M k37 · CMA I.B.9.a / 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who cut himself badly is pale and clammy. Besides controlling the bleeding, what position does first aid recommend?
opciones: Lay him flat, raise the feet about 12 inches, and cover him with a blanket
Sit him upright with the head between the knees to improve breathing
Lay him on his side in the recovery position with the legs straight
Stand him up and walk him slowly to keep blood circulating
preguntas.explicacion: Pallor, clammy skin, a fast pulse, dizziness and confusion are the signs of shock from blood loss. For severe bleeding the guidance is to call for help, keep the injured part still, get the person lying flat with the feet propped about 12 inches, 30 centimeters, off the ground, and cover them with a coat or a blanket, avoiding movement where an injury to head, neck, back or leg is possible. Lying down also makes fainting less likely, since blood reaches the brain more easily. The recovery position is for someone breathing after CPR, not for shock.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1 Devices for drawing blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 k54 blood collection devices · PBT II.J lancets · NCMA 2C.5 capillary equipment
preguntas.pregunta: What safety advantage do retractable lancets offer?
opciones: They retract and prevent needle-stick injuries
They allow many samples from one puncture
They eliminate transfer of blood into tubes
They can be heparinized for arterial blood
preguntas.explicacion: In the classification of blood-drawing devices, lancets appear among the passive safety-engineered devices with a single entry: retractable, they prevent needle-stick injuries. The other features belong to other rows of the same table: multiple samples from one venepuncture and no blood transfer are advantages of vacuum-tube systems, and heparinized use for arterial blood is listed for the hypodermic needle and syringe.

preguntas.subtema: Donor physical assessment · CPT D4 4D k82 complete screening
preguntas.pregunta: A prospective donor's blood pressure reads 186/86 mm Hg. What does the regulation require?
opciones: The responsible physician must examine and document before she may donate
She is permanently deferred, since systolic pressure over 180 is disqualifying
She may donate, because only the diastolic reading is used for screening
She is deferred for 8 weeks and asked to return with a physician's note
preguntas.explicacion: Systolic pressure must not read above 180 or below 90 mm Hg, and diastolic must not read above 100 or below 50. A donor outside those limits may still be allowed to donate, but only after the responsible physician has examined her and has determined, in writing, that giving blood would not harm her health. A pulse that is irregular or out of range has an escape clause of its own, and there the physician determines and documents without examining the donor.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cholesterol Screening", section Specimen Collection
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: In which situation is a non-fasting lipid profile acceptable?
opciones: Initial risk estimation in an untreated primary-prevention patient
Establishing the diagnosis of hypertriglyceridemia in a patient
Following a patient whose family has a history of genetic hyperlipidemia
Assessing a patient who is at risk for pancreatitis or has it
preguntas.explicacion: Two situations sit on the non-fasting side: estimating risk for the first time in an untreated primary-prevention patient, and clarifying a diagnosis of metabolic syndrome. The other three options belong to the list where fasting is preferred or mandatory, along with judging residual risk in a treated patient. The clinical question decides whether the patient fasts.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Limitations and Who Decides Which Aid or Service Is Needed
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(4) / 2027 F.1.d(1)
preguntas.pregunta: How does the ADA guidance define an 'undue burden' that excuses a particular aid or service?
opciones: Significant difficulty or expense, judged against the entity's resources
Any cost that exceeds the fee the entity charges for the service in question
Any request made with less than 24 hours of advance notice
Any aid the patient did not ask for in writing before the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Undue burden means significant difficulty or expense, weighed against the resources of the entity, and even then another effective aid must be offered if one exists. Reasonable advance notice may be required but not excessive notice, and walk-in requests are honored to the extent possible; nothing ties the duty to a written request or to the price of the visit.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii)(A)-(B); and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex E
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D1 1G k30 · D3 k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wants to keep the tube holder and pulls the used needle off it with a gloved hand. Which rule does this break?
opciones: Under OSHA, contaminated needles are removed only by a mechanical device or one-handed technique, when no alternative is feasible
Under OSHA, contaminated needles may be removed by hand as long as clean gloves are worn and the tube holder is disinfected afterwards
The WHO allows removal by hand provided the needle is dropped into a sharps container that is within arm's reach
Removal by hand is permitted when the holder is reused on the same patient within two minutes
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii) forbids bending a contaminated needle, recapping it or taking it off unless the employer can show no alternative is feasible or a specific medical procedure requires it, and then only with a mechanical device, or one-handed; shearing a needle or breaking it is prohibited outright. WHO Annex E says an exposed used needle is never disassembled with bare hands, and Chapter 3 prefers discarding barrel and needle together.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex E, One-hand scoop technique

preguntas.pregunta: After a needle has been re-sheathed with the scoop technique on a work surface, what is the next step?
opciones: Disinfect the surface, so no blood is left behind on it
Rinse the surface with water and dry it with a paper towel
Cover the surface with fresh paper until the session ends
Leave the surface as it is until the end of the working shift
preguntas.explicacion: The maneuver is done beside a sharps container, and the needle goes into it straight afterwards. Because the cap was resting on the surface, that surface is then cleaned with disinfectant so that no blood is left on it. An exposed used needle is never taken apart by hand.
