preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 first drop · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the first drop of blood wiped away after a skin puncture?
opciones: It can carry tissue fluid, or debris such as loose flakes of skin
It is arterial in oxygen content, and the test needs a venous value
It holds the alcohol that has not yet dried, which hemolyses it
It is the drop richest in platelets, which would clump in the tube
preguntas.explicacion: The first drop goes onto the gauze because tissue fluid or loose skin may have got into it. On a glucometer the reasoning is the same: that drop can hold interstitial or intracellular fluid, or be hemolysed, so the strip takes the second one. Capillary blood does resemble arterial blood in oxygen, but that is another matter.

preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: What makes an accidental arterial puncture more painful than a venous one?
opciones: Arteries have thicker walls and more nerves associated with them
Arteries have thinner walls and fewer nerves associated with them
Arteries carry a higher volume of blood at a much lower pressure
Arteries lie deeper and are always covered by the bicipital sheet
preguntas.explicacion: Veins are preferred for a draw because they run superficially, while arteries have thicker walls and carry more nerves with them, so puncturing one hurts more. The point matters at the elbow, where an artery and a nerve run under the basilic vein and make that route the more painful choice.

preguntas.subtema: 24-hour start and end · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient starting a 24-hour urine collection at 7 a.m. asks what to do with the urine he passes at 7 a.m. on the first day. What is the correct instruction?
opciones: Void into the toilet and discard it; collect every void after that, including the 7 a.m. void the next morning
Collect it as the first specimen of the period, and stop with the last void before 7 a.m. the next morning
Void into the toilet and discard it, and also discard the 7 a.m. void of the next morning to keep exactly 24 hours
Collect it as a separate first-morning specimen for urinalysis, and start the timed collection with the next void
preguntas.explicacion: The period starts with an empty bladder: the void at the starting time goes into the toilet and is not kept. From then on all urine is saved for 24 hours, and the void at the same clock time the next morning is the last one collected and does go into the container. Keeping the opening void or dropping the closing void both shift the measured period. The container is refrigerated throughout.

preguntas.pregunta: Which set of records should a waived testing site keep so that any result can be traced and problems found?
opciones: Test results, QC results, lot numbers with receipt and expiration dates, temperature and function checks, training and PT
Only the patient results and the QC results, since CLIA requires no other documentation from waived sites
The manufacturer's inserts and the fee receipts for the certificate, which the state agency reviews at renewal
A daily census of patients tested and the names of the operators, retained until the next certificate cycle
preguntas.explicacion: Documentation is not spelled out in most inserts and therefore is not a CLIA requirement for waived sites, but it is a core good practice: test orders and results with any confirmatory results, QC results, lot numbers with dates received, used and expiring, daily temperatures and function checks, failures and corrective actions, recall notices, training and competency, and proficiency testing results. In CMS surveys 45 % of sites did not record name, lot and expiration.

preguntas.pregunta: Recapping a needle cannot be avoided in one particular situation. Which technique is then required?
opciones: The one-hand scoop, never a recap made with both hands
A two-handed recap made slowly with the cap held steady
A recap made by an assistant while the worker holds still
A recap made after the needle has been rinsed and dried
preguntas.explicacion: Where recapping is unavoidable the one-hand scoop is used, and recapping with both hands is expressly forbidden. The scoop is performed near the sharps container, the device is discarded immediately afterwards, and the surface used is then cleaned with disinfectant.

preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic phlebotomy · CPT D4 4D k82 standards for blood donation
preguntas.pregunta: A donor with hereditary hemochromatosis is prescribed phlebotomy every two weeks. How does that fit the donation frequency rules?
opciones: Therapeutic phlebotomy may be collected more often than once in 8 weeks
Therapeutic phlebotomy follows the same 8-week interval as any donation
Therapeutic phlebotomy is barred once the donor has been given a diagnosis
Therapeutic phlebotomy is allowed weekly only if the unit is then discarded
preguntas.explicacion: Where an eligible donor has a therapeutic phlebotomy prescribed for their own health, blood may be taken more often than once in 8 weeks, or than once in 16 weeks for double red cell apheresis, so long as the disease or condition behind the phlebotomy is stated conspicuously on the container label. Hereditary hemochromatosis is one of the conditions that can lift that labeling requirement.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia 003345 Blood typing, How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k5 (applied D4 4D) · PBT I.B.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In the second step of blood typing, called back typing, what is mixed with red cells known to be type A and type B?
opciones: The patient's serum, to look for anti-A and anti-B antibodies
The patient's red cells, to look for the A antigen or B antigen
The patient's plasma with anti-D reagent, to look for Rh factor
The patient's whole blood, to look for clumping of the donor cells
preguntas.explicacion: Blood typing has two steps. In ABO typing the sample's cells are mixed with anti-A and anti-B antibodies and watched for clumping. In back typing the serum, the liquid part without cells, is mixed with cells known to be type A and type B; since type A people have anti-B, type B have anti-A and type O have both, the serum reaction confirms the type. Rh typing is a similar but separate test.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lactose tolerance tests (003500), What Abnormal Results Mean; StatPearls, "Lactose Intolerance", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Lactose test follow-up · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139
preguntas.pregunta: A lactose tolerance blood test is abnormal. What test is recommended afterwards, and why?
opciones: A glucose tolerance test, to rule out a problem absorbing glucose itself
A second lactose tolerance test, to confirm the result on another day
A blood culture set, to rule out bacterial overgrowth of the small bowel
A fasting glucose, to rule out the diabetes that flattens the lactose curve
preguntas.explicacion: An abnormal lactose blood test is followed by a glucose tolerance test, which tells you whether the body absorbs glucose properly in the first place: if it does not, a flat curve after lactose says nothing about lactase. Diabetes and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth are known causes of a false negative on the lactose test, not something a repeat or a culture would settle.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that results never be left as a message on his home phone, only mailed to his address. How is that request treated?

preguntas.explicacion: The list of patient rights includes stating how one's information is to be handled and communicated to others; the example given is a patient who wants any message from the pharmacy or the hospital mailed to his home rather than left on his telephone. preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k143 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A cerebrospinal fluid specimen sits at the nursing station for three hours before anyone walks it down. Beyond any effect on culture, what does the delay cost?
opciones: The cells degenerate and the biochemistry shifts, glucose being the value singled out as affected
The cells degenerate and the protein climbs, while the glucose is unchanged by the wait itself
The specimen clots, so no cell count can be reported from any of the three numbered tubes
The organisms lose viability, which is why the specimen is refrigerated as soon as it is drawn
preguntas.explicacion: A lumbar puncture fills three sterile tubes, and the laboratory is meant to work on them straight away: delay lets the cells degenerate and shifts the biochemistry, glucose first of all. Refrigeration is no fix either, since cold costs the survival of Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria meningitidis, so the specimen waits at room temperature.

preguntas.pregunta: You are choosing a vein in the antecubital area. Which vein is the most common venipuncture site, and what does it connect?
opciones: The median cubital vein, linking the cephalic and basilic veins
The basilic vein, linking the median antebrachial and axillary veins
The cephalic vein, running superficially along the biceps brachii
The brachial vein, formed where the radial and ulnar veins join
preguntas.explicacion: More venous blood is drawn from the median cubital than from any other vein: it leaves the basilic in the bend of the elbow and runs diagonally to meet the cephalic, tracing a V, and it lies very shallow in the roof of the cubital fossa, easy to reach. The brachial vein is deep, born where the radial and the ulnar veins meet.

preguntas.pregunta: The clerk asks which of the panels she books usually need a fast. Which grouping is named among the common tests that do?
opciones: Blood glucose, a lipid panel and a basic metabolic panel
Blood glucose, a complete blood count and a coagulation panel
A lipid panel, a troponin test and a complete blood count
A basic metabolic panel, a troponin test and a strep screen
preguntas.explicacion: The tests said usually to require fasting are blood glucose tests, cholesterol level tests, that is the lipid panel, and the basic metabolic panel. Liver function tests and a renal function panel may also call for a fast in some cases. A blood count is part of a routine checkup, and troponin is a blood enzyme test used after a suspected heart attack.

preguntas.pregunta: A methotrexate level is being sent to the laboratory. Under which transport condition will the specimen be accepted?
opciones: Carried on ice and protected from light
Carried at room temperature in a gel tube
Carried frozen at –20 °C in an EDTA tube
Carried at 37 °C in a heated transport block
preguntas.explicacion: Blood samples for methotrexate measurement are accepted only if they were carried on ice and in the dark; specimens transported otherwise are rejected. preguntas.pregunta: A pregnant patient is due for group B strep screening. Which specimen is collected, and when?
opciones: A swab of the vagina plus the rectum, usually between 36 and 38 weeks of pregnancy
A cervical swab taken with a speculum, usually between 36 and 38 weeks of pregnancy
A swab of the vagina plus the rectum, usually between 12 and 14 weeks of pregnancy
A clean-catch urine specimen only, usually between 36 and 38 weeks of pregnancy
preguntas.explicacion: Group B strep lives in the vagina and the rectum, so screening swabs both sites, and ACOG, the college of obstetricians and gynecologists, puts the timing at 36 to 38 weeks; a patient who goes into labor earlier may be tested then. A urine test is the other option offered, not the only one. A positive result means antibiotics during labor to protect the baby.

preguntas.pregunta: In addition to anchoring the vein, what does the WHO's Step 6 ask the patient to do so the veins stand out?
opciones: Form a fist
Pump the hand
Lower the arm
Hold a breath
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 lists three actions in sequence: anchor the vein with a thumb below the site, ask the patient to make a fist so the veins are more prominent, and enter the vein swiftly at 30 degrees or less. Pumping the hand, dangling the arm and breath-holding are not part of the WHO procedure; the warm compress and tapping are the only other vein-raising measures in the material.

preguntas.pregunta: Before handing a batch of samples to the courier, what final check does the WHO procedure place immediately before dispatch?
opciones: Rechecking the labels on the tubes against the forms
Rechecking that the request form is folded inside the bag
Re-verifying the patient's fasting status by telephone
Recording the tourniquet time for each tube on the form
preguntas.explicacion: Once the draw is done, hands washed and waste discarded, the WHO sequence has the phlebotomist match every tube label against its form before anything is sent, then tell the patient the procedure is over and look at the puncture site again. Patient-to-sample matching, which is the labeling, and the conditions the sample travels under both appear on the list of things that shape a result while it is being collected and moved. The request form does travel with the samples, but in the pocket on the outside of the leak-proof bag, never folded in among the tubes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Invasive Techniques); and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine culture - catheterized specimen (003752), What Abnormal Results Mean
preguntas.subtema: Indwelling catheter: not from the bag · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(d) · RMA III.C.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with an indwelling urinary catheter needs a urine culture. From where should the specimen be taken?
opciones: Never from the drainage bag, whose contents are considered contaminated
From the drainage bag, after mixing it so the sample is representative
From the drainage bag, provided it was emptied less than 2 hours earlier
From the drainage bag, after adding boric acid to stop any overgrowth
preguntas.explicacion: When a catheter is already in place, urine that has pooled in the collection bag is regarded as contaminated and is never used for culture, no matter how recently the bag was emptied or what preservative is added afterward. Patients with a permanent catheter often carry bacteria in the urine without true infection, which is called colonization, and bag urine would exaggerate that.

preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory audits a full year of identification errors and finds that most of them share one feature. Which feature is that?
opciones: The sample carried fewer than two patient identifiers
The barcode had been printed for a different test panel
The sample had been labeled after arriving in the laboratory
The requisition and the tube listed different collection times
preguntas.explicacion: In the laboratory that measured its preanalytical quality indicators, identification problems were the second most frequent error, and most of them consisted of a label with fewer than two identifiers; in newborns the rate was ten times higher because the small tubes leave little room to write two. Wrong panels, late labeling and time mismatches are other errors, not the one that dominated.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Continuing Education Activity and section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C k42 · PBT II.A · CCMA 3E2 k124
preguntas.pregunta: Which pair appears among the contributing factors named for laboratory testing errors?
opciones: Improper patient preparation and transcription mistakes
Delayed billing and missing diagnosis codes on the form
Ordering too few tests for a complex discharge diagnosis
Holding serum at 2 to 8 degrees before serological testing
preguntas.explicacion: Errors turn up in the preanalytical phase, the analytical one and the postanalytical one, and the contributing factors named run from a patient prepared improperly and mistakes in collecting the specimen, through delays in transport, instruments that malfunction and reagents that are unstable, to transcription errors and critical values communicated poorly. Serum waiting for prompt serological testing is meant to sit at 2 to 8 degrees.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the Teach-Back Method
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.D Interpersonal Relations · CPT D2 2B k40 · CCMA 6 k199 therapeutic communication · CMA II.F.3.a level of understanding
preguntas.pregunta: After explaining a 24-hour urine collection, the assistant asks the patient whether he understands. Why does that question not count as teach-back?
opciones: It can be answered yes or no, and patients tend to say yes whether they followed it or not
It tests the patient's memory instead of checking how well the explanation was delivered
It has to be asked at the very end of the visit, once every instruction has been given
It should be put to the caregiver, who is the person actually carrying out the collection
preguntas.explicacion: Teach-back asks the patient to put back into their own words whatever they need to know or to do. A question that can be closed with a yes, asking whether something makes sense for instance, is explicitly not teach-back, because a yes comes just as readily from someone who missed the point. The framing that works puts the burden on the explainer, not on the patient.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the Teach-Back Method, Action
