preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for a fasting glucose says he skipped breakfast but had a coffee with sugar an hour ago. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: He has broken the fast; tell the provider, since the test may need rescheduling
Coffee does not count as food, so the draw may proceed as a fasting sample
Proceed and mark the sample 'non-fasting' only if he also ate solid food
Wait one more hour so the sugar clears, then draw it as a fasting sample
preguntas.explicacion: Fasting means no food or drink except plain water; juice, coffee, soda and other beverages get into the bloodstream and affect results, and a patient who eats or drinks before the test should tell the provider because the test may have to be rescheduled. A fasting glucose needs at least 8 hours without caloric intake, not one more hour.

opciones: Blood not thoroughly mixed with its additive can give erroneous results

preguntas.explicacion: The footnote to the order-of-draw table asks for additive tubes to be inverted gently and warns that erroneous results may follow if blood and additive are not properly combined. preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: The sharps container in a drawing station is full to the top, so a phlebotomist sets the used needle on the tray to dispose of it later. Which risks are being ignored?
opciones: Injuries happen when sharps containers are overfilled and when used needles are not placed in them immediately
The needle should have been recapped with two hands and left on the tray until a container was available
The needle should have gone into the regulated-waste bag, since bags are acceptable whenever containers are full
There is no added risk once the safety feature is activated, so the delay is acceptable
preguntas.explicacion: Used needles go straight into an approved sharps container kept close to the point of use; injuries also happen when a needle ends up in an ordinary waste bag, or when a container is filled past the line or handled badly. Recapping as a routine is no longer advised, because handling a used needle is what raises the risk of a puncture, and the WHO requires the container to be within arm's reach and clearly visible.

preguntas.subtema: Collection methods · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.F II.J · CCMA 3E7 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Several tubes are needed from one venipuncture. Which system does the WHO's Step 7 say to use, and what if it is not available?
opciones: Vacuum tubes with a needle and a tube holder; failing that, a syringe or a winged set
A syringe, because it lets the phlebotomist control the pressure; otherwise evacuated tubes
A winged needle set attached to a syringe; otherwise a hypodermic needle and syringe
Evacuated tubes only; if they are not available the draw is postponed
preguntas.explicacion: Step 7 says that when several tubes are needed, vacuum tubes with a needle and a tube holder are used because the tubes fill directly, and that a syringe or winged needle set is the alternative when that system is unavailable. preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E10 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: A serum specimen for a serology test will be examined later the same day, once the afternoon run is set up. Where does the published guidance have it kept in the meantime?
opciones: In the refrigerator at 2 to 8 °C, the condition given for serum awaiting prompt serological testing
In the freezer at −20 °C or lower, the condition given for delayed transport or long-term storage
At room temperature on the bench, since the blood has to clot before it can be processed at all
On wet ice in a transport cooler, the condition given for a bronchoalveolar lavage in transit
preguntas.explicacion: Blood for serology is allowed to clot before processing, and in transit it is protected from extremes of temperature. Serum that will be examined promptly is held at 2 to 8 °C until it is tested. Freezing at −20 °C or lower is the instruction for long-term storage or delayed transport, which is a different situation from a specimen due to run in a few hours.

Glass tubes with screw caps only, because plastic reacts with additives
Plastic tubes with rubber caps only, since glass may break in transport
preguntas.explicacion: Blood may go into sterile tubes of glass or plastic with rubber caps, into vacuum-extraction tubes, or into glass tubes with screw caps, and which of them is used depends on what has been agreed with the laboratory. Large volumes call instead for a sterile glass or collapsible pack.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Issues of Concern: Standard Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Standard precautions · CPT D1 1J k11 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C1 k100 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2.d · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which practices make up standard precautions, the framework applied at every patient encounter?
opciones: Hand hygiene, protective equipment, cough etiquette, placement and safe sharps
Isolation rooms, contact tracing, daily temperature checks and visitor logs
Sterile gloves, sterile fields, surgical scrub and sterile drapes for each draw
Testing every patient on admission and treating those who test positive
preguntas.explicacion: Standard precautions are the baseline for every encounter, before anything is known about the patient: hand hygiene whether or not gloves were worn, both before and after contact with a patient or with body fluids; appropriate protective equipment, including gown, gloves and eye protection where fluid exposure is possible; respiratory and cough etiquette; patient placement that takes single rooms and routes of transmission into account; and safe handling of needles and instruments.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Tissue and Biopsy Specimens)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(2)
preguntas.pregunta: A skin biopsy is sent for histopathology and a second piece for bacterial culture. Which pair of handling instructions is correct?
opciones: Histopathology piece in 10 % neutral buffered formalin; culture piece sterile and refrigerated at 2 to 8 °C
Histopathology piece sterile and refrigerated at 2 to 8 °C; culture piece in 10 % neutral buffered formalin
Both pieces in 10 % neutral buffered formalin, the culture piece being rinsed in sterile saline before plating
Both pieces sterile at room temperature, since formalin is reserved for cytology and body fluid specimens
preguntas.explicacion: Tissue for histopathology goes into 10 % neutral buffered formalin. Tissue headed for microbiology or molecular testing has to stay sterile and cold instead, held between 2 and 8 °C, and is frozen only when the assay specifically calls for it. Each fragment therefore travels in its own sterile, leak-proof container carrying its own label: labeling and paperwork are what tie both pieces back to one patient and one anatomical site.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic drug levels (003430), How to Prepare for the Test; MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?
preguntas.subtema: Drug level preparation · CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D patient preparation · CCMA 3E k139 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2 pre-test conditions
preguntas.pregunta: A patient due for a drug level asks whether to skip the morning dose so the result comes out low. What is the right answer?
opciones: No: doses are not stopped or changed without talking to the provider first
Yes: the dose is always held on the morning of a therapeutic drug level
Yes, if the level is a trough, since a trough must be drawn off therapy
No, but the dose may be delayed two hours without a new order
preguntas.explicacion: Patients must not stop or change their medicines before a drug level without speaking to the provider; the provider is the one who says whether the times of any doses need to change. Depending on the drug, the test is scheduled before or after the regular dose, which is exactly why an unannounced skipped dose ruins the result. A trough is drawn on therapy, just before the next dose.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Patients with Impaired Decision-Making Capacity; and StatPearls, "Refusal of Care", section Issues of Concern, Psychiatric Patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: An inpatient carries a schizophrenia diagnosis and is being asked to agree to a draw. What follows?
opciones: The diagnosis by itself does not remove the right to give informed consent
A surrogate signs for any patient who carries a psychiatric diagnosis
Consent is waived, because the admission paperwork already covers draws
The nearest relative decides once a psychiatric diagnosis is on the record
preguntas.explicacion: Neither cognitive impairment, nor mental illness, nor a severe medical condition strips away by itself the right to give informed consent, so long as the person can understand, weigh and communicate a decision. Research shows that carrying a diagnosis such as schizophrenia does not preclude capacity, so each patient gets a full assessment.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Fire safety, the RACE rule; StatPearls, "OSHA Fire Safety", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: RACE · CPT D1 1A 1L k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 · CMAA 3A k45
preguntas.pregunta: Smoke starts pouring from a centrifuge in the processing room while two patients sit in the waiting area. Under the RACE sequence, what is the first action?
opciones: Rescue or remove everyone in immediate danger
Activate the alarm system and call the operator
Confine the fire by closing the doors
Extinguish it with the nearest CO2 unit
preguntas.explicacion: RACE orders the response to a fire: R, rescue or remove all occupants from danger; A, activate the alarm system; C, confine the fire by closing doors; E, evacuate or extinguish. In healthcare the first step matters most because patients may be unable to move on their own. Extinguishing comes last and only for a fire that can be handled with a portable unit; the PASS rule, pull, aim, squeeze, sweep, governs how the extinguisher is used once that point is reached.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Lactose Intolerance", section Proper Performance of Hydrogen Breath Testing
preguntas.subtema: Lactose breath test preparation · CPT D4 4H · PBT V.C.3 breath testing
preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for a hydrogen breath test finished a course of antibiotics ten days ago. Why does that matter?
opciones: Antibiotics should be avoided for at least 4 weeks before the test
Antibiotics should be avoided for at least 24 hours before the test
Antibiotics raise breath hydrogen, so the cutoff moves from 20 to 30 ppm
Antibiotics have no effect; only bowel preparation for colonoscopy does
preguntas.explicacion: Hydrogen breath testing done properly means no antibiotics in the four weeks before, and no test within two weeks of a bowel prep done for surgery or colonoscopy. Fiber and FODMAPs come out for 24 hours because they lift the baseline hydrogen, and probiotics, prokinetics, laxatives, lactose and lactulose stop 24 hours before and during. The 20 ppm cutoff itself does not move.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (equipment compatibility); and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex C, Table C.1
preguntas.subtema: Equipment selection · CPT D3 3A 3B k58 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic buys needles from one company, tube holders from another and tubes from a third. What is the guidance on mixing brands like that?
opciones: Needle, holder and tubes should come from the same manufacturer, since mixing brands can cause problems in use
Mixing brands is acceptable as long as every component is within its expiration date and sterile
Only the needle and the holder must match; the tubes are interchangeable across manufacturers
Mixing brands is acceptable for adults but not for pediatric tubes with reduced vacuum
preguntas.explicacion: Needle, tube holder and tubes are chosen from the same manufacturer to ensure compatibility; otherwise the volume aspirated, the gel stability and the additives can be affected. The WHO device table lists parts from different makers mixed together as a disadvantage of vacuum systems that can create a problem during use. Neither text limits the rule to adults or to two of the three parts.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix B, Temperature Log Instructions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic stores some test kits and patient samples on an open shelf rather than in the refrigerator. Which range is typically kept for a room used for testing and storage?
opciones: 15 to 30 °C, that is 59 to 86 °F
2 to 8 °C, that is 36 to 46 °F
18 to 22 °C, that is 64 to 72 °F
10 to 25 °C, that is 50 to 77 °F
preguntas.explicacion: Rooms used for testing and for storing reagents, kits, controls and patient samples are typically held between 15 and 30 °C, or 59 to 86 °F. The colder band, 2 to 8 °C, belongs to the refrigerator and −25 to −15 °C to the freezer. Whatever the room reads, the manufacturer's instructions decide which condition a given product may be stored in.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Chambers and Circulation through the Heart; Layers; Left Ventricle
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which chamber pumps blood into the systemic circuit, and why is its wall so much thicker than its counterpart's?
opciones: The left ventricle; it must overcome the high resistance of the long systemic circuit
The right ventricle; it must push blood through the dense capillary beds of both lungs
The left atrium; it receives oxygen-rich blood from all four of the pulmonary veins
The right atrium; it receives blood from both venae cavae and from the coronary sinus
preguntas.explicacion: The ventricles are the primary pumping chambers, and the left ventricle is the major pump for the systemic circuit, ejecting blood into the aorta. Although both ventricles move the same volume per beat, the left wall is much thicker because it must generate far more pressure to overcome the resistance of the long systemic circuit; the pulmonary circuit is shorter and offers less resistance.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine culture - catheterized specimen (003752), How the Test is Performed and Why the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Catheterized specimen technique · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(d) · RMA III.C.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: How is a catheterized urine specimen for culture obtained?
opciones: The urethral opening is washed with an antiseptic, a thin catheter is passed into the bladder, and urine drains into a sterile container
The urethral opening is washed with an antiseptic, a needle is passed through the lower abdomen, and urine is aspirated
The patient voids the first portion into the toilet and the midstream portion into a sterile container held by the nurse
A thin catheter is passed into the bladder without cleansing, and the first urine to drain is discarded before collecting
preguntas.explicacion: A nurse or trained technician cleans the area around the urethral opening with an antiseptic, passes a thin rubber tube through the urethra into the bladder, lets the urine drain into a sterile container and removes the catheter. It is used when the patient cannot void, when infection is suspected or in urinary retention. A needle through the abdominal wall is suprapubic aspiration, which is rare and mostly done in infants.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lactose tolerance tests (003500), Normal Results and What Abnormal Results Mean
preguntas.subtema: Lactose blood test result · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139
preguntas.pregunta: On a lactose tolerance blood test the glucose rises 24 mg/dL in two hours. How is that read?
opciones: Inconclusive: a rise of 20 to 30 mg/dL falls between the two categories
Normal: any rise above 20 mg/dL rules out lactose intolerance
Abnormal: a rise under 30 mg/dL is diagnostic of lactose intolerance
Invalid: the rise has to be measured at 30 minutes, not at two hours
preguntas.explicacion: A glucose rise of more than 30 mg/dL within two hours of the lactose drink is normal, a rise of less than 20 mg/dL is abnormal, and 20 to 30 mg/dL is inconclusive, which is where 24 falls. Because the test hinges on the size of the rise, the fasting sample and the timed ones both have to be drawn as scheduled.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A faint during a blood draw is usually vasovagal. Which other forms of reflex syncope are described alongside it?
opciones: Situational syncope, such as cough or micturition, and the carotid sinus form
Cardiac arrhythmia and orthostatic syncope, such as rising from a lying position
Hypoglycaemic syncope and febrile syncope, such as a faint during an infection
Carotid sinus syncope and cardiac syncope, such as a faint from a heart block
preguntas.explicacion: Reflex syncope covers episodes in which the control of blood pressure fails and brain perfusion drops. The vasovagal form is the commonest of them, and the other members of the group are situational syncope and the carotid sinus form, the kind brought on by coughing or passing urine.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Conventional devices
preguntas.subtema: Device selection · CPT D3 k54 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: For which two situations is a needle and syringe listed as the easier choice?
opciones: Small or difficult veins, and arterial sampling with a heparinized syringe
Small or difficult veins, and drawing many tubes from one single puncture
Prominent forearm veins, and arterial sampling with a heparinized syringe
Prominent forearm veins, and drawing many tubes from one single puncture
preguntas.explicacion: For a patient with small or difficult veins, drawing with a syringe can be easier than with an evacuated tube system, and a heparinized syringe can also be used for arterial blood. Collecting large or multiple samples is where the syringe is described as difficult, not where it shines.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Petechiae", section Introduction; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding into the skin
preguntas.subtema: Terminology: petechiae and purpura · CPT D3 3L k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A non-blanching spot at the puncture site measures about four millimeters. What is it called?
opciones: Purpura, because it is larger than two millimeters
Petechia, because it is smaller than ten millimeters
Erythema, because it sits over an inflamed puncture
Ecchymosis, because it is smaller than ten millimeters
preguntas.explicacion: The dividing line is two millimeters: a non-blanching spot below that size is a petechia and one above it is purpura. A very large bruised area of bleeding under the skin is called an ecchymosis, and redness that fades under pressure is erythema, not bleeding at all.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1242(d), Standard: Specimen submission, handling, and referral
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k92 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E14 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A reference laboratory accepts specimens from outside clinics. What must it make available to those clients according to CLIA?
opciones: Written instructions on patient preparation, collection, labeling, storage, transport, processing and acceptability
A copy of its CLIA certificate and the qualifications of its laboratory director and testing personnel
A monthly report of the number and condition of specimens rejected from each client's collection site
A price list for each test together with the turnaround time expected from receipt to final report
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1242(d) obliges a laboratory that takes referral work to keep written instructions available to its clients covering, as applicable, the same ground its own policies must cover: how the patient is prepared, how the specimen is collected and labeled, how it is stored, preserved and transported, how it is processed, and when it is accepted or rejected. Certificates, rejection statistics and price lists are not in the standard.

preguntas.fuente: SAMHSA, Urine Specimen Collection Handbook for Federal Agency Workplace Drug Testing Programs (2024), Chapter 7 collection steps 17, 18 and 20
preguntas.subtema: Split specimen · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 chain-of-custody · CCMA 3E k127 · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: How is a federal drug test specimen split between the two bottles?
opciones: At least 30 mL into bottle A and at least 15 mL into bottle B
At least 15 mL into bottle A and at least 30 mL into bottle B
At least 22.5 mL into each bottle, so the volumes match
All of it into bottle A, keeping bottle B for a later recollection
preguntas.explicacion: In the donor's presence the collector unwraps the sealed bottles and pours 30 mL or more into bottle A and 15 mL or more into bottle B, then caps both. Whatever urine is left in the collection container is discarded. The two volumes are not interchangeable: bottle A is tested first and bottle B is kept for a retest, which is why it may hold less.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(b)(3)(iv), application to laboratories
preguntas.subtema: A laboratory that ships · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital laboratory ships a hazardous chemical to another employer. How does the Hazard Communication standard treat it then?
opciones: As a manufacturer or distributor: it must label and send the sheet
As a laboratory still: only the incoming label rules apply to it
As a transporter: only the shipping name and number are needed
As an exempt employer, since the chemical is used in patient care
preguntas.explicacion: The reduced set of duties for laboratories has a limit. Where a laboratory employer ships hazardous chemicals, the rule counts it as a manufacturer of chemicals or as a distributor, so containers leaving the laboratory carry the label paragraph (f) requires of shipped containers, and a safety data sheet goes to distributors and to other employers. Inside the laboratory the short list applies; on the way out, the full labeling rules do.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Winged steel needles (butterfly)
preguntas.subtema: Device selection · CPT D3 k55 k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A 3-year-old with small, difficult veins needs one tube of blood. Which device does the WHO device table favor, and what advantage does it list?
opciones: A winged (butterfly) needle, which allows better precision than a hypodermic or evacuated tube needle
A vacuum-tube system, which eliminates blood transfer and allows numerous samples from a single puncture
An auto-disable syringe, which prevents reuse and reduces the risk of needle-sticks
A 21 G straight needle with a syringe, which is the most common means of blood sampling
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 describes winged steel needles as good for drawing blood from pediatric patients or from patients with small or difficult veins, allowing better precision than a hypodermic or evacuated tube needle, at higher cost and with the air-in-the-tubing caveat. Auto-disable syringes are explicitly not recommended for phlebotomy, and Table 3.1 gives no 21 G option for children.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure; Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Stages of POCT · CPT D5 k90 · PBT IV.C · CCMA 3D9 k111 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: In which stage of point-of-care testing do most errors and interfering factors arise?
opciones: The pre-analytical stage, when the sample is collected, handled, prepared and loaded
The analytical stage, while the device is actually measuring the loaded sample
The post-analytical stage, when results are transcribed and communicated to the team
The stages contribute equally, since single-use devices remove most handling steps
preguntas.explicacion: POCT has three stages: pre-analytical, which is collecting the sample, moving it, preparing it and loading it; analytical, which is running the test; and post-analytical, communicating and interpreting results, critical values included. The pre-analytical phase is the controllable variable that matters most, and most interference arises there, through misidentification, hemolysis, clotting, under- or overfilling, a long tourniquet, bubbles and microclots. Such errors fall away with operator experience and training.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 3N k9 k59 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: An ESR specimen that was poorly mixed reaches the laboratory with a clot in it. How does the clot affect the reading?
opciones: It disrupts the stacking of red cells and lowers the value obtained
It disrupts the stacking of red cells and raises the value obtained
It leaves the value unchanged, since only the plasma column is read
It raises the value, in the same way that a tilted tube raises it
preguntas.explicacion: Clotted blood breaks up the rouleaux, the coin-like stacks of red cells whose settling is being measured, so the value comes out lower than the patient's true one. The faults that raise the value are physical ones: a tilted tube, vibration, warmth and an inadequate fill.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Complications
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K 3L k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Bright red blood pulses back into the hub during an attempted venous access. What is done?
opciones: The device is removed at once and direct pressure applied
The device is advanced further until the flow settles down
The device is left in place and the tourniquet reapplied
The device is withdrawn slightly and the tubes are filled
preguntas.explicacion: An artery entered by accident calls for prompt removal of the line and direct pressure over the site to control the bleeding. Arterial injury sits among the local complications of this kind of procedure, alongside nerve injury, hematoma, bleeding and simple failure of the attempt.

preguntas.subtema: Reports to authorities · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA II.E.6 · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k37
preguntas.pregunta: Which disclosure may be made to a public authority without the patient's authorization?
opciones: A report of a communicable disease or of suspected child abuse, as authorized by law
A report of the patient's employer and insurance details for a workplace injury claim
A report of the patient's diagnosis to a school for enrollment, beyond proof of immunization
A report of psychotherapy notes to a family member concerned about the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Public health disclosures in 164.512(b) include reporting disease and injury to a public health authority and reporting child abuse or neglect to an authority authorized to receive it; disclosures to a school are limited to proof of immunization required by law, with the parent's or adult's documented agreement. Disclosures to an employer are confined to workplace medical surveillance and work-related illness findings with written notice to the worker. Psychotherapy notes need an authorization in almost every case, and a concerned relative is not a public authority.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Blood Plasma; and 18.5 Hemostasis, Fibrinolysis; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia 003423 Venipuncture, Why the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5 k87) · PBT I.B.3 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A red-top tube is left to clot and then centrifuged. What is the fluid above the clot called, and how does it differ from plasma?
opciones: Serum; it is plasma from which the clotting factors have been removed
Plasma; it still contains fibrinogen and the other clotting factors
Buffy coat; the pale layer of leukocytes and platelets above the cells
Whole blood; the formed elements are suspended in the fluid again
preguntas.explicacion: Serum is plasma after the clotting factors have been removed: in a clotted tube it is the fluid squeezed out of the clot as it retracts. Plasma is the fluid part of circulating blood, still carrying fibrinogen and the other factors; serum is what remains liquid after the blood clots in a tube. The buffy coat is the layer of white cells and platelets in a spun, unclotted sample, and whole blood has all the formed elements suspended.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Please sit down and make yourself comfortable; and StatPearls, "Vancomycin" (NBK459263)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K 2L k46 k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: Besides fainting and allergies, which time-bound question does the WHO pre-draw interview include?
opciones: Whether anything has been eaten or drunk in the last two hours
Whether the patient has fasted for the past twelve hours or more
Whether the patient took any medicine in the past 24 hours
Whether the patient exercised hard in the past 30 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: Annex C asks whether the patient has had blood taken before, is scared of needles, is allergic to anything, has ever fainted while blood was being drawn, whether anything has been eaten or drunk in the last two hours, and how they feel at that moment. Twelve hours is the fasting recommendation for morning sampling, 24 hours the alcohol window, and 30 minutes the vancomycin trough window.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 3186, Model Exposure Control Plan, Procedures for Evaluating the Circumstances Surrounding an Exposure Incident; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(1)(ii)(C)
preguntas.subtema: Reviewing an exposure incident · CPT D1 1H 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic reviews a needlestick that happened while a phlebotomist recapped a butterfly needle. Which findings does that review put on record?
opciones: The engineering controls in use, the device brand, the PPE worn and the employee's training
The anti-HBs level of the employee and the hepatitis B status of the source patient
The dates of the last two annual sessions and the names of everyone who attended
The disinfectant used on the surface and the schedule for cleaning that work area
preguntas.explicacion: The written plan has to contain a procedure for looking into the circumstances of every exposure incident, and the model plan spells out what that review determines: which engineering controls were in use, which work practices were followed, the type and brand of the device, the protective clothing worn, where it happened, what procedure was under way, and what training the employee had. Serology results belong to the confidential medical evaluation, not to this review, and training dates and attendance are the separate training record.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge sizes · CPT D3 k55 k56 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A supply list gives the size of some catheters in gauge and of others in French. What does the French figure describe?
opciones: Three times the outer diameter in millimeters
One third of the outer diameter in millimeters
Three times the inner diameter in millimeters
One third of the usable length in millimeters
preguntas.explicacion: French sizing takes the outer diameter of the catheter in millimeters and multiplies it by three, so a device measuring six millimeters across is an 18F. It is kept for larger devices and specialized catheters: peripheral lines are not sized that way but by gauge, where the lower number is the wider device and the range stocked runs from fourteen to twenty-six.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Cortisol", sections Introduction and Mechanism
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: Cortisol follows a diurnal rhythm. When is secretion at its peak?
opciones: Near the time of awakening, after rising in the last hours of sleep
Around 4 p.m., after rising steadily through the afternoon
At night, when ACTH release from the pituitary is highest
About two hours after the first meal of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Cortisol secretion follows a diurnal rhythm: levels begin to rise in the final hours of sleep, peak near the time of awakening, decline gradually through the day and reach their lowest concentration at night; healthy adults produce 8 to 30 mg per day. Around 4 p.m. levels are much lower than in the morning, which is why the second sample is drawn then.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination: A Quality Tool for Clinical Laboratory Professionals
preguntas.subtema: Blood culture volume · CPT D4 4A k77 · PBT II.G common tests · CCMA 3E k139 blood cultures
preguntas.pregunta: A blood culture set is ordered before antibiotics for a febrile adult. Following the CDC model collection procedure, how much blood goes into each bottle, and what is the target for the set?
opciones: 10 mL in each bottle, for a target of 20 mL in the set
5 mL in each bottle, for a target of 10 mL in the set
20 mL in each bottle, for a target of 40 mL in the set
15 mL in each bottle, for a target of 30 mL in the set
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's model procedure for adult blood cultures calls for 10 mL of blood in each bottle, so that a set of one aerobic and one anaerobic bottle holds 20 mL, and two sets reach 40 mL. Volume is what drives detection: underfilled bottles produce false negatives that can delay therapy. The 40 mL figure belongs to two sets, not to one set of two 20 mL bottles.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), At a glance
preguntas.subtema: Two tiers of precautions · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C2 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How do Transmission-Based Precautions relate to Standard Precautions, according to the CDC?
opciones: A second tier added to Standard Precautions for patients with certain known or suspected infections
A replacement for Standard Precautions once a pathogen has been confirmed by the laboratory
The first tier, applied to every patient until an infection has been ruled out
A set that covers bloodborne pathogens only, while Standard Precautions cover respiratory ones
preguntas.explicacion: Transmission-Based Precautions form the second tier of basic infection control: they are layered on top of Standard Precautions whenever a patient may carry, or be colonized by, an agent that calls for extra measures. They never take the first tier's place, and what triggers them is a known or suspected infection rather than a blanket rule for everyone. Contact, Droplet and Airborne are the three categories, chosen by the route of transmission; bloodborne exposure is handled by Standard Precautions and by the OSHA standard.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Glucose screening tests during pregnancy (007562), Normal Results and How the Test is Performed; StatPearls, "Gestational Diabetes", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Gestational screening follow-up · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139
preguntas.pregunta: A 1-hour gestational screening result comes back at 152 mg/dL. What happens next?
opciones: She returns fasting for a 3-hour, 100 g glucose tolerance test
She is told she has gestational diabetes and is started on a diet
She repeats the same 50 g screening drink at her next prenatal visit
She returns fasting for a 2-hour, 75 g glucose tolerance test
preguntas.explicacion: Above 140 mg/dL the screen is not a diagnosis: the patient comes back after an 8- to 14-hour fast for the diagnostic test, a 100 g load with a draw before the drink and one every 60 minutes for three hours. About one in five patients fails the screen, and roughly two out of three of those turn out not to have gestational diabetes. The 75 g 2-hour test belongs to the one-step pathway.

preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: Where does latex rank among the causes of anaphylaxis in the operating room?
opciones: Second, after muscle relaxants
First, ahead of muscle relaxants
Third, after antibiotics and dyes
Second, after the antiseptic used on skin
preguntas.explicacion: Latex allergy ranks among the frequent triggers of anaphylaxis during surgery, and its prevalence rose as latex gloves came into wide use from the 1980s onward. In occupational health it is named the commonest cause of contact urticaria, and among cases of intraoperative anaphylaxis it comes second, behind the muscle relaxants.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.2, Definitions: CLIA certificate (1)-(5); 42 CFR 493.15(c)
preguntas.subtema: CLIA certificates · CPT D1 1B k25 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1 · NCMA 4.12
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic performs only fingerstick glucose and other tests on the CLIA waived list. Which CLIA certificate does it need?
opciones: A certificate of waiver from CMS
A certificate of compliance
A certificate of accreditation
A certificate for PPM procedures
preguntas.explicacion: A certificate of waiver is issued to a laboratory that restricts itself to the waived tests listed in 42 CFR 493.15(c) and no others. A certificate of compliance follows an inspection finding compliance with all condition-level requirements; a certificate of accreditation rests on accreditation by an organization approved by CMS; and a certificate for PPM procedures covers a physician, a dentist or a midlevel practitioner doing only provider-performed microscopy plus, if desired, waived tests. A registration certificate lets an entity do moderate or high complexity testing until surveyed.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F.2 Specimen collection · CPT D1 1B k25 operational standards · CCMA 7A k214
preguntas.pregunta: Under CLIA, what must a laboratory's written policies guarantee about a patient's specimen?
opciones: Positive identification and integrity from collection or receipt through testing and reporting
Positive identification at the moment of collection, after which the accession number takes over
Positive identification by a second staff member whenever the patient cannot state their own name
Integrity during transport above all, since the analyzer confirms the identity when it is received
preguntas.explicacion: The specimen identification standard covers a whole span, not a moment: the written policies and procedures have to guarantee that the patient's specimen is positively identified and kept in the best condition possible, from the time it is collected or received right through to the end of testing and the reporting of the result. Labeling at the bedside is where that chain starts, but it is not where it ends.

preguntas.subtema: Donor screening sample · CPT D4 4D k82 complete screening
preguntas.pregunta: How may the sample for a donor's hemoglobin or hematocrit be obtained?
opciones: By fingerstick or venipuncture, but not from the earlobe
By fingerstick or from the earlobe, but not by venipuncture
By venipuncture only, since capillary values are unreliable
By fingerstick only, since venipuncture wastes donor volume
preguntas.explicacion: Hemoglobin or hematocrit is measured on a sample taken by fingerstick, by venipuncture, or by any method whose results are equivalent; an earlobe sample will not do. The earlobe is the trap in this rule, because it looks like just another capillary site and is named specifically to rule it out.

preguntas.pregunta: A dark green sodium heparin tube and a light green PST are both ordered. Which comes first in the WHO sequence?
opciones: The dark green sodium heparin tube, then the light green PST
The light green PST, then the dark green sodium heparin tube
Either one, because both contain heparin and share position 6
The light green PST, because gel tubes precede plain heparin tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 lists the dark green sodium heparin tube at position 6 and the light green plasma separator tube, with lithium heparin and a gel separator, at position 7. They are two separate rows, not a shared position, and the gel tube comes after the plain heparin tube. Footnote d confirms that the PST, if used, is drawn in the position shown.

preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 heel anatomy · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: A colleague suggests puncturing the back (posterior curve) of a newborn's heel. Why is that spot avoided?
opciones: In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance there is only 2.33 mm, so the lancet may hit bone
In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance there is 3.32 mm, too deep for a lancet to reach blood
The posterior heel is where the tibial artery runs closest to the skin surface
The posterior heel is the site the WHO reserves for premature neonates with a 0.85 mm lancet
preguntas.explicacion: In a 7 pound (3 kg) baby, skin sits 3.32 mm above bone at the medial and lateral heel, 2.33 mm at the posterior heel and 2.19 mm at the toe. The posterior heel is left alone precisely because bone is that close. The tibial artery is the hazard of the medial aspect, and the 0.85 mm lancet is simply the size stocked for premature neonates.

preguntas.pregunta: A 24-hour urine for porphyrins is ordered. Which container feature does this analyte require?
opciones: An amber-colored container, because porphyrins are light sensitive
A clear container, so the laboratory can see the color of the pooled urine
A vacuum tube, which draws the sample without opening the container
A sterile container, because porphyrin testing requires a bacteriological culture
preguntas.explicacion: Light-sensitive analytes such as porphyrins and urobilinogen call for amber containers, in addition to the general requirements that the container be non-absorbing and free of interfering agents. Sterile collection is mandatory for culture, not for chemistry, and vacuum systems are limited to chemical analysis because the pressure difference breaks up brittle casts and lowers cast counts.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is transferring blood from a syringe into three tubes. How is the rack handled?
opciones: Keep the tubes in the rack, draw the rack closer, and inject downwards
Lift each tube out of the rack and hold it steady in the free hand
Keep the tubes in the rack and tilt them so the blood runs down the wall
Lift the rack up to eye level so the colored stoppers stay in view
preguntas.explicacion: Where it can be done, the tubes stay in their rack and the rack is moved towards the worker, with the blood injected downwards into the appropriately colored stopper. Holding a tube in the free hand is what the needle-stick precaution for this step is meant to avoid.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Use of Improved Engineering Controls in a Prevention Strategy
preguntas.subtema: Limits of safety devices · CPT D1 1A k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Why do devices with safety features reduce needlestick injuries without eliminating them?
opciones: Some cannot be activated until the needle is out, and some users bypass them
Their shields are made of plastic, which a needle can pierce from inside
They are sold only for hypodermic needles, not for blood collection sets
They must be removed before the tube is filled, leaving the tip exposed
preguntas.explicacion: Several things keep the risk above zero. With some designs the safety feature cannot be engaged until the needle has already left the patient; a needle can be dislodged during the procedure and leave the sharp exposed; some workers do not activate the feature at all; the feature itself can fail; and with some systems users can work around it, as when a needle is used to connect parts of a needleless intravenous system. Training and monitoring after implementation are what close that gap.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Indications; CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, Clinical Safety guidance, duration
preguntas.subtema: Using the hand rub · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k102 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How much alcohol-based hand rub goes on the hands, and how is it worked in?
opciones: About 3 to 5 mL, rubbed over every surface until the hands are dry
A single small drop, rubbed into the palms and wiped with a towel
About 15 to 20 mL, poured over the hands and rinsed off with water
Enough to fill a cupped hand, left to evaporate without any rubbing
preguntas.explicacion: When hands are not visibly soiled the alcohol rub is the preferred method, and it is used as the manufacturer directs: roughly three to five milliliters in the palm, rubbed vigorously over all hand surfaces until dry, which takes about twenty seconds. Rubbing until dry is what does the work, so wiping the product off with a towel or letting it sit unrubbed cuts the contact short, and the rub is never rinsed away with water.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(xiii)(A) and (g)(1)(i)(A), specimen containers and labels
preguntas.subtema: Specimen labeling exemption · CPT D1 k31 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Tubes of blood go from the draw room to the in-house laboratory in a closed rack, and the facility applies Universal Precautions to all specimens. Is a biohazard label required?
opciones: Not while they stay in the facility and are recognizable as specimens; it is required once they leave
Yes, always: every container of blood must carry the fluorescent orange-red biohazard label
No, never: labeling applies to regulated waste containers, not to specimens of blood
Only if the primary container becomes contaminated on the outside and needs a second container
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xiii)(A) wants the containers that carry specimens for storage, for transport or for shipping labeled or color-coded and closed, but it exempts a facility handling every specimen under Universal Precautions, provided those containers are recognizable as specimens; the exemption holds only inside that facility, and the label returns the moment the specimens leave it. Labeling is not limited to waste: (g)(1)(i)(A) reaches any container in which blood is stored, transported or shipped. Contamination on the outside triggers a second container under (d)(2)(xiii)(B), which is a different rule.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6; and StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Angle of insertion · CPT D3 3I k65 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: The bevel is inside the vein and blood has appeared. How is the needle advanced from there?
opciones: Along the vein, at whichever angle of entry proves easiest
Straight down at ninety degrees until the hub meets the skin
Back out a few millimeters and then in again at a steeper angle
Sideways across the vein so the bevel opens against the wall
preguntas.explicacion: The vein is entered swiftly at thirty degrees or less, and the needle then travels along the vein at whatever angle of entry is easiest, rather than being pushed deeper. Driving it beyond the lumen of the vein is what produces a hematoma, the pooling of blood under the skin.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", What are physical safeguards and How do you protect electronic information; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Storage of PHI Data and Computers
preguntas.subtema: Physical safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38
preguntas.pregunta: Which physical safeguard for PHI applies to the computer at a phlebotomy station?
opciones: Point the screen away from public view and log off when stepping away
Leave the session open so the next phlebotomist can chart without delay
Store the patient list on a personal flash drive as an unencrypted backup
Print the day's schedule and post it at the check-in window
preguntas.explicacion: Physical safeguards regulate access to equipment that holds PHI: computer screens are turned away from public view, privacy barriers are used at reception, PHI is never left unattended, and workstations are logged off whenever the user leaves, even for a few minutes. Portable devices are a known source of breaches, so patient data is not stored on personal laptops or flash drives, and if it must be, it is encrypted. A posted schedule and an open session both expose identifiable information to people not involved in care.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Throat swab culture (003746), How to Prepare for the Test and How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Mouthwash before throat culture · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.C.1 / V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.iii · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a sore throat says she gargled with antiseptic mouthwash on the way to the office. Why does that matter for a throat culture?
opciones: Antiseptic mouthwash is specifically to be avoided before the test, which is otherwise unprepared for
Antiseptic mouthwash is required before the test, so the swab picks up only pharyngeal organisms
Antiseptic mouthwash makes the patient gag more, which prevents the swab from reaching the tonsils
Antiseptic mouthwash stains the pharynx, so the provider cannot see where to place the swab
preguntas.explicacion: The one preparation instruction for a throat swab culture is to skip antiseptic mouthwash beforehand, and the sheet lists nothing else to do. The swab is rubbed at the back of the throat near the tonsils, and the provider may scrape several times to improve the chance of catching the organism. Rinsing with plain water belongs to sputum collection, to clear oral contaminants.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, and Will I need to do anything to prepare
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C 2K k45 · PBT II.A II.D · CCMA 3E2 k125 k128 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for a drug level ordered as a trough but says he took this morning's dose an hour ago. What matters?
opciones: Timing relative to the dose changes the result; report it before drawing
The level is stable through the day, so proceed and label the tube as ordered
Draw it now and relabel the sample as a peak level instead of a trough
Wait 30 minutes, which is the standard window for any trough sample
preguntas.explicacion: For TDM the test may need to be scheduled before or after the regular dose depending on the medicine, and the level in the blood varies over time as the body processes the drug. The trough is the point just before the next dose; a sample an hour after dosing is not that. Relabelling it as a peak invents a measurement that was not ordered.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Issues of Concern: Types of PPE
preguntas.subtema: Glove quality levels · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.c · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Two boxes of gloves list different acceptable quality levels. What does a lower number mean?
opciones: A better glove, with fewer pinholes and micro-perforations
A thicker glove, made to be worn as the outer of two pairs
A cheaper glove, meant for handling clean supplies only
A sterile glove, treated so that microbes are eliminated
preguntas.explicacion: The acceptable quality level counts how many defective units a batch may contain, so the lower the figure the better the glove: fewer pinholes and less potential for micro-perforation. The recommended minimum sits at 1.5 for surgical gloves; for medical examination gloves it is 2.5. Sterility is a separate property; surgery calls for gloves processed so that no microbes remain, and the evidence supports wearing two layers during an operation.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Bloodborne Infectious Disease Risk Factors (Feb. 13, 2025), Treatment and Reporting; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Step 3
preguntas.subtema: Reporting an exposure · CPT D1 1H k33 k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Immediately after washing a needlestick with soap and water, what does NIOSH tell the worker to do?
opciones: Report the incident to the supervisor and seek medical care right away
Wait 72 hours to see whether symptoms appear before reporting
Test the discarded needle for virus before deciding whether to report
Start the hepatitis B vaccine series on their own before reporting
preguntas.explicacion: NIOSH's steps run in order: wash a puncture or a cut with soap and water, flush a splash, irrigate the eyes, tell the supervisor what happened, and get medical care immediately so the risk can be judged; where applicable an incident report is filled in. The 72-hour figure is the outer limit for starting HIV PEP, not a waiting period. The WHO annex says specifically that a discarded needle or syringe is not tested for virus, and any prophylaxis or vaccination is decided during the medical evaluation.

preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: A trainee is taught the boundaries of the fossa before palpating it. Which muscles form its lateral and medial borders?
opciones: Brachioradialis on the lateral side and pronator teres on the medial side
Pronator teres on the lateral side and brachioradialis on the medial side
Biceps brachii on the lateral side and brachialis on the medial side
Brachialis on the lateral side and supinator on the medial side of the fossa
preguntas.explicacion: The triangle is bounded laterally by the medial edge of brachioradialis and medially by the lateral edge of pronator teres, with a line drawn between the epicondyles of the humerus closing the triangle above. Brachialis and supinator lie deeper: they form the floor rather than the sides.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Families and caregivers as part of the health care team
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 k49 · CCMA 3E1 k127 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient arrives with her adult son, who answers every question for her. How should you handle the visit?
opciones: Ask the patient how she sees her son's role, and keep addressing her directly
Speak mainly to the son, since he manages her medications at home
Ask the son to leave the room before any question is put to her
Record the son as her legal decision-maker for the rest of the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Check with the patient about how they see the companion's role, to protect privacy, and keep the patient involved, sitting so both can be addressed face to face and not directing remarks only to the companion. Asking the companion to step out is an option for sensitive topics, and legal authority to decide exists only for a named health care agent or proxy.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, section Can I continue taking medicine during a fast
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 k128 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether to skip his blood-pressure pill before a fasting draw. What is the correct guidance?
opciones: Do not stop a medicine unless the provider said to; ask the provider
Skip every medicine on the morning of the draw, because all pills break a fast
Take it only with a little juice so that the stomach is protected
Take it after the draw with water, never before a fasting sample
preguntas.explicacion: Patients should ask the provider whether their usual prescription and over-the-counter medicines are fine; for some tests the provider may ask them to stop, but a medicine is never stopped unless the provider says so. Vitamins and supplements should also be reported. Juice is on the list of drinks that break a fast.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being evaluated for pulmonary tuberculosis. Which sputum collection and storage instruction is correct?
opciones: Three early-morning specimens of 8 to 10 mL each, kept in a refrigerator
One early-morning specimen of 8 to 10 mL, kept at room temperature
Three specimens collected at any time of day, each frozen at −20 °C
Three early-morning specimens of 2 to 3 mL each, kept in a CO2 incubator
preguntas.explicacion: For Mycobacterium tuberculosis a series of three early-morning sputum specimens, 8 to 10 mL each, is collected and stored refrigerated; in patients who cannot cooperate the organism may be recovered from gastric contents obtained by stomach aspiration. Freezing is not part of the instruction, a single specimen is not a series, and the carbon dioxide incubator belongs to cerebrospinal fluid awaiting culture.

preguntas.subtema: Where the container goes · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Where should the sharps container sit while a phlebotomist is drawing blood at the bedside?
opciones: Visible and within arm's reach, and sealed once it is used up
On the cart outside the room, so the patient does not see it
In the utility room, where the used needles are carried after
On the floor by the bed, where it cannot be knocked over easily
preguntas.explicacion: The best-practice table asks for containers that resist puncture and do not leak, sealed once they are finished with, and kept in sight within arm's reach; the reason given is that this prevents needlestick injuries to patients, to health workers and to the community around them. The bloodborne pathogens standard puts the same idea in regulatory language: while in use the container stays easily accessible, as close as feasible to where the sharps are used, upright, and it is replaced before it overfills.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Introduction and Negligence or breach of duty
preguntas.subtema: Standard of care · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.b · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31
preguntas.pregunta: How is the standard of care defined when negligence is alleged?
opciones: The care a similarly trained peer in the same community would reasonably give
The care described in the facility's written policies, as approved by its governing body
The best care available anywhere in the country at the time of the event
The care the patient expected when consenting, as recorded on the consent form
preguntas.explicacion: Negligence is measured against the standard of care, which the law describes as what a reasonable physician in that community, holding comparable training and experience, would have done for this patient. Perfection is not the yardstick, and some states use the term gross negligence instead. Malpractice is care that falls short of what a colleague in the same post, with the same credentials, would have given, with injury resulting. Written policies and a patient's expectations may serve as evidence, but the legal measure is the reasonable, similarly trained clinician.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vancomycin", section Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: What target serum trough range is given for vancomycin, varying with the indication?
opciones: 10 to 20 micrograms per milliliter
1 to 2 micrograms per milliliter
30 to 40 micrograms per milliliter
100 to 200 micrograms per milliliter
preguntas.explicacion: Trough concentrations let the team judge whether the dosing regimen is working and how the drug is being cleared. The target serum trough depends on the indication and typically runs from 10 to 20 micrograms per milliliter. It is obtained ideally within the 30 minutes before a dose, once steady-state conditions have been reached.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, Is there anything else I need to know about fasting before a blood test?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient fasted twelve hours before a blood count on his own initiative, though nobody asked him to. What is the concern?
opciones: Fasting when it was not ordered can itself skew some test results
Fasting beyond eight hours voids any test drawn that same morning
Fasting without an order has to be logged as a protocol deviation
Fasting is harmless here, and the sample is unaffected either way
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are told plainly not to fast unless the provider asks them to, because fasting for some blood tests may itself affect the results and hand the provider an inaccurate picture of the patient's health. The instruction is to follow the preparation instructions given; no rule voids a sample because the fast ran long.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic drug levels (003430), Normal Results and Why the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Timed drug levels · CPT D2 k45 time of day · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A transplant patient is scheduled for a tacrolimus level. What timing does the reported reference range assume?
opciones: The sample is taken 12 hours after the dose
The sample is taken 2 hours after the dose
The sample is taken immediately before the dose
The sample is taken at any hour of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Tacrolimus is reported as 5 to 25 ng/mL with the sample drawn 12 hours after the dose, and the two other drugs used to suppress the immune response against transplanted organs carry the same note: cyclosporine 25 to 525 ng/mL and sirolimus 4 to 14 ng/mL, both at 12 hours. A level drawn off that schedule cannot be read against the published range.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Emancipated Minor", section Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: An unaccompanied 10-year-old with an emergency medical condition needs urgent labs and no parent can be reached. What protects the team that proceeds?
opciones: The emergency exception, also called the doctrine of implied consent
The mature minor doctrine, because the child understands the test
Informed permission, granted on the spot by the hospital administrator
Title X of the Public Health Service Act, covering minors' services
preguntas.explicacion: EMTALA calls for a screening exam whatever the consent situation, and when an unaccompanied minor turns out to have an emergency condition, care that saves life or limb goes ahead without waiting for a parent. The emergency exception, also called the doctrine of implied consent, covers that: the law supposes a reasonable parent would have agreed. Title X covers reproductive services.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Structure of the Heart, Blood Supply to the Myocardium; and Circulatory Pathways; and OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Right Atrium
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 I.A.2 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Where do the coronary arteries arise, and where does most of the blood from the coronary veins drain?
opciones: From the ascending aorta; into the coronary sinus and then the right atrium
From the aortic arch; into the coronary sinus and then the left atrium
From the pulmonary trunk; directly into the superior vena cava
From the ascending aorta; into the four pulmonary veins and left atrium
preguntas.explicacion: The right and left coronary arteries come off the ascending aorta and are its only branches. Once blood has crossed the capillaries of the myocardium, most cardiac veins empty into the coronary sinus, and that sinus opens on the back wall of the right atrium, just above and toward the midline from where the inferior vena cava enters.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Clinical Guidance for PEP, Recommendations and Treatment options; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Antiretroviral drugs for PEP; CDC, HIV at Work
preguntas.subtema: HIV PEP window and duration · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: When must HIV post-exposure prophylaxis begin, and how long does the course last, according to the CDC?
opciones: As soon as possible and within 72 hours; a 28-day course
As soon as possible and within 7 days; a 14-day course
As soon as possible and within 24 hours; a 7-day course
Within 72 hours; a 6-month course, the length of follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Patients who seek care within 72 hours are evaluated rapidly; PEP is not recommended more than 72 hours after exposure because it is unlikely to work, and the regimen is 28 days of a three-drug antiretroviral combination. WHO's annex gives the same limits: start within 72 hours and take the drugs continuously for 28 days. Six months is the length of antibody follow-up after an exposure, not the length of treatment, and the CDC's occupational page adds that PEP must start within 72 hours.

preguntas.fuente: The Joint Commission, National Patient Safety Goals for the Laboratory Program (January 2026), NPSG.01.01.01, Rationale and EP 1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2E k41 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3A2 k43 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist arrives at room 412 to collect a CBC. Which pair of identifiers satisfies The Joint Commission's NPSG.01.01.01 for laboratory services?
opciones: The patient's stated full name plus the assigned identification number
The room number 412 plus the assigned identification number on the band
The patient's stated full name plus the physical location of the bed
The assigned identification number read from the chart, used on its own
preguntas.explicacion: NPSG.01.01.01 asks for at least two identifiers whenever blood or another specimen is collected. The goal's rationale accepts a name, an assigned identification number, a telephone number or another identifier specific to the person, and EP 1 says outright that where the patient physically is, the room included, does not serve as one. A single identifier off the chart does not reach two.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Laboratory: OSHA Laboratory Standard, 29 CFR 1910.1450
preguntas.subtema: Chemical Hygiene Plan · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory works with hazardous chemicals. Which written program does 29 CFR 1910.1450 require it to develop and implement?
opciones: A Chemical Hygiene Plan
An Exposure Control Plan
A Fire Prevention Plan
A Hazard Communication Program
preguntas.explicacion: The Laboratory Standard reaches workplaces where hazardous chemicals are handled in fairly small amounts, outside any production line, across several different procedures, and it obliges the employer to write and implement a Chemical Hygiene Plan, a document setting out the work practices, the equipment, the protective gear and the procedures able to shield employees from the health hazards of the chemicals in that workplace. The Exposure Control Plan is the bloodborne pathogens document, the Fire Prevention Plan comes from 29 CFR 1910.39, and the written hazard communication program belongs to 1910.1200.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.4, Avoidance of contaminated phlebotomy equipment
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet and infection control · CPT D3 k60 · D1 1K k35 · PBT II.J VI.G · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Tourniquets have been found carrying methicillin-resistant staphylococci. By which two routes does that happen?
opciones: Poor hand hygiene by the phlebotomist and reuse of a contaminated band
Poor hand hygiene by the patient and storage of the band in a closed tray
Reuse of a contaminated band and application over a sleeve rather than skin
Poor hand hygiene by the phlebotomist and washing the band between patients
preguntas.explicacion: Up to a quarter of tourniquets have been found carrying this organism, and the two causes named are the phlebotomist's lack of hand hygiene and the reuse of bands that are already contaminated. That is why a disposable band is preferred and why gloves go on before the band.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2 Unsuccessful attempts in paediatric patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4B pediatric collection · PBT II.B II.I age-specific needs · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10
preguntas.pregunta: Two heel-pricks on an infant have failed to give a satisfactory sample. What is the next step?
opciones: Seek a second opinion on whether to try again or cancel the tests
Make a third attempt on the other heel with a longer lancet size
Switch to a finger-prick, which is allowed once the heel fails twice
Repeat the puncture on the same site, since it is already open
preguntas.explicacion: The number of sticks a child may get is capped: after two tries without a usable sample, someone else's judgment is asked for before deciding between one more attempt and calling the tests off. Reopening a puncture site is barred, and the choice of heel or finger rests on age and weight, not on how many tries have failed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D3 3F k62 · D2 2O · PBT II.E II.G · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: For which purpose is an arterial sample, rather than a venous one, the indicated specimen?
opciones: Gathering data on arterial blood gases
Gathering data on a complete blood count
Gathering data on coagulation factor levels
Gathering data on a fasting plasma glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Routine draws use veins because they are superficial and the puncture is more comfortable, and arterial sampling is reserved for the case where arterial blood is what the test needs, namely blood gases. The counts, clotting studies and chemistries of everyday work are all run on venous blood.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination: A Quality Tool for Clinical Laboratory Professionals, SOP model step 4; and Overview (2022), section 1
preguntas.subtema: Blood culture collection · CPT D4 4A · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139
preguntas.pregunta: Blood cultures and the first dose of an IV antibiotic are ordered together for a patient with suspected sepsis. What is the correct sequence?
opciones: Draw the blood cultures first, then let the antibiotic be started
Start the antibiotic and draw the cultures at any point within 24 hours
Draw one set before the antibiotic and the second set after the first dose
Draw the cultures 12 hours after the dose, when the drug is at its trough
preguntas.explicacion: Blood should be collected for culture before antimicrobial therapy whenever possible; that is step 4 of the CDC procedure and the recommendation for suspected sepsis in its overview. Without a culture taken before antibiotics, the causative organism is more likely to stay unknown and therapy is harder to de-escalate. The 24-hour period defines the septic episode for counting sets, and the 12-hour figure is a drug-level timing, not a culture rule.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 6.2.1 Patient identification
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k41 patient identifiers, D4 4B · PBT II.C patient identification · CCMA 3E12 match specimen to patient
preguntas.pregunta: How is a newborn in a hospital cot identified before drawing blood?
opciones: Use a band attached to the baby, ask the parent for the first and last names, and match the form
Use the band attached to the cot and the cot number, since a newborn cannot wear a band safely
Ask the nurse on duty to confirm the cot number and rely on that as the single identifier
Match the mother's wristband to the form, since the baby is registered under her record
preguntas.explicacion: In a baby or a child, a band counts only if it is on the patient: never the cot number, never a band tied to the cot or the bed. A parent or guardian who is present is asked to give the child's full name, and the name, birth date and hospital or file number written on the request have to match the patient in front of you.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation; and The Joint Commission, National Patient Safety Goals for the Laboratory Program (January 2026), NPSG.01.01.01, EP 1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2E k41 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3A2 k43 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: The ward holds two patients named John Ramirez. Beyond the full name and date of birth, what does the accepted practice add before the draw?
opciones: One further general identifier, such as the social security number or address
The bed each of the two men occupies, written by hand on both laboratory forms
The middle initial only, since the ward clerk keeps the two charts well apart
The list of tests ordered, because the two requisitions ask for different work
preguntas.explicacion: Every admitted patient carries an ID bracelet, and the name and date of birth are asked and recorded. The accepted consensus adds one more general identifier, a social security number or an address, because supplementary data lowers the rate of preventable errors. Location never counts: the identification goal rules out the room number or physical place.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Infection risk · CPT D3 k9 · D1 1K k31 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C k97 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which pathogens beyond HIV and the hepatitis viruses are named as transmissible through this procedure?
opciones: Viral haemorrhagic fevers and dengue, with malaria and syphilis through contaminated blood
Influenza and tuberculosis, with malaria and syphilis through contaminated blood
Viral haemorrhagic fevers and measles, with tetanus through the puncture wound
Dengue and influenza, with tetanus and rabies through the puncture wound itself
preguntas.explicacion: Drawing blood can expose workers and patients to bloodborne pathogens, and the list runs beyond HIV and hepatitis B and C to the viruses of Ebola, Lassa, Marburg and Crimean Congo haemorrhagic fever, and to dengue. Malaria and syphilis may also travel in contaminated blood.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Parenteral, Exposure Incident
preguntas.subtema: Parenteral exposure · CPT D1 k31 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A combative patient bites a phlebotomist's forearm and breaks the skin. Under the standard, this contact is best described as which of these?
opciones: A parenteral exposure, since piercing the skin barrier by a human bite is listed as parenteral
Not an exposure incident, because saliva is not OPIM outside dental procedures
An occupational exposure but not an exposure incident, because no needle was involved
A contact exposure that requires Contact Precautions rather than post-exposure follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b) defines parenteral as piercing through the mucous membranes, or through the skin barrier, in an event such as a needlestick, a human bite, a cut or an abrasion, and an exposure incident as parenteral, mucous-membrane or non-intact-skin contact with blood or OPIM arising from the employee's duties. A bite that breaks the skin is therefore a parenteral route, and if blood is involved the post-exposure evaluation of (f)(3) applies. Saliva is OPIM only in dental procedures, but the bite itself is the parenteral event; needles are one example of the route, not the only one.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7: Fill the laboratory sample tubes
preguntas.subtema: Syringe transfer · CPT D3 k54 k59 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k134 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Blood was drawn with a syringe and must be transferred into evacuated tubes. How does the WHO say the tube should be held and filled to prevent a needle-stick?
opciones: Place the tube in a rack and fill it with one hand, or use a needle shield between needle and hand
Hold the tube firmly in the free hand and pierce the stopper at an angle toward the fingers
Remove the stopper, rest the tube in the palm and inject slowly against the inner wall of the tube
Hold the tube against the patient's arm so the syringe can be steadied on the skin
preguntas.explicacion: Step 7 says best practice with a syringe or winged set is to put the tube in a rack before filling, and to use one hand to fill it, or a shield placed between the needle and the hand that holds the tube. The stopper is pierced from directly above with slow, steady pressure and is never removed, because that releases the vacuum. Holding the tube in the hand is exactly the exposure the step is designed to avoid.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Universal Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Standard and universal precautions · CPT D1 1J k31 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C k99 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2.d · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Under the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens standard, what does the term "Universal Precautions" mean?
