preguntas.subtema: Respirator removal · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: When doffing PPE after caring for a patient on Airborne Precautions, where should the respirator be removed?
opciones: After exiting the patient room, unlike the other PPE items
Inside the room, immediately after the gloves
Inside the room, before the gown so the ties are reachable
At the nurses' station, once hands have been washed
preguntas.explicacion: Doffing takes place outside patient rooms, and when a respirator is in use it is not removed until after exiting the patient room. In the sequence the respirator comes off last, after gloves, eye protection and gown, by releasing the ties or straps behind the head without touching the front or mouth area. Removing it inside the room would expose the wearer to the air the respirator was protecting against, and hand hygiene is performed after the removal, not before.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", section Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: OGTT load · CPT D4 4H tolerance tests · PBT II.G common tests · CCMA 3E k139
preguntas.pregunta: What glucose load is given to a nonpregnant adult for a standard diagnostic oral glucose tolerance test?
opciones: 75 g of glucose dissolved in 250 to 300 mL of water
50 g of glucose, taken without any prior fasting
100 g of glucose after a fast of 8 to 14 hours
1.75 g of glucose per kilogram of body weight
preguntas.explicacion: The standard adult OGTT uses 75 g of glucose, dissolved in 250 to 300 mL of water and drunk over about five minutes, with venous plasma glucose measured fasting and again 2 hours after the load. Fifty grams is the nonfasting screening drink used in pregnancy, 100 g is the 3-hour diagnostic test that follows a positive screen, and 1.75 g per kilogram, capped at 75 g, is the dose for children.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1241(e), Standard: Test request
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F k92 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E k146
preguntas.pregunta: A clerk types the tests from a paper requisition into the laboratory information system. What does CLIA require of that step?
opciones: That the requisition information be transcribed or entered accurately
That the paper requisition be destroyed once the entry is complete
That a pathologist countersign every entry made from a paper form
That the entry be made within 30 days of the specimen's arrival in the lab
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1241(e) says that when requisition or authorization data are transcribed or entered into a record system or an LIS, the laboratory must ensure the entry is accurate. Data entry of the request is one of the pre-analytical quality indicators precisely because missing, added or misread tests at this step change what gets done. The 30-day figure belongs to oral orders, and no countersignature or destruction of the form is required.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(2)(iii), (f)(2)(ii) and (f)(1)(ii), Hepatitis B Vaccination
preguntas.subtema: Hepatitis B vaccination, later acceptance · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist declined the hepatitis B vaccine when hired. Six months later, still in the same job, she asks for it. What does OSHA require?
opciones: The employer must make the vaccine available at that time, at no cost, while she remains covered
She must pay for the series herself, since the employer's offer ended with the signed declination
The employer may require a prescreening antibody test before agreeing to provide the series
She must wait for the next annual training session, when the vaccine is offered again to staff
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(2)(iii) covers exactly this case: an employee who first declines and later, while still covered by the standard, decides to accept gets the vaccination made available at that point. Nothing in the standard makes the earlier declination final. Paragraph (f)(1)(ii) keeps every medical procedure under (f), the vaccine included, free of charge and at a reasonable time and place, and (f)(2)(ii) bars the employer from requiring prescreening first. The annual training is a separate duty and is not the trigger for the offer.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vancomycin", section Monitoring; and section Mechanism of Action, Pharmacokinetics
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C k45 · PBT II.A II.D · CCMA 3E2 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is on oral vancomycin for colitis and the ward asks for a trough. What does the guidance say?
opciones: Oral vancomycin usually needs no serum concentration monitoring
Oral vancomycin needs a trough within 30 minutes before the dose
Oral vancomycin needs a peak drawn as the capsule is swallowed
Oral vancomycin needs a trough only once steady state is reached
preguntas.explicacion: Taken by mouth, vancomycin usually calls for no serum concentration monitoring, unlike the intravenous route, because barely any of it reaches the circulation: oral bioavailability sits under 10%. The pre-dose trough at steady state and the peak taken at the end of the infusion both belong to the intravenous drug.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: Discarding the first drop · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.4 · CCMA 3D2 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.ii · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the first drop of blood wiped away before applying blood to a glucose test strip?
opciones: It may be hemolyzed, or carry interstitial and intracellular fluid, either of which skews the reading
It contains alcohol from the skin preparation, which the guidance says lowers the glucose reading by about 10 %
It is arterial rather than capillary blood and therefore reads higher than the venous reference method does
It clots too quickly on the strip, so most meters will display an insufficient-sample error message
preguntas.explicacion: Once the lancet has fired, clean gauze wipes the first drop away: it may be hemolyzed, or carry fluid from between and inside the cells, and either distorts the result. Gentle pressure near the site brings a second drop up, and that one touches the tip of the strip with volume enough; some meters flag an insufficient sample and let more blood go onto the same strip.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Elbow Cubital Fossa", section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: Into which vessels does the brachial artery divide, and at what point?
opciones: Into the ulnar and radial arteries, at the apex of the cubital fossa
Into the radial and ulnar arteries, at the superior border of the fossa
Into the cephalic and basilic branches, at the apex of the cubital fossa
Into the radial and median branches, at the medial epicondyle of the humerus
preguntas.explicacion: The brachial artery supplies the forearm and splits into the ulnar and the radial artery at the apex of the fossa, the corner that points downwards. Cephalic and basilic are veins, not branches of an artery, and they join one another through the median cubital vein higher in the triangle.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Complications
preguntas.subtema: Complications · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which problems are grouped together as the local complications of a venous puncture?
opciones: Failure of the attempt, arterial or nerve injury, hematoma or bleeding
Failure of the attempt, low blood sugar, dehydration or a raised pulse
Arterial injury, latex allergy, a broken tube or a mislabelled specimen
Nerve injury, hemoconcentration, a clotted tube or an expired needle
preguntas.explicacion: Grouped as local complications are failure of the procedure itself, injury to an artery or a nerve, and bleeding or a hematoma where the catheter went in. Faults such as a clotted tube or a wrong label are specimen problems rather than injuries to the patient, though they cost a second draw.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Removal of PPE; StatPearls, "Universal Precautions", Removing PPE
preguntas.subtema: Doffing sequence · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which item comes off first when removing PPE, in the CDC-recommended sequence?
opciones: Gloves, peeled so the contaminated outside stays inside
The mask or respirator, released from behind the head
The gown, pulled from the shoulders and turned inside out
Eye protection, lifted by the earpieces or the strap
preguntas.explicacion: The doffing sequence starts with the gloves: grasp the palm of one glove with the other gloved hand and peel it off, then slide the bare fingers under the remaining glove at the wrist and peel it over the first. Eye protection follows, handled by strap or earpieces without touching the front; then the gown, untied and pulled away from neck and shoulders, turned inside out; and the mask or respirator last, by the ties behind the head. Hand hygiene follows removal and any time contamination is suspected.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(e)(1)(i) and (e)(1)(ii), Written hazard communication program
preguntas.subtema: The written program · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Besides describing labels, data sheets and training, what must a written hazard communication program contain?
opciones: A list of the hazardous chemicals present, and how non-routine tasks are handled
A copy of every safety data sheet, arranged by section and by supplier
The exposure limits of each chemical and the results of air monitoring
The signed acknowledgment of each employee who attended the training
preguntas.explicacion: The written program describes how the employer will meet what is required on labels and other warnings, on safety data sheets, and on informing and training employees. Beyond that it carries two more pieces: a list naming the hazardous chemicals known to be there, identified as the corresponding data sheet identifies them, and the methods by which employees will be told about the hazards of non-routine tasks and of chemicals inside unlabeled pipes in their work areas. The list may cover the whole workplace or be drawn up area by area.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw with cultures · CPT D4 k78 order of draw for blood cultures · PBT II.H.1 venous order of draw · CCMA 3E6 k132
preguntas.pregunta: Which tube is filled immediately after the blood culture bottle in the recommended order of draw?
opciones: The non-additive tube
The light blue citrate tube
The lavender EDTA tube
The gray fluoride tube
preguntas.explicacion: In the recommended sequence the culture bottle is drawn first and the non-additive tube second, ahead of the light blue citrate tube at position three. EDTA sits at eight and the gray oxalate/fluoride tube last at ten. Keeping the bottles ahead of everything else protects the culture from additive carried over on the needle, and the citrate tube keeps its own place because it needs a full draw.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Gestational Diabetes", Evaluation; MedlinePlus, Glucose screening tests during pregnancy (007562), What Abnormal Results Mean
preguntas.subtema: Gestational OGTT interpretation · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139
preguntas.pregunta: On the 3-hour gestational glucose tolerance test, how many abnormal values are needed for the diagnosis?
opciones: Two or more of the four values
One value, whichever hour it is
Three or more of the four values
All four of the values must be high
preguntas.explicacion: Gestational diabetes is established by two or more abnormal results on the 3-hour test. When only one value is above normal, the provider may simply ask for changes in diet and repeat the testing afterwards, so a single high hour settles nothing. That is why four measurements are taken rather than one, and why the screening step is not a diagnosis on its own.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 3.3 Specimen collection containers
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3E k129 k136 · NCMA 2C.6 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c)
preguntas.pregunta: A green-top heparin tube arrives for a viral PCR. Why do current guidelines say to reject it, and which tubes are recommended instead?
opciones: Heparin inhibits DNA amplification in a dose-dependent way and is carried through extraction; EDTA or ACD tubes are recommended
Heparin chelates the magnesium the polymerase needs for amplification; citrate or fluoride tubes are recommended instead
Heparin degrades RNA through its own nuclease activity during storage; serum tubes with clot activator are recommended instead
Heparin causes hemolysis during centrifugation and releases heme into the plasma; plain red-top tubes are recommended instead
preguntas.explicacion: Heparin inhibits the amplification of DNA in a way that depends on the dose, and on which polymerase is in use, and it survives both DNA and RNA extraction, so the consensus is that heparinised plasma has no place in molecular infectious disease testing and current guidelines have heparin-containing specimens rejected. The anticoagulants recommended instead are K2/K3-EDTA and acid citrate dextrose, chelators that lock up the calcium the DNA-degrading nucleases need.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Complications · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which serious adverse event is described as rare during phlebotomy?
opciones: Loss of consciousness accompanied by tonic clonic seizures
Loss of consciousness lasting under a couple of minutes only
Pain at the puncture site with anxiety about the procedure
Bruising and hematoma at the site of the venepuncture
preguntas.explicacion: Serious adverse events tied to drawing blood are rare, and the example given is a loss of consciousness with tonic clonic fits. Pain at the site, anxiety and fainting are put in the less severe group, and bruising with hematoma is the best documented event of all.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, opening paragraph; 18.6 Blood Typing, Antigens, Antibodies, and Transfusion Reactions; 18.2 Production of the Formed Elements
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k3 k8 (applied D3) · PBT I.C · RMA I.B.2.a · NCMA 1.2 EKB 3
preguntas.pregunta: Which term names the process that stops blood loss after a vessel is damaged?
opciones: Hemostasis
Hemolysis
Hemorrhage
Hemopoiesis
preguntas.explicacion: Hemostasis is the sealing of a torn vessel so that blood loss stops; when it fails the result is hemorrhage, bleeding out of control. Hemolysis is the rupture of red cells with hemoglobin spilling out, as after an incompatible transfusion, and hemopoiesis, from the roots for blood and production, is the making of the formed elements in the marrow.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Interfering Factors; and StatPearls, "Thrombocytopenia", section Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Additives and pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 k57 · PBT II.J II.G · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A blood count drawn in EDTA reports a platelet count far below the patient's usual value, and the smear shows clumps. Which repeat specimen is suggested?
opciones: A repeat count on blood collected into a citrate tube
A repeat count on blood collected into a heparin tube
A repeat count on serum from a clot activator tube
A repeat count on the same EDTA tube after warming it
preguntas.explicacion: Platelets can clump in EDTA because of antibodies that act only in the presence of that anticoagulant, and the analyser then reports a falsely low count. The way round it is to repeat the count on blood taken into a citrate tube instead. Serum has no platelets left to count.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Obtaining a thorough history
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 k40 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA I.A.3 / 2027 A.3.c · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient has just given her history to the rooming assistant. What does the guidance ask of the next person?
opciones: Have the patient tell the story once, since repeating it tires her
Take the whole history again, so two versions can be compared
Take the history only from the relative who came with her today
Skip the history, since a form was filled in the waiting room
preguntas.explicacion: Flexibility is advised in taking an older patient's history: wherever it can be arranged, she tells her story a single time, even where other staff in the office would normally help gather it, because giving the account once and then again is tiring. Preliminary data may instead be pulled from records or from forms filled in at home.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: Incorrect urine collection stayed at 9.2 % in the audited hospital even after staff began speaking to patients. What were patients told about?
opciones: The sampling itself, the type of container, and collecting the midstream portion
Fasting for twelve hours, the type of container, and the time of the first void
The volume required, the transport temperature, and the use of a preservative
The sampling itself, the labeling of the cup, and the delivery time to the bench
preguntas.explicacion: Urine testing is unusually exposed to preanalytical trouble because the patient, not a trained collector, takes the sample. In that laboratory the receiving secretary explained the sampling, the container types, sterile and with or without preservative, and how to catch the midstream portion. Even so, incorrect collection remained at 9.2 % of the urine samples received.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 3F k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's chart records a vascular graft in the arm the phlebotomist was about to use. What does that mean for the draw?
opciones: The graft is a listed contraindication, so another site is chosen
The graft is acceptable if the puncture is made well below it
The graft is acceptable once the tourniquet is placed above it
The graft only rules out the arm when dialysis is being given
preguntas.explicacion: Among the contraindications tied to the site are scar tissue from earlier attempts, cellulitis or an abscess, a hematoma, a vascular graft, venous fibrosis felt on palpation, a previous radical mastectomy on that side, and any device placed for venous access.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix B, Instructions for Recording Temperatures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT VI.A · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: Every row of a refrigerator temperature log is dated and initialled by the person who read the thermometer. Who else reviews and signs the log, and when?
opciones: Whoever directs or supervises the testing, once the month is complete
Whoever directs or supervises the testing, each day a reading is entered
Whoever directs or supervises the testing, only when a reading is out of range
Whoever reads the thermometer, again at the end of every working week
preguntas.explicacion: Each reading is dated and initialled or signed by whoever took it; on top of that, whoever directs or supervises testing reviews and signs the log when it is complete for the month. That same person is contacted straight away when a temperature falls outside the recommended range, but the signature is a monthly review, not a daily one and not an out-of-range one.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 6.2.2 Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4B k80 assisting with pediatric collection · PBT II.B age-specific needs · CCMA 3E1 prepare patient
preguntas.pregunta: In the table position for infant venipuncture, why does the immobilizer reach across the child to hold the wrist palm up?
opciones: It anchors the shoulder against twisting, and the wrist grasp acts as a tourniquet
It keeps the child's face turned away so the needle is never seen by the child
It compresses the brachial artery, which slows the flow and prevents a hematoma
It frees the phlebotomist's second hand to apply a rubber tourniquet above
preguntas.explicacion: Two adults face each other across the examination table. The one holding the child lays the baby on its back with its head resting on the outstretched arm, pulls it in close, takes the elbow, and reaches over the child with the free arm to hold the wrist palm up. Reaching over pins the shoulder so the child cannot twist or rock, and the firm hold on the wrist does the work of a tourniquet.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Why is there no single free-hemoglobin concentration above which every test result must be rejected?
opciones: The interference is optical, chemical or immunological, so the acceptable limit depends on the test and the method
The interference affects only enzymes, so a single limit applies to LDH and CK and none to other analytes
The interference disappears once the serum is diluted, so any sample can be reported after dilution
The interference is constant across analyzers, but each laboratory is free to pick its own limit
preguntas.explicacion: Free hemoglobin interferes in different ways, optically, chemically, or by interacting with antigen or antibody in immunoassays, so the upper limit of hemoglobin tolerated in serum or plasma is test- and method-dependent; the reagent's method description should state the serum index limitations, and laboratories are advised to load those cut-offs into their analyzers. Even specific proteins such as CRP and haptoglobin can be affected.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A bronchoalveolar lavage specimen for molecular detection of Pneumocystis and Mycobacterium tuberculosis is being sent from the bronchoscopy suite. How is it transported and stored?
opciones: Transported on ice; stored at 4 °C for up to 72 hours, or at −20 to −80 °C for the long term
Transported at room temperature; stored at 4 °C for up to 4 hours, then discarded as unsuitable
Transported on wet ice only if RNA is the target; stored at room temperature for up to 7 days
Transported frozen at −70 °C; stored at 4 to 8 °C for up to 7 days with a mucolytic additive
preguntas.explicacion: For bronchoalveolar lavage the general guideline is transport on ice, storage at 4 °C for up to 72 hours, and −20 to −80 °C for long-term keeping; time and temperature are the preanalytical variables listed for it. Wet ice reserved for RNA targets is the CSF entry, 4 to 8 °C for 7 days with N-acetyl-L-cysteine or dithiothreitol is the sputum entry, and −70 °C is the transport temperature for viral culture.

preguntas.fuente: 21 CFR 630.10(f)(5); StatPearls, "Blood Donation", section Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Donor weight standard · CPT D4 4D k82 weight
preguntas.pregunta: What is the minimum weight for a blood donor?
opciones: 50 kilograms, that is 110 pounds
45 kilograms, that is 100 pounds
57 kilograms, that is 125 pounds
68 kilograms, that is 150 pounds
preguntas.explicacion: A minimum weight of 50 kilograms is required, which the regulation gives as 110 pounds; the same floor turns up in the eligibility criteria blood centers use. It is part of the day-of-donation physical assessment, along with temperature, blood pressure, hemoglobin or hematocrit, pulse and the skin examination.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Tourniquet and Gloves; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(iii)
preguntas.subtema: Latex and the tourniquet · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a history of latex allergy and the phlebotomist has no elastic band at hand. What must she not do?
opciones: Use a latex glove as a tourniquet on that patient
Ask a colleague to bring a latex-free band to the room
Draw the sample without applying a tourniquet at all
Use a clean band that has been reprocessed since its last use
preguntas.explicacion: The best-practice table is explicit that a latex glove must never stand in as a tourniquet where the patient reports a history of latex allergy, since some patients react to latex. Gloves follow the same logic: one clean, well-fitting disposable pair, latex or latex-free, for each patient or each procedure. The employer must also keep hypoallergenic gloves or similar alternatives within reach for workers who react to the ones normally supplied.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C k42 · PBT II.A · CCMA 3E2 k124
preguntas.pregunta: A new phlebotomist asks where the reason for each draw is meant to be written down. Where does the WHO expect the indications to be set out?
opciones: In a written protocol, or in documented laboratory-form instructions
In the verbal handover the ward nurse gives the phlebotomist each morning
On the tube labels, which carry the tests along with the patient details
In the training record each phlebotomist keeps for supervised sampling
preguntas.explicacion: Clear instructions means the indications for taking blood are set out plainly, whether in a written protocol or in instructions that have been documented, and the laboratory form is offered as the example. Tube labels carry names, file number, date of birth and the time of the draw; training and supervision are dealt with in another part of the chapter.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2M · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO Annex C script, what is the patient told about where the results will go?
opciones: They are returned to the named clinician who ordered the tests
They are mailed to the patient's home address within one week
They are read to the patient by the phlebotomist before leaving
They are posted in the patient portal on the same day
preguntas.explicacion: The script says the tubes will be labeled with the patient's name and details, sent to the laboratory, and that the results will be returned to the doctor whose name the worker mentions, the clinician who ordered the tests. It then asks whether the patient has questions, understood the explanation, and is willing to be tested.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Glucose tolerance test (003466), Normal Results and What Abnormal Results Mean; StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings
preguntas.subtema: OGTT interpretation · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139
preguntas.pregunta: A nonpregnant adult's 2-hour value on a 75-g OGTT is 165 mg/dL. How is it interpreted?
opciones: Impaired glucose tolerance (140 to 199 mg/dL)
Normal glucose tolerance (below 200 mg/dL)
Diabetes, since it exceeds 126 mg/dL
Impaired fasting glucose (100 to 125 mg/dL)
preguntas.explicacion: At two hours, below 140 mg/dL is normal, 140 to 199 mg/dL is impaired glucose tolerance (what a provider may call prediabetes) and 200 mg/dL or higher is diagnostic of diabetes, so 165 is impaired tolerance. The 126 cutoff applies to fasting glucose repeated on two tests, and 100 to 125 defines impaired fasting glucose, another fasting category; below 200 is the 1-hour reference, not the 2-hour one.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guidelines for Health Care Personnel Exposed to Hepatitis C Virus, Test the source patient; Test the HCP; Follow-up testing
preguntas.subtema: HCV testing algorithm · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: According to the CDC, when is the source patient tested for hepatitis C after an occupational exposure?
opciones: Right away, within 48 hours if possible, ideally by RNA testing
Within 72 hours, using an antibody test with no reflex to RNA
At 3 to 6 weeks, when HCV RNA becomes detectable in the source
At 4 to 6 months, alongside the exposed worker's final antibody test
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC has the source patient tested right away, within 48 hours where that can be managed, and prefers a nucleic acid test for HCV RNA, or else an antibody test that reflexes to NAT when positive; the exposed worker is tested at the same time with an antibody test that reflexes to RNA. Where follow-up is indicated, the worker gets an RNA test at 3 to 6 weeks and a final antibody test at 4 to 6 months. Those later dates belong to the worker's schedule, not the source's, and 72 hours is the HIV PEP window.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Drug Testing", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings
preguntas.subtema: Drug screen interpretation · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 · RMA III.C.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: A patient known to take clonazepam has a negative benzodiazepine screen. What is the most likely explanation?
opciones: The immunoassay targets oxazepam and may miss other benzodiazepines
The specimen was collected outside the 1-to-2-hour appearance window
The patient's urine was too dilute for any immunoassay to read it
Benzodiazepines are only measurable in blood, never in urine at all
preguntas.explicacion: A negative result means the substance the assay looks for was not detected, either because the concentration sat below the threshold or because there was no use in the relevant window. False negatives are common when the analytes an immunoassay targets are not known: benzodiazepine testing often aims at the metabolite oxazepam and may miss clonazepam or alprazolam. A negative does not rule out use.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, scope of practice · CPT D1 1D scope of practice · CCMA 7A k214 · RMA I.C.6 scope of practice · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the phlebotomist whether her potassium result means she has kidney disease. What is the appropriate response?
opciones: Say that the ordering provider interprets results, and route the question to that provider
Read the reference interval aloud and show her where her own value falls against it
Tell her the value is normal for her age, since age-based intervals are on the report
Refuse to discuss the report at all, because privacy rules bar giving results to patients
preguntas.explicacion: CLIA puts interpretation on the far side of the bench: reference intervals go to whoever was authorized to order the test and to whoever is responsible for using the results, and the results themselves are released only to those people. Refusing outright is wrong for another reason, since a patient may request access to her own completed report.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Complications
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2E k41 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3E12 k124 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: A quality meeting asks where phlebotomy most often goes wrong. Which two problems are reported as the most likely errors?
opciones: Patient identification and improper labeling of the tubes
Nerve injury and added pain from poor needle technique
Hematoma at the site and bleeding after the needle is out
Expired tubes and a needle and holder of different makes
preguntas.explicacion: The complications section lists pain and possible nerve injury from poor technique, and hematoma where pressure is not applied during and after the draw. But the studies it cites put two other things first as the likeliest errors: identifying the patient, and labeling the tube badly. That is why identity and labels are double-checked with the patient there.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 4: Communicate Clearly, Actions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 · CCMA 6 k199 k202 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Which word choice matches plain-language guidance for talking with patients?
opciones: 'Helpful' rather than 'beneficial'
'Exacerbate' rather than 'make worse'
'Abdomen' rather than 'tummy or belly'
'Venipuncture' rather than 'blood draw'
preguntas.explicacion: The examples are direct: say 'helpful' where you would have said 'beneficial', and 'make worse' where you would have said 'exacerbate', and use everyday words such as tummy or belly rather than abdomen, keeping clear of acronyms. If a medical term really matters, ask whether the patient knows it and then define it simply. The three distractors each run the advice backwards.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, Blood alcohol concentration in the clinical laboratory: a narrative review, Biochemia Medica 2024 (PMC10564119), section Sample container
preguntas.subtema: Forensic alcohol handling · CPT D4 4I k85 and D5 5C k91 · PBT III.A.4 special sample types
preguntas.pregunta: Apart from the antiseptic, what is the one procedural difference between a diagnostic and a medico-legal blood alcohol draw?
opciones: A chain of custody is adopted so the specimen can be traced
A second specimen is drawn from the opposite arm as a control
The specimen is frozen immediately rather than refrigerated
The tube is sealed with tamper-evident tape by a police officer
preguntas.explicacion: Correct diagnostic preanalytical handling already gives a forensically defensible result: transport, processing at room temperature for under three hours, short-term storage at 4 °C and long-term storage frozen all meet the forensic requirement. The only remaining differentiation is adopting a chain of custody for traceability whenever the request has an explicit medico-legal purpose. Freezing is for monthly or yearly storage.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", section Pathophysiology; and "Vasovagal Episode", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: During a difficult draw the patient begins to sweat and turn pale but does not lose consciousness. What is this state called?
opciones: Near syncope or presyncope
Vasovagal or reflex syncope
Situational reflex syncope
Carotid sinus syncope
preguntas.explicacion: Near syncope or presyncope is the feeling that one is going to pass out without actually doing so, and says it shares the mechanism of syncope, cerebral hypoperfusion. Vasovagal, situational and carotid sinus syncope are the three types of reflex syncope in the vasovagal chapter, all of which involve an actual transient loss of consciousness.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Oral Glucose Tolerance Test
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k45 k46 · PBT II.D II.G · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: Which sequence correctly describes the oral glucose tolerance test?
opciones: Fasting sample, a 75 g glucose load, and a second sample at 2 hours
Fasting sample, a 75 g glucose load, and a second sample at 1 hour
Random sample, a 75 g glucose load, and a second sample drawn at 2 hours
Fasting sample, 150 g of carbohydrate, and a sample at 3 hours
preguntas.explicacion: The OGTT runs like this: a fasting sample after at least 8 hours without food, then 75 g of anhydrous glucose taken dissolved in water, then a second sample at 2 hours; a 2-hour value of 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or above meets the diabetes criterion. The one-hour sample belongs to the challenge test, and 150 g of carbohydrate refers to the traditional three-day pre-test diet.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders
preguntas.subtema: Safe patient handling · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G · CMA I.B.9 / 2027 I.B.8 · NCMA 2A.5
preguntas.pregunta: Why does OSHA promote Safe Patient Handling programs with lifting equipment in healthcare?
opciones: Musculoskeletal disorders lead lost-workday injuries in healthcare, largely from manual lifting
Needlesticks are the leading cause of lost-workday injuries, and lifts keep hands away from sharps
Falls on wet floors are the leading cause, and lifting devices keep patients off the floor
Latex allergy is the leading cause, and lifting devices reduce glove use
preguntas.explicacion: In healthcare, no other category costs more lost workdays than work-related musculoskeletal disorders, the ones affecting the neck, the upper limbs and the low back; sprains and strains are the commonest injuries, and the shoulders and the low back the areas most often hurt. The driver is lifting, moving and repositioning patients by hand, work made harder as patients get heavier. Safe Patient Handling programs answer it with transfer and lifting devices, commitment from management, workers taking part in choosing the devices, hazard assessment and training.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(iii)(A), Contaminated Sharps Discarding and Containment
preguntas.subtema: Sharps containers and regulated waste · CPT D1 k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: OSHA requires that contaminated sharps be discarded into containers with which combination of features?
opciones: Closable, puncture resistant, leakproof on sides and bottom, and labeled or color-coded
Closable, leakproof and labeled or color-coded, with no requirement at all to resist punctures
Fluorescent orange-red with the biohazard symbol, and emptied by hand when it is three-quarters full
Puncture resistant and leakproof on sides and bottom, but left open during use to speed up disposal
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(iii)(A) lists four features for the container that receives contaminated sharps: it closes, it resists punctures, it does not leak through the sides or the bottom, and it carries the biohazard label or the color code the standard prescribes. While in use it also has to be easy to reach, kept upright, and replaced before it overfills. A container without puncture resistance is the description of a regulated-waste bag in (d)(4)(iii)(B), not a sharps container; reusable sharps containers must never be opened or emptied by hand; and a container left open during use fails the first requirement.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 3.1, Recommended needle gauge, length and device
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge and device by age · CPT D3 k56 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A blood specimen is needed from a neonate. Which needle gauge, device and length does WHO Table 3.1 recommend?
opciones: 23 G winged (butterfly) set, 0.5 inch or 0.75 cm
22 G straight needle, 1 inch or 2.54 cm
21 G straight needle, 1 to 1.5 inch or 2.54 cm long
25 G winged (butterfly) set, 0.5 inch or 0.75 cm
preguntas.explicacion: For the neonatal column, Table 3.1 marks only one option: a 23 G winged butterfly set of 0.5 inch or 0.75 cm, the same device listed for pediatric, elderly and small-vein patients. The 22 G 1 inch needle is for adults and pediatric patients, the 21 G 1 to 1.5 inch needle for adults only, and 25 G does not appear in the table at all.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Testing Procedures; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 first drop · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10
preguntas.pregunta: After lancing a fingertip for a glucometer reading, which drop is applied to the test strip?
opciones: The second drop, after the first is wiped away with clean gauze
The first drop, before any tissue fluid has time to mix with it
The third drop, after two drops are wiped to clear the alcohol
Any drop, provided gentle pressure was applied before the puncture
preguntas.explicacion: The operator wipes the first drop away with clean gauze or tissue, since it may be hemolysed or carry fluid from inside and between the cells, then presses gently near the site for a second drop, which touches the tip of the strip. Some meters flag an insufficient sample and let more blood onto the same strip. That first-drop rule holds for every skin puncture.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Chambers and Circulation through the Heart
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 I.A.2 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which arteries are the exception to the rule, carrying blood that is poor in oxygen after birth?
opciones: The pulmonary trunk and its branches
The four pulmonary veins to the left atrium
The coronary arteries off the ascending aorta
The venae cavae entering the right atrium
preguntas.explicacion: The pulmonary trunk and the two arteries it splits into carry oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle out to the lungs, the one exception among arteries once a person is born; the pulmonary veins are the matching exception among veins, bringing richly oxygenated blood into the left atrium. The coronary arteries leave the ascending aorta carrying oxygenated blood, and the venae cavae are veins.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.512(f)(1) and (f)(2), Disclosures for law enforcement purposes
preguntas.subtema: Law enforcement disclosures · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k37
preguntas.pregunta: A police officer asks the laboratory for a patient's blood type and home address to locate a suspect. Which statement reflects HIPAA?
opciones: Name, address and ABO blood type may be given; analyses of body fluids may not
No information may be disclosed without a court order, not even the name
The full record may be disclosed, since law enforcement requests override the Privacy Rule
Only the results of body fluid analyses may be disclosed, not the address
preguntas.explicacion: When the purpose is to identify or locate a fugitive, a suspect, a material witness or someone missing, 164.512(f)(2) lets a covered entity release only a fixed list: name and address, date and place of birth, Social Security number, ABO blood type and Rh factor, type of injury, date and time of treatment or death, and distinguishing physical characteristics. DNA, dental records and the typing, sampling or analysis of body fluid or tissue are expressly left out. Other law-enforcement disclosures need a court order, a warrant, a subpoena or a qualifying administrative request.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 4: Communicate Clearly, Research Findings
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 · CCMA 6 k199 k202 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h
preguntas.pregunta: Kessels (2003) measured how much of the medical information given at a visit is forgotten immediately. How much?
opciones: Up to 80%
Up to 50%
Up to 20%
Up to 65%
preguntas.explicacion: Kessels found that up to 80% of the medical information a patient hears at an office visit is gone straight away, and that nearly half of what does stay is wrong. That is the basis for holding the message to a few points, repeating them, and confirming with teach-back instead of asking whether the patient understood.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Green
preguntas.subtema: Additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: How does the heparin in a green top tube prevent coagulation?
opciones: It inactivates thrombin, so fibrin is not formed and the sample stays as plasma
It chelates calcium ions, the same mechanism the citrate tube uses
It preserves the viability of microorganisms in a broth mixture
It works as an antiglycolytic agent that keeps glucose stable for days
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 gives the mode of action of sodium or lithium heparin as inactivating thrombin and thromboplastin, and the tube review says heparin inhibits thrombin formation. Calcium chelation is the mechanism the review assigns to EDTA and to citrate; the broth belongs to the blood culture bottle; and the antiglycolytic agent is the sodium fluoride in the gray tube.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, PSNet Patient Safety Primer: Reporting Patient Safety Events
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 6 k211 · CMA I.B.11.c · 2027 I.B.10.c · CMAA 3 k44 · NCMA 4.10 · CPT 1N k39
preguntas.pregunta: Who normally files the report after a patient falls in the clinic hallway?
opciones: The frontline staff member who was involved in or saw the event
The risk manager, once the chart has been reviewed for the week
The provider who signs the chart at the end of that patient's visit
The office manager, who collects the accounts of everyone involved
preguntas.explicacion: Event reporting is voluntary and depends on the people who were there: the first report usually comes from a frontline staff member who was involved in the event itself, or in what led up to it, rather than from management or the patient safety staff. Falls and medication errors are among the events reported most often through these systems.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Collecting Specimens for Novel Influenza A Virus Testing, Recommended swabs and Swabs that are not recommended
preguntas.subtema: Swab material · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.C.2 / V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(c) · NCMA 2C.15
preguntas.pregunta: Which swab is acceptable for collecting a respiratory specimen for viral testing?
opciones: A polyester or Dacron tip on an aluminum or plastic shaft
A cotton tip on a wooden shaft, the classic bacterial culture swab
A calcium alginate tip on an aluminum or plastic shaft
A cotton tip on an aluminum shaft, moistened with saline
preguntas.explicacion: Respiratory specimens for viral testing are taken on a synthetic tip, polyester or Dacron, mounted on an aluminum or plastic shaft. Wooden shafts and cotton tips are not recommended, and a swab of calcium alginate is simply not acceptable. The tip then goes into a vial holding 1 to 3 mL of sterile viral or universal transport medium.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Ionizing Radiation, personnel monitoring; StatPearls, "Radiation Safety in Medical Imaging", dosimeters
preguntas.subtema: Dosimetry · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.3 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which device measures an individual worker's occupational radiation exposure?
opciones: A film badge, TLD or pocket dosimeter carrying the wearer's name and period
A ground-fault circuit interrupter mounted on the imaging equipment's cord
A lead apron, which records the cumulative dose on an internal strip
A Geiger counter kept at the department entrance for all of the staff
preguntas.explicacion: The Ionizing Radiation standard requires personnel monitoring for workers likely to be exposed, and the devices are film badges, thermoluminescent dosimeters and pocket dosimeters; the standard device is a clip-on or ring badge bearing the assignee's name, the monitoring period and a unique number, processed by an accredited commercial service. A lead apron reduces dose but records nothing, and dosimeters are worn both outside and inside the apron so the two readings can be compared. A GFCI is an electrical safeguard.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: The median cubital vein sends a named connection to each of the two main superficial veins. What are they called?
opciones: The median cephalic vein and the median basilic vein
The median antebrachial vein and the median basilic vein
The dorsal venous arch and the median antebrachial vein
The accessory cephalic vein and the perforating basilic vein
preguntas.explicacion: Where it links the two superficial channels, the median cubital vein is described as having a link to the cephalic, called the median cephalic vein, and a link to the basilic, called the median basilic vein. The median antebrachial vein is a separate forearm vessel dominant in one variant.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.B Quality Improvement, turnaround times · CPT D1 1N k23 documentation and reporting
preguntas.pregunta: The chemistry analyzer is down and a routine panel will not be resulted inside the laboratory's stated turnaround time. What does CLIA require the laboratory to do?
opciones: Weigh how urgent the test is and decide whether the requesting individual has to be told of the delay
Alert the requester at once, because a missed turnaround time is handled exactly like a panic value
Hold the report and release it as a corrected report once the analyzer passes its controls again
Send a preliminary report carrying the reference intervals but no result, and recollect the specimen
preguntas.explicacion: Where results cannot go out inside the laboratory's own time frames, the rule is a judgment call weighed on the urgency of the tests ordered: the laboratory decides whether the appropriate people have to be told about the delay. Immediate notification belongs to a different paragraph, the one about a result showing a panic value or a condition that threatens life imminently. Corrected reports belong to reporting errors that have been detected.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Grey
preguntas.subtema: Additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: The gray top tube holds two substances. Which one is the anticoagulant, and what does the other one do?
opciones: Potassium oxalate binds calcium; sodium fluoride blocks glycolysis
Sodium fluoride binds the calcium; potassium oxalate blocks glycolysis
Sodium citrate binds calcium; sodium fluoride preserves the cells
Potassium oxalate inhibits thrombin; sodium fluoride binds calcium
preguntas.explicacion: The gray tube contains potassium oxalate, which binds calcium and so prevents coagulation, together with sodium fluoride, which acts as an antiglycolytic agent; that combination is why the tube is used for plasma glucose and lactic acid. Swapping the two roles reverses the review, citrate belongs to the light blue tube, and thrombin inhibition is heparin.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", sections Nursing, Allied Health, and Interprofessional Team Interventions and Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A ward nurse sees a colleague filling the tubes in the wrong sequence. What is asked of staff outside the laboratory in that situation?
opciones: To know the order of draw and call attention to it at once
To leave the sequence entirely to the laboratory personnel
To let the laboratory refuse the tubes and request a repeat
To write it up and raise it at the next meeting of the staff
preguntas.explicacion: Nurses and clinicians are asked to be aware of the order of draw so that, seeing the sequence go wrong at the bedside, they can call attention to it before the patient is affected. Filling the tubes out of sequence pushes results falsely up or falsely down in biochemistry, hematology, serology and microbiology, and an unnoticed result can reach the clinician.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Newborn Screening", section Blood Sample; and HRSA, About Newborn Screening, Are Screening and Diagnostic Testing the Same?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4C metabolic screening information · PBT III.A.4 newborn screening
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn screening result comes back 'positive' for a metabolic condition. How should this be read?
opciones: As a risk value, not a diagnosis: a repeat screen or confirmatory test should follow promptly
As a diagnosis, since the dried blood spot assays are quantitative and highly specific for each condition
As a laboratory error until the second card in a two-screen state confirms it
As a result to be reported directly to the parents by the phlebotomist who collected it
preguntas.explicacion: A screen returns a risk value, where a diagnostic test returns a value against a reference range, so a positive screen is followed as soon as possible by a confirmatory test specific to the disease, or by a repeat screen, with results usually routed to the primary care provider. In short: screening says a baby might have a condition, diagnostic testing says whether it does.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3: Select the site
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet application · CPT D3 k60 · PBT II.F II.J · CCMA 3E 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the WHO say the tourniquet should be applied when selecting a venipuncture site?
opciones: About four to five finger widths above the venipuncture site, then re-examine the vein
About 2 cm above the site, the width of the area the swab must cover
About four to five finger widths below the site, so the vein fills from the hand
Right over the median cubital vein, with the thumb anchoring just below it
preguntas.explicacion: In Step 3 the WHO guideline places the tourniquet roughly four to five finger widths above the point where the needle will go in, and then has the phlebotomist look at the vein again. The same step says the vein should already be visible before the tourniquet goes on, and that finding it helps in choosing the right needle size. The 2 cm figure belongs to Step 5, the area the alcohol swab has to cover; the thumb below the site is the anchoring hand in Step 6, not the tourniquet; and below the site is the wrong side altogether.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Fire safety, extinguisher types; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157(c)(3)
preguntas.subtema: Extinguisher types · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which extinguishers are most common in a laboratory, and which type is not acceptable for laboratory use?
opciones: Dry chemical BC or ABC and carbon dioxide; water-filled units are not acceptable
Water-filled and foam units; carbon dioxide is not acceptable near electronics
Class D dry powder for all fires; dry chemical units are not acceptable
Carbon dioxide only; ABC units are not acceptable because the powder damages equipment
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA's laboratory guidance names two types as the most common in a chemistry laboratory, pressurized dry chemical of type BC or ABC and carbon dioxide, with a specialized Class D dry powder unit added where flammable metals are handled, and it says flatly that a water-filled unit has no place in a laboratory. The same guidance asks employers to train workers on the different types under 29 CFR 1910.157, which also bans carbon tetrachloride and chlorobromomethane agents.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Common Pitfalls), Value judgments
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6 k193 · CMA F.2.b / 2027 F.1.c · RMA I.D.1.e
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist thinks 'people like him never fast properly' before asking the question. What does therapeutic communication require here?
opciones: Identify the personal bias and avoid placing that value judgment on the patient
Voice the concern openly so the patient has a chance to correct the record
Skip the fasting question, since the answer is already predictable
Document the impression in the chart as a compliance risk factor
preguntas.explicacion: The first pitfall in the table is value judgments: the provider is told to identify their own biases and judgments and to keep from imposing them on the patient. Implicit bias worsens outcomes and that progress is blocked by denying it exists. Voicing or charting the assumption imposes it; skipping the question forfeits the information.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Injection Safety: Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices, Key points for multi-dose vials
preguntas.subtema: Multi-dose vial beyond-use date · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C7 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A multi-dose vial was first punctured on March 1 and the manufacturer gives no date for opened vials. Under USP 797 as cited by the CDC, by when should it be discarded?
opciones: Within 28 days of opening, and never past the manufacturer's expiration date
Within 7 days of opening, the limit for single-dose vials kept for the same patient
Within 72 hours of opening, unless it is kept in a clean medication area
On the manufacturer's expiration date, regardless of when it was opened
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC cites USP General Chapter 797: from the first puncture, a multi-dose vial is dated and then thrown out 28 days later, unless the manufacturer names a different date for the opened vial, and that beyond-use date can never run past the original expiration date. A vial never opened simply follows the manufacturer's expiration date. Single-dose vials are not saved for later use at all, not even for the same patient, so the 7-day option describes a rule that does not exist.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(ix)(C) and (d)(4)(iv)(B), Gloves and Laundry
preguntas.subtema: Utility gloves · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: The heavy utility gloves kept in the draw room for cleaning spills are cracked and peeling. What does the standard say?
opciones: Discard them: utility gloves are reused only while their integrity holds up
Wash and reuse them, since only single-use gloves are barred from reuse
Reuse them for handling contaminated laundry, where no barrier is needed
Keep them until the yearly review of the written exposure control plan
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ix)(C) is the only place the standard allows a glove to be decontaminated and used again, and it puts a condition on it: the glove's integrity has to be intact. Cracking, peeling, tears, punctures or any other sign of deterioration send it to the trash, and so does the loss of its barrier. Employees who handle contaminated laundry must wear gloves and other appropriate equipment under (d)(4)(iv)(B), so that is not a place to use a failing glove.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 3186, Model Exposure Control Plan, Recordkeeping: Training Records and Medical Records
preguntas.subtema: Getting a copy of the record · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA II.B.5.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist asks her employer for a copy of her bloodborne pathogens training record. Within what period is it provided?
opciones: Fifteen working days from the request
Ten working days from the request
Thirty calendar days from the request
Three years from the training date
preguntas.explicacion: The model plan allows fifteen working days for handing the employee, or a representative the employee has authorized, a copy of the training record, and the same period for the medical record when the employee, or someone holding written consent, asks for it. Ten working days is the deadline for offering the hepatitis B vaccine after initial assignment; three years is how long the training record itself is kept under (h)(2)(ii), which is a different thing from the time allowed to hand over a copy.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Background: HBV; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030

preguntas.pregunta: Occupational hepatitis B infections among healthcare workers fell sharply after the 1980s. What is that credited to?
opciones: Wide vaccination of workers plus universal precautions and the OSHA standard
The arrival of immune globulin as a treatment for chronic hepatitis B
The switch from glass to plastic tubes in blood collection systems
The end of the use of hollow-bore needles for drawing blood samples
preguntas.explicacion: Surveillance figures put roughly 17,000 new hepatitis B infections among healthcare workers in 1983 and an estimated 800 in 1995, a decline of about 95 percent. It is attributed to the widespread immunization of healthcare workers with the hepatitis B vaccine and to universal precautions and the other measures the bloodborne pathogens standard requires. Immune globulin is post-exposure prophylaxis, not a treatment for chronic infection, and hollow-bore needles are still in daily use.

preguntas.pregunta: One antecubital fossa is inflamed with cellulitis and the other holds a fresh hematoma. Where does the search for a vein continue?
opciones: Along the forearm, which is inspected together with the antecubital fossa
Through the intravenous line running in one of the two arms
In the antecubital fossa with the smaller of the two problems
On the dorsum of the hand, the site the chapter prefers for an IV
preguntas.explicacion: Site selection begins by extending the arm and inspecting the antecubital fossa or the forearm, so the forearm is the next place to look when both elbows are ruled out. Cellulitis, an abscess and a hematoma are each listed as reasons not to puncture, and an existing line is not used either.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient started an antibiotic yesterday and now gives a urine for culture. What should be documented, and why?
opciones: The antibiotic, because it can cause a false-negative culture
The antibiotic, because it can cause a false-positive culture
The time of the last void, because a culture needs urine held 8 hours
The antibiotic, because it turns the urine alkaline and lyses the cells
preguntas.explicacion: Antibiotics already on board can suppress growth and give a false-negative urine culture, so the medication is recorded for the laboratory and the provider. The same rule drives other cultures: throat swabs are taken before antimicrobial treatment starts, and antibiotics can alter the growth in a sputum culture. Alkaline urine and cell lysis come from a stale specimen, not from the drug.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient who takes warfarin has a point-of-care INR of 1.5. What does this value indicate?
opciones: It is below the usual therapeutic target of 2.0 to 3.0, so the patient may be at risk of forming a clot
It is above the usual therapeutic target of 0.8 to 1.1, so the patient may be at risk of serious bleeding
It is within the usual therapeutic target of 1.0 to 2.0, so no change in the warfarin dose is expected
It is a normal value for someone who is not on anticoagulants, so the warfarin can be discontinued
preguntas.explicacion: For a person not taking anticoagulants the PT is about 11 to 13.5 seconds and the INR 0.8 to 1.1. For most patients on warfarin the provider aims to keep the INR between 2.0 and 3.0: results above 3.0 carry a higher bleeding risk, while results below 2.0 may leave the patient at risk of developing a blood clot. An INR of 1.5 is therefore under target and the dose is reviewed by the provider, not stopped by the tester.

preguntas.pregunta: A molecular section wipes its benches and the places hands touch most at the end of every shift. Which strength of bleach is given, and what does it accomplish?
opciones: A 10 to 15 % bleach solution, about 0.5 % sodium hypochlorite, which destroys DNA and RNA
A 1 to 2 % bleach solution, about 0.5 % sodium hypochlorite, which destroys DNA and RNA
A 10 to 15 % bleach solution, which kills the organisms but leaves any amplicon intact
A 70 % alcohol solution, which clears nucleic acid from the bench faster than bleach does
preguntas.explicacion: Aseptic cleaning of surfaces, and above all of the points hands touch often, uses a bleach solution of 10 to 15 %, which works out at about 0.5 % sodium hypochlorite. Bleach at 10 % or above was found to destroy both DNA and RNA. Ultraviolet irradiation is the other route for surfaces and for reagent mixes, used carefully where the mixture holds UV-sensitive enzymes.

preguntas.pregunta: When must an employer train workers on hazardous chemicals under the Hazard Communication standard?
opciones: When first assigned, and again each time a new chemical hazard appears in the work area
At initial assignment and at least annually thereafter, within one year of the last session
Once, at hire, with a written test kept for the duration of employment plus 30 years
Every three years, when the written hazard communication program is reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(1) of 29 CFR 1910.1200, as the eTool summarizes it, calls for effective training when the worker is first assigned, and again each time a new chemical hazard turns up in the work area; it has to be given in a language the workers understand, leave room for questions, and cover the protective measures the employer has put in place. The annual cycle inside one year of the previous session belongs to the bloodborne pathogens standard, and employment plus 30 years is that standard's retention period for employee medical records.

preguntas.pregunta: Which element must a written Exposure Control Plan contain?
opciones: The exposure determination listing job classifications and tasks with occupational exposure
The sharps injury log, with the brand of each device and the department where it happened
The medical record of each exposed employee, including hepatitis B vaccination dates
The safety data sheet for every disinfectant used to decontaminate work surfaces
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(1)(ii) names three required elements: the exposure determination of (c)(2), the schedule and method for implementing paragraphs (d) through (h), and the procedure for evaluating the circumstances of exposure incidents. The exposure determination lists job classifications where all or some employees are exposed and the tasks involved. The sharps injury log and the employee medical record are kept under paragraph (h) as separate records, and safety data sheets belong to the Hazard Communication standard at 29 CFR 1910.1200.

preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k87 · PBT III.C · CCMA 3E11 k140 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.d
preguntas.pregunta: After centrifugation, the serum in a red-top tube shows fibrin strands floating above the gel. What is the most probable cause?
opciones: The tube was centrifuged before the blood had finished clotting
The tube was left at room temperature for too long before being spun
The tube was drawn through an intravenous catheter during an IV start
The tube was inverted too many times right after it was collected
preguntas.explicacion: Blood must be allowed to clot before serum is processed; the high rate of fibrin-containing samples in the emergency laboratory was linked to the short interval between collection and centrifugation, on average about 10 minutes. Waiting longer does not produce fibrin, catheter draws are tied to hemolysis rather than fibrin, and inversion helps additives mix instead of causing strands.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Adult Dehydration", sections Epidemiology and Pathophysiology
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k49 age and physical condition · PBT II.D patient assessment, II.I considerations
preguntas.pregunta: Why are older adults 20 to 30% more prone to dehydration, a factor that can make veins harder to access?
opciones: A less sensitive thirst mechanism, immobility, diabetes, renal disease and polypharmacy
A higher proportion of body water, which is lost faster through thinner and less elastic skin
Overactive antidiuretic hormone, which makes the kidneys waste water in the collecting ducts
Greater sweating from more active glands, especially during long hospital stays in summer
preguntas.explicacion: Older people run a 20 to 30% higher risk of drying out, and the reasons listed are immobility, a thirst mechanism that no longer works well, diabetes, kidney disease and a long medication list; the hypothalamic thirst response loses sensitivity with age. Diuretics, laxatives and some blood pressure drugs add to it, as do failing cognition and depending on a carer for something to drink.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Why first morning urine · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.a · RMA III.C.4.b.v
preguntas.pregunta: A urinalysis is ordered and the patient is told to bring the first sample of the day. What makes that void the best one to test?
opciones: It sat in the bladder overnight, so it is concentrated enough to show trace substances and how well the kidneys concentrate
It is the cleanest of the day, because the urethral area has not been used since the previous evening's void
It is the least acidic of the day, so cells, casts and crystals hold their shape for longer in the container
It is drawn before any food or drink, so the glucose and the protein are not raised by what the patient ate
preguntas.explicacion: Urine starts changing the moment it leaves the body, so which void is collected matters. The one held in the bladder through the night comes out concentrated, and that is the point: a concentrated sample shows what the kidneys can do with water, and it carries substances in high enough amounts to be picked up that a watery daytime sample would hide. Other timings are ordered when the question calls for them — a random void, one two hours after a meal, a full 24-hour collection. Cleanliness is a matter of the collection technique, not of the hour.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Sections 2, 4, 6 and 8; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.151(c)
preguntas.subtema: Using the SDS in an emergency · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist splashes a disinfectant concentrate into her eye. Which section of the product's Safety Data Sheet gives the first-aid measures?
opciones: Section 4, First-Aid Measures, by route of exposure
Section 2, Hazard Identification and signal word
Section 8, Exposure Controls and Personal Protection
Section 6, Accidental Release and cleanup measures
preguntas.explicacion: Section 4 sets out the immediate care an untrained bystander can give, sorted by how the chemical got in: breathed in, onto the skin or into the eye, or swallowed, together with the main symptoms and any warning that a doctor is needed at once. Section 2 classifies the hazard and carries the signal word and pictograms; Section 8 lists exposure limits, engineering controls and the equipment to put on before handling; Section 6 covers containing and cleaning up a spill. For the eye itself the practical first step is the eyewash: 29 CFR 1910.151(c) demands equipment able to drench or flush the eyes and the body quickly, inside the work area, wherever workers may meet injurious corrosive materials.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic freezer that stores patient samples has a continuous temperature monitoring system with an alarm. How often must its temperature still be checked and recorded?
opciones: Daily, and before the room is used for testing, regardless of the alarm or data logger
Weekly, since a continuous monitoring system replaces the manual daily check
Only when the alarm sounds, because the logger already records the temperature
Monthly, when the log sheet is reviewed and filed with the quality records
preguntas.explicacion: It makes no difference whether the unit carries a chart recorder, a temperature alarm, a digital data logger or continuous monitoring: a refrigerator or freezer is read and logged daily, and testing rooms are checked before use. Sample freezers often sit between −25 and −15 °C (−13 to 5 °F), but the range that counts is the one the manufacturer's instructions give for what is inside, since waived testing under CLIA means following those instructions.

preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet and site location · CPT D3 3F k60 k61 · PBT II.E II.F · CCMA 3E4 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has veins that are hard to see and three tubes are needed. What is recommended instead of keeping the tourniquet on while the veins are located?
opciones: Using a venous illumination device to visualize the veins
Applying a second tourniquet below the first to raise the pressure
Drawing with a syringe, which tolerates a longer tourniquet time
Switching to a 16 to 18 gauge needle so the tubes fill faster
preguntas.explicacion: Venous illumination devices are recommended rather than a prolonged tourniquet to find non-prominent veins, especially when two or more tubes are to be collected, because they avoid the venous stasis that alters biochemistry and coagulation results. Sixteen to eighteen gauge is the WHO's blood donation size, and neither a second tourniquet nor a syringe extends the permitted time.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Throat and Nasal Swabs)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k89 · PBT V.E · CCMA 3D5 k121 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A nasal specimen has just been taken, the swab having been inserted and rotated repeatedly within one nostril. What does the written procedure have the collector do next?
opciones: Spread the material evenly over two or three smears and let the slides air-dry before sending them
Spread the material over a single smear and send the slide to the laboratory while it is still wet
Place the swab in 10 % neutral buffered formalin and send the container without making a smear
Spread the material over two or three smears and refrigerate the slides at 2 to 8 °C for transport
preguntas.explicacion: Swabs are taken under direct vision with good lighting, from areas of exudate, inflammatory membranes or the tonsillar crypts, and for a nasal specimen the patient sits with the head tilted slightly back and facing the light. The material is then spread evenly on two or three smears, the slides are air-dried, and they go to the laboratory for examination.

preguntas.subtema: Risk analysis is repeated · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k34
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic finished its security risk analysis two years ago and has bought new equipment since. What does the guidance say?
opciones: Repeat it regularly, and whenever practice or technology changes
Repeat it only after a breach has actually been discovered
Repeat it every six years, when the documentation is renewed
Treat the first one as final once the flaws found were fixed
preguntas.explicacion: The security requirements put their weight on risk analysis, and it is not a one-off exercise: the system in place is audited for flaws and gaps that threaten the confidentiality, the integrity or the security of health information; whatever turns up goes through the risk management process and gets corrected; and the analysis is run again at intervals, because technology keeps arriving and clinical practice keeps shifting. The six-year figure is how long the required documentation is kept.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(e)(1) and (b), Definitions: Production Facility, Research Laboratory
preguntas.subtema: Scope of paragraph (e) · CPT D1 1A k31 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C2 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital laboratory only analyzes patient specimens. Do the extra rules for HIV and HBV research laboratories apply to it?
opciones: No: those rules cover culture and production work, not diagnostic analysis
Yes: any laboratory that handles blood must meet them along with the rest
Yes, but only in the area where HIV testing is performed on patient samples
No: they apply only to facilities that manufacture the hepatitis B vaccine
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (e)(1) draws the line itself. The extra requirements bind laboratories doing research and facilities producing, where HIV and HBV are cultured, concentrated, experimented with or manipulated, and they do not reach a clinical or diagnostic laboratory that only analyzes blood, tissue or organs. A production facility is defined in (b) as one working at industrial scale, in large volume or at high concentration with the viruses themselves, which is not the same as making a vaccine. The rest of the standard still applies to the hospital laboratory.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, types of consent · CPT D2 2F k43 · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA II.E.3.a informed consent · RMA I.C.1.a consents · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: A thorough consent discussion is expected to cover all the relevant risks. Which set does it take in?
opciones: The general risks, those particular to this procedure, the risks of no treatment, and the alternatives
The general risks, those particular to this procedure, the cost to the patient, and the recovery time
The risks particular to this procedure only, since the general ones are printed on the facility's form
The risks particular to this procedure and those of the alternatives, with no treatment left out of it
preguntas.explicacion: Consent is not informed if the risk talk is narrow. It is expected to run across four fronts: what any intervention of this kind can bring, what this one in particular can bring, what follows if nothing is done at all, and what the reasonable alternatives carry with them. Declining care is itself an option that has to be weighed, so dropping it shortens the list. The forms promise nothing either: many say outright that the method proposed is not guaranteed to settle the problem. Cost and recovery time belong to the conversation about the visit, not to the risks this discussion has to cover.

preguntas.pregunta: A serum lithium level is ordered on a patient taking lithium carbonate. Which heparin tube does the WHO table specify?
opciones: Sodium heparin, because a lithium heparin tube would interfere with the result
Lithium heparin, because it is the anticoagulant of the light green PST as well
