Instead of engineering controls, when the employer documents that safer devices cost more
Only when an exposure incident has already occurred and follow-up is under way
Before engineering controls are considered, as the first line of protection
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(i) sets the order: engineering and work practice controls come first, to remove exposure or cut it down, and PPE is added where exposure survives them. OSHA's page on evaluating and controlling exposure reads that to mean the employer has to look at an effective control fit for the clinical setting, a safety-engineered sharp for instance, and put it in place; the text grants no exemption for cost. PPE is preventive, not something that begins after an incident.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1252(b); CDC, MMWR RR-54(13) (2005), Physical Requirements for Testing
preguntas.subtema: Environmental conditions · CPT D5 k90 · PBT VI.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.9.d · RMA III.C.3.e
preguntas.pregunta: Which environmental conditions does CLIA say a laboratory must monitor and document when they affect reagent storage or test performance?
opciones: Temperature, humidity, water quality and protection from electrical fluctuations
Temperature, lighting, noise level and the number of operators per shift
Humidity, barometric pressure, altitude and the color of the work surfaces
Water quality, air exchanges per hour, and the distance to the nearest sink
preguntas.explicacion: The laboratory sets out the conditions essential for storing reagents and specimens and for running and reporting reliably, in line with what the manufacturer's instructions say, then monitors and documents them. The four named, where they apply, are water quality, temperature, humidity, and keeping instruments safe from current that fluctuates or cuts out. Extremes of humidity can degrade reagents and blur test endpoints.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, How to Obtain a CLIA Certificate of Waiver (2019): Do I need to notify anyone if I make any changes?
preguntas.subtema: Changes reported within 30 days · CPT D1 k29 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.1.a.v
preguntas.pregunta: A waived testing site moves to a new suite across town and hires a new laboratory director. What does CLIA require?
opciones: Notify the state agency of both changes within 30 days of the change
Notify the state agency of both changes within 90 days of the change
Apply for a new certificate, since a certificate cannot move with the site
Notify CMS only of the new director; the address is updated at renewal
preguntas.explicacion: For every certificate type, changes in ownership, name, location or laboratory director must be reported to the state agency within 30 days. Accredited laboratories also tell their accreditation organization, and high complexity COC laboratories report a change of technical supervisor on the same timeline. A move does not require a brand-new application; adding nonwaived tests does.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Devices Associated with Needlestick Injuries and Figure 1
preguntas.subtema: Devices behind the injuries · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which devices account for most of the percutaneous injuries hospitals report to national surveillance?
opciones: Hollow-bore needles, above all hypodermic and winged-steel needles
Suture needles, followed by the scalpel blades used in minor surgery
Glass items, above all broken capillary tubes and specimen slides
Retractable lancets used for the finger and heel sticks of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Surveillance over four years collected close to 5,000 percutaneous injuries, and hollow-bore needles were involved in 62 percent of them: hypodermic needles on disposable syringes took 29 percent and winged-steel needles 13 percent. Glass followed at 17 percent and suture needles at 15 percent, with phlebotomy needles themselves at 4 percent. Hollow-bore needles weigh most because they carry a measurable volume of blood, which is why devices that enter a vein or an artery get the highest priority for replacement with safer ones.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Other Issues: Violations of HIPAA; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Civil and Criminal Violations
preguntas.subtema: Penalty tiers · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k34
preguntas.pregunta: Among the HIPAA civil penalty tiers, which category carries the highest penalty per violation?
opciones: Willful neglect that is not corrected
Willful neglect corrected within the period
Reasonable cause, not willful neglect
A violation the person did not know about
preguntas.explicacion: The four civil tiers climb with culpability: not knowing of the violation, reasonable cause short of willful neglect, willful neglect put right inside the required period, and willful neglect left uncorrected, which tops the scale at $50,000 per violation. Criminal liability is a separate ladder, starting with knowingly obtaining or disclosing identifiable information, rising when it is done under false pretenses, and rising again when it is done for commercial advantage, for personal gain, or to do malicious harm. The civil side is enforced by the Office for Civil Rights.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.5 Circulatory Pathways, Veins Draining the Upper Limbs; and StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins" (2023), section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k7 (applied D2 k53) · PBT I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which veins join to form the brachial vein, and is the brachial vein superficial or deep?
opciones: The radial and ulnar veins; it is a deep vein
The cephalic and basilic veins; it is superficial
The median cubital and cephalic veins; it is superficial
The axillary and subclavian veins; it is a deep vein
preguntas.explicacion: The radial and the ulnar veins run alongside the bones of the forearm and come together to form the brachial vein, a deep vessel that carries on into the axillary vein; in the forearm those deep veins travel in pairs beside the arteries as venae comitantes and merge at the cubital fossa. Cephalic and basilic are the superficial pair, and the axillary and subclavian lie further along.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Composition of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5 k87) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In a spun hematocrit tube, what makes up the thin pale layer between the packed red cells and the plasma?
opciones: Leukocytes and platelets, normally under 1 percent of the sample
Reticulocytes, normally 1 to 2 percent of the red cell count
Plasma proteins, roughly 7 percent of the plasma volume
Fibrin strands with trapped platelets from a forming clot
preguntas.explicacion: That pale band is the buffy coat. It holds the formed elements that are not red cells, the white cells and the platelets, and normally amounts to less than 1 percent of the sample. Reticulocytes are immature red cells, not a separate layer; the plasma proteins are dissolved in the plasma above; and fibrin only appears if the sample has been allowed to clot, which an anticoagulated hematocrit tube has not.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 6.2.2 and Annex C, Table C.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4B k80 equipment when assisting · PBT II.J syringes
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these syringes is NOT appropriate for drawing blood from a child?
opciones: An auto-disable (AD) syringe, which is made for injecting
A 1 to 5 mL syringe fitted to a 23-gauge butterfly needle
A syringe whose needle retracts manually into the barrel
A self re-sheathing syringe with a sleeve over the needle
preguntas.explicacion: Safety devices with needle covers are used wherever they can be, but the auto-disable syringe is built for giving injections and is not for drawing blood. The annex adds that its safety mechanism can fire while the operator is still probing, which forces a fresh venepuncture, and that it does nothing against needle-sticks. Retractable and re-sheathing syringes are listed among the active safety devices.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2D 2E k41 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3E1 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which opening request follows WHO step 2, 'Identify and prepare the patient', for a conscious adult?
opciones: 'Please tell me your full name.'
'You are Mr. Johnson, correct?'
'Is this bed 7, the CBC for Dr. Ruiz?'
'Which tests are you here for today?'
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 tells the health worker to introduce themselves and to ask the patient to state their full name, then to check that the laboratory form matches that identity. Feeding the patient a name to agree with, or identifying by bed number, is not what the step describes; asking which tests are ordered hands the patient a job that belongs to the form.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Rh Blood Groups
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1 · CPT Core k5
preguntas.pregunta: When is RhoGAM (Rh immune globulin) normally given to an Rh negative pregnant patient?
opciones: In weeks 26 to 28 of pregnancy and within 72 hours after the birth
In weeks 26 to 28 of pregnancy and within 3 hours after the birth
In weeks 12 to 14 of pregnancy and within 72 hours after the birth
Only within 72 hours after the birth of a second Rh positive baby
preguntas.explicacion: RhoGAM temporarily prevents the Rh negative parent from forming anti-Rh antibodies by destroying any fetal Rh positive cells that cross the placenta, and it is normally given during weeks 26 to 28 of pregnancy and within 72 hours of birth. Since its introduction in 1968 the incidence of hemolytic disease of the newborn in such pregnancies fell from about 13 to 14 percent to about 0.1 percent.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Airborne Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Susceptible staff and airborne pathogens · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C2 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.3
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist who has never had chickenpox or the vaccine is assigned to a patient with varicella on Airborne Precautions. What does the CDC recommend?
opciones: Restrict her from the room if immune personnel are available to do the draw
Let her draw with an N95, since the respirator makes immunity irrelevant
Let her draw with a surgical mask, since varicella spreads by droplets
Restrict her permanently from all patients on Transmission-Based Precautions
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's airborne recommendations keep susceptible staff out of the room of a patient who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox, measles, smallpox or disseminated zoster, provided immune colleagues are on hand to do the work, and they ask that susceptible people be immunized as soon as possible after an unprotected contact with a vaccine-preventable infection. Whoever does go in wears the respirator, but that does not cancel the preference for immune staff. Varicella belongs on the airborne list, not the droplet one, and the restriction attaches to this patient rather than to every isolation room.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, rows 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · D2 k47 · PBT II.J II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A serology test is ordered. Which two tubes list immunology and serology among their uses?
opciones: The red clot activator tube and the gold serum separator tube
The red clot activator tube and the purple top EDTA tube
The gold serum separator tube and the light green PST tube
The pale yellow ACD tube and the gold serum separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: Immunology and serology appear against two rows of the table: the red clot activator tube at position 4 and the separator tube at position 5, both of which give serum. EDTA is assigned to hematology and cross-match, the PST to chemistries, and the ACD tube to tissue typing and DNA work.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Personal protection and hygiene
preguntas.subtema: Between procedures · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How often should hand hygiene be performed when two different samples are collected from the same patient?
opciones: Before and after the contact, and also between the procedures
Once before the first procedure and once after the last one
Only after the second procedure, when the gloves come off
Only if the gloves tore or blood reached the skin underneath
preguntas.explicacion: The best-practice table sets hand hygiene before and after each patient contact and also between procedures on the same patient, because the point is to reduce cross-contamination, which can happen within one encounter as well as between two patients. The gloves follow the same logic, one clean pair per patient or per procedure. Waiting for a torn glove or visible blood is a different rule, the one that forces washing after contact with blood.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Table 1, Needle Shield
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: After activating the shield on a safety needle, the phlebotomist notices the tip is still visible at the end of the shield. Against which FDA design recommendation does this fall short?
opciones: The shield must fully enclose the needle and block finger access
The sharp should end up drawn right back inside the body of the device
The housing of a fixed recessed needle should extend beyond the sharp
Color should be used for a clear, specific purpose
preguntas.explicacion: FDA Table 1 gives one recommendation per feature type: a needle shield should enclose the needle completely and keep fingers away once activated; a retractable sharp should end up drawn right back inside the housing; and a fixed recessed needle should have a housing that extends beyond and fully covers the sharp. A shield that leaves the tip exposed fails the first of these; the retraction rule applies to a different design.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k126 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which simple step may significantly decrease a patient's anxiety just before the needle goes in?
opciones: Counting down with the patient
Applying the tourniquet early on
Dimming the room lighting
Offering a sugary drink first
preguntas.explicacion: A simple countdown may significantly reduce anxiety and optimize the conditions for venipuncture. Applying the tourniquet early works against the patient, since it should be released within one minute to avoid hemoconcentration; a sugary drink breaks a fast; and adequate lighting, not dim light, is what the guidance for older patients calls for.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 3.1, Recommended needle gauge, length and device; and CDC, NIOSH Alert: Preventing Needlestick Injuries in Health Care Settings, DHHS (NIOSH) Publication No. 2000-108 (Nov. 1999), PDF de CDC Stacks
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge sizes and lengths · CPT D3 k56 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: For a routine venipuncture on an adult with ordinary veins, which needle does WHO Table 3.1 list with a length of 1 to 1.5 inches?
preguntas.explicacion: Table 3.1 gives the adult 21 G needle a length of 1 to 1.5 inch (2.54 cm), and the adult 22 G needle 1 inch. The 23 G appears for adults at 1 to 1.5 inch as a straight needle, but for children and neonates only as a 0.5 inch winged set. Sixteen to eighteen gauge is reserved for blood donation, and 19 to 20 G is marked not applicable for every age group.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2, Selecting the length of lancet
preguntas.subtema: Lancets · CPT D3 k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.5
preguntas.pregunta: When choosing a lancet for an adult finger-prick, why does the WHO advise one slightly shorter than the depth that seems necessary?
opciones: Pressure compresses the skin, so the puncture ends up slightly deeper than the lancet length
Shorter lancets give more blood, because the capillary bed lies in the upper dermis
The finger-prick must never exceed 1.5 mm, and most lancets are longer than that
Thinner and shorter lancets are the only ones that retract to prevent needle-sticks
preguntas.explicacion: Section 7.1.2 explains that the lancet picked is a little shorter than the depth estimated because the pressure applied compresses the skin, making the actual puncture a little deeper than the lancet length; pain rises with penetration depth, though blood volume rises with it too. Lengths run from 0.85 mm to 2.2 mm, and an adult finger-prick should not exceed 2.4 mm, not 1.5 mm.

preguntas.fuente: govinfo, Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, Pub. L. 106-430, sec. 3(2) and 3(3); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b)
preguntas.subtema: Definitions added by the Act · CPT D1 k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which two terms did the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act add to the definitions in the bloodborne pathogens standard?
opciones: Sharps with engineered protections, and needleless systems
Universal Precautions, and the definition of an exposure incident
Regulated waste, and the definition of a contaminated sharp
Occupational exposure, and the definition of regulated waste
preguntas.explicacion: The Act put two definitions into 29 CFR 1910.1030(b). One covers sharps that carry engineered sharps injury protections: a needle or non-needle sharp used to draw fluids, reach a vein or artery, or give medication, built with a feature that lowers the risk of exposure. The other covers needleless systems, devices that take fluids out once access is established, deliver medication, or handle other tasks carrying percutaneous risk, all without a needle. Universal Precautions, exposure incident, occupational exposure, regulated waste and contaminated sharps were already defined in the 1991 standard.

preguntas.subtema: Donor physical assessment · CPT D4 4D k82 standards for blood donation
preguntas.pregunta: On the day of donation, what oral temperature disqualifies a prospective blood donor?
preguntas.explicacion: The physical assessment done on the day of donation requires the donor's oral body temperature not to exceed 37.5 °C, that is 99.5 °F, or the equivalent measured at another site. It sits alongside blood pressure, hemoglobin or hematocrit, pulse, weight and a skin examination as the minimum findings that establish the donor is in good health before collection.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Conventional devices
preguntas.subtema: Device selection · CPT D3 3D k54 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A syringe draw is planned for a small child. Which adjustment does the device table call for?
opciones: A smaller syringe together with a pediatric laboratory tube
A larger syringe together with a standard adult laboratory tube
A smaller syringe together with a standard adult laboratory tube
A larger syringe together with two pediatric laboratory tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Where a needle and syringe is used on a pediatric patient, the table asks for a smaller syringe and a pediatric laboratory tube. The parallel adjustment for the evacuated system is a smaller tube with a reduced vacuum, which is there to keep the specimen from haemolysing.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Green and Red
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: The emergency department wants immediate chemistry results. Which tube is commonly used for stat chemistry, and what type of sample does it produce?
opciones: A green heparin tube, which yields plasma rather than serum
A red tube with no additive, which yields serum after clotting
A lavender EDTA tube, which yields plasma for hematology
A gray oxalate tube, which yields plasma for glucose and lactate
preguntas.explicacion: Green heparin tubes are often used when stat or immediate chemistry results are requested for emergency cases, and unlike red tubes the sample they give is plasma, not serum. The red tube has to clot first, typically 10 to 15 minutes, before centrifugation. The lavender tube is for hematologic assays and the gray tube for glucose and lactic acid.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.3 Modes of Disease Transmission, Contact Transmission and Vehicle Transmission
preguntas.subtema: Fomites and indirect contact · CPT D1 1K k11 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C k94 · CMA I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A doorknob contaminated by an infected person's hands is an example of which element of disease transmission?
opciones: A fomite, in indirect contact transmission
A vehicle, like contaminated food or water
A mechanical vector, like a fly carrying bacteria
A droplet nucleus, the residue of an evaporated droplet
preguntas.explicacion: Indirect contact transmission works through fomites, inanimate objects that pick up pathogens from an infected person or reservoir and pass them to a new host who touches them and then a portal of entry; doorknobs, towels and tablecloths are the everyday examples, and improperly sterilized syringes, needles and catheters are the clinical ones behind many healthcare-associated infections. Vehicle transmission is through water, food or air; a mechanical vector is an animal carrying the pathogen on its body; and a droplet nucleus is what remains when a droplet desiccates in the air.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.404(c), Content of notification
preguntas.subtema: Breach notice content · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3E k33
preguntas.pregunta: Which element must a breach notification letter to an individual include?
opciones: Steps the individual can take to protect against potential harm
The name of the workforce member who caused the breach
A copy of the covered entity's complete privacy policies and procedures
The civil penalty amount the covered entity expects to pay to HHS
preguntas.explicacion: In plain language, and as far as it can, the letter describes what happened, with the date of the breach and the date it was discovered; which types of unsecured PHI were involved, such as a name, a Social Security number, a date of birth or a diagnosis; what individuals should do to protect themselves; what the entity is doing to investigate, to limit the harm and to stop it happening again; and how to make contact, by toll-free number, e-mail, website or postal address. Naming the employee, attaching the policies and estimating penalties are no part of the required content.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Common Pitfalls), Negative body language
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 · CCMA 6 k197 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Standing over a seated patient with arms crossed while asking about allergies illustrates which communication pitfall?
opciones: Negative body language
Value judgments
Approving or disapproving
Agreeing or disagreeing
preguntas.explicacion: The table pictures negative body language as arms folded, an air of distraction, or looming over the seated patient. The recommended posture is the reverse: eye contact, an interested expression, leaning forward, sitting close. Value judgments and approving or disapproving responses are verbal pitfalls about the provider's opinions, not matters of posture.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Ten minutes after a faint the patient is awake but still noticeably pale. What does that persisting pallor suggest?
opciones: Symptomatic anemia, which calls for a fuller evaluation
A normal recovery, since pallor lingers after every faint
A seizure rather than a faint, as the tongue was not bitten
Hemoconcentration from the tourniquet used during the draw
preguntas.explicacion: After a simple vasovagal event the examination should be entirely normal. Pallor that carries on suggests symptomatic anemia and, like a bitten tongue or an atypical story, prompts a search for another cause rather than a comfortable label.

preguntas.subtema: Donor skin examination · CPT D4 4D k82 complete screening
preguntas.pregunta: A donor has healed needle scars along both forearms. What does the skin examination require?
opciones: Deferral: arms must be free of scars indicative of injected drugs of abuse
Deferral only if the puncture marks are still fresh and inflamed today
Collection from another site, such as a hand vein, and documentation
Collection as usual, since scars do not affect the sterility of the unit
preguntas.explicacion: The skin examination has two parts. The site chosen for the draw has to be clear of infection, of inflammation and of lesions, and the arms and forearms must show no punctures or scars that point to injected drugs of abuse. The second half is not about the sterility of the unit but about the donor's own risk of a transfusion-transmitted infection, so moving to another site does not answer it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.3
preguntas.subtema: OGTT specimen · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.J tubes/anticoagulants · CCMA 3E k136 additives k139
preguntas.pregunta: OGTT samples will wait more than an hour before they can be separated from the cells. Which tube should they be collected in?
opciones: Gray top with sodium fluoride and potassium oxalate
Light blue top with sodium citrate, filled completely
Green top with lithium heparin and a gel separator
Lavender top with EDTA, inverted eight to ten times
preguntas.explicacion: Cells have to come off the plasma inside 60 minutes, and off serum inside 90, unless the tube carries a glycolysis inhibitor. Sodium fluoride inhibits enolase at 2.5 mg of fluoride per mL of blood and travels with potassium oxalate as the anticoagulant; glucose then holds steady for 72 hours at room temperature. That is the gray fluoride/oxalate tube, last in the order of draw and needing a full draw. Heparinized plasma reads about 5% lower than serum.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(b)(1) and (b)(2), Standard: Minimum necessary
preguntas.subtema: Minimum necessary exceptions · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: To which disclosure does the HIPAA minimum necessary standard NOT apply?
opciones: A disclosure to a health care provider for treatment
A disclosure to a health plan for payment
A disclosure to a business associate for operations
A disclosure to a researcher under a privacy board waiver
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity using, disclosing or requesting PHI must make reasonable efforts to keep it to the minimum necessary for the purpose. Section 164.502(b)(2) sets out where that does not apply: a provider disclosing for treatment or asking for what treatment needs; uses and disclosures to the individual; anything done under an authorization; disclosures to the Secretary for compliance; and uses required by law or by the rule itself. Payment, operations and research disclosures all stay under the minimum necessary limit.

preguntas.subtema: Business associate agreements · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: An outside company will digitize the clinic's paper charts. What does HIPAA require before it receives the PHI?
opciones: Satisfactory assurances in a written business associate contract that it will safeguard the PHI
A signed authorization from every patient whose chart will be digitized by the company
Only the notice of privacy practices, since scanning counts as a health care operation
A certificate of accreditation for the company from a CMS-approved organization, renewed yearly
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(e) lets a covered entity disclose PHI to a business associate, and let it create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI on its behalf, if it first secures satisfactory assurances that the associate will safeguard the information, documented in a written contract or arrangement meeting 164.504(e); the associate may then use the PHI only as its contract or the law permits, and must secure the same assurances from any subcontractor. Patient authorizations are not needed for this kind of operational service, and accreditation is a CLIA concept.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.3 · CCMA 3D k117 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.b.iii
preguntas.pregunta: An EDTA tube for an erythrocyte sedimentation rate sat in a rack for four hours before the test was set up. What effect is expected?
opciones: A falsely low ESR, because delayed red cells lose their biconcave shape; testing should start within 2 hours
A falsely high ESR, because delayed red cells aggregate faster; testing should start within 2 hours
A falsely low ESR, because the anticoagulant loses activity; testing should start within 4 hours
A falsely high ESR, because plasma viscosity falls on standing; testing should start within 6 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Delays in processing make red cells lose their biconcave shape, which reduces the ESR, so the test should be started within 2 hours of collection; clotted blood also lowers it by disturbing rouleaux formation. The factors that raise the value are different: a warm room, direct sunlight, tube tilt (3° from vertical can add up to 30 %), vibration, and air bubbles from an under-filled tube.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section Introduction; and "Syncope", section Etiology
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 k68 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which form of syncope is the most common, and which of its triggers matter in a phlebotomy setting?
opciones: Vasovagal syncope, triggered among other things by pain or emotional upset, with bradycardia and hypotension
Carotid sinus syncope, triggered by pressure on the neck, with tachycardia and high blood pressure
Situational syncope, triggered by coughing or urination, with normal heart rate and pressure
Cardiac syncope, triggered by exertion, with ventricular tachycardia and pallor
preguntas.explicacion: The vasovagal episode is the most common form of reflex syncope and can be set off by pain or by emotional upset, though often no trigger is found; it accounts for nearly half of all cases, with severe pain and stress among its situations, leading to vasodilation and bradycardia. During the event the patient is typically slow of pulse, hypotensive, pale and sweating.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient identification and tube labeling)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E k145 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A tube arrives in the laboratory bearing only the patient's full name. Which element is missing that is normally required on a labeled specimen?
opciones: The date and time of collection and the identity of the person who collected it
The diagnosis code and the name of the insurance carrier that covers the requested test
The room number and the bed number where the specimen was collected
The color of the stopper and the lot number of the evacuated tube used
preguntas.explicacion: A complete label carries, beside the patient's names and date of birth, the exact date and time of collection and the collector's identification, according to each center's policy; the requesting provider and the specimen's own identifying details may also be included. Diagnosis codes belong on the requisition, not the tube; room or bed numbers cannot serve as identifiers; stopper color and lot are not label content.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Contaminated, Contaminated Sharps, Regulated Waste
preguntas.subtema: Contaminated sharps definition · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which item meets the standard's definition of a contaminated sharp?
opciones: A broken capillary tube with dried blood on it
A sealed tube of blood in a transport rack
A dressing soaked with liquid blood that would drip if squeezed
An unused lancet still in its sterile package
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b) calls a contaminated sharp any contaminated object capable of penetrating the skin, and its examples run from needles and scalpels to broken glass, broken capillary tubes and the exposed ends of dental wires. Two conditions have to hold at once: the object can pierce skin, and blood or OPIM is on it or is reasonably anticipated to be. A sealed tube pierces nothing; a gauze pad that would drip is regulated waste of the liquid kind rather than a sharp; and an unused lancet can pierce but carries nothing, so it is not a contaminated sharp yet.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Exposure Incident; and (f)(3), Post-exposure Evaluation and Follow-up
preguntas.subtema: Exposure incidents and post-exposure follow-up · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these events meets OSHA's definition of an "exposure incident"?
opciones: Blood splashes into a technician's eye while a tube is being uncapped
A drop of blood lands on the intact skin of a gloved hand
A technician is assigned to a job where contact with blood is reasonably anticipated
A contaminated needle is found in a regulated waste bag, without any parenteral contact
preguntas.explicacion: The definition names the routes that count: the eye, the mouth or another mucous membrane, skin that is not intact, or a parenteral route such as a needlestick, with the contact coming from the employee's duties. A splash to the eye is mucous-membrane contact and qualifies. Intact gloved skin is not a listed route. A job where contact is reasonably anticipated is Occupational Exposure, the neighbouring definition, not an incident. A contaminated needle in a waste bag is regulated waste in the wrong container, but without parenteral contact there is no exposure incident. The label matters because reporting an exposure incident is what obliges the employer to make the post-exposure evaluation and follow-up available at once.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural care and bandaging · CPT D3 3Q k73 k74 · PBT II.F II.I · CCMA 3E9 k137 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.13
preguntas.pregunta: How is pressure maintained on the site after the needle is removed?
opciones: Gauze pressed over the site as the needle comes out, then taped in place, or a bandaid applied over it
The patient bends the elbow over the gauze, which keeps pressure on the vein without tape
An ice pack wrapped in a towel is held on the site for 15 minutes to prevent a hematoma
The tourniquet is reapplied loosely over the gauze for one minute to compress the vein
preguntas.explicacion: Once the draw is done, clean gauze is used to apply pressure as the needle is swiftly removed, pressure is continued, and the gauze is taped in place to provide continuous pressure against a hematoma; alternatively a bandaid goes over the gauze. Bending the arm is what the WHO forbids, and ice is first aid for a bruise that has already formed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cultural Religious Competence in Clinical Practice", sections Religion and Healthcare, and Islam (Clinical Significance)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6 k193 · CMA F.2.a / 2027 F.1.d(8) · RMA I.D.1.d · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: A Muslim woman asks for a female phlebotomist. What is the culturally competent response?
opciones: Find a same-sex practitioner unless the situation is an acute emergency
Explain that staff assignments cannot be changed for religious reasons alone
Proceed with the male phlebotomist if her husband gives his agreement
Ask her to sign a waiver acknowledging the delay before rescheduling
preguntas.explicacion: Religion can shape a patient's preference for the gender of their health provider, along with diet, medicines from animal products and modesty, and the clinical note for Islam reads: find a same-sex practitioner if it is not an acute emergency. Health professionals are asked to accommodate such needs rather than refuse them or route the decision through a relative.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, sections Why do I need to fast, and What if I make a mistake; StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Diagnostic Tests in Diabetes Mellitus
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E k125 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a)
preguntas.pregunta: During check-in a patient admits to having eaten a pastry two hours before a fasting glucose. What is the correct action?
opciones: Report it to the provider; the test may need to be rescheduled for a day when the patient can fast
Draw the sample anyway and write the time of the pastry on the tube so the laboratory can adjust the result
Have the patient wait in the lobby for six more hours and then draw, since 8 hours will have passed by then
Draw the sample and order a random glucose instead, since the two tests share the same normal value
preguntas.explicacion: If the patient eats or drinks anything other than water during the fast, the instruction is to tell the provider, who may reschedule the test for another time when the patient can fast, because nutrients absorbed from food change the levels of substances in the blood and an inaccurate result gives an inaccurate picture of health. Fasting and random glucose have different normal values, and no note on the tube converts one into the other.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Angle of insertion · CPT D3 3I k65 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: At what angle to the surface of the arm is the phlebotomy needle inserted?
opciones: Between 15 and 30 degrees
Between 30 and 45 degrees
Less than 45 degrees
Between 5 and 10 degrees
preguntas.explicacion: The needle goes in slowly at an angle of 15 to 30 degrees to the surface of the arm, after the skin has been pulled taut with the thumb. The WHO gives 30 degrees or less, which is consistent. The 'less than 45 degrees until a flash of blood appears' figure belongs to the peripheral line placement chapter and describes an IV cannula, not a phlebotomy needle.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A dry cervical swab collected for a molecular sexually transmitted infection panel cannot be couriered until the next day. Which storage condition matches the general guideline?
opciones: Dried, at or below room temperature, for as long as seventy-two hours
Dried, at or below room temperature, for no longer than twelve hours
In viral transport medium at 2 to 8 °C, for as long as seventy-two hours
Frozen at −20 °C from collection, because the targets are unstable
preguntas.explicacion: Urethral, vaginal and cervical swabs are taken for organisms such as Trichomonas vaginalis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, herpes simplex virus and Chlamydia trachomatis, and what governs them is time, temperature and transport medium. The general storage guidance for this family of swabs is dried, at room temperature or below, for up to seventy-two hours.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Dialysis Fistula", section Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A dialysis patient has an arteriovenous fistula in the left forearm. What should be avoided on that side?
opciones: Peripheral venous access, blood draws and blood pressure measurements
Blood draws only; blood pressure cuffs are safe if inflated briefly
Blood pressure measurements only; draws are permitted below the fistula
Only the puncture of the fistula itself; draws above it are permitted
preguntas.explicacion: Nurses help save the veins by keeping peripheral lines, blood draws and pressure cuffs OFF the side of the fistula or of planned fistula creation, and they should know how to assess the thrill and recognize its loss. Checking the thrill is part of monitoring the access, not a clearance to puncture that arm.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Table 1, Colored Feature or Component
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: When a sharps safety device uses color on a component, what is expected of that color?
opciones: It should serve a purpose and follow conventions users know already
It should be red, so the used device is visible in the sharps bin
It should differ between hospitals, so devices are not mixed up
It should change once the safety feature has been activated once
preguntas.explicacion: Color is expected to achieve a specific purpose, such as distinguishing models or sizes, and to fit conventions the user already recognizes, the example given being the orange hubs and needle covers of insulin syringes. Whether the feature has fired is judged by design, not by a color change.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Fire safety, classes of fire and extinguisher types; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157(d)
preguntas.subtema: Classes of fire · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which fuels define a Class B fire?
opciones: Flammable liquids and gases, such as organic solvents
Ordinary combustibles that leave ash, such as paper
Combustible metal powders, flakes or shavings
Energized electrical equipment such as a centrifuge motor
preguntas.explicacion: Class A fires involve ordinary combustibles, fuels that burn and leave ash, and Class B flammable liquids and gases; many organic solvents and compressed gases in a laboratory are Class B hazards. Combustible metals are Class D, handled with a specialized dry powder extinguisher, and 29 CFR 1910.157 treats electrical equipment as Class C, distributing those units by the pattern of the A or B hazards present. The most common laboratory extinguishers are dry chemical BC or ABC and carbon dioxide.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Composition of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5 k87 centrifuging) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A whole-blood sample is spun in a centrifuge. Which component settles at the very bottom of the tube?
opciones: The erythrocytes, the heaviest formed elements
The buffy coat of leukocytes and platelets
The straw-colored plasma, over half the sample
The serum, once the clotting factors are gone
preguntas.explicacion: In a spun sample the heaviest formed elements, the red cells, pack at the bottom; above them sits a thin pale layer of white cells and platelets, the buffy coat; and the plasma, a pale straw-colored liquid, floats on top as the lightest component and makes up more than half of the sample. Serum is not a layer of whole blood: it is plasma minus its clotting factors, obtained only after the blood has clotted.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Chain of Custody", section Chain of Custody in Legal Drug Testing
preguntas.subtema: Chain of custody · CPT D5 5C k91 · PBT III.A.4 special sample types · CCMA 3E k127 witness · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: An unconscious patient arrives after a crash and a legally defensible urine specimen is needed. Who identifies the specimen?
opciones: The nurse who collects it identifies it in the patient's place
The police officer who brought the patient in identifies it
The laboratory identifies it on arrival from the requisition
No one: the collection waits until the patient can identify it
preguntas.explicacion: In legal drug testing the donor normally identifies the sample and seals the cup, preferably in person, and signs the custody form ahead of the collector. Where the patient is insentient in the emergency room, whoever draws the urine or blood, the nurse, identifies it in the patient's place. Everyone who takes charge of it afterwards signs the form in sequence and may be called to testify.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.E · CCMA 3D9 k117 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A stat laboratory measured its errors the same way in 1996 and again in 2006. What did the comparison show?
opciones: The error rate fell by about a third, but the split between phases hardly moved
The error rate fell by about a third, and the analytical share grew to a half
The error rate held steady, while the preanalytical share fell to under a third
The error rate doubled, driven by the growth in the number of tests requested
preguntas.explicacion: Ten years apart, that laboratory cut its overall error rate by 34 %, yet the distribution stayed essentially where it had been: 62 % of errors before the analysis, 15 % during it and 23 % afterwards. Working harder inside the laboratory does not move a problem that mostly happens outside it, which is the argument for managing the extra-analytical phases directly.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Equipment assembly · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these belongs on the organized collection tray prepared before a venous draw?
opciones: A stirrer for tubes and waterproof transport bags
A centrifuge rotor and a rack of reagent cartridges
A capillary microtube warmer and a slide staining kit
A pair of sterile scissors and a suture removal blade
preguntas.explicacion: The tray is set out with a utility cart, gloves, a collection apparatus with safety measures, a complete series of unexpired tubes in various volumes, a tourniquet, antiseptic, dressings and gauze pads, a waste bin, a stirrer for tubes and waterproof transport bags.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Newborn Screening", section Neonatal Intensive Care Unit
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4C metabolic screening · PBT III.A.4 newborn screening acceptability
preguntas.pregunta: A NICU infant had its first screening card collected at 12 hours of age. What is recommended?
opciones: Re-screen seven days after admission, since the first was taken before 24 hours
Re-screen at 6 months of age, when premature enzyme systems have matured enough
No repeat is needed, since NICU laboratories run more sensitive assays on preterm blood
Repeat only if the infant is on total parenteral nutrition
preguntas.explicacion: A NICU baby needs extra thought: born early, its enzymes are immature and its metabolism unsettled, which throws up more false positives. If the first card was taken under 24 hours of age, the screen is repeated a week after admission. Babies on total parenteral nutrition are often flagged wrongly for carnitine deficiency.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Skin or nail culture (003762), How the Test is Performed and Normal Results
preguntas.subtema: Skin and nail culture · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.C / V.D.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(b)
preguntas.pregunta: A nail sample was sent for culture. What should the patient be told about the result?
opciones: It can take up to 3 weeks, and organisms that normally live on skin are not a sign of infection
It can take up to 3 days, and any organism at all that grows in the dish is a sign of infection
It can take up to 3 weeks, and any organism at all that grows in the dish is a sign of infection
It comes back the same day, and organisms that normally live on skin are not a sign of infection
preguntas.explicacion: A nail culture can take as long as three weeks to report. Some organisms live on skin normally, and finding them is considered a normal result rather than an infection. The sample itself is taken with a swab or a blade from an open rash or sore, by scraping or clipping the affected nail, or by a skin biopsy taken after a numbing injection.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vancomycin", section Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C k45 · PBT II.A II.D · CCMA 3E2 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A vancomycin trough is ordered and the next dose is due at 10:00. When should it be drawn?
opciones: Within the 30 minutes before the 10:00 dose, at steady state
Immediately after the 10:00 infusion has finished running
Exactly 2 hours after the 10:00 dose has started
At any point between doses, as long as the time is recorded on the tube
preguntas.explicacion: A serum trough is ideally obtained within 30 minutes before a dose is given, under steady-state conditions, which are typically reached after the third dose; the usual target trough is 10 to 20 μg/mL. The peak, by contrast, occurs immediately after the intravenous infusion is completed. A random time between doses is neither.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Fecal Occult Blood Test", Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Povidone-iodine false positive · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.2 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.8.b · RMA III.C.4.a.iv
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse applied povidone-iodine to the perianal area shortly before a guaiac stool card was prepared. What can this cause?
opciones: A false-positive result, since iodine oxidizes the guaiac reagent
A false-negative result, since iodine is a reducing agent like vitamin C
An invalid card, since iodine prevents the developer from wetting the paper
An unchanged result, since antiseptics interfere only with immunochemical kits
preguntas.explicacion: Iodine oxidises the guaiac directly, and a povidone-iodine dilution of 1:1000 has produced a false positive in vitro from as little as 0.005 mL; the antiseptic should not go on the perianal area, nor into the urinary tract during catheterization, before the test. Chlorine-generating toilet sanitizers also fake positives with guaiac, while non-chlorine sanitizers cut the sensitivity of immunochemical kits.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Auxiliary Aids and Services
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Which aid is called particularly useful for people with hearing loss who do not use sign language?
opciones: Real-time captioning, a computer-assisted transcription shown on a screen
A tactile interpreter, working alongside a support service provider
A qualified reader supplying an audio recording of printed material
A videophone connected to the free video relay service for signers
preguntas.explicacion: Real-time captioning, the computer-assisted transcription known as CART, has a transcriber type what is being said while the computer throws the words up on a screen, on site or from a distance, and it is singled out for people who are deaf or hard of hearing and do not sign. Qualified readers and audio recordings serve people with vision loss.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Licensed Healthcare Professional; and (f)(1)(ii)(C)
preguntas.subtema: Who does the evaluation · CPT D1 1D 1H k33 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: Who may perform the post-exposure evaluation the bloodborne pathogens standard requires?
opciones: A licensed professional whose scope of practice covers vaccination and follow-up
Only a physician licensed in the state where the exposure incident happened
The employer's safety officer, who then signs the written opinion for the file
Any registered nurse in the facility, working under the employer's supervision
preguntas.explicacion: The definitions in paragraph (b) create the term licensed healthcare professional for exactly this: someone whose legally permitted scope of practice lets them independently carry out what paragraph (f) requires, the hepatitis B vaccination and the post-exposure evaluation and follow-up. Paragraph (f)(1)(ii)(C) puts the work in the hands of a licensed physician, or of some other licensed healthcare professional, or of someone they supervise, so it is not confined to physicians, and it is not something a safety officer or an employer may supervise.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 4.1 Time, temperature and freeze-thaw cycles
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3
preguntas.pregunta: A ward asks the laboratory for the exact number of hours whole blood may sit at 2 to 8 °C before a nucleic acid extraction. What is the honest answer?
opciones: No absolute limit is published, but long holds raise hemolysis and degrade the nucleic acid
A firm limit of 24 hours applies, after which the specimen is rejected for any nucleic acid target
No limit applies at all, because the cold halts the white cell lysis that would degrade it
A firm limit of 72 hours for RNA and 4 hours for DNA applies, from the stability tables
preguntas.explicacion: There is no absolute time limit for whole blood at room temperature or at 2 to 8 °C, but prolonged storage at either is discouraged: hemolysis becomes more likely and lysis of the white cells degrades the nucleic acid. Storage below 0 °C is not recommended for whole blood; when extraction has to wait, the red cells are removed and the plasma or serum frozen at −20 °C or colder.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen is collected an hour after a contrast-enhanced scan from a patient who jogged to the appointment. Which two readings should be treated with caution?
opciones: Specific gravity, raised by the contrast, and the electrolytes, moved by exercise
Nitrite, raised by the contrast, and the pH, moved by the exercise beforehand
Bilirubin, raised by the contrast, and the ketones, moved by the exercise
Protein, raised by the contrast, and the specific gravity, moved by exercise
preguntas.explicacion: Contrast media can lift the specific gravity falsely, and exercise can shift both the specific gravity and the electrolyte concentration of the specimen. Neither is the laboratory's doing, which is why the collection history counts: an alkaline pH can read as protein, and bacteria multiplying in a pot left standing will fake a positive blood pad while dragging the pH with them.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cultural Religious Competence in Clinical Practice", section Jehovah's Witness (Health)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6 k193 · CMA F.2.a / 2027 F.1.d(8) · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: Which religious group refuses blood transfusions and blood products?
opciones: Jehovah's Witnesses
Orthodox Christians
Baha'i believers
Seventh-day Adventists
preguntas.explicacion: Jehovah's Witnesses will not accept a blood transfusion, nor blood products, while whether to prolong life is left to the individual. The Baha'i entry says transfusion is acceptable and the Eastern Orthodox one allows transfusions and blood products, while the Seventh-day Adventist entry records no restriction on blood or blood products at all. Knowing these positions is what lets a phlebotomist respond without judgment.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Signal Words and Hazard Statements
preguntas.subtema: Signal words · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A chemical carries two hazards: one warrants the signal word Danger and the other Warning. What appears on the label?
opciones: Only Danger, since one signal word appears and it is the more severe
Both words, each next to its own hazard statement
Only the word Warning, since the less severe word applies to the mixture as a whole
Neither; when hazards conflict the label shows pictograms only
preguntas.explicacion: There are only two signal words. Within a hazard class, Danger marks the more severe hazards and Warning the less severe ones, and a label carries a single signal word no matter how many hazards the chemical has; when one hazard calls for Danger and another for Warning, only Danger appears. The hazard statements, by contrast, are all included, and may be combined to improve readability. Pictograms never replace the signal word; they are a separate required element.

preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's serum returns a hemolysis index around 700 and the neonatologist still wants the C-reactive protein. What does the laboratory expect at that level?
opciones: The C-reactive protein would read low, so the figure is not reportable
The C-reactive protein would read high, so the figure is not reportable

preguntas.explicacion: Specific proteins withstand hemolysis better than many routine chemistry analytes, but severe in vitro hemolysis still reaches them: above an index of roughly 622 mmol/L it is underestimated. As a double packaging: a leakproof primary receptacle and a rigid outer box with a liner
As a triple packaging whose outer layer may be a padded envelope for small volumes
As a triple packaging in which only the outer box has to resist punctures and leaks
preguntas.explicacion: Category B substances travel as a triple packaging: a rigid outer packaging, a secondary packaging inside it and the primary receptacle inside that. preguntas.pregunta: An ESR specimen is drawn at 08:00 and reaches the analyser at 11:30. Why may the result be reported lower than it should be?
opciones: Testing should begin within two hours; standing changes the red cell shape
Testing should begin within twelve hours; standing dilutes the citrate added
Testing should begin within thirty minutes; standing lets the plasma evaporate
Testing should begin within twenty-four hours; standing warms the specimen up
preguntas.explicacion: Timely handling matters for this test: it should be started within two hours of collection, because red cells that stand too long lose their biconcave shape and stack less readily, which lowers the reading. preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO blood spill procedure, what happens right after the broken glass has been removed with tongs?
opciones: Absorb the fluid with paper towels, wipe with detergent, then apply hypochlorite
Apply hypochlorite directly to the wet blood, then wipe with paper towels
Rinse the area with running water, then discard the towels in regular waste
Remove gloves and wash hands, then record the incident before cleaning further
preguntas.explicacion: The sequence is fixed: put on non-sterile gloves; lift the glass with tongs or with a pan and brush, never by hand, and drop it into a sharps container or, if the pieces are too big, wrap them in paper inside a separate container; soak up as much fluid as possible with disposable paper towels; wipe with water and detergent until nothing is visible; saturate the area with 0.5 percent hypochlorite; rinse the pan, brush and tongs under the tap; take the gloves off; wash with soap and water and dry on single-use towels; and record the incident if a specimen was lost or somebody was exposed.

preguntas.pregunta: A program wants to document substance use over the past several months. Which matrix fits?
opciones: Scalp hair, which reflects roughly the last three months of exposure
Oral fluid, which reflects roughly the last three months of exposure
Blood, which reflects roughly the last three weeks of exposure
Urine, which reflects roughly the last three weeks of exposure
preguntas.explicacion: Hair is the cumulative window: scalp hair covers about three months, and body hair, which grows more slowly, axillary or pubic, can show use as far back as twelve months. Write the labels for the tubes that have been drawn

Place the tubes into the leak-proof transport bag

preguntas.pregunta: Why does the guidance describe informal caregivers as 'hidden patients'?
opciones: They carry a higher risk of health problems, poor sleep and burnout
They are billed at the same rate as the patient they bring to clinic
They are recorded in the chart as a second patient at every visit
They may consent on the patient's behalf without any paperwork
preguntas.explicacion: Family caregivers face emotional, financial and physical demands, often handing out medicines, giving injections and carrying out other treatments on top of their own jobs and families. Their own risk runs higher for health problems of body and mind, for sleep trouble and for chronic conditions, so they are viewed as hidden patients, with staff alert for illness, stress and burnout.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Regulated Waste
preguntas.subtema: Sharps containers and regulated waste · CPT D1 k30 k32 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.6.a / 2027 I.B.5.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which of the following counts as "regulated waste" under the OSHA standard?
opciones: Gauze caked with dried blood that could release it while being handled
A pair of exam gloves worn for a draw, with no blood on them at all
An alcohol swab used to clean the skin before the needle, with no blood on it
A gauze pad with one dry spot of blood that cannot be released during handling
preguntas.explicacion: The definition covers five things: blood or OPIM (other potentially infectious materials) that is liquid or semi-liquid; items that would release it in that state if squeezed; items caked with dried blood or OPIM that could shed it while being handled; contaminated sharps; and pathological or microbiological waste containing blood or OPIM. The caked gauze is the third case. Gloves and a swab with no blood on them would release nothing if squeezed and are not caked, and a pad with one dry spot that cannot release anything fails the same test: the definition asks for dried blood that is caked AND capable of coming off during handling.

preguntas.pregunta: A centrifuge with blood inside its rotor chamber cannot be fully decontaminated before the repair technician arrives. What does the standard require?
opciones: A readily observable label saying which parts remain contaminated, and telling the technician
Sending the centrifuge for service in a red bag, which replaces the label

Recording the contamination in the sharps injury log before the technician touches it
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xiv) requires equipment that may be contaminated to be examined and decontaminated before servicing or shipping, unless the employer can show that is not feasible; in that case (d)(2)(xiv)(A) demands a readily observable label per (g)(1)(i)(H) stating which portions remain contaminated, and (d)(2)(xiv)(B) requires that information to reach the employees concerned, the service representative and the manufacturer before anyone handles it. A red bag substitutes for a label on waste, not on equipment, and the sharps injury log records percutaneous injuries only.

preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿Puede un médico negarse a tomar a un paciente o a dar un tratamiento que se le pidió?
opciones: Sí, como cuando el tratamiento no está indicado por la historia que se le dio
Sí, pero sólo donde otro profesional de la salud ya haya aceptado tomarlo
No, una vez que la persona quedó registrada como paciente del consultorio
No, salvo que una emergencia en otro sitio le vuelva imposible la agenda
preguntas_es.explicacion: El derecho corre en las dos direcciones. Un médico puede en muchas circunstancias negarse a entrar en la relación o a dar un tratamiento: puede llegarle un referido para un tratamiento en particular y parecerle que tomarlo no está justificado, o la historia que le dieron puede no indicar el tratamiento del todo. El privilegio es viejo, viene de la época hipocrática, y aun así ninguna ley lo protege tan ampliamente como la profesión reclama, y las leyes que sí lo protegen se apoyan por lo común en la libertad de religión.

preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿En qué entorno puede un empleador decidir que los guantes no se exigen de rutina en cada flebotomía?
opciones: Un centro de donación voluntaria de sangre, con condiciones como guantes para quien está en formación
Un laboratorio clínico, si aplica las precauciones universales a todas las muestras

Aun ahí el empleador tiene que reevaluar la política de forma periódica, tener guantes disponibles para quien los quiera, nunca desalentar su uso, y exigirlos cuando el empleado tiene cortes o heridas en la piel, cuando la contaminación de la mano es probable —por ejemplo con un donante poco cooperador— y durante la formación en flebotomía. Ningún otro entorno recibe la excepción.

Desenroscar la aguja a mano y echarla en el recipiente para objetos punzocortantes, quedándose con el portatubos

preguntas_es.explicacion: La sección 3.1.1 manda descartar el portatubos (tube holder) y la aguja como una sola pieza donde se pueda; si hay que reutilizar el portatubos, la aguja se quita con la técnica del cucharón (one-hand scoop technique) o con un recipiente para objetos punzocortantes que tenga una ranura para soltarla, siempre con una sola mano. El anexo E añade que una aguja usada al descubierto nunca se desarma con las manos desnudas, y OSHA prohíbe volver a taparla y quitarla con las dos manos, salvo donde no haya otra alternativa posible.

preguntas_es.pregunta: Un paciente no puede expectorar esputo por sí solo y se inicia la inducción del esputo. ¿Cuándo se detiene el procedimiento?
opciones: Cuando se ha obtenido de 1 a 2 mL, a los 15 minutos de nebulización, o si empieza la opresión en el pecho
Cuando se ha obtenido de 1 a 2 mL, tras nebulizar 60 minutos, o si el paciente tose fuerte
Cuando se ha obtenido de 10 a 20 mL, tras nebulizar 15 minutos, o si el paciente tose fuerte
Cuando se ha obtenido de 1 a 2 mL, a los 5 minutos de nebulización, o si el paciente empieza a tener arcadas
preguntas_es.explicacion: En la inducción el paciente respira una neblina nebulizada de solución salina hipertónica al 3 por ciento durante unos cinco minutos para aflojar las secreciones, y después toma respiraciones profundas y tose. Se detiene cuando hay de 1 a 2 mL de esputo en el recipiente, a los 15 minutos de nebulización, o si aparecen opresión en el pecho, falta de aire o silbidos, porque una bulla pleural puede romperse y causar un neumotórax. La saliva va en una bandeja para vómito, no en el recipiente.

preguntas_es.pregunta: El panel de coagulación de un paciente vuelve una y otra vez hemolizado. ¿Qué dos rasgos de la extracción se señalan para protegerlo?
opciones: Una venopunción atraumática y el menor tiempo de torniquete posible

Un paciente en ayuno y una punción puesta sobre la vena basílica
Un segundo tubo de descarte y una aguja más fina que el calibre veintitrés
preguntas_es.explicacion: Para el trabajo de coagulación la punción debe ser atraumática y hacerse sin demora, y el torniquete debe quedarse puesto el menor tiempo posible, porque los dos fallos producen artefactos como la hemólisis. preguntas_es.pregunta: El conductor de una clínica lleva las muestras de sangre al laboratorio del hospital cada tarde. Además de una gradilla o un soporte acolchado para los tubos, ¿qué debe llevar el vehículo según la OMS?
opciones: Un kit para derrames de sangre, para poder limpiar sin riesgo una muestra rota por el camino
Una centrífuga portátil, para poder separar el suero si el viaje se retrasa
Una incubadora de dióxido de carbono, para que las muestras de cultivo mantengan viables sus organismos
Un segundo juego de tubos vacíos, para poder volver a recolectar una muestra rota al llegar
preguntas_es.explicacion: Para transportar muestras de sangre fuera de un hospital, la OMS (WHO) pide que el vehículo lleve un kit para derrames (spill kit) de sangre, porque una muestra se puede romper durante el transporte igual que en el área de flebotomía; el derrame se maneja después con guantes y, en los derrames grandes, una bata o un delantal, toallas de papel que van al desecho infeccioso, y una solución de blanqueador recién preparada. Varios tubos viajan en una gradilla o en un soporte acolchado justamente para evitar esa rotura.

preguntas_es.pregunta: Se aplica una crema en la piel antecubital de un niño antes de una venopunción. ¿Qué es la EMLA y cuándo alcanza su pico?
opciones: Lidocaína al 2,5 % con prilocaína al 2,5 %; el pico plasmático llega de 2 a 6 horas después bajo oclusión
Lidocaína sola al 5 %; el pico plasmático llega de 15 a 30 minutos después, igual que con la infiltración
Lidocaína al 2,5 % con bupivacaína al 2,5 %; el pico plasmático llega dentro de 1,5 a 2 horas, su vida media
Gel de cloroprocaína al 2 %; el pico plasmático llega enseguida, y por eso se prefiere en neonatos
preguntas_es.explicacion: La EMLA es una mezcla eutéctica de lidocaína al 2,5 % y prilocaína al 2,5 %, que se pone en la piel antes de una venopunción (venipuncture), una vía intravenosa o una punción lumbar. Bajo un apósito oclusivo el pico plasmático llega tarde, hacia las dos a seis horas, mientras que los dos fármacos se eliminan con una vida media cercana a la hora y media o las dos horas. El pico de 15 a 30 minutos es el de la lidocaína infiltrada, y la cloroprocaína es un éster inyectable.

preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿Qué medidas se propusieron para reducir la sangre que se pierde en la flebotomía seriada en cuidados intensivos?
opciones: Menos pruebas y agrupadas, tubos más pequeños y dispositivos de conservación de sangre
Menos pruebas y agrupadas, tubos más grandes y lavado del catéter más frecuente
Muestreo capilar para cada prueba, para que no haga falta ningún tubo venoso
Extraer todas las pruebas del día por el acceso vascular de una vez
preguntas_es.explicacion: Buena parte de la flebotomía diaria de la unidad no es sangre que llegue a un tubo: se desecha como residuo mientras se consigue el acceso vascular. Las medidas que se discuten son recortar el número y la frecuencia de las pruebas, agrupar las muestras y ofrecer órdenes añadidas, guardar menos volumen en los tubos de recolección, y los dispositivos de conservación de sangre que acaban con el residuo del acceso. Los tubos más pequeños se describen como un complemento, no como un sustituto de pedir menos pruebas.

preguntas_es.pregunta: Una paciente citada para el primer paso de la detección gestacional de dos pasos pregunta qué debe hacer con la comida antes. ¿Qué se le dice?
opciones: Ni ayuno ni cambio de dieta: el paso de detección no necesita ninguno de los dos
Nada de comer ni beber, salvo sorbos de agua, durante 8 a 14 horas antes
Comer una dieta libre con 150 g de carbohidratos al día durante 3 días
Comer un desayuno ligero exactamente una hora antes de la cita
preguntas_es.explicacion: Para el paso de detección la paciente no tiene que prepararse ni cambiar su dieta de ninguna manera: bebe el líquido con glucosa y se le extrae sangre una hora después. El ayuno (fasting) de 8 a 14 horas es de la prueba de seguimiento de 3 horas y de la prueba de 75 g de un paso; la carga de carbohidratos de tres días es una condición de la prueba de tolerancia a la glucosa oral diagnóstica fuera del embarazo. Comer normalmente en los días previos es la única indicación que se da.

preguntas_es.pregunta: Un lactante de 4 meses que pesa 5 kg necesita una muestra capilar. ¿Qué sitio indica la tabla 7.1 de la OMS y en qué parte de él se pone la lanceta?
opciones: El talón, en la superficie plantar medial o lateral
El talón, en la curva posterior, donde la piel es más gruesa
El dedo medio o el anular, en el lado de la yema
El pulgar o el índice, en el lado de la yema
preguntas_es.explicacion: La tabla 7.1 asigna la punción del talón a los lactantes desde el nacimiento hasta unos 6 meses y de unos 3 a 10 kg, y la lanceta va en la superficie plantar medial o lateral; la punción del dedo es para niños de más de 6 meses y de más de 10 kg. El capítulo 7 dice que el talón posterior se debe evitar porque el hueso queda sólo a 2,33 mm de la piel, y la propia tabla advierte contra el pulgar y el índice.

preguntas_es.pregunta: En una venopunción de rutina, ¿qué forma de consentimiento describe obtener el paso 2 de la OMS?
opciones: Consentimiento verbal, después de conversar la prueba con el paciente
Consentimiento por escrito, firmado por el paciente y atestiguado por el personal
Consentimiento implícito, que se ve en la presencia del paciente en la clínica
Consentimiento que da el médico que ordena en el formulario del laboratorio
preguntas_es.explicacion: El paso de la OMS (WHO) dice: converse la prueba que se va a hacer y obtenga el consentimiento verbal, y añade que el paciente puede rechazarla en cualquier punto antes de la recolección. StatPearls describe la documentación por escrito del consentimiento informado en general, pero el paso de flebotomía de la OMS se apoya en un sí hablado después de una explicación. Nada en ninguna de las dos fuentes deja que la firma de quien pide la prueba sustituya a la del paciente.

preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿Cómo se describen mejor los vasos de los que se toma una muestra de sangre capilar?
opciones: Los vasos más pequeños, de 5 a 10 μm de ancho, que conectan arteriolas y vénulas
Las arterias más pequeñas, de alrededor de 30 μm de ancho, que conectan las arterias con los capilares
Vasos de pared delgada, de 8 a 100 μm de ancho, que llevan la sangre hacia las venas
Venas superficiales que corren en el techo de la fosa cubital del brazo
preguntas_es.explicacion: Los capilares son los vasos más pequeños del cuerpo, de 5 a 10 micrómetros de diámetro, y unen las arteriolas con las vénulas; la muestra capilar se toma por lo común con una punción del talón o del dedo, y en los capilares más estrechos apenas cabe un eritrocito. Las arteriolas promedian 30 micrómetros o menos y las vénulas de 8 a 100 micrómetros, y las venas superficiales de la fosa cubital son sitios de venopunción, no capilares.

preguntas_es.pregunta: Una enfermera pregunta por qué una glucosa marcada como valor crítico se maneja distinto de una prueba pedida como STAT. ¿Qué distingue a las dos?
opciones: Un valor crítico se define sólo por cuánto se aparta el resultado del rango normal; una prueba STAT la designa el clínico que ordena
Un valor crítico lo designa el clínico que ordena; una prueba STAT se define por cuánto se aparta el resultado del rango normal
Un valor crítico se aplica sólo a los resultados de los analizadores del laboratorio; la designación STAT se aplica sólo a los aparatos del punto de atención
Un valor crítico debe repetirse en una muestra nueva; una prueba STAT se informa de la primera corrida sin ninguna repetición
preguntas_es.explicacion: Lo que vuelve crítico un valor es puramente cuánto queda fuera del rango de referencia; el aspecto del paciente no entra en la definición. Una prueba STAT o urgente es lo contrario: la etiqueta el clínico que ordena, y normalmente lo hace sabiendo el estado del paciente. Un resultado del punto de atención que cae en territorio crítico se atiende en el acto y a menudo cambia el manejo, así que se documentan tanto la cifra como las acciones que se tomaron.

opciones: Es aceptable aunque no lo ideal, cuando se está colocando la cánula y antes de conectar los líquidos

Es aceptable sólo para hemocultivos, que deben extraerse antes de conectar ningún líquido
preguntas_es.explicacion: El paso 3 lo llama aceptable aunque no ideal: se puede extraer sangre mientras se está colocando un dispositivo venoso permanente, antes de conectar la cánula a los líquidos intravenosos. El mismo pasaje prohíbe extraer de un acceso que ya está en uso por los resultados falsos, y anota que las muestras de catéter venoso central que toman enfermeras o médicos siguiendo protocolos traen riesgo de contaminación.

preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿Cuál de las venas superficiales del brazo suele ser la más grande de las dos?
opciones: La vena basílica, aunque a veces la cefálica es más grande
La vena cefálica, aunque a veces la basílica es más grande
La vena mediana cubital, que es más grande que cualquiera de las dos
Las dos tienen el mismo calibre, porque drenan territorios iguales
preguntas_es.explicacion: El tamaño varía mucho de un paciente a otro, pero la basílica suele ser la vena superficial más grande del brazo y a veces ese puesto lo ocupa la cefálica. El calibre por sí solo no decide la punción: con la basílica viajan una arteria y un nervio, y eso la hace la más arriesgada de las dos.
